name: LLD-MMRI
full_name: Liver Lesion Diagnosis on Multi-phase MRI
protocol_note: non-contrast, arterial, venous, delayed, T2W, DWI, T1 in/out-of-phase
size: 498 patients, 8 sequences each
description: Multi-phase liver MRI for focal liver lesion diagnosis with per-lesion class labels and bounding boxes.

label_schema: Classification task: 7 liver lesion categories, integer-labeled 0-6 in the label files (-1 marks unlabeled validation/test cases)
Each case has 8 co-registered MRI phases: T2WI, DWI, T1 In Phase, T1 Out Phase, C-pre (non-contrast), C+A (arterial), C+V (venous), C+Delay (delayed)
Per-lesion 3D bounding boxes plus lesion category, stored in Annotation.json (also holds true voxel spacing)
March 2025 update adds pixel-wise segmentation masks (available via Hugging Face)
details.file_structure: Per-case folders (e.g. images/MR-a/) each hold the 8 phases as separate compressed NIfTI files (T2WI.nii.gz, In Phase.nii.gz, Out Phase.nii.gz, C-pre.nii.gz, C+A.nii.gz, C+V.nii.gz, C+Delay.nii.gz, DWI.nii.gz); an Annotation.json stores spacing + bounding-box + category info, and plain-text label files map case names to integer class ids.
details.splits: 316 training / 78 validation / 104 test cases (498 total); training labels released, validation/test labels initially withheld for the LLD-MMRI2023 challenge.
details.extra: Distributions include full-volume data, lesion bounding boxes, and pre-cropped lesion patches; released under CC BY-NC 4.0 for noncommercial research only.

name: CT Colonography
full_name: CT COLONOGRAPHY (ACRIN 6664)
protocol_note: paired prone and supine CT
size: 825 patients (prone + supine)
description: Large screening CT colonography collection (prone/supine) with polyp annotations from the ACRIN 6664 trial.

label_schema: Case-level polyp status grouped into 3 Excel spreadsheets: 35 cases with polyp(s) >=10 mm
243 cases with no polyps found by both CT colonography and optical colonoscopy
Per-polyp descriptors: polyp size, location within colon segment, morphology, and some CT slice locations
Histological classification of polyps (from optical colonoscopy / biopsy reference standard)
details.file_structure: CT images are DICOM (prone and supine acquisitions per patient, downloaded via TCIA Data Retriever); polyp/finding labels are provided as separate Excel (.xls) spreadsheets keyed by patient case ID rather than as pixel-level segmentation masks.
details.extra: No voxel-level polyp segmentations are provided (labels are tabular case/lesion descriptions from the ACRIN 6664 National CT Colonography Trial); TCIA/NCI notes the spreadsheet data cannot be assured error-free since the original analysis was performed externally.

name: MRNet
full_name: MRNet Knee MRI Dataset
protocol_note: sagittal, coronal and axial series per exam
size: 1,370 knee MRI exams
description: 1,370 knee MRI exams from Stanford with binary labels for abnormality, ACL tears and meniscal tears.

label_schema: 3 binary study-level labels: abnormal, ACL tear, meniscal tear
details.file_structure: Per exam: sagittal.npy, coronal.npy, axial.npy (stack of slices, s×256×256) + train/valid label CSVs.
details.splits: 1,130 train / 120 validation (internal) / 120 hidden test

name: fastMRI knee
full_name: fastMRI Knee Raw k-Space and DICOM Dataset
protocol_note: coronal proton-density with and without fat suppression
size: >1,500 fully-sampled knee k-space MRIs + 10,000 clinical DICOM knee MRIs (~1.35 TB)
description: Raw k-space and DICOM knee MRI data released by NYU and Meta AI for accelerated MRI reconstruction research.

label_schema: No pathology labels — raw fully-sampled multi-coil k-space + reconstructed images for MRI reconstruction
details.file_structure: HDF5 per volume (kspace, reconstruction_rss); singlecoil and multicoil tracks; DICOMs separately.
details.splits: Official train / val / test / challenge splits

name: OAI
full_name: Osteoarthritis Initiative
protocol_note: multiple knee MRI sequences (DESS, T2 mapping, TSE) plus radiographs
size: 4,796 participants, longitudinal bilateral knee MRI and X-ray
description: Longitudinal osteoarthritis cohort of 4,796 participants with serial bilateral knee MRI, radiographs and clinical data.

label_schema: Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grade 0-4 for tibiofemoral knee OA severity from central radiographic reading: 0 none, 1 doubtful, 2 minimal/mild, 3 moderate, 4 severe
OARSI-atlas semiquantitative individual radiographic features: joint space narrowing (JSN) and osteophytes graded per compartment (medial/lateral, ~0-3)
Quantitative joint space width (JSW/minimum JSW) measurements from fixed-flexion PA knee radiographs
Patient-reported/clinical OA outcomes: WOMAC (pain, stiffness, function) and related symptom/function scores
Labels are tabular clinical + central-read variables keyed to knees/visits, NOT pixel-level image annotations in the base release
details.file_structure: Bilateral knee radiographs and multi-sequence 3T knee MRI (e.g., sagittal 3D DESS, coronal/sagittal intermediate-weighted TSE) are distributed as DICOM per participant and visit; labels/reads and clinical variables are separate tabular datasets (SAS/ASCII/CSV) linked by participant ID, knee side, and visit rather than embedded masks.
details.extra: OAI is a longitudinal observational cohort (~4,796 participants, baseline plus multi-year follow-up visits) with no official train/val/test split; pixel-level segmentations come only from third-party companions (e.g., OAI-ZIB / Ambellan et al., which manually segmented femoral & tibial bone and cartilage on OAI DESS MRIs).

name: MURA
full_name: MURA: Musculoskeletal Radiographs
protocol_note: Multi-view upper extremity radiographs; seven study types: elbow, finger, forearm, hand, humerus, shoulder, wrist (Stanford Hospital, 2001-2012).
size: 40,561 images / 14,863 studies / 12,173 patients
description: Large upper-extremity radiograph dataset covering seven body parts with radiologist normal/abnormal study labels.

label_schema: Binary study-level classification: normal vs abnormal
Each study labeled y in {0,1}: abnormal (positive) = 1, normal (negative) = 0
7 upper-extremity study types: elbow, finger, forearm, hand, humerus, shoulder, wrist
Labels assigned by board-certified radiologists at time of clinical interpretation (train/valid); test set gold standard = majority vote of 3 radiologists (6 total)
details.file_structure: PNG images organized as MURA-v1.1/{train,valid}/XR_<BODYPART>/patientXXXXX/studyN_<positive|negative>/imageN.png, where the folder name suffix (positive=abnormal, negative=normal) encodes the label; accompanying CSV files (train_labeled_studies.csv / valid_labeled_studies.csv map study folder path to 0/1 label, and train_image_paths.csv / valid_image_paths.csv list per-image paths).
details.splits: Train: 13,457 studies (8,280 normal + 5,177 abnormal); Validation: 1,199 studies (661 normal + 538 abnormal); Test: 207 studies (held out, labels not released). Totals: 14,863 studies / 40,561 images from 12,173 patients.
details.extra: Test set has multi-reader annotations: read by 6 board-certified radiologists (3 used to build the majority-vote gold standard, 3 for measuring radiologist performance); labels are per-study, not per-image, and no lesion segmentation or bounding boxes are provided.

name: RSNA Bone Age
full_name: RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge (2017)
protocol_note: Pediatric left-hand radiographs
size: 14,236 pediatric hand radiographs
description: Pediatric left-hand radiographs labeled with skeletal bone age and sex for bone-age estimation.

label_schema: Regression target: skeletal (bone) age in months, from left-hand radiographs
Sex covariate provided per image: male = True/False (boolean)
Ground truth derived from radiology reports; annotated by multiple expert pediatric radiologist observers
details.file_structure: Left-hand radiographs stored as individual PNG images in train/validation/test image folders, with labels in accompanying CSV files (columns: id, boneage, male) keyed by image filename ID.
details.splits: ~12,611 training images / 1,425 validation images / 200 test images
details.extra: The 200-image held-out test set was reviewed by multiple radiologists, so its ground-truth ages reflect a multi-reader consensus/average rather than a single reader.

name: SKM-TEA
full_name: Stanford Knee MRI Multi-Task Evaluation (SKM-TEA)
protocol_note: Quantitative double-echo steady-state (qDESS) knee MRI acquired clinically at Stanford (GE); 2x1 parallel imaging with 8 or 15 coils, elliptical sampling; missing data estimated with ARC (GE Orchestra SDK) to give fully-sampled k-space; T2 maps derivable.
size: 155 qDESS knee scans (~1.6 TB)
segmentation_detail: 4 tissues (patellar, femoral, tibial cartilage, meniscus)
description: Quantitative double-echo steady-state knee MRI with raw k-space, DICOM, tissue segmentations and pathology bounding boxes.

label_schema: Dense tissue segmentation: manual masks for 4 tissues, stored one-hot in the HDF5 'seg' key as 6 channels: Patellar Cartilage, Femoral Cartilage, Tibial Cartilage - Medial, Tibial Cartilage - Lateral, Meniscus - Medial, Meniscus - Lateral (the 4 clinical tissues, with tibial cartilage and meniscus split into medial/lateral compartments)

Pathology detection: 2D bounding-box annotations for 16 clinically relevant pathology categories spanning joint effusion and meniscal, ligament, and cartilage lesions; each category is a pathology type + subtype (e.g. 'Meniscal Tear - Myxoid')
Quantitative MRI (qMRI): raw dual-echo (qDESS) k-space enabling T2 relaxation-time / biomarker estimation as a downstream quantitative target
details.file_structure: One HDF5 file per scan: the image/DICOM track holds keys echo1, echo2 (image volumes), seg (segmentation), and stats; the raw-data track holds kspace, maps, and target (complex-valued); scanner DICOMs and NIfTI segmentation masks are also provided, and detection labels are COCO-style JSON annotation files (train.json/val.json/test.json).
details.splits: 155 total scans: 86 train, 33 validation, 36 test (test drawn from patients who underwent arthroscopic surgery)
details.extra: ~25,000 slices from 155 patients (~1.6 TB); segmentations and pathology bounding boxes were manually annotated, and the DICOM-track and raw-data (reconstruction) tracks share the same underlying scans.

name: KneeMRI
full_name: KneeMRI Dataset (Clinical Hospital Centre Rijeka)
protocol_note: Sagittal proton-density weighted knee MRI volumes, 12-bit grayscale
size: 917 sagittal PD-weighted knee MRI volumes
description: 917 sagittal PD-weighted knee MRI volumes from Rijeka, Croatia, labeled for anterior cruciate ligament condition.

label_schema: Task: volume-level classification of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) condition, target column `aclDiagnosis`
Per-volume ROI annotation: a manually extracted wider rectangular region of interest around the ligament, given as position (roiX, roiY, roiZ) and size (roiWidth, roiHeight, roiDepth)
Other metadata columns: volumeFilename, kneeLR (left/right knee), examId (and volumeId)
details.file_structure: 917 12-bit grayscale sagittal knee MRI volumes stored as Python pickle (.pck) files (each a single 3D NumPy array, one file per volume), plus one comma-delimited metadata.csv holding the per-volume aclDiagnosis label and ROI coordinates; an example.py loader is shipped with the dataset.
details.extra: No official train/test split (the source paper, Stajduhar et al., CMPB 2017, evaluated with cross-validation); labels are single-reader radiologist diagnoses and the class distribution is strongly imbalanced (reported ~690 healthy, 172 partially injured, 55 completely ruptured of the 917 volumes). Note: the dataset's descriptive text lists conditions as (1) healthy, (2) partially injured, (3) completely ruptured, but the actual aclDiagnosis column in metadata.csv is 0/1/2-coded.

name: Digital Hand Atlas
full_name: Digital Hand Atlas for Skeletal Development
protocol_note: Left-hand radiographs of normally developing children; image format not stated on the official page.
size: ~1,400 normal pediatric hand radiographs
description: Reference collection of ~1,400 normal pediatric hand radiographs across ages, sexes and ethnic groups for bone-age assessment.

label_schema: Primary label: bone age assessment ground truth - each left-hand radiograph carries two independent radiologist bone-age readings (fields 'Reading1' and 'Reading2')
Chronological age and date of birth recorded per subject (basis for bone-age comparison)
Race/ethnicity: ASI (Asian), BLK (African American), CAU (Caucasian), HIS (Hispanic)
Age group index 0-18 (19 groups spanning ages 0 to 18 years)
Additional per-subject metadata: height, weight, trunk height, Tanner stage, exam date
details.file_structure: Collection of pediatric left-hand radiograph images with per-subject tabular metadata (readings/demographics) held in a relational database; browsable/queryable by race, gender, and age group, with the full atlas available as a ~7GB download.
details.extra: Multi-reader annotation: two independent bone-age readings are provided per image; the atlas consists of normal-development pediatric hand radiographs intended as a reference for computer-aided bone age assessment. Exact total image count and on-disk image file format are not stated on the official page and were not verified.

name: LERA
full_name: LERA — Lower Extremity Radiographs
protocol_note: Radiographs of the foot, knee, ankle or hip acquired at Stanford University Medical Center 2003-2014; images vary in size, resolution and color and may include duplicates.
size: 182 patients (foot, knee, ankle, hip)
description: Lower-extremity radiographs (foot, knee, ankle, hip) from 182 patients with radiologist normal/abnormal labels.

label_schema: Binary patient-level classification: normal (y=0) vs abnormal (y=1)
'Abnormal' is a catch-all covering varied findings including degeneration, hardware, arthritis, and fractures, among others
Radiograph type / body-part field per study: foot, knee, ankle, or hip
No fine-grained finding categories or segmentation/bounding-box annotations - abnormality is a single binary label
Note: one label is assigned per patient and applies to ALL of that patient's images (patient-level, not image-level)
details.file_structure: A single .csv file maps patient ID numbers to their binary diagnosis label (normal/abnormal) and radiograph type (body part); the radiograph image files are grouped per patient. Images are highly variable in size, resolution, and color (collected 2003-2014) and may include duplicates.
details.extra: Multi-reader ground truth: the original attending radiologist's read was re-adjudicated by two additional board-certified radiologists (each ~6 years post-graduate experience) who independently labeled the images, with final labels by majority-vote consensus among the two radiologists and the prospective exam report. LERA (182 patients) was released specifically as a held-out TEST set for generalized lower-extremity abnormality detection, so no train/validation split is provided.

name: RSNA Screening Mammography
full_name: RSNA Screening Mammography Breast Cancer Detection (2023)
protocol_note: Four-view screening mammograms (CC/MLO etc.) from two sites; DICOM, many JPEG 2000-compressed
size: Just under 20,000 screening exams from 2 sites (Kaggle training split: 54,706 images / 11,913 patients)
license: RSNA MIRA Dataset Research Use Agreement (non-commercial research and education; no sharing or redistribution)
host: RSNA MIRA / AWS Open Data (controlled access)
description: De-identified four-view screening mammograms (DICOM) from two sites (Emory, USA and BreastScreen Victoria, Australia), enriched to ~4% cancer, with breast-level cancer labels and BI-RADS/density metadata, officially released by RSNA via MIRA/AWS after the 2023 Kaggle challenge.

label_schema: Task: image/breast-level binary classification - predict presence of breast cancer
cancer - target label, 0/1, whether malignancy was found in that breast
biopsy - 0/1, whether a follow-up biopsy was performed on the breast
invasive - 0/1, if the breast is positive for cancer, whether the cancer is invasive
density - breast density rating A, B, C, or D (A=mostly fatty ... D=extremely dense)
implant - 0/1, whether the patient has breast implants
laterality - L or R (which breast the image is of)
view - mammography view orientation (e.g. CC, MLO, ML, LM, AT)
Metadata IDs: site_id, patient_id, image_id, machine_id; prediction_id (patient_id + laterality) used for test submission
details.file_structure: Zip archive of DICOM files ([train|test]_images/{patient_id}/{image_id}.dcm; many images JPEG 2000-compressed) plus CSV metadata, in the controlled-access S3 bucket arn:aws:s3:::screening-mammography-breast (us-west-2); access requested via MIRA (email registration + acceptance of the research use agreement).
details.splits: Training set: ~54,706 images from ~11,913 patients across 2 sites; official test set is hidden (held-out for Kaggle scoring), so no released validation count.
details.extra: Dataset DOI 10.1148/dataset.smbc.2024 (cite as 'RSNA-SMBC Dataset, November 2022'); data descriptor: Trivedi et al., Radiology: AI 2026 (doi:10.1148/ryai.250375). Enriched to ~4% cancer prevalence (about 5x the screening rate); interval cancers excluded; no lesion-level annotations. Fields biopsy/invasive/BIRADS/density are training-split only. Per the descriptor paper, negatives had 1-year (site 1, US) or 2-year (site 2, Australia) negative follow-up.
details.label_readers: No research re-reading; BI-RADS (0/1/2) and density come from the sites' clinical screening assessments
details.reference_standard: Cancer = screen-detected cancer with biopsy/surgical pathology proof (per breast); negatives = screen-negative with negative follow-up, biopsy-proven benign, or recalled with benign/negative work-up; interval cancers excluded

label_variants.name: Kaggle RSNA Screening Mammography Breast Cancer Detection (competition release)
label_variants.note: Original 2022-23 competition distribution under the competition data license; test labels hidden

details.third_party_note: AWS/MIRA license: 'for non-commercial purposes only, including academic research and education' ... 'You may not share or redistribute a copy of any portion or all of the data in any form.' No explicit API/online-service language.

name: CBIS-DDSM
full_name: Curated Breast Imaging Subset of DDSM
protocol_note: Scanned film mammography (DDSM) from several scanners at different institutions; LJPEG decompressed to 16-bit TIFF and converted to DICOM; CC and MLO views.
size: 10,239 images / 1,566 subjects
segmentation_detail: ROI masks and bounding boxes for masses and calcifications
description: Curated DICOM-converted subset of DDSM screening mammograms with pathology labels, BI-RADS and ROI segmentations.

label_schema: Pathology: BENIGN / BENIGN_WITHOUT_CALLBACK / MALIGNANT; BI-RADS assessment 0–5; breast density 1–4
ROI segmentation mask + cropped patch per lesion
details.file_structure: DICOM full images + ROI mask + cropped images; CSV descriptors for mass/calc train and test separately.
details.splits: ~2,458 train / ~645 test lesions (predefined)
details.label_readers: Labels and BI-RADS carried over from the original DDSM metadata; a trained mammographer reviewed questionable mass cases (unclear masses removed); mass ROIs refined by a level-set algorithm initialised from DDSM contours (calcifications not re-segmented)
details.reference_standard: Pathology label (BENIGN / BENIGN_WITHOUT_CALLBACK / MALIGNANT) from DDSM 'verified pathology information'; BENIGN_WITHOUT_CALLBACK is not defined on the official pages
details.third_party_note: CC BY 3.0 (TCIA Data Usage Policy: citation required). Digitized film decompressed from LJPEG to TIFF and then converted to DICOM, so there are no original acquisition headers.

related.name: DDSM (Digital Database for Screening Mammography)
related.note: Curated subset of DDSM; LJPEG decompressed losslessly to DICOM, questionable masses removed, mass ROIs refined by level-set segmentation, standardized train/test splits

name: VinDr-Mammo
full_name: VinDr-Mammo: full-field digital mammography benchmark
protocol_note: Full-field digital mammography, four-view exams (L/R x CC/MLO); DICOM retains Manufacturer and Model Name tags
size: 5,000 exams / 20,000 images
segmentation_detail: bounding-box annotations for findings (BI-RADS 3-5)
description: Full-field digital mammography benchmark of 5,000 four-view exams with breast-level BI-RADS/density and bounding-box finding annotations.

label_schema: Breast density: BI-RADS density A, B, C, or D (per breast/image)

Bounding-box findings (10 categories): Mass, Suspicious Calcification, Asymmetry, Focal Asymmetry, Global Asymmetry, Architectural Distortion, Suspicious Lymph Node, Skin Thickening, Skin Retraction, Nipple Retraction
Each bounding-box finding carries its own local BI-RADS assessment (only findings graded BI-RADS 3, 4, or 5 are annotated)
Bounding boxes given as pixel coordinates xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax
details.file_structure: Full-field digital mammograms stored as DICOM under images/ (one folder per study, 4 files each: L/R x CC/MLO views); labels in CSV files (breast-level_annotations.csv, finding_annotations.csv, metadata.csv) with bounding boxes as xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax columns.
details.splits: 5,000 studies (20,000 images) split into 4,000 training and 1,000 test studies, stratified to preserve BI-RADS and finding distributions.
details.extra: Each exam was independently double-read by two radiologists with disagreements resolved by a third arbitrating radiologist; findings graded BI-RADS 1-2 (benign) were not given bounding boxes.
details.label_readers: 3 radiologists (>10 years mammography experience): each exam double-read independently by 2, disagreements arbitrated by the third
details.reference_standard: BI-RADS radiologist assessment only; no pathology confirmation stated
details.third_party_note: PhysioNet Restricted Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0, clause 3: 'I will not share access to PhysioNet restricted data with anyone else.' No explicit API language; PhysioNet's LLM guidance (written for credentialed MIMIC data) treats API submission as sharing access, so treat as likely restricted. DICOM keeps image-processing tags, age, Manufacturer and Model Name.

name: CMMD
full_name: The Chinese Mammography Database
protocol_note: Full-field digital mammography acquired on a GE Senographe DS system; images collected as TIFF and converted to DICOM.
size: 5,202 images / 1,775 patients
description: Mammography database of 1,775 Chinese patients with biopsy-confirmed benign/malignant labels and molecular subtype for a subset.

label_schema: Pathology classification (image/breast-level): Benign or Malignant, biopsy-confirmed
Molecular subtype (subset of 749 patients / 1,498 mammographies): Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-positive (HER2-enriched), Triple-negative
Breast laterality: L or R (LeftRight column)
details.file_structure: Images are DICOM (converted from original TIFF), organized in the standard TCIA per-patient folder hierarchy; labels are in a single Excel clinical-data spreadsheet (e.g., CMMD_clinicaldata_revision.xlsx) keyed by patient ID (ID1/ID2), with columns for LeftRight, Age, number of images, abnormality, classification, and subtype. No segmentation masks or ROI/RTSTRUCT files are provided.
details.extra: This is a classification-only dataset with no pixel-level annotations; molecular subtype labels exist only for a 749-patient subset, while benign/malignant classification and abnormality (calcification/mass) cover the full cohort (1,775 patients, 3,728 studies, 5,202 images).
details.reference_standard: Benign/malignant = biopsy-confirmed (TCIA); molecular subtype for 749 patients (determination method not stated on TCIA page)
details.third_party_note: CC BY 4.0 (TCIA Data Usage Policy: citation required). DICOM files were created from the original TIFF images, so no original acquisition headers exist.

name: INbreast
full_name: INbreast: full-field digital mammographic database
protocol_note: Full-field digital mammography, Siemens MammoNovation; CC and MLO views
size: 410 images / 115 cases
segmentation_detail: expert pixel-level lesion contours (XML)
description: Full-field digital mammography database (410 images) from Porto with BI-RADS, density and expert XML lesion contours; access by request.

label_schema: Pixel-level ROI contours (expert-drawn) per finding, each ROI tagged by a 'Name' lesion type
ROI finding types: Point / pectoral muscle annotation
Per-image metadata: ACR breast density category (1-4)
Per-image binary finding flags: mass, micros (calcifications), distortion, asymmetry; plus free-text findings notes (in Portuguese)
details.file_structure: Images are full-field digital mammograms stored as DICOM (.dcm) files; per-image expert lesion contours are stored as separate XML files in Apple plist / OsiriX format (ROIs with a 'Name' type and 'Point_px' polygon vertices in pixel coordinates); global case/image metadata (BI-RADS, ACR density, laterality, view, finding flags) is provided in an accompanying spreadsheet (CSV/XLS).
details.extra: 115 cases / 410 images total (90 cases with both breasts = 4 views each, 25 mastectomy cases = 2 views each); acquired on a Siemens MammoNovation FFDM system. Not every image is annotated with contours for every finding type, and contour segmentation may be incomplete for some cases; masks must be rasterized from the XML polygon points (e.g. via cv2.fillPoly).
details.label_readers: Lesion contours 'made by specialists' (official page and paper abstract); per-image reader protocol not verifiable from accessible official sources
details.third_party_note: No published license; the official access page states the database is no longer supported by the group and access is by contacting the authors.

name: Duke Breast Cancer MRI
full_name: Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI of Breast Cancer Patients (Duke)
protocol_note: DCE-MRI: non-fat-sat T1, fat-sat pre-contrast and 3-4 post-contrast sequences
size: 922 patients / ~773,000 images
segmentation_detail: radiologist 3D bounding boxes around lesions
description: DCE-MRI of 922 invasive breast cancer patients with 3D tumor bounding boxes plus extensive clinical, genomic and radiomic data.

label_schema: Radiologist-drawn 3D bounding box around the primary tumor per patient (one box per case), given as pixel/slice index ranges: Start Row, End Row, Start Column, End Column, Start Slice, End Slice

Clinical/pathology features per patient: demographics (age, race/ethnicity, menopausal status), tumor receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), molecular subtype, tumor grade and histologic type, staging, treatment (surgery, chemo, radiation), and outcomes (recurrence, survival)
922 computer-extracted / imaging feature values and MRI acquisition + mammography/ultrasound descriptors provided as tabular columns
details.file_structure: Images are DICOM MRI series (pre-contrast and multiple post-contrast dynamic T1 sequences) organized per patient/study; annotations are supplied as separate XLSX spreadsheets ('Annotation Boxes', 'Clinical and Other Features', 'Imaging Features', and a filepath-mapping file) keyed by Patient ID (Breast_MRI_XXX), not as per-image mask files.
details.extra: The primary lesion annotation is a single axis-aligned 3D bounding box per patient (row/column/slice index ranges) rather than a voxel-level segmentation mask; the box is drawn on the first post-contrast sequence.

name: Breast-Diagnosis
full_name: BREAST-DIAGNOSIS
protocol_note: 3+ MR pulse sequences (T2, STIR, BLISS) with contrast; plus PET, CT, mammography
size: 88 subjects / ~105,050 images
description: Multi-modality breast imaging (multi-sequence MR, PET, CT, mammography) for 88 subjects with lesion-type and biomarker data.

label_schema: Case/diagnosis categories: high-risk normals, DCIS, fibroids, and lobular carcinomas
Pathology molecular markers per patient: ER, PR, HER2 status and Oncotype DX recurrence scores
BI-RADS MRI descriptive features extracted from imaging reports
Approximate lesion localization: key image slice number with approximate X-Y center position when a mass was found (point/location annotation, not a pixel segmentation)
details.file_structure: Radiology images are stored as DICOM (MR, CT, PET/PT, and MG modalities) organized per subject/study/series in the standard TCIA layout; the labels/annotations are supplied as a separate XLSX spreadsheet containing clinical, pathology, molecular-marker, BI-RADS, and lesion-location fields.
details.extra: No tumor segmentations, RTSTRUCT, or DICOM-SEG objects are provided; lesion 'annotation' is limited to an approximate key-slice X-Y center point, and molecular/pathology labels come only from the companion spreadsheet. Collection covers 88 subjects (148 studies, 429 series).

name: BCS-DBT
full_name: Breast Cancer Screening — Digital Breast Tomosynthesis
protocol_note: Reconstructed digital breast tomosynthesis volumes, one compressed DICOM file per view (CC/MLO, up to 4 views per exam); some headers have incorrect laterality/orientation requiring correction.
size: 5,060 patients / 22,032 scans (~1.63 TB)
segmentation_detail: bounding boxes for lesions
description: Large digital breast tomosynthesis screening dataset of 5,060 patients with normal/actionable/benign/cancer labels and lesion bounding boxes.

label_schema: Per-volume classification into 4 mutually exclusive study labels: Normal, Actionable (recall requested, not biopsied), Benign (biopsy-proven), Cancer (biopsy-proven)
Lesion bounding boxes provided ONLY for biopsy-proven volumes (benign and cancer cases)
Architectural distortion flagged via a binary 'AD' column
details.file_structure: Images are DICOM reconstructed DBT volumes (one 3D volume per view, up to 4 views RCC/LCC/RMLO/LMLO per exam); labels/annotations are separate CSV spreadsheets - a file-paths/label CSV mapping PatientID + StudyUID + View to Normal/Actionable/Benign/Cancer, and a boxes CSV with columns PatientID, StudyUID, View, Slice (central slice of lesion), X, Y, Width, Height (0-indexed box), Class, AD, and VolumeSlices.
details.splits: Total 5,060 patients / 22,032 DBT volumes. Train: 4,362 patients (19,148 volumes); Validation: 280 patients (1,163 volumes); Test: 418 patients (1,721 volumes).
details.extra: Bounding boxes mark only the biopsied lesion on its central slice (single-slice annotation with a listed VolumeSlices for evaluation tolerance); Normal and Actionable volumes have no box annotations. Companion CSVs are distributed alongside the DICOM collection on TCIA.

name: ISPY1 (ACRIN 6657)
full_name: Breast DCE-MRI from the I-SPY 1 / ACRIN 6657 trial
protocol_note: DCE-MRI across 4 neoadjuvant-chemo timepoints; T2 + pre/post-contrast T1
size: 222 patients
segmentation_detail: functional tumor volume segmentations
description: Multi-center serial DCE-MRI (222 patients, 4 timepoints) with functional tumor volume segmentations for predicting chemotherapy response.

label_schema: Functional Tumor Volume (FTV): binary segmentation mask of enhancing tumor voxels, defined on DCE-MRI by peak-enhancement / signal-enhancement-ratio (SER) thresholding criteria (the trial's primary imaging biomarker)
Tumor Volume of Interest (VOI): a 3D rectangular bounding box drawn to enclose the enhancing tumor region plus surrounding peritumoral tissue, used as the input region for FTV/SER computation
Structural Tumor Volume (STV): full 3D voxel-wise delineation of the entire primary lesion, including both enhancing and non-enhancing tumor regions (companion segmentation analysis result)
Note: masks are single-lesion binary tumor labels (foreground = tumor), not multi-class organ/tissue segmentations
details.file_structure: Main TCIA collection is DICOM: breast DCE-MRI series plus derived SEG (DICOM-SEG) functional-tumor-volume analysis maps generated at UCSF, organized by TCIA patient/study/series folders with clinical & outcome variables in accompanying Excel spreadsheets; the separate STV/FTV/VOI tumor-segmentation analysis result is distributed as NIfTI images/masks (~6.1 GB) with radiomic features in XLSX and a CaPTk parameter CSV.
details.extra: No ML train/val/test split; the collection is instead tiered into quality-control Levels 0-3 (Level 0 = 222 subjects/847 studies down to Level 3 = 162 subjects). The Structural Tumor Volume (STV) segmentations come from a separate TCIA analysis result covering 163 subjects / 1,467 studies and were reviewed and approved by a board-certified fellowship-trained breast radiologist; FTV segmentations were produced centrally by the UCSF Breast Imaging Research Program.

name: ISPY2
full_name: I-SPY 2 TRIAL Breast DCE-MRI
protocol_note: DCE-MRI + T2 across 4 treatment timepoints; derived parametric maps
size: 719 patients
segmentation_detail: functional tumor volume masks (DICOM SEG)
description: I-SPY 2 trial serial breast DCE-MRI (719 patients, 4 timepoints) with parametric maps and DICOM-SEG functional tumor volume segmentations.

label_schema: Functional Tumor Volume (FTV) analysis mask - a DICOM SEG segmentation of the tumor region derived from DCE-MRI (series description 'ISPY2: VOLSER: uni-lateral cropped: Analysis Mask')

Mask is bit-encoded, capturing the FTV computation steps: pre-contrast background threshold, minimum percent-enhancement threshold (nominally 70%), a manually defined rectangular VOI, and manually defined 'OMIT' regions excluding non-tumor enhancement
Accompanying parametric maps (derived DICOM objects): PEearly (percent enhancement ~120-150 s), PElate (percent enhancement ~450 s), SER (signal enhancement ratio, scaled x1000 for integer storage)
Clinical/outcome labels in supplementary spreadsheets: demographics, molecular/receptor status, treatment arm, follow-up, and pathologic complete response (pCR)
details.file_structure: DICOM DCE-MRI image series with the FTV segmentation stored as a separate DICOM SEG series (series number = original DCE series root + 1900) plus derived parametric-map objects; clinical outcomes and radiomic features provided as supplementary Excel spreadsheets.
details.extra: Collection covers ~719 patients from the I-SPY2 TRIAL (neoadjuvant breast cancer); supplementary clinical/radiomic spreadsheets are available only for a ~384-patient subset, and the maps/segmentations are stated to be 'believed identical' to those in the primary trial analyses (not independently re-verified).
details.label_readers: FTV masks computed by thresholding with a manually defined VOI and OMIT regions (operator not stated)
details.reference_standard: pCR = pathologic complete response at surgery (histopathologic outcome data)
details.third_party_note: CC BY 4.0 (TCIA); TCIA Data Usage Policy requires citation; no clause restricting external services.

name: BreastDM
full_name: BreastDM: DCE-MRI dataset for breast tumor segmentation and classification
protocol_note: DCE-MRI with pre-contrast, post-contrast and subtraction sequences
size: 232 cases (147 malignant, 85 benign)
segmentation_detail: tumor segmentation masks (PNG)
description: Breast DCE-MRI dataset of 232 cases with tumor segmentation masks and benign/malignant labels, distributed via GitHub.

label_schema: Two annotated tasks: binary classification and tumor segmentation (from breast DCE-MRI)
Classification: 2 classes (num_class=2) - 'B' = benign, 'M' = malignant, encoded by folder name
Segmentation: single-class binary tumor mask (num-classes=1) - foreground pixels = breast tumor region, background = 0
No sub-typing, BI-RADS, or multi-class tissue labels - malignancy label is patient/tumor-level benign-vs-malignant only
details.file_structure: Processed 2D slices are distributed via Google Drive: for classification, .jpg images sorted into B/ and M/ folders; for segmentation, paired .png files in images/ and masks/ directories matched by identical filenames (001.png, 002.png, ...) where masks are single-channel binary PNGs; the repo also hosts raw sample cases as DICOM (.dcm) organized as Benign|Malignant / BreaDM-Be|Ma-<id> / <series> with DCE-MRI series (VIBRANT pre-contrast, VIBRANT+C1..C8 post-contrast, and SUB1..SUB8 subtraction series).
details.extra: No fixed official train/val/test split is provided; the classification training code defaults to a configurable 80/20 split (--split_train_ratio 0.8). The repo separately links a 'RoI image' Google Drive archive of tumor region-of-interest crops.

name: EMBED
full_name: EMory BrEast imaging Dataset (EMBED)
protocol_note: 2D full-field digital mammography, synthetic 2D (C-view) and 3D digital breast tomosynthesis; open release is 20% of the 2D and C-view data, with DBT, US and MRI to be added later
size: 3.4M images from ~110,000 patients; 60,000 annotated lesions
description: Large, racially diverse Emory mammography dataset (2D, C-view and DBT) with 60,000 lesions linked to BI-RADS descriptors and pathologic outcomes.

label_schema: BI-RADS assessment (`asses` field): 0=Additional evaluation needed, 1=Negative, 2=Benign, 3=Probably benign, 4=Suspicious, 5=Highly suggestive of malignancy, 6=Known biopsy-proven malignancy
Breast density (`tissueden`, BI-RADS A-D): 1=Almost entirely fat (A), 2=Scattered fibroglandular (B), 3=Heterogeneously dense (C), 4=Extremely dense (D)
Pathologic severity (`path_severity`): 0=Invasive cancer, 1=Non-invasive cancer, 2=High-risk lesion, 3=Borderline lesion, 4=Benign, 5=Negative/normal, 6=Non-breast cancer
Detailed pathology diagnoses in text columns path1-path10
BI-RADS imaging descriptors: mass shape (`massshape`), mass margin (`massmargin`), mass density (`massdens`), calcification type (`calcfind`), calcification distribution (`calcdistri`)
Lesion ROI bounding boxes (`ROI_coords`) as (ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax) with a `match_level` reliability score (1=primary, 2=secondary)
Image type (`FinalImageType`): 2D, 3D (DBT tomosynthesis), C-view synthetic; laterality (L/R) and view position (CC, MLO, etc.)
details.file_structure: Images are DICOM files organized on disk as ./cohort/patientID/studyID/SOPinstanceUID.dcm; labels come as CSV files — EMBED_OpenData_metadata.csv (one row per image file, with DICOM tags, ROI_coords, and file paths), a reduced metadata variant, and EMBED_OpenData_clinical.csv (one row per finding, with BI-RADS assessment, density, and pathology labels).
details.extra: No official train/test split is provided; clinical and metadata CSVs must be joined on patient ID (empi_anon), exam ID (acc_anon), and laterality (clinical `side` vs metadata `ImageLateralityFinal`) to link labels/ROIs to the correct images. The full release contains ~3.4M+ images with roughly 60,000 annotated lesions across 110,000+ patients.
details.label_readers: Clinical interpreting radiologist (single reader): BI-RADS and descriptors recorded at interpretation in MagView; ROIs are circles drawn by the interpreting radiologist on screen-save images, auto-extracted and mapped back
details.reference_standard: BI-RADS = clinical radiologist assessment; pathology outcomes recorded per finding in MagView and cross-checked against CoPath pathology reports with NLP (path_severity 0-6)
details.third_party_note: EMBED Research Use Agreement: 'YOU MAY NOT DISTRIBUTE, PUBLISH, OR REPRODUCE A COPY of any portion or all of EMBED to others without specific prior written permission'; 'You may not otherwise copy, reproduce, retransmit, distribute, publish ... or otherwise transfer any material.' No explicit API language.

name: HECKTOR
full_name: HEad and neCK TumOR segmentation and outcome prediction challenge
protocol_note: FDG-PET/CT (PET and low-dose CT of PET/CT) from 9 centers (Canada, Switzerland, France, USA)
size: ~882 cases (2022 edition)
segmentation_detail: primary tumor (GTVp) and lymph node (GTVn) contours
paired_text_detail: clinical data (age, sex, HPV, treatment) and recurrence-free survival endpoints
description: MICCAI challenge for automatic segmentation of head and neck tumors and lymph nodes and outcome prediction in FDG-PET/CT.

details.file_structure: Per patient: CT.nii.gz, PT.nii.gz (PET) and a GTV label NIfTI; clinical CSV with HPV, treatment and survival.
details.splits: ~524 train / ~359 test (2022, 9 centers)

name: HNSCC
full_name: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (MD Anderson)
protocol_note: CT, PT, MR with RTPLAN/RTSTRUCT/RTDOSE; baseline contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) for oropharyngeal subset; whole-body PET-CT or abdominal CT before and after RT for CT-Atlas subset; some PET exams have two AC series (head & neck and eyes-to-thighs). MRI sequences not specified.
size: 627 patients
segmentation_detail: primary and nodal gross tumor volume contours (RTSTRUCT)
paired_text_detail: demographics, risk factors, stage, recurrence, survival and treatment data
conditions: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
description: TCIA collection of imaging, radiation therapy and clinical data from 627 head and neck squamous cell carcinoma patients at MD Anderson.

label_schema: GTVp - primary gross tumor volume (RTSTRUCT contour)
GTVn - nodal gross tumor volume (RTSTRUCT contour)
ROIs named per AAPM TG-263 nomenclature; manual segmentations by radiation oncologists
details.file_structure: DICOM images (CT, PET/PT, MR) with radiotherapy DICOM objects (RTSTRUCT for tumor contours, plus RTPLAN and RTDOSE) organized per-patient on TCIA.
details.extra: Manual GTV contours are provided for the oropharyngeal-cancer subset (~412 patients), not for all 627 patients in the full collection.

name: HN1
full_name: HEAD-NECK-RADIOMICS-HN1
protocol_note: Pre-treatment CT (some PT series) of HNSCC patients treated by radiotherapy; contrast phase and PET tracer not stated.
size: 137 patients
segmentation_detail: pre-treatment gross tumor volume (DICOM SEG and RTSTRUCT)
paired_text_detail: demographic, follow-up, chemotherapy and survival data
conditions: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
description: TCIA radiomics collection of pre-treatment CT and clinical/outcome data for 137 head and neck cancer patients from MAASTRO.

label_schema: Primary gross tumor volume (GTV) of the primary neoplasm, manually delineated on pre-treatment CT by an experienced radiation oncologist
Single structure of interest (primary-tumor GTV); no organs-at-risk or nodal GTV schema documented on the collection page
details.file_structure: DICOM-based collection: CT (and some PT) image series with tumor delineations provided as DICOM RTSTRUCT (from v1) and DICOM SEG (added in v2, Sept 2019); accompanying clinical/demographic data provided as tabular files with a data dictionary.
details.extra: 137 head-and-neck squamous cell carcinoma patients; images fall under the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy due to facial-reconstruction re-identification risk. Clinical data includes demographics, treatment, and follow-up/survival fields (a 'chemotherapy_given' field added in v3, July 2020).

name: TCGA-HNSC
full_name: TCGA Head-Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma Collection
protocol_note: Heterogeneous multi-site routine-care imaging (CT 211, MR 28, PT 33 cases by modality/site); scanners, manufacturers and acquisition protocols vary; RTDOSE/RTSTRUCT/RTPLAN for a subset.
size: 227 patients (479 studies)
segmentation_detail: radiation therapy structures (RTSTRUCT) for a subset
paired_text_detail: matched clinical, pathological and genomic data via TCGA/GDC
conditions: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
license: CC BY 3.0; some imaging controlled access
description: TCIA imaging collection for 227 head and neck cancer patients matched to genomic and clinical data in The Cancer Genome Atlas.

label_schema: Annotations are original clinical radiation-therapy DICOM objects (RTSTRUCT structure sets, plus RTDOSE and RTPLAN), available only for a subset of patients

RTSTRUCT files contain clinician-drawn ROI contours from treatment planning (target volumes and organs at risk); the collection does NOT publish a curated or standardized list of structure/organ names, so exact contour labels vary by institution and are not enumerated
No image-level classification labels; matched clinical/genomic/pathology metadata is available separately via the NCI Genomic Data Commons (GDC), not as imaging annotations
details.file_structure: All data is stored as DICOM under a per-patient TCIA folder hierarchy (patient > study > series); imaging series are CT/PT/MR DICOM, and the radiation-therapy annotations are separate DICOM RTSTRUCT (contours), RTDOSE, and RTPLAN series rather than DICOM-SEG or NIfTI/CSV.
details.extra: This is a TCIA archival collection (227 subjects; CT, PT, MR, RTDOSE, RTSTRUCT, RTPLAN, OT), not a segmentation challenge — RT structures are original clinical contours available only for a subset of patients, so there is no consistent, verified per-class segmentation schema across the cohort.

name: Head-Neck-PET-CT
full_name: Head-Neck-PET-CT
protocol_note: Pre-treatment FDG-PET/CT plus radiotherapy planning CT; RTSTRUCT, RTDOSE, RTPLAN and REG series; contrast use not stated
size: 298 patients
segmentation_detail: radiotherapy GTV contours (RTSTRUCT)
paired_text_detail: histopathology, tumor grade and follow-up outcomes
description: TCIA collection of FDG-PET/CT and radiotherapy planning CT with GTV contours and outcome data for 298 head and neck cancer patients.

label_schema: Radiotherapy GTV contours stored as named ROIs in DICOM-RTSTRUCT (no integer label indices)
GTV primary - gross tumor volume at the primary tumor site
GTV lymph nodes - gross tumor volume of involved lymph nodes
A companion spreadsheet lists the exact ROI/structure names used for 'GTV primary' and 'GTV lymph nodes' across the RTSTRUCT files (names are inconsistent and comma-separated per patient)
Clinical/outcome labels per patient: age, sex, TNM/tumor stage, histopathological type, tumor grade, and follow-up outcomes (metastases, survival)
details.file_structure: Per-patient DICOM studies containing CT, PET, and RTSTRUCT (plus RTDOSE, RTPLAN, and REG) series; GTV contours are stored as named ROIs inside the DICOM-RTSTRUCT files rather than pixel masks, and clinical/structure-name metadata is provided in accompanying Excel spreadsheets.
details.extra: 298 patients from 4 Quebec institutions (2 of the original 300 excluded); RTSTRUCT ROI naming is not standardized, so the provided structure-name spreadsheet is needed to map ROIs to GTV-primary vs GTV-lymph-node classes.

name: RADCURE
full_name: CT Images from a Large Head and Neck Cohort (RADCURE)
protocol_note: Radiotherapy planning CT collected 2005-2017 at UHN Toronto on systems from three manufacturers using standard clinical protocols; clinical table has a 'Contrast Enhanced' column indicating which patients received contrast.
size: 3,346 patients
segmentation_detail: primary GTV, nodal GTV and 19 organs-at-risk contours
paired_text_detail: demographic, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up data with survival status
description: TCIA head and neck CT dataset of 3,346 patients treated with definitive radiotherapy, with tumor and organ-at-risk contours and outcomes.

label_schema: Annotations are DICOM-RTSTRUCT region-of-interest contours (polygon ROIs), NOT integer-indexed voxel label maps
19 organs-at-risk (OAR) contours per applicable patient, with TG263-standardized ROI names (individual OAR names not enumerated on the TCIA page; 'parotid' is one explicitly referenced example)
Contour ROI names standardized via a provided mapping spreadsheet from original contour names to TG263 nomenclature
Companion tabular clinical/outcome labels (demographics, diagnosis, treatment, follow-up/survival status) provided alongside the imaging annotations

name: QIN-HeadNeck
full_name: QIN-HEADNECK
protocol_note: 18F-FDG PET/CT scans before and after therapy, with follow-up scans where clinically indicated; series CT and PT plus SR, SEG, RWV objects
size: 279 subjects
segmentation_detail: DICOM SEG segmentations plus DICOM SR quantitative PET/CT results
paired_text_detail: clinical data (demographics, treatment, follow-up) in XLSX
license: CC BY 3.0; some imaging controlled access
description: TCIA collection of serial pre/post-therapy FDG-PET/CT with DICOM SEG/SR quantitative analysis objects for head and neck cancer.

label_schema: DICOM SEG: binary segmentations of PET-avid tumor/lesion regions of interest delineated on the PET/CT scans (one segment per ROI; no fixed multi-class integer palette — each SEG encodes a region)
DICOM SR (TID 1500 measurement report): quantitative SUVbw (standardized uptake value, body-weight normalized) statistics computed over each segmented region, i.e. structured PET/CT analysis results
DICOM RWV (Real World Value Mapping): objects that map stored PET pixel values to SUVbw units
DICOM SR 'Clinical Data' (series description = 'Clinical Data'): structured demographic, exposure, treatment, diagnosis, follow-up, and family-history records
details.file_structure: All data are DICOM, organized on TCIA by patient/study/series — images as CT and PT (PET) series; labels/annotations as DICOM SEG (segmentation), DICOM SR (quantitative measurement reports and clinical-data reports), and DICOM RWV (real-world value mapping) objects; a supplementary clinical-data spreadsheet is also provided in XLSX format.
details.extra: Collection = 279 subjects (1,032 studies) of head-and-neck cancer PET/CT. The DICOM SEG, SR, and RWV analysis objects were added in Version 2 (2017) as a standards-based re-encoding of quantitative PET/CT results (Fedorov et al.); exact SUV sub-metric names and per-lesion counts could not be fully enumerated from the public pages.

name: DENTEX
full_name: Dental Enumeration and Diagnosis on Panoramic X-rays (MICCAI 2023)
protocol_note: Panoramic dental X-rays (orthopantomograms)
size: 1,005 fully-annotated panoramic X-rays (3,903 total)
description: Panoramic dental X-rays hierarchically annotated (FDI) for abnormal-tooth detection with quadrant, enumeration and diagnosis.

label_schema: Hierarchical FDI-system annotation with 3 levels: quadrant, tooth enumeration, diagnosis (bounding-box detection)
Quadrant (4 classes): 1 = top-right, 2 = top-left, 3 = bottom-left, 4 = bottom-right
Enumeration: tooth position 1-8 within a quadrant (FDI numbering, e.g. tooth 48 = quadrant 4 position 8); combined with quadrant gives 32 tooth classes
Diagnosis (4 classes): Caries, Deep Caries, Periapical Lesion, Impacted (labeled per abnormal tooth)
Three progressively-labeled sets: Set 1 quadrant-only, Set 2 quadrant+enumeration, Set 3 fully labeled quadrant-enumeration-diagnosis (the benchmarked task)
details.file_structure: Panoramic dental X-ray images (PNG/JPG) stored in per-set image folders, with object-detection annotations (bounding boxes + hierarchical category labels) provided as COCO-style JSON files; distributed via Grand Challenge / Hugging Face.
details.splits: Fully-annotated diagnosis set (1,005 X-rays): 705 train (labels released), 50 validation (labels withheld), 250 test (hidden). Partially-labeled sets: 693 quadrant X-rays and 634 quadrant-enumeration X-rays. Plus 1,571 unlabeled X-rays for optional pre-training.
details.extra: Annotations are hierarchical: only Set 3 carries diagnosis labels, and diagnoses are assigned only to abnormal teeth; the paper/benchmark is HierarchicalDet (arXiv:2305.19112).

name: Tufts Dental Database
full_name: Tufts Dental Database (TDD): multimodal panoramic X-ray dataset
protocol_note: 1000 panoramic dental radiography images
size: 1,000 panoramic X-rays
segmentation_detail: teeth masks, maxillomandibular masks and abnormality masks
paired_text_detail: radiologist think-aloud text descriptions plus eye-tracking gaze maps
description: 1,000 expert-annotated panoramic dental radiographs with tooth/abnormality masks plus radiologist eye-tracking and text descriptions.

label_schema: 1000 panoramic dental radiographs, each with expert labeling of abnormalities and teeth
Segmentation: abnormality masks (pixel regions marking the pathological finding)
Per-image abnormality annotation across 5 categories: (1) anatomical location, (2) peripheral characteristics, (3) radiodensity, (4) effect on the surrounding structure, (5) abnormality category
Radiologist's expertise captured as eye-tracking gaze maps + think-aloud (text) protocol per image
details.file_structure: Data is organized into separate folders for the radiographs and for each annotation type (teeth masks, maxillomandibular masks, abnormality masks, plus eye-tracking maps and label text); radiographs and segmentation masks are stored as image files and the 5-category abnormality labels as accompanying text/label files.
details.extra: Multimodal, multi-reader dataset: it captures a radiologist's diagnostic process via eye-tracking and a think-aloud protocol alongside the standard masks and labels. Exact on-disk file formats (JPG/PNG/JSON) and any expert-vs-student annotation split could not be confirmed from the public page without downloading the data.

name: ToothFairy2
full_name: ToothFairy2: Multi-Structure Segmentation in CBCT (MICCAI 2024)
protocol_note: Dental/maxillofacial CBCT volumes at 0.3 mm isotropic voxel spacing; Set B has a wider field of view showing the full upper teeth.
size: 480 public training CBCT volumes
segmentation_detail: 42-class 3D masks: teeth (FDI), mandible, maxilla, alveolar canals, sinuses, implants
description: First fully-annotated public CBCT dataset with 42-class 3D expert segmentations of dental and maxillofacial structures at 0.3mm voxels.

label_schema: Multi-class 3D semantic segmentation of CBCT; 42 foreground classes; each voxel has one integer label
Teeth use FDI World Dental Federation codes AS the integer label value (not contiguous)
Labels 11-18 - Upper-right teeth: 11 central incisor, 12 lateral incisor, 13 canine, 14 first premolar, 15 second premolar, 16 first molar, 17 second molar, 18 third molar (wisdom)
Labels 21-28 - Upper-left teeth (FDI 21-28, central incisor through third molar)
Labels 31-38 - Lower-left teeth (FDI 31-38, central incisor through third molar)
Labels 41-48 - Lower-right teeth (FDI 41-48, central incisor through third molar)
details.file_structure: CBCT volumes and their single multi-class label mask are stored as .mha files in the nnU-Net dataset layout (imagesTr / labelsTr with dataset.json), all at 0.3 mm isotropic voxel spacing.
details.splits: Public training set: 480 volumes total, split into Set A (417 volumes, overlapping the original ToothFairy v1 data) and Set B (63 new wider field-of-view volumes showing full upper teeth); the test set is held private and its count is not disclosed.
details.extra: Label integers are intentionally non-contiguous: tooth values mirror FDI codes so 19, 20, 29, 30, 39, 40 are never used; the '42 classes' count refers to foreground structures (10 anatomy/appliance labels + 32 teeth), excluding background. Released under CC BY-SA.

name: CTooth
full_name: CTooth: 3D Tooth Volume Segmentation on CBCT
protocol_note: Dental cone beam CT; in-plane ~0.25x0.25 mm, slice thickness 0.25-0.3 mm
size: 22 annotated CBCT volumes (CTooth+ adds 146 unlabeled)
segmentation_detail: 3D tooth-volume voxel masks
description: Fully annotated CBCT tooth-volume segmentation benchmark of 22 volumes, extended by CTooth+ with 146 additional unlabeled volumes.

label_schema: Binary tooth-region segmentation (single foreground class, not per-tooth)
Label 1 - tooth (whole-tooth foreground; all teeth merged into one class, no individual tooth numbering/classes)
Voxel masks manually delineated by 4 dental trainees (~4 years experience) in ITK-SNAP, marked slice-by-slice in axial view then refined in coronal/sagittal views
details.file_structure: 22 CBCT volumes totaling 7,363 axial slices from 22 patients, of which 4,243 slices contain tooth annotations; each scan is paired with a binary 3D tooth-volume voxel mask (images resized to 256x256 in the benchmark); the exact on-disk container format (e.g. NIfTI/NRRD) is not stated in the paper.
details.extra: Annotations took ~10 months to collect/label/review (~6 h to annotate a volume plus ~1 h to check/refine); in-plane resolution ~0.25x0.25 mm and slice thickness 0.25-0.3 mm. Caveat: this is whole-tooth (foreground vs background) segmentation only - it does not provide per-tooth instance labels, tooth numbering (e.g. FDI), or pulp/root sub-structures.

details.splits: Training data = 1611 whole-body studies pooled from two cohorts: FDG-PET-CT-Lesions = 1014 studies / 900 patients (501 with lesions across lymphoma, melanoma, NSCLC; 513 negative controls) and PSMA-PET-CT-Lesions = 597 studies / 378 male prostate-cancer patients (539 with lesions, 58 without). Official test set is private/held-out on Grand Challenge (count not publicly disclosed).
details.extra: The two tracer cohorts are multi-center (FDG from University Hospital Tuebingen, PSMA from LMU Munich); the PSMA cohort has lower image resolution and greater heterogeneity than the FDG cohort, and the segmentation task is a single unified binary tumor class despite the differing tracers.

name: ROCO

UMLS Concept Unique Identifiers per image (cuis.txt): UMLS CUIs mapped from the caption (used for the ImageCLEF 2019 Concept Detection Task)

details.splits: Three official splits (train, validation, test), each further divided into radiology and non-radiology subsets; exact per-split image counts not verified from the fetched sources.
details.extra: Images come from PubMed Central Open Access articles automatically filtered to non-compound figures; labels are auto-generated (captions from source articles, CUIs/SemTypes via UMLS mapping), not expert manual annotations. size: 25,692 CT volumes with 665K grounded report regions + 1.3M VQA
segmentation_detail: 197 organ-level segmentation masks per volume linked to report sentences
paired_text_detail: multi-granularity grounded reports and grounded QA pairs linked to regions
description: Grounded vision-language extension of CT-RATE adding organ segmentation masks, region-linked reports and grounded VQA pairs for 3D chest CT.

label_schema: Organ-level segmentation masks covering 197 anatomical categories, one mask set per CT volume
Grounded (region-guided) reports: each report sentence is linked to the anatomical region it describes (columns include Volumename, Anatomy, and Sentence)
Grounded VQA pairs, organized into 4 question types: abnormality, location, presence, and size
Each report sentence and each VQA question/answer is tied to a reference segmentation mask (grounding)
details.file_structure: CT volumes and 197-category segmentation masks are stored as 3D NIfTI (.nii.gz) files (imaging built on the CT-RATE volumes); the grounded annotations live under dataset/radgenome_files/ as CSV files split by task and split, e.g. train_region_report.csv / validation_region_report.csv for reports and train_vqa_{abnormality,location,presence,size}.csv (plus case_disorders CSVs) for VQA.
details.splits: Train and validation only (no separate test split): ~665K grounded reports (~625K train / ~40.3K validation rows) and ~1.3M grounded VQA pairs, built over 25,692 non-contrast chest CT volumes from 20,000 patients (CT-RATE).
details.extra: All grounded reports and VQA pairs in the validation set were manually verified for quality; the dataset extends CT-RATE and there is no dedicated test split released.

related.name: CT-RATE
related.note: 197-category organ masks from a universal segmentation model plus LLM-generated region-grounded report sentences and VQA pairs over the CT-RATE volumes and reports; CT volumes are obtained from CT-RATE

name: INSPECT
full_name: Integrating Numerous Sources for Prognostic Evaluation of Clinical Timelines
protocol_note: CT pulmonary angiography (single pulmonary-arterial phase)
size: 23,248 CTPA studies / 19,402 patients with reports and EHR
paired_text_detail: radiology report impressions plus structured longitudinal EHR data
description: Multimodal dataset linking CTPA images, radiology reports and structured EHR at scale for pulmonary embolism diagnosis and prognosis.

label_schema: PE diagnosis (3 binary labels derived from radiology reports): PE positive, Acute PE, Subsegmental PE
12-month prognosis / classification outcomes: mortality, readmission, and pulmonary hypertension (PH)
Mortality and readmission also provided at 1-month and 6-month horizons (1/6/12-month each)
Label values are True / False / Censored (censored for time-to-event outcomes without complete follow-up)
No pixel-level segmentation or bounding-box annotations; labels are study-level classification/outcome targets
details.file_structure: CTPA scans distributed as anonymized DICOM; a master cohort CSV holds demographics and all study-level labels; radiology report impression sections in CSV; and linked structured EHR (OMOP/FEMR) as gzipped CSV files, all linked by patient/study identifiers.
details.splits: Train 18,945 studies (15,789 patients), Validation 1,089 studies (913 patients), Test 3,214 studies (2,700 patients); total ~23,248 CTPA studies from 19,402 patients.
details.extra: Multimodal dataset (CT + radiology reports + longitudinal structured EHR with 225M+ events); PE diagnosis labels are automatically extracted from reports rather than expert-annotated per-image, and prognosis labels use a Censored value for incomplete follow-up. Per the paper (arXiv 2311.10798), CTPA is released as DICOM with only 10 header tags kept (InstanceNumber, ImagePositionPatient, PixelSpacing, RescaleIntercept, RescaleSlope, WindowCenter, WindowWidth, Manufacturer, PhotometricInterpretation, SliceThickness) - no SeriesDescription or contrast tags; slices with burned-in patient information were removed.
details.label_readers: PE labels from a fine-tuned Clinical Longformer on report impressions (trained on 4,351 radiologist-annotated reports; positive if p > 0.5); mortality/readmission from STARR-OMOP EHR; pulmonary hypertension from an ICD-code phenotype validated on 120 hand-labeled patients
details.reference_standard: Report-derived PE status; EHR-derived outcomes with censoring
details.third_party_note: Non-commercial research data use agreement (Stanford AIMI); agreement text not reviewed here; no verified clause on external services.

paired_text_detail: Anonymized, LLM-structured radiology reports (clinical information, technique, findings, impression) per study, plus pathology labels across 37 brain/spine categories grounded in SNOMED CT/RadLex
description: A large-scale brain and spine MRI dataset of over 705,000 multi-sequence volumes from ~98,000 studies paired with structured radiology reports and segmentation masks.

label_schema: Structured radiology reports split into 4 sections: clinical_information, technique, findings, impression (plus full report text)

37 brain and spine MRI pathology categories (multi-label classification), each grounded to SNOMED CT / RadLex; classified from the report findings section (exact category names not enumerated on the public card - given in the pathology-labels CSV header)

Anatomical multi-label voxel-wise segmentations from the NV-Segment-CTMR model: a brain segmentation (center-modality volumes) and a whole-body segmentation (all modalities), following the NV-Segment-CTMR label_dict.json (integer class values not listed on the public card)
Per-series brain masks (binary) and defacing masks (binary)
details.file_structure: Per-study folders (<study_uid>/) with NIfTI volumes under img/ (<study_uid>_<series_id>.nii.gz) and masks/segmentations under seg/ (e.g. _brain-mask.nii.gz, _defacing-mask.nii.gz, _nvseg-ctmr-brain.nii.gz, _nvseg-ctmr-wb.nii.gz); reports, metadata, and pathology labels are stored as CSV; co-registration and atlas-registration derivatives add coreg_img/atlas_img NIfTIs plus .mat transform matrices, distributed across separate HuggingFace repos.
details.splits: Patient-level splits: Train 75,000 patients / 88,985 studies / 638,345 series; Validation 3,425 / 3,781 / 27,003; Test 5,000 / 5,568 / 39,906 (total 83,425 patients / 98,334 studies / 705,254 series).
details.extra: Companion derivative repos provide within-study co-registered volumes (MR-RATE-coreg) and MNI152 atlas-registered volumes (MR-RATE-atlas) with .mat transforms, plus NV-Segment-CTMR segmentations (MR-RATE-nvseg-ctmr); reports were anonymized and LLM-structured/translated to English.
details.label_readers: 37 pathology categories assigned by an LLM pipeline (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 via vLLM) from structured report findings; anatomical masks from NV-Segment-CTMR
details.third_party_note: Gated terms: 'Redistribution of the dataset or any portion thereof is not allowed'; commercial use needs permission; no API-specific clause.

name: Merlin
full_name: Merlin: A Computed Tomography Vision-Language Foundation Model and Dataset
protocol_note: One CT series per scan; metadata.csv records the CT phase per scan (Merlin Plus metadata shows the values portal_venous, arterial_late, native)
size: 25,494 abdominal/pelvic CT scans from 18,317 patients
segmentation_detail: Automated (TotalSegmentator, not manually annotated) multi-label anatomical segmentations with up to 117 structures for 23,496 of the 25,494 scans, distributed as supplementary .nii.gz files with labels.json (merlin-segmentations.zip, 11.7 GB) on the stanfordmimi/Merlin Hugging Face repo
paired_text_detail: Free-text Findings section of the radiology report for every scan (reports_final.xlsx); the >1.8M EHR ICD diagnosis codes used for pretraining in the paper are not part of the released files
license: Stanford University Dataset Research Use Agreement (personal, non-commercial research use only)
description: A native-3D abdominal/pelvic CT dataset of 25,494 scans from 18,317 Stanford emergency-department patients (2012–2018), each paired with the Findings section of its radiology report plus report-derived findings labels and metadata, released with the Merlin CT vision-language foundation model (Nature 2026).

label_schema: Released: free-text 'Findings' section of the radiology report for each of the 25,494 scans (reports_final.xlsx), with per-scan train/validation/test split and few-shot flag

Released: zero-shot findings labels (zero_shot_findings_disease_cls.csv), made by regex matching of positive/negative prompts on the Findings text: 1 = positive, 0 = explicitly negated, -1 = not mentioned; the paper evaluates 30 radiologist-selected findings, e.g. ascites, pleural effusion, splenomegaly, appendicitis, lymphadenopathy, free air, metastatic disease, abdominal aortic aneurysm, prostatomegaly, anasarca
Released: multi-disease 5-year prediction labels for a subset of the test set (five_years_disease_task.csv; merlin_split column)
Released: per-scan metadata (metadata.csv): age, gender, race; CT phase, manufacturer, manufacturer model, kVp, slice thickness, tube current
Released (supplementary, Hugging Face): automated TotalSegmentator multi-label anatomical segmentations, labels 1–117 mapped in labels.json, for 23,496 scans

Paper only, not among the released files: EHR ICD-9/ICD-10 diagnosis codes (2,995,293 assigned / 16,553 unique) mapped through PheWAS Phecodes to 1,692 phenotypes (692 used for evaluation); documentation/phenotypes.csv in the GitHub repo is only the phecode vocabulary (phecode, phecode_str)
report-derived findings labels (1 positive / 0 negated / -1 not mentioned)
metadata (age, gender, race, CT phase, scanner, kVp, slice thickness, tube current)
details.file_structure: merlinabdominalctdataset/ is downloaded with AzCopy from a secure Azure Blob URL issued after DUA approval. It contains: merlin_data/ (25,494 CT volumes as NIfTI .nii, one per exam, named by accession ID; for each exam the DICOM series with the largest slice count was kept, converted to NIfTI, compressed and de-identified); reports_final.xlsx (Findings-section report text, train/validation/test split and few-shot flag per scan); zero_shot_findings_disease_cls.csv (regex-derived findings labels: 1 positive, 0 negated, -1 not mentioned); five_years_disease_task.csv (multi-disease 5-year prediction labels, with a merlin_split column); metadata.csv (age, gender, race; phase, manufacturer, manufacturermodelname, kvp, slicethickness, ma/xraytubecurrent). Supplementary files on the stanfordmimi/Merlin Hugging Face model repo: Merlin_Embeddings.zip (1.45 GiB; one 2048-d MONAI MetaTensor .pt per exam, named by accession ID) and merlin-segmentations.zip (11.7 GB; TotalSegmentator multi-label .nii.gz for 23,496 scans, labels 1–117, labels.json).
details.splits: Per-scan train/validation/test assignment (and a few-shot-experiment flag) is provided in reports_final.xlsx. Paper cohort: 60/20/20 split by patient, 15,331 train / 5,060 validation / 5,137 test CTs (25,528 total, vs 25,494 scans in the public release, so released split counts may differ slightly). The five-year disease-prediction task uses only part of the test set, split further in the merlin_split column of five_years_disease_task.csv. The external test cohorts from other institutions used in the paper are not part of this release.
details.extra: Release announced on 23 Sep 2025 in the StanfordMIMI/Merlin README and documentation/download.md (commit 2d3409c); CT images and reports are hosted by the Stanford AIMI Center under a data-use agreement. The paper was posted to arXiv in June 2024 (2406.06512) and published in Nature in 2026 (doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10181-8). The EHR ICD codes and the phenotype labels derived from them via PheWAS Phecodes, used in the paper, are not among the files listed in the official download documentation. Zero-shot findings labels are regex-derived from report text, so -1 (not mentioned) can hide true positives or negatives. The supplementary Merlin_Embeddings.zip and TotalSegmentator merlin-segmentations.zip are hosted on the stanfordmimi/Merlin Hugging Face model repository. Merlin Plus (MICCAI 2026; huggingface.co/datasets/AbdomenAtlas/MerlinPlus, github.com/MrGiovanni/MerlinPlus) is a separate derivative that adds radiologist-created tumor masks across 9 organs, AI-generated organ/sub-structure masks, and longitudinal metadata (patient IDs and scan dates) for the Merlin scans; it requires the original Merlin images from Stanford AIMI.
details.label_readers: Findings labels regex-matched from report Findings text (1/0/-1); anatomical masks from TotalSegmentator (automated); EHR phecodes used in the paper are not released
