name: Merlin Plus
full_name: Merlin Plus: A Large-Scale, Multi-cancer, Image-Mask-Report Dataset
anatomy: Abdomen and pelvis: tumors of the adrenal glands, spleen, stomach, uterus, bladder, gallbladder, duodenum, prostate and esophagus, plus 44 AI-segmented anatomical classes (organs, femurs, blood vessels, liver/pancreas sub-segments, ducts and a CBD stent)
protocol_note: Labels the Merlin CTs; merlin_longitudinal_metadata.csv has a phase column (observed: portal_venous, arterial_late, native) and a contrast flag
size: 1,193 radiologist-created tumor masks (9 organs) + 44-class AI organ masks for the 25,494 Merlin CT scans (18,317 patients); 3,830 patients with 2+ scans; no images included
segmentation_detail: 1,193 per-voxel tumor masks created or verified by radiologists across 9 organs: adrenal glands 266, spleen 192, stomach 160, uterus 131, bladder 127, gallbladder 97, duodenum 83, prostate 83, esophagus 54. They cover all confirmed malignant tumors plus over 200 benign ones. The release also has AI-generated per-voxel masks for 44 anatomical classes in total (organs, blood vessels, organ parts such as liver segments 1-8 and pancreas head/body/tail, ducts, femurs and a CBD stent), made by models trained on more than 14,000 Johns Hopkins CT scans.
paired_text_detail: Each Merlin CT scan is paired with its free-text radiology report (Findings section), distributed as reports_final.xlsx with the CT scans in the Stanford AIMI Merlin release, not in the Hugging Face mask repo; the longitudinal metadata links scans and reports over time. Reports were also used to auto-refine tumor masks during report-based active learning.
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 for the Merlin Plus masks and metadata (commercial use not allowed); the underlying Merlin CT scans and reports are under the Stanford University Dataset Research Use Agreement
description: An extension of the Stanford Merlin abdominal/pelvic CT dataset adding 1,193 radiologist-created tumor masks across 9 organs, AI-generated masks for 44 anatomical classes and longitudinal patient-ID/scan-date metadata; masks and metadata only, so the CT scans and reports come from Stanford AIMI (Merlin) under its data-use agreement.

label_schema: Tumor masks (per-voxel), 1,193 in total across 9 organs: adrenal glands 266, spleen 192, stomach 160, uterus 131, bladder 127, gallbladder 97, duodenum 83, prostate 83, esophagus 54

Tumor annotation scope: all confirmed malignant tumors are annotated, plus over 200 benign tumors. Unannotated tumors are other benign tumors and cases where malignancy could not be confirmed or radiologists could not clearly see the tumor. The public release documents no per-mask benign/malignant label.

The authors describe these as the first public tumor masks for the spleen, bladder, gallbladder, stomach, duodenum and prostate. Esophagus, uterus and adrenal tumor masks are not flagged as first-public.

Organ masks: 44 AI-generated classes (organs, blood vessels, liver/pancreas sub-segments, ducts) from models trained on more than 14,000 Johns Hopkins CT scans: adrenal gland left, adrenal gland right, aorta, bladder, cbd stent, celiac artery, celiac trunk, colon, common bile duct, duodenum, esophagus, femur left, femur right, gall bladder, hepatic vessels, intestine, kidney left, kidney right, liver, liver segment 1, liver segment 2, liver segment 3, liver segment 4, liver segment 5, liver segment 6, liver segment 7, liver segment 8, lung left, lung right, pancreas body, pancreas head, pancreas tail, pancreas, pancreatic duct, portal vein and splenic vein, postcava, prostate, rectum, renal vein left, renal vein right, spleen, stomach, superior mesenteric artery, superior mesenteric vein (there is no uterus organ class, although uterus has tumor masks)
Paired free-text radiology report (Findings section) per CT, from reports_final.xlsx in the Merlin release at Stanford AIMI

Longitudinal/scan metadata CSV (merlin_longitudinal_metadata.csv) with columns: Encrypted Accession Number, Patient ID (e.g. Merlin_3375), Exam Completed Date, spacing, Age, Gender, Race, contrast (True/False), manufacturer, manufacturermodelname, kvp, xraytubecurrent, phase (observed values: portal_venous, arterial_late, native)
Integer label indices are not documented on the public README, so they are omitted
longitudinal metadata (anonymized patient IDs, scan dates)
scan acquisition metadata (contrast, phase, scanner manufacturer/model, kVp, tube current, voxel spacing)
details.file_structure: The Hugging Face dataset repo AbdomenAtlas/MerlinPlus holds only the masks and metadata, with no CT images or reports. Masks are packed in 1,000-case tar.gz shards (MerlinMasks_BDMAP_<start>_<end>.tar.gz; the last shard reportedly ends at BDMAP_00025456), downloaded with `hf download AbdomenAtlas/MerlinPlus --repo-type dataset --local-dir ./MerlinPlusCompressed` and extracted with `bash MerlinPlusCompressed/unzip.sh --archive_dir MerlinPlusCompressed --out_dir MerlinPlus --workers 6`. merlin_longitudinal_metadata.csv is on HF and in the GitHub repo. The per-case mask layout and the BDMAP-to-Merlin-accession mapping are not documented in the Merlin Plus README; JHU's R-Super Merlin demo reads Merlin Plus organ masks as per-case folders of per-structure NIfTI files (<case>/segmentations/<structure>.nii.gz), but this is unconfirmed for the current shards. CT volumes (NIfTI .nii) and reports (reports_final.xlsx) come from the Stanford AIMI Merlin release. The GitHub repo also holds report_based_mask_refinement/ (Python code with requirements.txt that refines AI tumor masks against report descriptions) and document/ (figures, MICCAI 2026 poster).
details.splits: The README publishes no official train/val/test split (the HF card could not be read directly). The Merlin-Cancer-Net model card (search snippet) says it was trained on 423 masks from 'the Merlin Plus training dataset', and the MICCAI poster reports internal and external validation, so an internal split exists, but its IDs are not released in the sources read. The parent Merlin dataset ships its own patient-level 60/20/20 train/validation/test split in reports_final.xlsx.
details.extra: Tumor masks were made by report-based active learning: R-Super drafted masks from CT-report pairs, the masks were auto-refined to match the tumor count, size and location in the reports, and 4 radiologists revised the low-confidence ones (3-5x faster); all tumor masks were verified or corrected by radiologists. The GitHub 'About' blurb says 1,153 tumor masks; the README and MICCAI poster say 1,193. Longitudinal: 3,830 patients with 2 or more scans, 1,524 with 3 or more, up to 18 scans per patient, median span 193 days, longest 2,051 days. Released models: Merlin-Super (R-Super) and Merlin-Net (nnU-Net). Stanford Merlin + JHU R-Super collaboration, MICCAI 2026; commercial use not allowed. Mask file format: the per-case layout inside the tar.gz shards is not documented; NIfTI is inferred from the group's R-Super code, which reads Merlin Plus organ masks as <case>/segmentations/<structure>.nii.gz.
details.label_readers: Tumor masks drafted by R-Super from CT-report pairs, auto-refined to match report tumor count/size/location, low-confidence ones revised by 4 radiologists; all tumor masks verified or corrected by radiologists; organ masks AI-only
details.third_party_note: Masks/metadata are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, but the CT images and reports they label are under the Stanford Research Use Agreement (no distribution without permission; no API clause).

name: CancerVerse
full_name: CancerVerse: A Fully Open Longitudinal and Multimodal Dataset for Multicancer Screening
anatomy: Chest, abdomen and pelvis; target cancers of the liver, kidney, pancreas, colon, adrenal gland, bladder, duodenum, esophagus, gallbladder, prostate, spleen, stomach and uterus
protocol_note: Scans span 4 CT contrast phases, with the phase recorded per volume in the scan metadata (one ct.nii.gz per volume); the card does not name the phases, but third-party code reading the metadata uses values such as non-contrast, arterial/arterial_early, arterial_late and portal_venous/venous, plus 'u' for unknown.
size: 24,168 CT volumes from 13,863 patients (staged release; stage 1: 22,865 volumes with reports)
segmentation_detail: Not confirmed released: expert manual voxel-wise tumor masks for 13 cancer types (no AI-generated masks, per the card and paper) were scheduled 'by September 2026'; as of the BodyMaps viewer code on 2026-09-27, CancerVerse was still CT-only with 'no masks yet'. Re-check the HF repo.
paired_text_detail: Each CT volume is paired with the radiologist's original free-text report (full impression); the first release stage lists 22,865 scan-report pairs, and structured oncology labels are announced for a later release.
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial research use; commercial use licensed separately by BodyMaps)
description: A MICCAI 2026 longitudinal chest/abdomen/pelvis CT dataset for multicancer screening, with 24,168 scans from 13,863 patients paired with radiology reports and scan metadata, released in stages on Hugging Face with expert tumor masks for 13 cancer types announced.

label_schema: Released: one free-text radiology report per CT volume (the radiologist's full impression); the paper reports reports for 99.8% of patients

Released: scan-level metadata table (CancerVerse_dataset_metadata.csv, one row per CT volume keyed by 'CancerVerse ID', with 'Patient ID', 'exam_date' and 'phase' columns per third-party code) with sex, age, exam date, contrast phase (4 phases), scanner, and study/series/protocol descriptions

Released: longitudinal linkage through stable de-identified patient IDs plus exam dates, so each patient's imaging timeline can be rebuilt (HF card: up to 26 timepoints spanning up to 14.4 years; paper: 1-32 scans per cancer patient, median 3 scans among patients with follow-up, median follow-up 299 days)

Announced for September 2026, release not confirmed: manual voxel-wise, radiologist-verified tumor masks (no AI-generated masks; every lesion drawn by at least one of 28 expert annotators over more than 13 months) for 13 cancer types: liver, kidney, pancreas, colon, adrenal gland, bladder, duodenum, esophagus, gallbladder, prostate, spleen, stomach, uterus. Label indices and mask file layout are not published yet
Announced for August 2026, release not confirmed: pathology results as ICD-10 codes (the paper reports pathology results for 44.8% of patients)

Announced for September 2026, release not confirmed: a clinical and longitudinal layer with cancer histology, TNM stage, treatments received, surgical resections, RECIST treatment response, metastatic sites, disease-status narratives, follow-up recommendations, comorbidities and devices/implants (the paper reports demographics for 80.4% of patients and clinical variables for 74.7%)
Announced, not yet released: structured, machine-readable oncology labels (card: 'masks and structured oncology labels are coming next')
longitudinal metadata (de-identified patient IDs, exam dates)
scan acquisition metadata (contrast phase, scanner, study/series/protocol descriptions)
details.file_structure: Downloaded from the Hugging Face dataset repo BodyMaps/CancerVerse with the card's download_cancerverse.sh script after installing huggingface_hub[cli] and running `hf auth login`. The download root holds CancerVerse_dataset_metadata.csv (one row per CT volume) and a CancerVerse/ folder with one compressed NIfTI CT per case at CancerVerse/CV_########/ct.nii.gz (8-digit ids). This layout comes from third-party code that ran `hf download BodyMaps/CancerVerse` and from the BodyMaps viewer README, not from the HF file tree (BodyMaps' own server copy adds an image_only/ level). How the reports are stored is not documented in the sources read.
details.splits: No official train/val/test split is documented in the sources read. The paper evaluates multicancer screening as tumor detection/segmentation, measuring sensitivity at fixed false positives per scan, and uses a verified healthy cohort of 8,799 patients with more than 1 year of follow-up to estimate specificity; split IDs are not published.
details.extra: Staged release (HF card seen only through search snippets, since huggingface.co is blocked here): Stage 1 lists 22,865 CT volumes and reports from 13,863 patients; the remaining volumes/reports and pathology ICD-10 codes were scheduled by August 2026, and expert tumor masks and the clinical/longitudinal layer by September 2026. Whether these have shipped could not be verified; the BodyMaps viewer code (last commit 2026-09-27, reading JHU's internal copy) still says 'no masks yet', and a third-party project's notes count 22,863 scans in the downloaded metadata. Counts differ by source: the MICCAI Open Access abstract gives 23,742 scans from 9,316 patients (1-19 scans per patient), while the JHU-hosted paper PDF and HF card give 24,168 scans from 13,863 patients (1-32 per cancer patient). Data come from multiple institutions in Switzerland and Turkey, acquired 2010-2025 on multiple scanners. The HF card calls the scans abdominal/pelvic, while the paper and the BodyMaps releases page say chest, abdomen and pelvis. Access is assumed gated from the card's `hf auth login` step; switch to 'open' if the HF repo is ungated. The NV-Reason-CT model card lists CancerVerse (public) in its training data: 22,720 cases from 13,778 patients (4,668 chest and 4,438 abdomen crops). The RT-Super README describes CancerVerse as having 'per-voxel annotations for organs and 13 tumor types' and no overlap with Merlin Plus; organ masks are not mentioned elsewhere. There is no dedicated GitHub repo. Not to be confused with the AAPM 2026 abstract 'Cancerverse: Multicenter CT Segmentation of 16 Cancers for Radiotherapy Targets and OARs', whose relation to this release is not documented.

name: ReXGradient-160K
full_name: ReXGradient-160K: A Large-Scale Publicly Available Dataset of Chest Radiographs with Free-text Reports
protocol_note: Chest radiographs from 79 sites across 3 U.S. health systems; downsampled PNG; metadata includes manufacturer
size: 273,004 images from 160,000 studies of 109,487 patients across 79 sites (3 U.S. health systems)
paired_text_detail: Structured free-text radiology reports per study with four sections: indication, comparison, findings, and impression
license: Custom non-commercial research data use agreement (accepted on Hugging Face)
description: A large multi-site chest X-ray dataset of 273,004 PNG images from 160,000 studies across 79 U.S. sites, each paired with structured free-text radiology reports.

label_schema: Free-text radiology report per study, structured into 4 sections: Indication, Comparison, Findings, Impression
Primary task is chest X-ray report generation (image-to-text); no fixed finding-label taxonomy is provided
Companion bounding-box annotations: radiologist-drawn boxes marking interstitial patterns for ~400 examples (Label Studio coordinate format)
details.file_structure: Chest X-ray images are provided as downsampled PNGs packaged in split tar part-files (e.g. concatenate deid_png.part* into deid_png.tar, then extract); reports/metadata and the interstitial-pattern bounding boxes are provided as separate metadata files (metadata/interstitial_pattern_bbox.json).
details.splits: Train: 140,000 studies (238,968 images, 95,716 patients); Validation: 10,000 studies (17,007 images, 6,964 patients); Public Test: 10,000 studies (17,029 images, 6,807 patients); Private Test: 10,000 studies (held out for ReXrank benchmark). Total 160,000 studies / 273,004 images.
details.extra: The ~400 interstitial-pattern bounding boxes are a small companion annotation set; the vast majority of the dataset has only paired free-text reports, not structured finding labels or per-study multi-reader annotations.

name: PadChest-GR
full_name: PadChest-GR: A Bilingual Chest X-ray Dataset for Grounded Radiology Report Generation
protocol_note: Frontal-projection chest radiographs (mostly PA) selected from PadChest; pediatric and suboptimal studies excluded
size: 4,555 CXR studies (3,099 abnormal, 1,456 normal); 7,037 positive and 3,422 negative finding sentences; ~46 GB
paired_text_detail: Sentence-level grounded reports in English and Spanish describing present (positive) and absent (negative) findings
license: PADCHEST Dataset Research Use Agreement (free for research)
description: A manually curated bilingual (English/Spanish) chest X-ray dataset of 4,555 studies with sentence-level grounded radiology reports and radiologist-annotated bounding boxes for grounded report generation.

label_schema: Grounded radiology reports: each study's report is decomposed into individual sentences, each describing at most one finding, provided bilingually in English and Spanish (orig/translation)
7,037 positive-finding sentences and 3,422 negative-finding sentences across the dataset

Per positive finding: a 'finding category' label (e.g. aortic atheromatosis, apical pleural thickening, laminar atelectasis, aortic elongation, cardiomegaly, nodule, pleural effusion, scoliosis) drawn from PadChest's taxonomy; Fig.4 shows the 24 most common finding categories plus 'Other' and 'negative'
Per finding: anatomical 'locations' labels from a hierarchical taxonomy (e.g. aortic, pleural, basal, left, right, lung field / upper / middle / lower lung field, column)
Per finding: a 'progression' label classifying temporal change vs a prior study - one of new, worsening, stable, improving, resolved, or N/A/None

Bounding boxes localizing each positive finding on the image; a finding may have multiple boxes (e.g. bilateral), and each positive finding has up to two independent sets of boxes drawn by two different radiologist readers
Normal studies contribute negative findings only (1,819 negative findings from 1,456 normal studies)
bounding boxes per positive finding (up to two independent reader sets)
details.file_structure: Chest X-ray images are single-view (mostly PA) PNG files inherited from PadChest, paired with grounded-report annotations (per-sentence finding category, locations, progression, EN/ES text, and bounding-box coordinates); distributed as a gated dataset on Hugging Face (microsoft/padchest-gr) and via the BIMCV request form (~46 GB).
details.splits: 3,185 training studies / 455 validation studies / 915 test studies (total 4,555), split ~70/10/20 at random, stratified by finding category and keeping all studies of a patient within one partition
details.extra: Multi-reader: every positive finding sentence carries up to two independent bounding-box annotation sets from different radiologists (a 14-radiologist team reviewed/annotated); note ~6,217 positive findings have no manual box while 820 do (per Fig.4C), so not all findings are box-grounded, and images are reduced-grayscale PNG rather than DICOM.
details.label_readers: Finding sentences extracted/translated from the original Spanish reports by GPT-4 (Azure OpenAI), then reviewed by a team of 14 radiologists who drew boxes; up to 2 independent box sets per positive finding
details.reference_standard: Report findings verified and localized by radiologists on the image; no pathology/CT confirmation
details.third_party_note: Governed by the PADCHEST Dataset Research Use Agreement; requesters commit not to share the data and not to attempt re-identification (BIMCV page). No explicit API/online-service clause found.

name: MedTrinity-25M
full_name: MedTrinity-25M: A Large-scale Multimodal Dataset with Multigranular Annotations for Medicine
anatomy: Whole body (multiple regions, e.g. chest, brain, abdomen)
protocol_note: Aggregated 2D images across 10 modalities (incl. CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound, histopathology, endoscopy, dermoscopy, fundus); no sequence/phase information.
size: ~25M images (18M accessible image-text pairs) across 10 modalities
segmentation_detail: Automatically generated region-of-interest segmentation masks and bounding boxes included in the multigranular annotations
paired_text_detail: Multigranular text annotations: disease/lesion type, modality, region-specific descriptions, and inter-region relationships
license: Mixed (CC BY 4.0 for some sources; some constituent datasets proprietary/credentialed, e.g. CheXpert, MIMIC-CXR-JPG)
description: A large-scale multimodal medical dataset of ~25M images across 10 modalities (including CT, MRI, and X-ray) with automatically generated multigranular text annotations, bounding boxes, and segmentation masks.

label_schema: Each sample is an image paired with a single multigranular free-text 'caption' (no separate class-index label columns)
Caption encodes GLOBAL attributes: disease/lesion type, imaging modality, and region/organ identity
Caption encodes LOCAL attributes: region-of-interest (ROI) descriptions plus inter-regional spatial relationships
ROI bounding boxes and segmentation masks are auto-generated (via SAT/BA-Transformer-style tools) and expressed textually within the caption rather than as pixel-mask files
Coverage: 10 imaging modalities and 65+ diseases/conditions across whole-body regions (e.g., chest, brain, abdomen)
Per-sample metadata fields: file_name, id (UUID), caption, source (originating dataset)
details.file_structure: Images plus a metadata.jsonl file are grouped into numbered shards (to avoid filesystem limits); each JSONL line holds file_name, id, caption, and source, with the annotations living inside the caption text (no per-image NIfTI/DICOM-SEG mask files).
details.extra: No official train/val/test split; three released versions exist — a ~100k demo, the full 25M (text/metadata), and an ~18M 'accessible' subset with paired images. Annotations are automatically generated by an MLLM pipeline, not human-verified.

name: CheXpert Plus
full_name: CheXpert Plus: Augmenting a Large Chest X-ray Dataset with Text Radiology Reports, Patient Demographics and Additional Image Formats
protocol_note: Chest radiographs (frontal and lateral views) in DICOM and PNG
size: 223,228 chest radiographs paired with 187,711 radiology reports from 64,725 patients
paired_text_detail: De-identified free-text radiology reports (36M text tokens, ~1M PHI spans anonymized) paired with images, plus CheXbert structured labels and RadGraph-XL annotations
license: Stanford University Dataset Research Use Agreement
description: An augmentation of the CheXpert dataset pairing 223,228 chest radiographs (in DICOM and PNG) with 187,711 de-identified free-text radiology reports, patient demographics, and structured labels for 64,725 patients.

label_schema: 14 CheXbert pathology labels per report/image (multi-label): No Finding, Enlarged Cardiomediastinum, Cardiomegaly, Lung Opacity, Lung Lesion, Edema, Consolidation, Pneumonia, Atelectasis, Pneumothorax, Pleural Effusion, Pleural Other, Fracture, Support Devices
Label values follow CheXpert/CheXbert convention: 1 = positive, 0 = negative, -1 = uncertain, blank/NaN = not mentioned

Full free-text radiology reports parsed into up to 11 subsections: Narrative, Clinical History, History, Comparison, Technique, Findings, Impression, End of Impression, Summary, Accession Number (and related header/exam fields)
RadGraph (RadGraph-XL) structured entity/relation annotations extracted separately from the Findings and Impression sections
Patient demographics and clinical/socio-economic metadata plus DICOM image metadata attributes
details.file_structure: A master CSV (df_chexpert_plus_240401.csv) maps each row to an image path (e.g. train/patientXXXXX/studyY/viewZ_frontal.jpg) and the parsed report section text plus demographics; images are provided in both DICOM and PNG format; CheXbert labels are stored as JSON/JSONL (e.g. chexbert_labels/findings_fixed.json) and RadGraph annotations as JSON (e.g. radgraph-XL-annotations/section_findings.json).
details.extra: Contains 223,228 unique image-report pairs from 187,711 studies and 64,725 patients (~36M text tokens, ~1M PHI spans anonymized); pathology labels are machine-generated by CheXbert, and a held-out 1000-sample test set is annotated by 2 board-certified radiologists for evaluation.

description: A dataset of 50,188 digitally reconstructed chest radiographs generated from CT-RATE CT volumes via Siddon-Jacobs ray tracing (frontal and lateral views), paired with inherited radiology reports and 18-class binary pathology labels.

label_schema: Multi-label classification: 18 binary abnormality labels per DRR image, inherited from CT-RATE
Companion label: paired free-text radiology report (impression/findings) per study
details.file_structure: DRR images are 2D PNGs (frontal/lateral projections rendered from NIfTI CT volumes via Siddon-Jacobs ray tracing) organized under train/ and valid/ folders following the CT-RATE patient/study hierarchy; the 18 binary labels and text reports are provided as CSV files (train_predicted_labels.csv, valid_predicted_labels.csv, train_reports.csv, validation_reports.csv) plus metadata CSVs, downloaded from the gated CT-RATE HuggingFace repo via the included download_metadata_label.py script per license.
details.splits: Split into train/ and valid/ folders following CT-RATE; ~50,188 DRR volumes generated from 25,692 chest CT volumes (exact per-split image counts not confirmed).
details.extra: Labels are machine-generated ('predicted') multi-abnormality labels inherited verbatim from CT-RATE (not re-annotated for the DRR projections); labels and reports are not stored in the DRR-RATE repo and must be pulled from the gated CT-RATE dataset to comply with the CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 license.

name: AbdomenAtlas 1.1
full_name: AbdomenAtlas 1.1
anatomy: abdominal organs, thorax organs, vasculature, skeletal structures
protocol_note: CT volumes span multiple contrast phases (pre-contrast, arterial, portal-venous, delayed).
size: 9,262 CT volumes; >251,000 masks
segmentation_detail: Per-voxel annotations for 25 anatomical structures (organs, vascular and skeletal structures) plus pseudo-labels for 7 tumor types.
host: GitHub / Hugging Face (MrGiovanni/AbdomenAtlas, AbdomenAtlas HF org)
description: An expanded release of AbdomenAtlas with 9,262 multi-phase CT volumes annotated per-voxel for 25 anatomical structures plus pseudo-labels for seven tumor types.

label_schema: Voxel-wise multi-organ segmentation with 25 classes (class map, integer index - structure):
Separate tumor pseudo-labels stored in pseudo_label.nii.gz (README states 'six types of tumors'; exact tumor class names not enumerated on the official page, so not listed here)
details.file_structure: Per-case folders (e.g. BDMAP_00000001/) each containing ct.nii.gz plus a combined label mask and a segmentations/ subfolder of one NIfTI file per structure (spleen.nii.gz, liver.nii.gz, ...), all in compressed NIfTI (.nii.gz) format.
details.extra: Organ masks are real annotations but tumor labels are AI-generated pseudo-labels (README notes only ~8 organs are 'pretty accurate'); the README says 'six types of tumors' rather than seven, and the tumor class names are not enumerated on the official GitHub page.

name: AbdomenAtlas 2.0
full_name: AbdomenAtlas 2.0: The Multi-Tumor Segmentation Dataset
anatomy: Tumors of the liver, pancreas, kidney, colon, esophagus and uterus, plus abdominal and pelvic organs, vessels, lungs and femurs (26 anatomical classes in the label map)
protocol_note: Abdominal CT scans from 89 hospitals; contrast phase not specified in the source.
size: 10,135 CT scans from 89 hospitals; 15,130 tumor masks; 5,893 control scans (~400 GB)
segmentation_detail: Per-voxel masks for six tumor types (liver, pancreas, kidney, colon, esophagus, uterus), 15,130 tumor instances, built with the paper's SMART-Annotator pipeline: AI-generated tumor candidates at a high-sensitivity threshold, false positives removed by senior radiologists and final masks revised by junior radiologists (23 radiologists in total, per the paper). The 32-class label map also defines 26 anatomical classes (the 25 AbdomenAtlas 1.1 structures plus uterus); how the organ masks were made and whether they ship for every case is not documented. data/README.md shows one binary NIfTI mask per class; a combined_labels.nii.gz multi-label volume is also reported by users (issue #3).
host: GitHub (BodyMaps/AbdomenAtlas2.0) / Hugging Face (MrGiovanni/AbdomenAtlas2.0Mini: CT) / JHU web server (labels)
description: A Johns Hopkins multi-tumor abdominal CT segmentation dataset (ICCV 2025) of 10,135 scans from 89 hospitals, with 15,130 per-voxel tumor masks across six organs (liver, pancreas, kidney, colon, esophagus, uterus) and 5,893 control scans, released as NIfTI with a 32-class label map.

label_schema: Voxel-wise segmentation with 32 classes, per the official class_map_abdomenatlas_2_0 in data/README.md (integer index - structure). data/README.md shows one binary NIfTI mask per class under label/BDMAP_XXXXXXXX/segmentations/ (only lesion files are listed, e.g. liver_lesion.nii.gz), while a user report (GitHub issue #3) describes a combined_labels.nii.gz multi-label volume; which organ masks ship for each case is not documented:
Label 31 - endometrioma_tumor (the uterine tumor class; the README figure calls it 'uterus tumor')
Labels 1-25 are the same as the AbdomenAtlas 1.1 class map. Label 26 (uterus) and the six tumor classes, labels 27-32, are new.
The paper and README figure describe '31 annotated structures (25 organs + 6 tumors)', one fewer than the 32-entry class map.

Tumor totals (README / arXiv v2): 15,130 per-voxel tumor instances across the six organs, plus 5,893 control scans. Per-organ tumor counts are not listed in the README. The official download scripts fetch no metadata or tumor-vs-control list, and GitHub issue #1 (Nov 2025, unanswered) asks for the IDs of the control cases; the Hugging Face file listing could not be checked.
details.file_structure: Download with the two scripts in the repo's data/ folder. download_AbdomenAtlas2.0_ct.sh fetches the CT volumes from the Hugging Face dataset MrGiovanni/AbdomenAtlas2.0Mini (~400 GB) as 21 tar.gz shards of 500 case IDs each, AbdomenAtlas2.0Mini_ct_<start>_<end>.tar.gz, covering BDMAP_00000001 to BDMAP_00010500; it uses plain wget, with no token, and extracts each shard into AbdomenAtlas2.0/. download_AbdomenAtlas2.0_label.sh fetches a single archive, AbdomenAtlas2.0Mini_label.tar.gz, from www.cs.jhu.edu/~zongwei/dataset/ and copies its contents into AbdomenAtlas2.0/. data/README.md documents the layout AbdomenAtlas2.0/ct/BDMAP_XXXXXXXX/ct.nii.gz for the images and AbdomenAtlas2.0/label/BDMAP_XXXXXXXX/segmentations/<class>.nii.gz for the masks (e.g. liver_lesion.nii.gz, pancreatic_lesion.nii.gz, kidney_lesion.nii.gz). The archive internals were not inspected, so whether the extracted tree matches that layout is unconfirmed. GitHub issue #3 (Mar 2026, unanswered) loads BDMAP_00000030/combined_labels.nii.gz (474x362x194) against ct.nii.gz (512x512x194), with the same origin, i.e. the label volume appears cropped in-plane; no official script for realigning them is given.
details.splits: The README lists all 10,135 scans as the 'Official training and Validation set' but publishes no split file lists. GitHub issue #2 (Jan 2026, unanswered) asks for the IID train/val list used in paper Table 3. The README names four external out-of-distribution test sets, none of them part of this release: the proprietary JHH Pancreatic Dataset, 3D-IRCADb, PANORAMA and KiPA.
details.extra: Paper: Chen et al., 'Scaling Tumor Segmentation: Best Lessons from Real and Synthetic Data', ICCV 2025, pp. 24001-24013 (arXiv 2510.14831). The repo was created in July 2025; the CT download script was added on 23 Oct 2025 and the label script on 1 Nov 2025. Headline counts differ between versions: the README, the GitHub 'About' text and arXiv v2 give 10,135 scans / 15,130 tumors / 5,893 controls, while search snippets of arXiv v1 and the ICCV proceedings give 10,134 / 13,223 / 6,511. Per the paper, tumor masks were made with its SMART-Annotator pipeline (a model trained on public data proposed tumors at a high-sensitivity FROC threshold, senior radiologists removed false positives, junior radiologists revised the final masks), and it is the first public dataset with voxel-level esophageal and uterine tumor masks. The RadGPT paper (arXiv 2501.04678) uses the name AbdomenAtlas 2.0 for an earlier stage: the 9,262 AbdomenAtlas 1.1 CTs with AI-drafted, radiologist-revised liver, kidney and pancreatic tumor masks. How that relates to this 10,135-scan, six-tumor release, and which source datasets the scans come from beyond '89 source hospitals', is not documented in the sources read. The README does not say how many scans the 'Mini' download (HF MrGiovanni/AbdomenAtlas2.0Mini and AbdomenAtlas2.0Mini_label.tar.gz) contains; the CT shard names span IDs 00000001-00010500, and for AbdomenAtlas 1.0 'Mini' meant a subset. The README states 'The AI ranks first in Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD)' without giving results; its benchmark table has no numbers yet and no model checkpoints have been released. The README and LICENSE do not say how the licenses of the underlying public CT datasets apply; the README adds 'Paper content is covered by patents pending.' AbdomenAtlas 3.0 (RadGPT) is a separate catalog entry that pairs the 9,262 AbdomenAtlas 1.1 scans with reports. License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 per the GitHub LICENSE (© The Johns Hopkins University); the Hugging Face card's license tag could not be checked.

name: AbdomenAtlas 3.0
full_name: AbdomenAtlas 3.0 (RadGPT)
anatomy: abdominal organs, tumors (liver, kidney, pancreas), pancreas sub-segments, peripancreatic vessels
protocol_note: Includes contrast-enhanced phases; 3,220 scans have at least one contrast-enhanced phase.
size: 9,262 CT volumes (3,220 with a contrast-enhanced phase) + reports
segmentation_detail: Per-voxel segmentations of liver, kidney and pancreatic tumors, nine core organs, plus pancreas sub-segments and peripancreatic blood vessels.
paired_text_detail: First public abdominal CT dataset with paired radiology reports (>9,000 CT scans with structured/'superhuman' reports generated by RadGPT).
description: An ICCV 2025 abdominal CT dataset pairing over 9,000 CT volumes with radiology reports and per-voxel tumor, organ, pancreas sub-segment and vessel annotations in NIfTI format.

label_schema: Per-voxel segmentation masks (NIfTI) plus paired free-text radiology reports for each CT
9 core organ classes: liver, kidney, pancreas, spleen, adrenal glands, stomach, duodenum, aorta, postcava (inferior vena cava)
3 pancreas sub-segments: pancreas head, pancreas body, pancreas tail
5 peripancreatic vessels: superior mesenteric artery (SMA), superior mesenteric vein (SMV), celiac axis (CA), common hepatic artery (CHA), portal vein
3 tumor classes: liver tumor, kidney tumor, pancreatic tumor
Reports come in 3 styles: Structured (template with findings/measurements/staging), Narrative (prose), and Human-AI Fusion / Enhanced Human reports (240 reports)

Reports encode tumor measurements, organ volumes, Hounsfield-unit values, and pancreatic cancer T-stage (T1-T4) for 260 reports; note: exact integer index per mask class not documented on the public page, so indices are omitted
details.file_structure: Downloaded as NIfTI (.nii.gz) with two parallel directory trees, data/image_only (CT volumes) and data/mask_only (per-voxel masks), plus data/AbdomenAtlas3.0MiniWithMeta.csv metadata and a data/TrainTestIDS folder of split CSVs.
details.splits: No fixed train/val/test; two official split schemes provided as CSVs (IID_train.csv/IID_test.csv = random 90%/10%; OOD_train.csv/OOD_test.csv = cross-hospital, ~50% train). Total 9,262 CT-mask-report triplets.
details.extra: Of 9,262 scans, ~2,947 reports document tumors (929 liver / 1,674 kidney / 344 pancreatic) and ~6,061 report no tumor; aggregated from 17 public datasets across 88 institutions in 19 countries, so annotation provenance is mixed.

anatomy: thorax-abdomen (universal lesions: bone, pancreas, lymph node, liver, kidney, lung, etc.)
protocol_note: Thorax-abdomen CT lesion volumes-of-interest from Radboudumc, Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis and curated public datasets.
size: ~38,000 lesion VOIs across multi-part release; e.g. Part 1 = 1,618 lesions, 15.9 GB
segmentation_detail: 3D voxel-level segmentation masks of lesions across many organ types; novel fully-annotated Radboudumc/Jeroen Bosch data plus curated public sources (DeepLesion, KiTS21, LIDC-IDRI, LiTS, MSD, NIH-LN, CCC18)
description: A CT benchmark for universal 3D lesion segmentation aggregating novel fully-annotated data and curated public annotated lesion datasets across the thorax and abdomen, released as NIfTI lesion VOIs with 3D segmentation masks.

label_schema: Binary voxel-level segmentation mask per VOI (single foreground class)
Label 1 - lesion (universal; covers lung, mediastinal, abdominal, bone, pancreas, kidney, liver lesions)
No per-organ / per-lesion-type class index: all lesion types share value 1 (a 'universal' lesion segmentation target)
details.file_structure: 3D CT volumes-of-interest and their masks are stored as NIfTI files (one label file per lesion VOI, cropped/centered on the lesion with preserved voxel spacing); the GitHub repo (DIAGNijmegen/ULS23) is organized into annotations/ULS23/ (training labels), baseline_model/ (nnU-Netv2), data_processing/ (source-dataset prep), evaluation/, and GC_algorithm/, with the imaging data distributed via Zenodo releases.
details.splits: Novel ULS23_DeepLesion3D contribution = 750 fully-annotated lesions (200 abdominal, 100 bone, 50 kidney, 50 liver, 100 lung, 100 mediastinal, 150 assorted); overall train/val/test counts not confirmed from official pages (test set is a held-out multi-centre 'type II challenge' set on Grand Challenge)
details.extra: Mix of fully-annotated data (novel Radboudumc/Jeroen Bosch and DeepLesion3D lesions each segmented in triplicate with majority-vote consensus, plus hard-negative mining) and weakly/semi-supervised labels generated with GrabCut; training data curated from 7 public sources (DeepLesion, KiTS21, LIDC-IDRI, LiTS, MSD, NIH-LN, CCC18) alongside the new Radboudumc Bone and Pancreas sets.

related.name: DeepLesion
related.note: Lesion VOIs cropped; 750 lesions fully 3D annotated (ULS23_DeepLesion3D), others with weak GrabCut masks from RECIST

related.name: KiTS21
related.note: Kidney tumour masks cropped into lesion VOIs

related.name: LIDC-IDRI
related.note: Lung nodule masks cropped into lesion VOIs

related.name: LiTS
related.note: Liver tumour masks cropped into lesion VOIs

related.name: Medical Segmentation Decathlon
related.note: Lesion tasks cropped into lesion VOIs

related.name: NIH Lymph Nodes (NIH-LN)
related.note: Lymph node lesions cropped into VOIs

related.name: CCC18
related.note: Lesions cropped into VOIs

name: ATLAS
full_name: A Tumour and Liver Automatic Segmentation (ATLAS) MICCAI 2023 Challenge
protocol_note: T1 contrast-enhanced MRI with variation in image resolution, contrast phase, sequence and MRI manufacturer.
size: 90 T1 contrast-enhanced MRI scans (60 train / 30 test) from 90 unresectable HCC patients
segmentation_detail: Binary segmentation masks for two structures: liver (parenchyma) and tumor(s).
description: A MICCAI 2023 challenge dataset of 90 T1 contrast-enhanced liver MRI scans from unresectable HCC patients with liver and tumor segmentation labels.

details.file_structure: 3D volumetric NIfTI (.nii.gz): one contrast-enhanced T1 MRI volume per patient plus one matching segmentation label volume encoding liver and tumor, split into train and test folders, with per-patient acquisition metadata in patient_info_train.json / patient_info_test.json.
details.splits: 60 training patients / 30 test patients (90 total); test-set labels withheld during the challenge.
details.extra: Modality is contrast-enhanced T1 MRI (CE-MRI), not CT; masks were manually segmented and reviewed by radiologists, and dataset spans varied resolutions, contrast phases, sequences, and scanner manufacturers.

name: SegRap2023
full_name: Segmentation of Organs-at-Risk and Gross Tumor Volume of NPC (SegRap 2023)
anatomy: head and neck organs-at-risk and nasopharyngeal carcinoma tumor volumes
protocol_note: Paired non-contrast and contrast-enhanced CT per patient.
size: 400 CT scans (200 patients, paired contrast-enhanced + non-contrast); 120 train, 20 validation, 60 test
segmentation_detail: Voxel annotations of 45 organs-at-risk plus 2 gross tumor volumes (GTVnx primary, GTVnd nodal).
description: A MICCAI 2023 head-and-neck CT dataset of 200 nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients with paired contrast/non-contrast scans, annotated for 45 organs-at-risk and two gross tumor volumes.

label_schema: Task 1 (OAR segmentation): 45 head-and-neck organs-at-risk, voxel masks

OARs: Brain, Brainstem, Chiasm, Cochlea left, Cochlea right, Esophagus, Eustachian tube left, Eustachian tube right, Eye left, Eye right, Hippocampus left, Hippocampus right, Internal auditory canal left, Internal auditory canal right, Larynx, Larynx glottic, Larynx supraglottic, Lens left, Lens right, Mandible left, Mandible right, Mastoid left, Mastoid right, Middle ear left, Middle ear right, Optic nerve left, Optic nerve right, Oral cavity, Parotid left, Parotid right, Pharynx, Pituitary, Spinal cord, Submandibular left, Submandibular right, Temporal lobe left, Temporal lobe right, Thyroid, Temporomandibular joint left, Temporomandibular joint right, Trachea, Tympanic cavity left, Tympanic cavity right, Vestibular semicircular canal left, Vestibular semicircular canal right
Task 2 (GTV segmentation): 2 gross tumor volume classes
GTVnx - primary gross target volume of nasopharynx (nasopharyngeal carcinoma tumor)
GTVnd - gross target volume of involved lymph node(s)
details.file_structure: Each of the 200 patients has two co-registered CT volumes (a non-contrast and a contrast-enhanced scan) with corresponding voxel-level annotations; challenge submissions require 4D .mha masks (shape [45, *image_shape] for OARs, [2, *image_shape] for GTVs), with inputs organized under image folders (e.g. head-neck-ct and head-neck-contrast-enhanced-ct).
details.splits: 120 training / 20 validation / 60 testing patients (200 total)
details.extra: Two separate tasks: Task 1 = 45 OARs, Task 2 = 2 nasopharyngeal carcinoma GTVs; training and validation data were publicly released after MICCAI 2023 via Google Drive and Baidu Cloud.

name: PANORAMA
full_name: Pancreatic Cancer Diagnosis - Radiologists Meet AI (PANORAMA)
protocol_note: Routine upper-abdominal contrast-enhanced CT (CECT), retrospective, multi-center; the PANORAMA dataset uses portal-venous phase CECT.
size: ~2,238 CECT training scans (two centers) plus 194 MSD and 80 NIH external cases; ~197 GB
segmentation_detail: Segmentation labels provided in companion repo DIAGNijmegen/panorama_labels: PDAC lesion (manual), plus pancreas parenchyma, veins, arteries, pancreatic duct, and common bile duct (automatic). Manual lesion segmentations for PDAC cases.
description: A large multi-center contrast-enhanced abdominal CT dataset of ~2,200+ scans enriched for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with pancreas and tumor segmentation annotations.

label_schema: Label 1 - PDAC lesion (manual for annotated PDAC cases; automatic otherwise)
Non-lesion structures (labels 2-6) generated automatically via the Alves et al. 2021 algorithm
details.file_structure: Segmentation masks are single-file multi-label NIfTI volumes (.nii.gz) named by case (e.g. 100002_00001.nii.gz), stored in the companion GitHub repo DIAGNijmegen/panorama_labels under manual_labels/ and automatic_labels/, with a clinical_information.xlsx reference-standard spreadsheet; contrast-enhanced CT images are distributed separately on the Grand Challenge / Zenodo data pages.
details.splits: Public training/development set of 2,238 CECT studies; hidden test cohort of ~400 unseen scans used for challenge evaluation (no official validation split published).
details.extra: PDAC lesion labels come in two flavors: 482 manually segmented cases (ITK-SNAP v3.80, by two trained investigators supervised by an expert radiologist) and the remainder automatically generated; includes non-PDAC/healthy-pancreas cases plus cases derived from the NIH pancreas set and Medical Segmentation Decathlon.

related.name: MSD Pancreas (Task07)
related.note: 194 MSD pancreas CT cases included as external data with PANORAMA labels

related.name: Pancreas-CT (NIH)
related.note: 80 NIH Pancreas-CT cases included as healthy-pancreas data with PANORAMA labels

name: TopCoW 2024
full_name: Topology-Aware Anatomical Segmentation of the Circle of Willis
protocol_note: Paired CTA and MRA of the same patients (two modalities, not multi-sequence)
size: 125 training patients (250 paired CTA+MRA images), plus 10 validation and 70 test pairs
segmentation_detail: Multi-class voxel annotations of up to 13 Circle of Willis vessel components
license: Open use with attribution; commercial use requires data-owner permission
description: The first public dataset with paired CTA and MRA from the same patients and voxel-level multi-class annotations of the Circle of Willis vessels, released via the TopCoW 2024 MICCAI challenge.

label_schema: Multi-class voxel segmentation of Circle of Willis vessels (Task 1)
Companion Task 2 labels: 3D bounding box of the CoW region of interest (detection)
Companion Task 3 labels: anterior/posterior CoW edge-list annotations for graph classification
details.file_structure: Angiographic scans and masks are stored as NIfTI (.nii.gz, 16-bit signed, LPS+ orientation), organized in per-annotation-type folders (imagesTr, cow_seg_labelsTr, roi_loc_labelsTr, antpos_edges_labelsTr), with paired CTA and MRA acquired per patient.
details.splits: Training: 125 patients (250 CTA+MRA scans); Validation: 5 patients (10 scans, images only); Test: 70 patients (labels not publicly released).
details.extra: Voxel-level annotations were created using virtual-reality tooling with expert verification; each patient has paired CTA and MRA of the same anatomy.

name: CURVAS
full_name: Calibration and Uncertainty for multiRater Volume Assessment in multiorgan Segmentation
protocol_note: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT (portal venous phase per catalog entry); 90 CTs prospectively gathered at University Hospital Erlangen, Aug–Oct 2023
size: 90 CT scans (training set ~6.3 GB)
segmentation_detail: Multi-rater segmentations by three independent experts of pancreas, kidney and liver on contrast-enhanced (portal venous phase) abdominal CT
description: Ninety contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans, each segmented independently by three experts for pancreas, kidney and liver, to study inter-rater variability, uncertainty and model calibration in multi-organ segmentation.

label_schema: Each case carries 3 independent full-organ segmentations, one per expert rater (annotation_1, annotation_2, annotation_3)
multi-rater annotations for inter-rater variability, uncertainty and calibration
details.file_structure: Contrast-enhanced (portal venous phase) abdominal CT volumes in NIfTI (.nii.gz) format, one folder per case containing the CT image plus three separate multi-label expert annotation volumes (one per rater) using the shared 0/1/2/3 organ label map.
details.splits: 90 CT scans total: 20 training + 5 validation + 65 test (validation and test labels withheld during the challenge).
details.extra: Multi-rater dataset (CURVAS = Calibration and Uncertainty for multiRater Volume Assessment in multiorgan Segmentation); the 3 per-case annotations are meant for inter-rater variability/uncertainty modeling, not a single consensus ground truth. Cases are stratified by cyst count/pathology into hidden groups A/B/C. License CC BY-NC.

name: MAMA-MIA
full_name: MAMA-MIA: A Large-Scale Multi-Center Breast Cancer DCE-MRI Benchmark Dataset
protocol_note: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI with a pre-contrast phase and multiple post-contrast phases
size: 1,506 annotated training scans plus 574 external validation cases (multi-institutional)
segmentation_detail: Expert manual and automated primary-tumor segmentation masks
paired_text_detail: Structured clinical and demographic variables per case, including pathologic complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant chemotherapy
description: A large multi-institutional homogenized breast dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI dataset with expert primary-tumor segmentations and clinical variables for tumor segmentation and treatment-response prediction.

label_schema: Primary-tumor segmentation mask (single foreground class): experts segmented the primary breast tumor including non-mass-enhancement (NME) areas; background elsewhere
Two segmentation versions provided per case: expert-corrected gold-standard masks and the automatic (uncorrected) nnU-Net baseline masks
49 harmonized tabular variables per case: 21 clinical, 6 demographic, and 22 imaging/acquisition-parameter fields
Secondary clinical prediction target available: pathologic complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC)
details.file_structure: Images and masks are stored as compressed NIfTI (.nii.gz); each case is keyed by collection acronym + patient ID (e.g. ISPY1_1221), with DCE-MRI phases named CASE_0000 (pre-contrast), CASE_0001/_0002/... (post-contrast) in an images folder, and separate folders for expert vs. automatic tumor-segmentation masks; accompanying metadata/clinical data and automatic-segmentation QA scores and the train/test split are provided as CSV/Excel tables (hosted on Synapse, DOI 10.7303/syn60868042).
details.extra: 1,506 pre-treatment DCE-MRI cases aggregated from four TCIA collections (ISPY1, Breast-MRI-NACT-Pilot, ISPY2, Duke-Breast-Cancer-MRI); only 163 cases had pre-existing expert segmentations, the rest were auto-segmented by a deep-learning model then corrected/verified by 16 breast-cancer experts, yielding 1,506 expert + 1,506 automatic masks. A train/test split table is provided for reproducibility but exact counts were not confirmed from the sources reviewed.

related.name: ISPY1 (ACRIN 6657)
related.note: Pre-treatment DCE-MRI converted to NIfTI and harmonized, with expert-corrected tumor masks

related.name: ISPY2
related.note: Pre-treatment DCE-MRI converted to NIfTI and harmonized, with expert-corrected tumor masks

related.name: Breast-MRI-NACT-Pilot
related.note: Pre-treatment DCE-MRI converted to NIfTI and harmonized, with expert-corrected tumor masks

related.name: Duke Breast Cancer MRI
related.note: Pre-treatment DCE-MRI converted to NIfTI and harmonized, with expert-corrected tumor masks

name: HNTS-MRG 2024
full_name: Head and Neck Tumor Segmentation for MR-Guided Radiotherapy 2024
anatomy: Head and neck (primary tumor GTVp and nodal GTVn volumes)
protocol_note: Primarily T2-weighted MRI at each timepoint
size: ~150 training patients (pre-RT and mid-RT), ~50 test patients
segmentation_detail: Expert GTVp (primary tumor) and GTVn (nodal) segmentation masks on pre-RT and mid-RT MRI
description: An MRI dataset of head-and-neck cancer patients imaged pre- and mid-radiotherapy with expert primary and nodal tumor segmentations for MR-guided adaptive radiotherapy.

label_schema: Segmentation mask, single label volume with integer values
2 - GTVn (metastatic/nodal gross tumor volume; all nodes merged into this single label)
details.file_structure: NIfTI compressed (.nii.gz) files organized as HNTSMRG24_train/<patientID>/{preRT,midRT}/, where preRT holds the pre-RT T2w image (<id>_preRT_T2.nii.gz) and its mask (<id>_preRT_mask.nii.gz), and midRT holds the mid-RT T2w image (<id>_midRT_T2.nii.gz), mid-RT mask (<id>_midRT_mask.nii.gz), plus the pre-RT image and mask registered to mid-RT space (<id>_preRT_T2_registered.nii.gz, <id>_preRT_mask_registered.nii.gz).
details.splits: Training: 150 patient cases. Test set size not stated on the official dataset page.
details.extra: Two challenge tasks share the same patients: Task 1 = pre-RT segmentation, Task 2 = mid-RT segmentation. Masks are expert reference (ground-truth) GTVp/GTVn contours on T2-weighted MRI.

name: AortaSeg24
full_name: Multi-Class Segmentation of Aortic Branches and Zones in CTA
protocol_note: Computed tomography angiography (CTA); volumes resampled to isotropic 1 mm voxels
size: 100 annotated CTA volumes
segmentation_detail: Multi-class segmentation of the aorta, individual branch vessels, and clinically relevant SVS/STS aortic zones (23 classes)
description: A MICCAI 2024 challenge providing 100 annotated CT angiography volumes with multi-class labels of aortic branches and SVS/STS zones for automated aorta segmentation and surgical planning in type B aortic dissection.

label_schema: Multi-class 3D segmentation: 23 foreground classes (integer labels 1-23) plus background=0, stored in a single mask volume per subject
10 aortic SVS/STS zones: Zone 0, Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone 3, Zone 4, Zone 5, Zone 6, Zone 7, Zone 8, Zone 9

13 aortic branch vessels: Innominate (brachiocephalic) artery, Left common carotid artery, Left subclavian artery, Celiac artery, Superior mesenteric artery (SMA), Right renal artery, Left renal artery, Right common iliac artery, Left common iliac artery, Right internal iliac artery, Left internal iliac artery, Right external iliac artery, Left external iliac artery
details.file_structure: Data in .mha (MetaImage) format, organized as an images/ folder (e.g. subject001_CTA.mha) and a masks/ folder with a matching single multi-class label volume per subject (e.g. subject001_label.mha); CTA volumes resampled to isotropic 1 mm voxels.
details.splits: 100 total CTA volumes from 100 uncomplicated Type-B Aortic Dissection (uTBAD) patients, split into 50 training/development (released with labels), 10 validation (hidden), and 40 test (hidden).
details.extra: The exact integer-to-anatomy assignment for the 23 classes was not confirmed from the accessible sources (paper/challenge page list the class names but not a numbered mapping table); zones follow the SVS/STS aortic reporting standards. Contact weishao@ufl.edu for the official label dictionary.

name: LNQ2023
full_name: Mediastinal Lymph Node Quantification Challenge
protocol_note: Contrast-enhanced chest CT from oncology clinical trials (heterogeneous CT data)
size: 513 subjects (~35 GB) on TCIA
segmentation_detail: Segmentation masks of mediastinal lymph nodes >1 cm from cancer clinical-trial patients; partially annotated training (subset of nodes), fully annotated validation/test
description: A contrast-enhanced chest CT benchmark for weakly-supervised segmentation of enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes from oncology clinical-trial imaging, with data hosted on TCIA (MEDIASTINAL-LYMPH-NODE-SEG, 513 subjects).

label_schema: Binary segmentation mask: foreground = clinically relevant mediastinal lymph node(s) (short-axis > 1 cm), background = everything else
Single target class (lymph node); no multi-class/per-node instance labels
Training masks are PARTIAL: typically only one node per case (the trial-tracked lesion) is segmented, not all abnormal nodes
Validation/test masks are FULL: every abnormal mediastinal node with estimated short axis > 1 cm is segmented (total mediastinal nodal disease burden)
details.file_structure: Chest CT volumes and their segmentation masks are distributed as paired NRRD files (.nrrd), one image + one label mask per case.
details.splits: 383 training (partially annotated), 20 validation (fully annotated), 100 test (fully annotated)
details.extra: Data comes from oncology clinical-trial patients (2007-2020) via the Tumor Imaging Metrics Core (TIMC) at MGH/Dana-Farber/Brigham & Women's, Boston; the intended setup is weakly-supervised learning (train on partial labels, evaluate against full labels) scored by Dice and Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASSD).

name: ISLES 2024
full_name: Ischemic Stroke Lesion Segmentation Challenge 2024
protocol_note: Acute multimodal CT (NCCT, CTA, CT perfusion source and derived perfusion maps); final infarct ground truth derived from follow-up MRI (DWI)
size: ~150 training cases
segmentation_detail: Binary segmentation mask of the final post-treatment ischemic stroke infarct
description: A stroke imaging challenge providing acute multimodal CT (NCCT, CTA, CT perfusion) with follow-up-MRI-derived infarct masks and tabular clinical data for final ischemic lesion segmentation.

label_schema: Binary segmentation mask of the final ischemic stroke infarct
Value 1 - final post-treatment infarct lesion (delineated on follow-up MRI)
Companion label: vessel-occlusion masks derived from acute CT angiography (CTA)
details.file_structure: BIDS-organized directories of compressed NIfTI (.nii.gz) files: rawdata/ holds per-subject acute CT (NCCT, CTA, CTP) plus follow-up DWI/ADC, derivatives/ holds registered CTP perfusion maps (Tmax, MTT, CBF, CBV) and the binary infarct segmentation named like sub-strokecaseXXXX_ses-02_lesion-msk.nii.gz, and phenotype/ holds clinical tabular data.
details.splits: Full multicenter dataset described in the paper comprises 245 cases; the challenge released training data in batches with a separate hidden test set, but exact public-train vs. test counts are not confirmed from the sources reviewed.
details.extra: Ground-truth infarct masks were delineated on follow-up MRI (DWI/ADC) acquired 2-9 days after the acute CT; the task is to predict this final infarct from acute imaging alone.
details.reference_standard: Final infarct delineated on post-treatment follow-up MRI (DWI/ADC) 2-9 days after the acute CT
details.third_party_note: Zenodo training data and dataset paper are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike); no API-specific clause. (Catalog license field is null - CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 is the verified value.)

name: PENGWIN
full_name: Pelvic Bone Fragments with Injuries Segmentation Challenge
anatomy: Pelvic bones (sacrum and hipbone fracture fragments)
protocol_note: CT scans from 150 patients scheduled for pelvic reduction surgery, multiple institutions and scanners; 2D X-rays synthetically generated from CT with DeepDRR (virtual C-arm positions, surgical tools such as K-wires and screws).
size: 150 patient CT scans plus synthetically generated 2D X-ray images
segmentation_detail: Semi-automatically annotated and medical-expert-validated segmentations of sacrum and hipbone fracture fragments in 3D CT and in 2D X-ray
description: A MICCAI 2024 challenge dataset of 150 pelvic fracture CT scans and synthetically generated 2D X-rays with expert-validated fragment-level segmentation annotations of the sacrum and hipbone.

label_schema: Labels 1-10 = sacrum (SA) fracture fragments (one integer per fragment, up to 10)
Labels 11-20 = left hipbone/ilium (LI) fracture fragments (up to 10)
Labels 21-30 = right hipbone/ilium (RI) fracture fragments (up to 10)
An unfractured bone is represented as a single fragment (the whole bone)

Task 2 (X-ray): multi-label uint32 mask where each pixel is a binary bit-vector (bits allow overlapping fragments due to projection): bits 1-10 = SA fragments, bits 11-20 = LI fragments, bits 21-30 = RI fragments
details.file_structure: Task 1 CT images and label masks are stored as .mha volumes (images split across PENGWIN_CT_train_images_part1/2.zip, masks in PENGWIN_CT_train_labels.zip); Task 2 X-ray inputs and masks are TIFF files organized as train/input/images/x-ray/[ID].tif and train/output/images/x-ray/[ID].tif, filenames using a 3-digit CT/patient ID (001-100) plus a 4-digit image index (0000-0499).
details.splits: Training released publicly: Task 1 = 100 CT scans; Task 2 = 50,000 synthetic X-rays (500 projections per each of the 100 CTs). Test set counts are not confirmed from the sources reviewed.
details.extra: Ground-truth segmentations were semi-automatically annotated and then validated by medical experts; the X-ray masks are uint32 bit-encoded and cannot be viewed with standard image viewers, and about half the synthetic X-rays include K-wires and orthopedic screws.

name: CMRxRecon2024
full_name: Cardiac MRI Reconstruction Challenge 2024
protocol_note: Multi-contrast raw k-space: cine, T1/T2 mapping, tagging, phase-contrast (flow2d) and dark-blood imaging across long-axis, short-axis, outflow-tract and aortic views, with undersampling masks/trajectories and autocalibration signals
size: 330 healthy volunteers (200 training, 60 validation, 70 test)
description: A multi-contrast, multi-view raw cardiac MRI k-space dataset from 330 volunteers on a Siemens 3T scanner for developing accelerated undersampled reconstruction methods.

label_schema: No segmentation/classification/detection annotations - this is an MRI reconstruction challenge
Ground-truth 'label' = fully-sampled (reference) k-space, provided for training only
Reconstruction targets span contrasts: cardiac Cine, Aorta, T1/T2 Mapping, Tagging (train), plus unseen Flow2d and BlackBlood in val/test
Task 1 target: reconstruct from uniform undersampling at 4x, 8x, 10x acceleration
Task 2 target: reconstruct from uniform/Gaussian/pseudo-radial trajectories at 4x-24x acceleration
Companion arrays: undersampled k-space, sampling/undersampling masks, and autocalibration signal (ACS: 16 lines for Task 1, 16x16 region for Task 2)
details.file_structure: Data stored as MATLAB .mat files per subject/contrast; training files hold fully-sampled k-space (ground truth), while validation/test hold undersampled k-space plus sampling trajectories and ACS - arrays are 5D (nx,ny,nc,nz,nt) for Cine/Aorta/Mapping/Tagging, 4D for BlackBlood, with 2D masks (Task 1) or 3D masks (Task 2).
details.splits: 330 healthy-volunteer scans (3.0T Siemens MAGNETOM Vida): 200 training / 60 validation / 70 test
details.extra: No manual annotations or reader labels exist; evaluation is image-quality/reconstruction fidelity against the fully-sampled reference, and validation/test add two contrasts (Flow2d, BlackBlood) not present in training to test generalization.

name: CMRxMotion
full_name: Extreme Cardiac MRI Analysis Challenge under Respiratory Motion
anatomy: Heart (left ventricle, left ventricle myocardium, right ventricle)
protocol_note: Cine cardiac MRI acquired in healthy volunteers under four respiratory conditions (normal breath-hold, halved breath-hold, free breathing, intensive breathing); ED and ES frames provided.
size: ~40 healthy volunteers imaged under 4 respiratory-motion levels
segmentation_detail: Left ventricle, left ventricle myocardium and right ventricle segmentation on cine MRI (diagnostically adequate images)
description: Cine cardiac MRI from ~40 volunteers acquired under four respiratory-motion conditions with radiologist image-quality grades and LV/myocardium/RV segmentations for motion-robustness benchmarking (MICCAI 2022 STACOM).

label_schema: Task 1 image-quality assessment: 3 ordinal motion-artifact classes - Label 1 mild motion (radiologist score 4-5), Label 2 intermediate motion (score 3), Label 3 severe motion (score 1-2)
details.file_structure: Cine CMR volumes exported from DICOM to NIfTI (.nii.gz); per subject/respiratory-condition, 3D image volumes at ED and ES frames are provided, with a matching integer-labeled segmentation .nii.gz for diagnostically adequate images plus a per-image quality label for the IQA task.
details.splits: 40 healthy volunteers total: 20 training (images + quality labels + segmentation released), 5 validation (images only), 15 test (held out for offline evaluation).
details.extra: Each volunteer was imaged under 4 respiratory conditions (normal breath-hold, halved breath-hold, free breathing, intensive breathing) to induce varying motion artifacts; segmentation (Task 2) is only provided/evaluated on diagnostically adequate images (mild/intermediate motion), while severe-motion images are excluded from segmentation.

name: LUMIERE
full_name: Longitudinal Glioblastoma MRI Dataset
protocol_note: Multiparametric MRI: pre-contrast T1, post-contrast T1, T2 and FLAIR at each timepoint (599 of 638 studies have all four)
size: 91 patients, 638 study dates, 2487 MRI images (~32.5 GB imaging ZIP)
segmentation_detail: Automated tumor segmentations from DeepBraTumIA and HD-GLIO-AUTO for timepoints with all four sequences
paired_text_detail: Expert RANO tumor-response ratings plus demographics, pathology and survival/clinical data provided as separate tables
description: A longitudinal multiparametric MRI dataset of 91 glioblastoma patients across 638 study dates with automated tumor segmentations and expert RANO response ratings.

label_schema: Two automated tumor segmentation label maps per timepoint (only for study dates with all four MR sequences), from two different tools
DeepBraTumIA (seg_mask.nii.gz): multi-class tumor label map with 3 tumor tissue classes - necrosis, contrast-enhancing tumor, and edema
HD-GLIO-AUTO (segmentation.nii.gz): 2 tumor classes - label 1 = contrast-enhancing tumor, label 2 = non-enhancing T2/FLAIR signal abnormality (per HD-GLIO convention)

Expert RANO rating (LUMIERE-ExpertRating.csv): neuroradiologist response category per selected follow-up timepoint - Post-op (Op), Complete Response (CR), Partial Response (PR), Stable Disease (SD), Progressive Disease (PD)
RANO rating also records rationale/comments, presence of non-measurable/measurable/target/non-target lesions, and bi-dimensional (Macdonald) measurements for measurable lesions
Per-tumor-label radiomic features included: PyRadiomics features and CoLlAGe features for each segmentation label and MRI sequence
Pathology/demographics CSV: MGMT promoter methylation status, IDH1 status, sex, age at diagnosis, and overall survival time (subset of patients)
details.file_structure: On disk it is organized as Patient-XXX/week-00N folders holding skull-stripped NIfTI sequences (CT1, T1, T2, FLAIR .nii.gz) plus DeepBraTumIA-segmentation and HD-GLIO-AUTO-segmentation subfolders with label-map .nii.gz files in both atlas/registered and native/back-transformed spaces (with transform .tfm/.mat files); ratings, MRI acquisition info, demographics/pathology, and radiomic features are separate CSV files.
details.extra: No official train/val/test split; the two automated segmentations (DeepBraTumIA and HD-GLIO-AUTO) are provided deliberately to benchmark algorithm/segmentation variability, and both are automated (not manual ground truth); some RANO-rated timepoints have no segmentation because rating was possible with only a subset of the four sequences. Cohort: 91 GBM patients, 638 study dates, 2487 images.

name: BraTS 2024 Post-Treatment Glioma (BraTS-GLI)
full_name: 2024 Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge: Adult Glioma Post-Treatment
protocol_note: Co-registered, skull-stripped native T1, post-contrast T1 (T1c/T1Gd), T2, and T2-FLAIR sequences
size: ~2200 multi-institutional post-treatment MRI cases
segmentation_detail: Expert annotations of four sub-regions: enhancing tissue (ET), non-enhancing tumor core (NETC), surrounding non-enhancing FLAIR hyperintensity (SNFH), and resection cavity (RC)
description: The BraTS 2024 post-treatment adult glioma challenge provides multi-sequence brain MRI (T1, T1c, T2, T2-FLAIR) with expert segmentations of enhancing tissue, non-enhancing tumor core, FLAIR hyperintensity, and resection cavity for post-therapy glioma monitoring.

label_schema: Voxel-wise multi-class segmentation: single -seg NIfTI volume with 4 tumor sub-region classes over background
Label 1 - NETC (non-enhancing tumor core): necrosis/cysts, dark on both T1 and T1-Gd
Label 2 - SNFH (surrounding non-enhancing FLAIR hyperintensity): edema, infiltrating/non-enhancing tumor, radiation-related hyperintensity and gliosis
Label 3 - ET (enhancing tissue): thick/nodular T1-Gd enhancement, excluding vessels and thin linear treatment-related enhancement
Label 4 - RC (resection cavity): recent and chronic post-surgical resection cavities
details.file_structure: One folder per case (named BraTS-GLI-XXXXX-XXX) containing four co-registered, skull-stripped MRI channels as NIfTI .nii.gz (-t1n = pre-contrast T1, -t1c = post-contrast T1/T1-Gd, -t2w = T2, -t2f = T2-FLAIR) plus one multi-label ground-truth mask (-seg.nii.gz).
details.splits: Cases split ~70% training / 10% validation / 20% testing out of ~2,200 total cases from 7 institutions; public ground-truth segmentation labels released only for the training set, with validation/test labels withheld (exact per-split case counts not confirmed).
details.extra: Ground truth was generated by STAPLE-fusing five nnU-Net pre-segmentations then manual radiologist refinement and board-certified neuroradiologist approval; the held-out test set was independently annotated by two annotator/approver teams to assess inter-rater reliability. Evaluation uses lesion-wise Dice and Hausdorff-95.

name: BraTS-MEN-RT 2024
full_name: 2024 Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge: Meningioma Radiotherapy
protocol_note: Single 3D post-contrast T1-weighted radiotherapy-planning MRI in native acquisition space (defaced); not a multi-sequence set
size: 750 radiotherapy-planning brain MRIs (multi-institutional) with expert GTV annotations on the training/validation partitions
segmentation_detail: Single-label expert-annotated gross tumor volume (GTV) / at-risk post-operative site for radiotherapy planning, approved by neuroradiologists and radiation oncologists
description: BraTS-MEN-RT is the largest multi-institutional collection of 3D post-contrast T1-weighted radiotherapy-planning MRIs of intracranial meningiomas with expert gross tumor volume (GTV) annotations for automated radiotherapy target delineation.

label_schema: Single foreground class - radiotherapy target volume (binary mask): foreground = the GTV plus any at-risk post-operative site; background = 0
In the intact setting the label is the tumor portion visible on the post-contrast T1w (T1c) MRI; in the postoperative setting it covers the resection cavity / at-risk site per RT planning protocols
Annotations approved by expert neuroradiologists and radiation oncologists; derived from the treating institution's DICOM-RT structure sets
details.file_structure: One defaced 3D post-contrast T1-weighted (T1c) MRI and one single-label GTV segmentation mask per case, stored as NIfTI (.nii.gz) in per-case folders under the BraTS-MEN-RT-<ID> naming convention; converted from source DICOM / DICOM-RT with dcmrtstruct2nii.
details.splits: 750 total cases from 7 US/UK academic centers: Training 500 (images + reference labels released), Validation 70 (images only released), Testing 180 (not publicly released).
details.extra: Unlike earlier BraTS tasks, images are defaced (extracranial tissue preserved, not skull-stripped) and kept in native acquisition space rather than atlas-registered; only a single T1c sequence is provided (no multiparametric MRI). Non-target/non-segmented meningiomas may be present in scans.

name: BraTS-GoAT 2024
full_name: 2024 BraTS Generalizability Across Tumors (GoAT) Challenge
protocol_note: Co-registered, skull-stripped multiparametric MRI: T1, T1-contrast-enhanced (T1c), T2, and T2-FLAIR
size: Pooled multi-tumor BraTS cohort (thousands of cases across glioma, meningioma, metastases, pediatric)
segmentation_detail: Expert-annotated tumor sub-region masks (enhancing tumor, tumor core, whole tumor) pooled across glioma, meningioma, brain metastases and pediatric tumors
description: The BraTS-GoAT 2024 task benchmarks the generalizability of brain-tumor segmentation methods by pooling co-registered, skull-stripped multiparametric MRI across diverse tumor types with expert sub-region masks.

label_schema: Voxel-wise multi-class tumor sub-region segmentation mask, values consistent across all tumor types
Evaluated hierarchical regions derived from labels: Enhancing Tumor (ET = label 3), Tumor Core (TC = NCR + ET = labels 1+3), Whole Tumor (WT = NCR + ED + ET = labels 1+2+3)
Presence of each sub-region varies by case and tumor type (some lesions lack necrosis, edema, or enhancement), but label values never change
details.file_structure: Standard BraTS layout: one folder per subject containing four co-registered skull-stripped multiparametric MRI volumes (T1 native, T1-Gd/post-contrast, T2, T2-FLAIR) plus a ground-truth segmentation volume, all as NIfTI (.nii.gz) files with per-region integer labels.
details.extra: Data is pooled from five BraTS 2023 populations (adult glioma, sub-Saharan Africa adult glioma, intracranial meningioma, brain metastases, pediatric tumors); ground-truth annotations are created/approved by expert neuroradiologists, but for meningioma and brain-metastasis training subsets ground truth is released for only a subset, and the private test-set composition is undisclosed. Challenge site is now archived (data no longer downloadable there; continued in BraTS 2025 Lighthouse-GoAT). Evaluation uses Dice and 95% Hausdorff distance.

related.name: BraTS adult glioma (BraTS 2023 GLI)
related.note: Adult glioma cases pooled into GoAT

related.name: BraTS-Africa
related.note: Sub-Saharan Africa glioma cases pooled

related.name: BraTS-MEN
related.note: Meningioma cases pooled; labels for a subset

related.name: BraTS-Mets
related.note: Brain metastasis cases pooled; labels for a subset

related.name: BraTS-PEDs
related.note: Pediatric tumor cases pooled

name: UCSF-PDGM
full_name: University of California San Francisco Preoperative Diffuse Glioma MRI
protocol_note: Standardized 3T single-scanner protocol: 3D T1 pre/post-contrast, T2, T2/FLAIR, SWI, DWI, HARDI (high angular resolution diffusion), and ASL perfusion
size: 495 patients
segmentation_detail: Manual tumor segmentation masks with three compartments: enhancing tumor, non-enhancing/necrotic core, and surrounding FLAIR abnormality
description: UCSF-PDGM contains standardized preoperative multi-sequence 3T brain MRI of 495 histopathologically proven diffuse gliomas with manual tumor segmentations and molecular/clinical labels, hosted on TCIA in NIfTI format.

label_schema: Multicompartment tumor segmentation mask, 3 tumor classes: enhancing tumor
details.file_structure: Preprocessed, skull-stripped, co-registered NIfTI (.nii.gz) files at 1mm isotropic resolution organized in per-patient folders (e.g., UCSF-PDGM-0004), with one segmentation file per case named like *_tumor_segmentation.nii.gz and clinical/molecular labels in an accompanying spreadsheet/CSV.
details.extra: Tumor masks were first produced by an automated deep-learning ensemble model, then manually corrected by trained radiologists and approved by two expert reviewers; a deep-learning brain mask (skull-strip) is included but no full anatomic parcellation. Exact integer label values for the three compartments are not stated on the official TCIA page. Collection covers ~495 unique patients (originally reported as 501, six being follow-up scans).

name: UCSF-ALPTDG
full_name: University of California San Francisco Adult Longitudinal Post-Treatment Diffuse Glioma MRI
anatomy: Brain (adult diffuse glioma, post-treatment longitudinal follow-up)
protocol_note: Multimodal 3D brain MRI: T1 pre-contrast, T1 post-contrast, T2, and T2-FLAIR, acquired on a standardized 3.0-T protocol across two longitudinal timepoints
size: 298 patients; 596 post-treatment MRI exams (two consecutive posttreatment timepoints per patient)
segmentation_detail: Expert voxelwise segmentations of four tumor subregions (enhancing tissue, nonenhancing FLAIR hyperintensity, nonenhancing tumor core, resection cavity) plus longitudinal change annotations tracking ET and SNFH between timepoints
license: Noncommercial research use; data use agreement required
description: UCSF-ALPTDG is a longitudinal post-treatment adult diffuse glioma dataset of multimodal 3D brain MRI (T1 pre/post-contrast, T2, FLAIR) from 298 patients scanned at two consecutive posttreatment timepoints, with expert voxelwise tumor subregion and longitudinal-change segmentations, hosted by the UCSF Center for Intelligent Imaging under a data use agreement.

label_schema: Voxelwise tumor segmentation (4 foreground classes + background), from the official nnUNet dataset.json:
Label 2 - Edema (surrounding nonenhancing FLAIR hyperintensity, SNFH)

Longitudinal change annotations: separate masks tracking interval change in enhancing tissue (ET) and in SNFH between the two post-treatment timepoints, benchmarked via FLAIR-change and T1CE-change segmentation models using timepoint-1, timepoint-2, and subtraction images
details.file_structure: 3D MRI in NIfTI (.nii.gz), one folder per patient/timepoint with four co-registered, skull-stripped sequences (FLAIR, T1, T2, T1CE/post-contrast); expert segmentation masks are single-file multi-label NIfTI volumes (nnUNet-style imagesTr/labelsTr layout in the released benchmark).
details.splits: 298 patients total (each imaged at two consecutive post-treatment timepoints); official benchmark split 248 training / 50 test
details.extra: The four subregion class names/integers above come from the official rachitsaluja/UCSF-ALPTDG-benchmarks nnUNet dataset.json; the paper (Radiology: AI, ryai.230182) describes the same four compartments plus longitudinal ET and SNFH change annotations. Follow-up intervals between the two timepoints vary across patients, which may limit cross-patient comparisons.

name: SPIDER
full_name: Lumbar Spine Segmentation in MR Images: A Dataset and Public Benchmark
protocol_note: Sagittal T1- and T2-weighted lumbar MRI series
size: 218 studies, 447 sagittal T1/T2 MRI series (~3.8 GB)
segmentation_detail: Reference masks for vertebrae, intervertebral discs, and spinal canal
paired_text_detail: CSV/metadata with patient demographics, scanner parameters, and per-IVD radiological degenerative gradings (not free-text reports)
description: SPIDER is a multi-vendor lumbar spine MRI dataset of 218 studies (447 sagittal T1/T2 series from four hospitals) with reference segmentations of vertebrae, discs, and spinal canal plus per-level degenerative radiological gradings.

label_schema: Multi-class 3D segmentation mask, one per MRI series; three anatomical structures labeled: vertebrae, intervertebral discs (IVDs), and spinal canal
Vertebrae: integer labels numbered sequentially from the most caudal (lowest) vertebra upward, i.e. 1, 2, 3, ... (label 1 = lowest lumbar vertebra, typically L5)
Spinal canal (dural sac): fixed label value 100
Intervertebral discs (IVDs): label values 201, 202, 203, ... numbered from the lowest disc upward, each disc identified by the vertebra directly above it

Companion radiological_gradings.csv scores each disc level for: Modic changes (I-III), upper/lower endplate defects (Schmorl nodes), spondylolisthesis, disc herniation, disc narrowing, disc bulging, and Pfirrmann grade (1-5)
details.file_structure: Distributed on Zenodo as images.zip and masks.zip containing one MetaImage (.mha) volume per sagittal MRI series, with matching image/mask filenames per patient; plus overview.csv (patient/scanner metadata and set assignment) and radiological_gradings.csv.
details.splits: 218 patients / 447 sagittal T1 and T2 MRI series total, with training and validation assignments provided in overview.csv; an additional hidden test set (not publicly released) is used for the accompanying SPIDER Grand Challenge.
details.extra: Annotations were created/corrected in 3D Slicer (v5.0.3). Beyond the voxel segmentations, the dataset uniquely ships per-disc-level radiological degeneration gradings as a separate CSV, enabling both segmentation and classification/grading tasks.

name: RSNA 2024 Lumbar Spine Degenerative Classification
full_name: RSNA 2024 Lumbar Spine Degenerative Classification
protocol_note: Sagittal T1, sagittal T2/STIR, and axial T2 lumbar MRI series per study
size: ~1975 lumbar spine MRI studies
segmentation_detail: Coordinate (point) labels at disc levels rather than pixel masks
