protocol_note: Chest CT of COVID-19 suspects, France, March-April 2020; contrast/phase not specified on the page.
size: 2,000 public training CT scans (from a 10,735-patient cohort)
description: A French chest CT dataset from the first 2020 pandemic wave releasing 2,000 public training scans with COVID-19 severity and RT-PCR positivity labels for classification and prognosis.

label_schema: Binary classification - COVID-19 positive (RT-PCR confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection)
Binary classification - Severe COVID-19 (intubation or death within one month of CT acquisition)
Per-patient metadata - Age (binned to nearest 5 years) and Sex
severe-COVID outcome (intubation or death within one month)
details.file_structure: Chest CT volumes stored one file per patient as compressed .mha files (SimpleITK/MetaImage) under a data/mha folder, with labels in a metadata/reference.csv keyed by PatientID and columns probCOVID and probSevere (0/1); no voxel-level segmentation masks are provided.
details.splits: Public training sample: 2,000 scans; hidden test set: 1,000 scans (full cohort 10,735 individuals; final-round training allowed on the full set minus the 1,000 test scans).
details.extra: Image-level classification only (no segmentation/detection). Data collected from suspected SARS-CoV-2 patients in France, March-April 2020; public training data released under CC BY-NC 4.0.

name: COVID-CTset
full_name: COVID-CTset
protocol_note: Lung HRCT acquired on Siemens SOMATOM Scope (syngo CT VC30-easyIQ); 16-bit DICOM 512x512 converted to 16-bit TIFF; three reconstructions of different slice thickness per patient (SR_2, SR_3, SR_4).
size: 63,849 images, 377 patients (95 COVID, 282 normal)
description: An open Iranian chest CT dataset from Negin Medical Center (Sari) with 63,849 16-bit TIFF lung CT slices from 377 patients labeled COVID-19 or normal for classification.

details.file_structure: Per-patient folders each containing three subdirectories (SR_2, SR_3, SR_4) of 16-bit uint grayscale TIFF slices at 512x512; image-level class labels are provided via CSV files in the CSV folder (one set per fold), with Patient_details.csv holding scan-thickness metadata.
details.splits: Image-level binary classification (2 classes): COVID-19 = 15,589 images from 95 patients; Normal = 48,260 images from 282 patients; total 63,849 images from 377 patients. No bounding boxes or segmentation masks.
details.extra: Official evaluation uses a 5-fold, patient-stratified train/test split defined by the provided CSV files (patients do not overlap between train and test).

name: COVID-CT-MD
full_name: COVID-CT-MD
protocol_note: Volumetric chest CT scans in DICOM; contrast/dose not stated in evidence
size: 305 patients (169 COVID-19, 60 CAP, 76 normal); labeled subset of 54 COVID and 25 CAP cases with 4,957 infection-positive and 18,392 infection-negative slices
segmentation_detail: No pixel-level masks; instead provides slice-level binary infection labels (per-slice numpy arrays) and lobe-level 3D binary labels mapping infection to the five lung lobes
description: An Iranian volumetric chest CT dataset in DICOM (Babak Imaging Center, Tehran) of 305 patients spanning COVID-19, community-acquired pneumonia, and normal cases, with patient-, slice-, and lobe-level infection annotations.

label_schema: Diagnostic class (patient-level): COVID-19 (169 patients), CAP / Community Acquired Pneumonia (60 patients), Normal (76 patients)
Slice-level infection label (binary): 1 = infection present in slice, 0 = no infection (subset labeled: 4,957 infected slices, 18,392 non-infected slices)
Lobe-level infection label (binary) mapping infection to 5 lung lobes: index 0 = Left Lower Lobe, 1 = Left Upper Lobe, 2 = Right Lower Lobe, 3 = Right Middle Lobe, 4 = Right Upper Lobe
details.file_structure: DICOM slices organized in a hierarchy with top-level folders for COVID-19, CAP, and Normal, each containing per-subject folders of individual DICOM images (slices must be sorted by the Slice Location tag 0020,1041); annotations are supplied separately as NumPy arrays (Slice-level-labels.npy is a 2D array [case, slice]; Lobe-level-labels.npy is a 3D array [case, slice, lobe]) plus an Index.csv listing which patients have annotations.
details.extra: No pixel-level segmentation masks are provided; only slice-level and lobe-level binary infection labels exist, and only a subset of cases (identified in Index.csv) is annotated. Updated label versions were released in September 2021 for two refined cases.

name: ImageCHD
full_name: ImageCHD: A 3D Computed Tomography Image Dataset for Classification of Congenital Heart Disease
protocol_note: 3D cardiac CT images; the README does not state contrast phase or scanner details (the MICCAI paper describes CT angiography).
size: 110 3D CT images
segmentation_detail: Voxel-level segmentation of seven cardiac substructures: left ventricle, right ventricle, left atrium, right atrium, myocardium, aorta, and pulmonary artery
description: A 3D cardiac CT dataset of 110 congenital heart disease cases with seven-substructure segmentations and CHD-type diagnostic labels, openly available on Kaggle.

label_schema: Voxel-level segmentation masks of seven cardiac substructures, encoded as integer values:
Additional non-cardiac labels (e.g. Label 14 = airway) may appear and are to be disregarded
Each case also carries a case-level congenital-heart-disease (CHD) diagnosis label provided in an accompanying spreadsheet (covers most CHD types; individual type list not enumerated in the source)
congenital heart disease type / diagnosis (provided in accompanying XLSX)
details.file_structure: 110 3D cardiac CT volumes, each paired with a voxel-wise multi-label segmentation mask (image + label volumes per patient), plus an .xlsx file giving per-case CHD diagnosis details.
details.extra: Published at MICCAI 2020 (ImageCHD); dataset covers most types of congenital heart disease and is also mirrored on Kaggle. File-format specifics (e.g. NIfTI vs. other) were not explicitly confirmed in the fetched README.

name: ATM'22
full_name: ATM'22: Airway Tree Modeling Challenge
protocol_note: 500 chest CT scans collected from multiple sites (multi-domain, incl. COVID-19 CTs per cited work); contrast/dose not specified.
size: 500 chest CT scans
segmentation_detail: Binary airway tree segmentation masks carefully annotated by three radiologists with 5+ years of experience, emphasizing topological completeness
description: A MICCAI 2022 challenge providing 500 multi-site chest CT scans in NIfTI with expert-annotated pulmonary airway tree segmentations, accessible after signing a data usage agreement.

details.file_structure: Each case is a thoracic CT volume in NIfTI (.nii.gz) with a paired binary airway segmentation mask of identical origin and spacing (voxel value 1 = airway, 0 = background); predictions/labels are single-file per case.
details.splits: 300 training, 50 validation, 150 test (500 CT scans total); the 150 test cases are hidden.
details.extra: Annotations were carefully labeled by radiologists (5+ years experience) across the full airway hierarchy (trachea, main/lobar/segmental bronchi) with emphasis on topological completeness; evaluation post-processing keeps only the largest connected component of the binary result.

name: KiPA22
full_name: KiPA22: Kidney PArsing Challenge 2022
anatomy: Kidney, renal tumor, renal artery, renal vein
protocol_note: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) of kidneys; dual-source CTA per cited papers
size: 130 CTA cases (100 available: 70 training + 30 open test)
segmentation_detail: Voxel-wise masks for four structures: kidney, renal tumor, renal artery, and renal vein
description: A kidney CT angiography (CTA) challenge of 130 cases (100 openly released) with NIfTI segmentation labels for kidney, tumor, renal artery, and renal vein parsing.

details.file_structure: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT volumes and their voxel-wise segmentation masks are stored as paired compressed NIfTI (.nii.gz) files, one image and one label per case, organized into training and open-testing folders.
details.splits: 70 training cases, 30 open-testing cases, and 30 closed-testing cases (closed-test labels withheld for final evaluation)
details.extra: Single multi-class label file per case with integer values 1-4; the four target structures pose distinct difficulties (thin renal arteries ~0.27% of volume, low-contrast renal veins, and tumors with five subtypes).

name: SegTHOR
full_name: SegTHOR: Segmentation of Thoracic Organs at Risk in CT
protocol_note: Thoracic CT scans of patients for radiotherapy planning; contrast phase not stated in the entry.
size: 60 CT scans (40 train / 20 test)
segmentation_detail: Four thoracic organs at risk: heart, aorta, trachea, esophagus
description: SegTHOR challenge (ISBI 2019, University of Rouen) providing 60 thoracic CT scans with heart, aorta, trachea, and esophagus contours for radiotherapy planning.

details.file_structure: Each patient is a folder (train) or file (test) of a single-channel 3D thoracic CT in NIfTI format; images are named Patient_XX.nii.gz and the corresponding voxelwise multi-label ground-truth mask (integer values 0-4) is a separate file named GT.nii.gz inside each training patient folder.
details.splits: 60 3D CT scans total: 40 training patients (with GT masks) and 20 test patients (masks withheld for the challenge).
details.extra: Manually contoured by an experienced radiotherapist for radiotherapy planning; the four organs at risk are mutually exclusive classes in a single label volume, with the esophagus being the hardest/smallest to delineate. Class distribution is highly imbalanced (~99% background).

name: FUMPE
full_name: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad's Pulmonary Embolism dataset
protocol_note: CT pulmonary angiography (single phase)
size: 35 CT pulmonary angiography scans (35 subjects)
segmentation_detail: Voxel-level pulmonary embolism ground-truth masks annotated by two radiologist experts with semi-automated software assistance; masks provided as MATLAB (.mat) files
description: An open Iranian (Ferdowsi University of Mashhad) CT pulmonary angiography dataset of 35 subjects with radiologist-annotated voxel-level pulmonary embolism segmentation masks for PE detection and segmentation research.

label_schema: Voxel value 1 - pulmonary embolism (PE) region / clot (foreground)
details.file_structure: 35 chest CT-angiography (CTA) volumes organized as per-patient DICOM folders (Patient01–Patient35, 8,792 slices total), each paired with a binary 3D ground-truth mask stored as a MATLAB .mat file where PE voxels = 1 and background = 0.
details.extra: Annotations were manually delineated by one board-certified radiologist (5+ yrs PE-CTA experience) using the semi-automated MIS (Medical Image Segmenter) tool (thresholding + connected-component region growing from user seed points) and then reviewed/approved by the radiology department head (18 yrs experience); 3,438 PE regions labeled, ~67% in peripheral pulmonary arteries.
details.label_readers: Two radiologist experts: one delineated with the semi-automated MIS tool, the department head reviewed/approved
details.third_party_note: Figshare items are CC BY 4.0; CC BY 4.0 permits redistribution and adaptation with attribution; no clause restricting external services.

name: Brain Tumor Dataset (figshare)
full_name: Brain Tumor Dataset (Cheng et al., Nanfang Hospital & Tianjin Medical University)
protocol_note: 3064 T1-weighted contrast-enhanced images (2D slices); acquisition protocol described in README 2024
size: 3,064 T1-CE MRI slices from 233 patients
segmentation_detail: Manual tumor boundary masks and border coordinates provided per slice in each .mat file
description: A widely-used Chinese brain MRI dataset (Nanfang Hospital Guangzhou and Tianjin Medical University) of 3,064 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted slices from 233 patients, each labeled with tumor type and accompanied by a manual tumor boundary mask, distributed as MATLAB .mat files under CC BY 4.0.

label_schema: cjdata.label - tumor class: 1 = meningioma, 2 = glioma, 3 = pituitary tumor
cjdata.tumorMask - binary image (1s = tumor region, 0s = background)
cjdata.tumorBorder - vector of tumor-border point coordinates [x1,y1,x2,y2,...] from manual delineation, used to generate the mask
cjdata.image - the T1-weighted contrast-enhanced image data
tumor type (3 classes: meningioma, glioma, pituitary)
details.file_structure: Each image slice is stored as an individual MATLAB .mat file holding one struct named cjdata (with fields label, PID, image, tumorBorder, tumorMask); the 3064 files are split across 4 .zip archives of 766 slices each (ranges 1-766, 767-1532, 1533-2298, 2299-3064), plus cvind.mat holding cross-validation fold indices.
details.splits: No official train/val/test split; instead 5-fold cross-validation fold indices are provided in cvind.mat.
details.extra: 3064 T1-weighted contrast-enhanced MRI slices from 233 patients: meningioma (708 slices), glioma (1426), pituitary tumor (930); introduced in Cheng et al., PLoS ONE 2015.

name: MS-CMRSeg 2019
full_name: MS-CMRSeg 2019: Multi-sequence Cardiac MRI Segmentation Challenge
anatomy: Myocardium, left ventricle and right ventricle
protocol_note: Three CMR sequences per patient: late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), T2-weighted, and balanced-SSFP (bSSFP) cine
size: 45 cardiomyopathy patients (3 sequences each: LGE, T2, bSSFP)
segmentation_detail: Gold-standard manual contours of left ventricle blood pool, right ventricle blood pool, and left ventricular myocardium (LGE includes myocardial scar/edema regions)
description: A multi-sequence cardiac MRI dataset from Fudan University's ZMIC Lab comprising 45 cardiomyopathy patients with paired LGE, T2-weighted and bSSFP cine images plus ventricle and myocardium segmentations, distributed under a signed participant data-use agreement.

label_schema: Label 500 - left ventricle blood pool / LV cavity
Label 600 - right ventricle blood pool / RV cavity
details.file_structure: Per-subject 3D volumes in NIfTI (.nii.gz); each of 45 cardiomyopathy patients has three separate CMR sequences (LGE, T2-weighted, and bSSFP/C0 cine) as image files, with gold-standard manual contours stored as matching .nii.gz label maps in which the three structures are encoded by voxel intensity values 200/500/600 (0 = background).
details.splits: 45 patients total. For the LGE segmentation target: 5 labeled training cases (patients 1-5) and 40 test cases (patients 6-45, LGE images only in the original release). Auxiliary sequences: bSSFP and T2 manual labels provided for patients 1-35, images only for patients 36-45.
details.extra: The three sequences come from the same 45 patients but are separate (not spatially co-registered) acquisitions; LGE is the primary segmentation target, and gold-standard LGE contours have since been publicly released. Downstream works commonly remap the 200/500/600 values to 1/2/3 (or with background to 0-3).

name: TB Portals
full_name: NIAID TB Portals Program
protocol_note: Chest X-ray (frontal view) and chest CT of varying resolution; X-rays also as 512x512 JPEG when DICOM absent
size: 27,294 chest X-ray and CT imaging studies; 24,752 TB cases; 16 countries, 40 sites
paired_text_detail: Each case is linked to clinical records, drug-resistance profiles, and pathogen genomic sequences
description: An NIH/NIAID multi-national tuberculosis imaging repository of over 27,000 chest X-ray and CT studies from under-represented high-burden regions, linked to clinical, drug-resistance, and pathogen genomic data.

label_schema: Case-level TB diagnosis: pulmonary vs extrapulmonary vs combined tuberculosis (plus drug-resistance category, e.g. sensitive / MDR / XDR, from linked clinical record)
Radiologist image reading is a structured set of per-study findings (not pixel segmentation), including: presence/absence of pleural involvement (effusion)
Cavity size category: no cavities / <10 mm / 10-25 mm / >25 mm
Localization and size of pulmonary pathology (affected lung zones/regions)
Presence of inherited malformations and acquired complications
Physiological respiratory status and degree of contrast accumulation
Additional structured reading fields such as nodules, infiltrates, and overall affected-lung extent recorded per imaging study
details.file_structure: Images are stored per patient case as DICOM (chest X-ray in frontal view; CT of varying resolution), with X-rays also available as 512x512 JPEG when DICOM is absent; radiologist findings are stored as a structured reading/annotation record (tabular fields) attached to each image and linked to the clinical case record — there is no pixel-level segmentation mask (segmentation n/a).
details.extra: Not a fixed ML benchmark: TB Portals is a growing federated data-sharing platform (tens of thousands of images) where imaging is one facet joined to clinical, laboratory, and genomic data; full data access requires a data-use agreement/registration, and image annotation completeness varies by case.

name: MedSeg COVID-19 CT Segmentation
full_name: COVID-19 CT Segmentation Dataset (MedSeg)
protocol_note: Chest CT of COVID-19 patients; Dataset 1 = 100 axial slices assembled from SIRM JPG images, Dataset 2 = 9 volumetric CTs from Radiopaedia (~829 slices). Contrast phase not stated.
size: 100 axial CT slices (~40 patients) plus 9 CT volumes (~829 slices)
segmentation_detail: Expert voxel masks for ground-glass opacity, consolidation, pleural effusion and lungs
description: A free open COVID-19 CT segmentation dataset providing NIfTI images with expert infection and lung masks on 100 axial slices and 9 volumes derived from Italian (Radiopaedia/SIRM) COVID cases.

label_schema: Dataset 2 lung masks (separate files): left lung / right lung
Dataset 2 infection masks: COVID-19 infection (foreground vs background)
details.file_structure: NIfTI (.nii.gz) volumes: Dataset 1 stacks 100 axial slices into single files tr_im.nii.gz (images) + tr_mask.nii.gz (multi-class infection masks), plus an unlabeled test file val_im.nii.gz; Dataset 2 provides 9 per-patient volumetric CTs in rp_im/ with matching rp_msk/ (infection) and rp_lung_msk/ (lung) mask folders.
details.extra: Dataset 1 = 100 axial CT slices from >40 COVID-19 patients (assembled from the Italian Society of Medical and Interventional Radiology JPGs), radiologist-segmented; Dataset 2 = 9 volumetric CTs from Radiopaedia (~829 slices, 373 evaluated positive and segmented). GGO and consolidation are the classes most commonly used downstream (e.g. Inf-Net); pleural effusion voxels are rare. Distributed via figshare (MedSeg / medicalsegmentation.com), CC BY-NC-SA.

related.name: Radiopaedia
related.note: 9 volumetric COVID-19 CT cases taken from Radiopaedia, converted to NIfTI with infection and lung masks added

related.name: Italian Society of Medical and Interventional Radiology (SIRM) COVID-19 database
related.note: 100 axial CT slices from >40 patients assembled from SIRM JPG images into NIfTI with radiologist GGO/consolidation/effusion masks

name: CT Kidney Dataset: Normal-Cyst-Tumor-Stone
protocol_note: Coronal and axial whole-abdomen and urogram CT slices, contrast and non-contrast, exported from hospital PACS (Dhaka, Bangladesh) and converted from DICOM to lossless JPG.
size: 12,446 CT images (Normal 5,077; Cyst 3,709; Tumor 2,283; Stone 1,377)
description: A kidney CT classification dataset of 12,446 JPG images collected from Dhaka, Bangladesh hospital PACS, labeled as normal, cyst, tumor, or stone.

label_schema: Image-level classification (single label per image), 4 classes
details.file_structure: Whole-slice CT images (coronal and axial cuts, contrast and non-contrast whole-abdomen/urogram studies) exported from hospital PACS, converted from DICOM to lossless JPG, and organized into four folders named after the class (Cyst/Normal/Stone/Tumor) with the folder name serving as the label; no segmentation masks or bounding boxes are provided.
details.extra: Collected from PACS at a hospital in Dhaka, Bangladesh; each label was reconfirmed by a radiologist and a medical technologist. The source Scientific Reports paper (s41598-022-15634-4) used an ad-hoc 80/20 train/test split and a balanced 1,300-per-class subset, but no official split files ship with the dataset.

name: CT-ICH (PhysioNet)
full_name: Computed Tomography Images for Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection and Segmentation
protocol_note: Non-contrast head CT, ~30 slices per scan, 5 mm slice thickness; annotated on brain (WL 40/WW 120) and bone (WL 700/WW 3200) windows; Siemens syngo used for reading
size: 82 non-contrast head CT scans (75 public in NIfTI); 36 with hemorrhage
segmentation_detail: Slice-level intracranial hemorrhage regions delineated by two radiologists, provided as per-patient NIfTI masks
description: A non-contrast head CT dataset of 82 scans from Al Hilla Teaching Hospital, Iraq, with radiologist-delineated intracranial hemorrhage masks, hemorrhage subtype labels, and skull-fracture annotations.

label_schema: Segmentation masks (NIfTI): binary per-slice masks delineating intracranial hemorrhage region (value 1 = hemorrhage, 0 = background)
Per-slice classification labels (in hemorrhage_diagnosis_raw_ct.csv) covering 5 hemorrhage subtypes: Intraventricular (IVH), Intraparenchymal (IPH), Subarachnoid (SAH), Epidural (EDH), Subdural (SDH)
Additional per-slice binary flags: Fracture_Yes_No (skull fracture present) and No_Hemorrhage
Patient-level diagnostic and demographic labels (in patient_demographics.csv)
hemorrhage subtype (IVH, IPH, SAH, EDH, SDH)
details.file_structure: CT scans and corresponding hemorrhage segmentation masks are stored as per-subject 3D NIfTI (.nii) volumes (images in a scans/CT folder, masks in a separate masks folder), with slice-level diagnosis labels and patient demographics/diagnoses provided as CSV files (hemorrhage_diagnosis_raw_ct.csv and patient_demographics.csv); segmentation was delineated by two radiologists.
details.extra: 82 patients collected; ~75 subjects have complete NIfTI image/mask data (roughly 30 slices per scan). No official train/val/test split is provided.

name: StructSeg 2019
full_name: StructSeg 2019: Automatic Structure Segmentation for Radiotherapy Planning
anatomy: Head-and-neck and thoracic organs at risk and gross tumor volumes
protocol_note: Radiotherapy planning CT scans from Zhejiang Cancer Hospital; contrast/phase not stated.
size: Four tasks; 50 training CT scans (+10 test) each for head-neck and chest cohorts
segmentation_detail: 22 head-neck OARs, 6 thoracic OARs, plus nasopharynx and lung gross tumor volumes
description: A MICCAI 2019 Grand Challenge from Zhejiang Cancer Hospital providing head-neck and thoracic CT scans with organ-at-risk and gross-tumor-volume contours for radiotherapy planning.

label_schema: === Task 1: Head & Neck OAR (22 classes, integer label values 1-22 in annotation order) ===
=== Task 3: Thoracic/Lung OAR (6 classes, integer label values 1-6) ===
=== Task 2: Nasopharynx GTV (binary) - Label 1 = gross tumor volume ===
=== Task 4: Lung GTV (binary) - Label 1 = gross tumor volume ===
Note: numbers cited on the official page next to each OAR (e.g. eye 100, lens 50) are per-organ importance/scoring weights, NOT label index values.
details.file_structure: Distributed as one folder per patient, each containing a CT volume and a co-registered voxel-wise segmentation mask (integer label values) in NIfTI (.nii.gz) format; the four tasks (head-neck OAR, nasopharynx GTV, thoracic OAR, lung GTV) are provided as separate datasets.
details.splits: Each of the 4 tasks: 50 training patients + 10 test patients. Head&Neck OAR and Nasopharynx GTV use 60 nasopharynx-cancer CT scans (50 train/10 test); Thoracic OAR and Lung GTV use 60 lung-cancer CT scans (50 train/10 test).
details.extra: Each scan was delineated by one experienced oncologist and verified/refined by another. Task 1 (22 head-neck OARs) and Task 3 (6 thoracic OARs) are the widely reused subsets.

name: GRAZPEDWRI-DX
full_name: Graz Pediatric Wrist Digital X-ray
anatomy: Wrist and distal forearm (distal radius/ulna) in pediatric trauma patients
protocol_note: Digital wrist radiographs (pediatric trauma), distributed as PNG
size: 20,327 radiographs from 6,091 pediatric patients (~16.3 GB)
description: A large open pediatric wrist trauma radiograph dataset with radiologist-provided bounding-box and tag annotations for automated fracture detection and classification.

label_schema: Object-detection dataset with 9 bounding-box classes (multi-label per image):
Bounding-box object annotations for 9 classes (bone anomaly, bone lesion, foreign body, fracture, metal, periosteal reaction, pronator sign, soft tissue, text)
Fracture presence and fracture classification tags
Additional image descriptor tags in dataset.csv
details.file_structure: Grayscale pediatric wrist radiographs stored as PNG images, each paired with a same-named YOLO-format .txt annotation file (one line per object: class_id x_center y_center width height, normalized 0-1); a dataset.csv holds per-image metadata plus a patient_id key, and images/labels are organized into images/ and labels/ folders.
details.extra: Contains 20,327 annotated radiographs from 6,091 pediatric patients (distal radius/ulna trauma); the original Figshare release is unsplit, though a widely used third-party 70/20/10 patient-wise train/val/test split (Ju et al., YOLOv8 fracture-detection work) is available separately.

name: Chest X-Ray Images (Pneumonia)
full_name: Labeled Optical Coherence Tomography and Chest X-Ray Images (pediatric chest X-ray subset)
protocol_note: Anterior-posterior pediatric chest radiographs (JPEG)
size: 5,856 chest radiographs
description: Pediatric chest radiographs from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center labeled normal versus bacterial/viral pneumonia (Kermany et al. 2018).

label_schema: Pneumonia subtype (bacterial vs viral) is NOT a separate folder label but is encoded in filenames (e.g. 'person1_bacteria_1.jpeg', 'person1_virus_6.jpeg'), enabling an optional 3-way distinction
Image-level labels: normal, bacterial pneumonia, viral pneumonia
details.file_structure: Anterior-posterior chest radiographs as JPEG files; the label is the parent directory name, organized as chest_xray/{train,test,val}/{NORMAL,PNEUMONIA}/*.jpeg (no CSV or separate annotation files, no bounding boxes or segmentation masks).
details.splits: Official 3-way split: train = 5,216 (NORMAL 1,341 + PNEUMONIA 3,875); test = 624 (NORMAL 234 + PNEUMONIA 390); val = 16 (NORMAL 8 + PNEUMONIA 8). Kaggle describes ~5,863 JPEG images total across the 2 categories.
details.extra: Source: Kermany et al., Cell 2018 ('Identifying Medical Diagnoses and Treatable Diseases by Image-Based Deep Learning'). Images are pediatric patients aged 1-5 from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center; diagnoses were quality-screened and graded by two expert physicians, with a third physician checking the evaluation set. Note the tiny (16-image) validation set is a widely-noted limitation.

name: HVSMR 2016
full_name: Whole-Heart and Great Vessel Segmentation from 3D Cardiovascular MRI in Congenital Heart Disease
protocol_note: 3D whole-heart cardiovascular MR (CMR) images; axial full-volume, cropped axial and cropped short-axis versions provided
size: 20 3D cardiovascular MR images (10 training + 10 test)
segmentation_detail: Manual segmentations of the blood pool and ventricular myocardium
description: 3D cardiovascular MRI from congenital heart disease patients with blood pool and myocardium segmentations for whole-heart and great-vessel segmentation, released as the MICCAI 2016 HVSMR challenge.

label_schema: Label 2 - blood pool (cardiac chambers and great vessels: atria, ventricles, aorta, pulmonary veins/arteries, vena cava)
details.file_structure: 3D cardiovascular MRI volumes and their voxel-wise ground-truth masks are stored as NIfTI (.nii.gz), with each image paired to a co-registered '-label' NIfTI mask, provided in three subsets per case: axial full-volume, cropped axial, and cropped short-axis views.
details.splits: 10 training scans (with manual ground-truth labels) and 10 test scans (labels withheld for challenge evaluation).
details.extra: From the MICCAI 2016 Workshop Challenge on Whole-Heart and Great Vessel Segmentation from 3D Cardiovascular MRI in Congenital Heart Disease; only the myocardium and blood pool are labeled (the later HVSMR-2.0 release expands to eight structures).

name: HVSMR-2.0
full_name: HVSMR-2.0: A 3D Cardiovascular MR Dataset for Whole-Heart Segmentation in Congenital Heart Disease
anatomy: Whole heart (four cardiac chambers) and four great vessels
protocol_note: 3D cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) scans, preoperative; sequence and field strength not stated on the figshare page
size: 60 cardiovascular MR scans
segmentation_detail: Manual segmentation masks of eight structures (four cardiac chambers and four great vessels), plus masks of required and optional extents of the great vessels; released as orig, cropped, and cropped-normalized variants
paired_text_detail: Per-subject clinical diagnoses and technical metadata provided in accompanying CSV files (not free-text reports)
description: Public 60-scan cardiovascular MRI dataset of congenital heart disease patients with manual whole-heart segmentations of four cardiac chambers and four great vessels.

details.file_structure: 60 cardiovascular MR cases in NIfTI (.nii.gz), each provided in three image variants (orig = cropped at chin/no normalization; cropped = cropped around heart; cropped_norm = cropped + intensity-normalized), with per-case image (pat#_[variant].nii.gz), voxelwise segmentation mask (pat#_[variant]_seg.nii.gz using the same 8-structure integer labels), and an endpoints file (pat#_[variant]_seg_endpoints.nii.gz) that delineates the optional great-vessel extents.
details.extra: No official mandated split; the paper documents two reusable partitions - the original HVSMR-2016 20-image train/test split and the Pace et al. 2022 4-fold cross-validation + testing split over all 60 cases. Each great vessel has a required minimum extent plus an optional extent (marked via the endpoints files) so evaluation can ignore clinically-variable vessel terminations; no separate myocardium label is included in HVSMR-2.0 (unlike the original HVSMR blood-pool/myocardium scheme).

related.name: HVSMR 2016
related.note: Extends the 20-image HVSMR 2016 set to 60 CMR scans with new 8-structure chamber/great-vessel labels

name: BONBID-HIE
full_name: Boston Neonatal Brain Injury Dataset for Hypoxic Ischemic Encephalopathy
protocol_note: Diffusion-derived ADC maps and Z-score normalized ADC maps
size: 133 neonates
segmentation_detail: Expert manual lesion masks; many lesions occupy under 1% of brain volume
description: Neonatal brain diffusion MRI (ADC and Z-score ADC maps) from term neonates with hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy paired with expert manual lesion segmentations for a lesion-segmentation challenge.

label_schema: Binary HIE lesion segmentation mask (single foreground class)
details.file_structure: Per case there are three 3D volumes in .mha (MetaImage) format read/written with SimpleITK: a skull-stripped ADC map (ADC_ss), a Z-score-normalized ADC map (Z_ADC), and the manual binary lesion mask (LABEL), organized into separate per-modality folders inside the training archive (BONBID2023_Train.tar.gz).
details.splits: Challenge split: 85 train / 4 validation / 44 test (test set hidden), 133 total; the public Zenodo release provides the training data.
details.extra: Lesions are diffuse/multi-focal and very small - over half of patients have lesions occupying <1% of brain volume - making this a highly class-imbalanced segmentation task; label values 0/1 are inferred from the official challenge algorithm docker (BinaryThreshold insideValue=1) rather than an explicit codebook.

name: Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP)
full_name: Developing Human Connectome Project
protocol_note: T1w, T2w, diffusion MRI (DTI), and resting-state fMRI; native and processed, BIDS-organized
size: ~783 neonates (886 datasets) and ~273 fetuses (4th release)
segmentation_detail: Tissue segmentations and cortical/subcortical parcellations provided from the dHCP structural pipeline
description: Multimodal neonatal and fetal brain MRI (structural, diffusion, and functional) with tissue segmentations and parcellations from the Developing Human Connectome Project.

label_schema: dHCP anatomical pipeline (Draw-EM) provides TWO volumetric label maps per session:
=== 87-region parcellation (desc-drawem87_dseg.nii.gz), based on the ALBERTs neonatal atlas; examples of the 87 integer labels ===
Label 1 - Hippocampus left; Label 2 - Hippocampus right; Label 3 - Amygdala left; Label 4 - Amygdala right
Labels 5-16 & 20-39 - bilateral cortical GM regions (e.g. anterior temporal lobe, superior temporal gyrus, insula, occipital/frontal/parietal lobes, cingulate gyrus)
Labels 40-50 - subcortical/deep GM (caudate, thalamus, subthalamic nucleus, lentiform nucleus, corpus callosum, lateral ventricles L/R)
Labels 51-82 - bilateral cortical WM regions (mirroring the GM parcels)
Label 83 - CSF; Label 84 - Extra-cranial background; Label 85 - Intra-cranial background; Labels 86-87 - Thalamus low-intensity part L/R
Also provided: cortical ribbon segmentation (desc-ribbon_dseg.nii.gz) and per-vertex surface metrics (thickness, curvature, sulcal depth, myelin/T1-T2 ratio)
NOTE: newer pipeline versions optionally support the M-CRIB 2.0 protocol (94 labels), but the public release uses the 87-label Draw-EM/ALBERTs scheme
details.file_structure: BIDS-organized release (BIDS v1.5.0-dev); processed anatomical outputs under derivatives/dhcp_anat_pipeline/sub-{subid}/ses-{sesid}/anat/, with volumetric segmentations/parcellations as gzip NIfTI (e.g. sub-*_desc-drawem9_dseg.nii.gz, sub-*_desc-drawem87_dseg.nii.gz, desc-ribbon_dseg.nii.gz) and cortical surfaces/metrics as GIFTI (.surf.gii, .shape.gii, .label.gii); integer->name lookup tables ship with the dhcp-structural-pipeline / DrawEM repo (label_names/ALBERT/*.csv).
details.extra: Fourth data release (May 2024) contains 783 neonatal subjects / 886 sessions plus 273 fetal subjects / 297 sessions; every subject is fully processed rather than partitioned, so there is no official train/val/test split (users define their own). Access requires accepting a data-use agreement.

name: Healthy Brain Network (HBN)
full_name: Child Mind Institute Healthy Brain Network
protocol_note: T1w, T2w, diffusion MRI (DWI), and multiple resting-state and task fMRI runs, organized in BIDS
size: 5,000+ target subjects; thousands of MRI datasets released (8,000+ total participants enrolled)
host: Child Mind Institute / NITRC (INDI) / AWS Open Data
description: A large multimodal pediatric and adolescent brain MRI dataset (T1w, T2w, diffusion, and fMRI) with deep clinical and behavioral phenotyping across ages 5-21, released by the Child Mind Institute for developmental and psychiatric neuroscience research.

label_schema: No image-level annotations/segmentations — labels are per-subject phenotypic/clinical variables, not voxel or pixel labels

Consensus clinician DSM-5 diagnoses per participant (categorical; multiple comorbid diagnoses allowed) — a transdiagnostic community-referred sample, so common labels include ADHD, anxiety disorders, autism spectrum disorder, and 'No Diagnosis Given'
Diagnoses derived from a semi-structured clinical interview (KSADS-COMP) plus clinician review
Dimensional cognitive/IQ and academic scores (e.g. Wechsler WISC/WAIS, WIAT)
Parent- and self-report psychiatric symptom scales (e.g. CBCL, SCARED, SDQ, SRS/ASSQ) as continuous scores
details.file_structure: Neuroimaging released in BIDS format as NIfTI files (T1w, T2w, diffusion, resting-state and movie/task fMRI) with accompanying EEG (BIDS/EDF-style) and eye-tracking; phenotypic labels and diagnoses are distributed separately as de-identified tabular/CSV files (one row per participant, keyed by subject ID via the LORIS/COINS release), not embedded with the images.
details.extra: HBN is fundamentally a psychiatric/behavioral phenotyping resource (targeting ~10,000 NYC-area youth), not a labeled radiology segmentation/detection dataset; MRI acquisition ended April 2023 and data are released in periodic waves, so exact per-diagnosis counts depend on the release version.

name: ADHD-200
full_name: ADHD-200 Sample
protocol_note: Resting-state fMRI (BOLD) plus anatomical T1-weighted MRI
size: 973 subjects (8 sites)
description: Openly shared resting-state fMRI and structural T1-weighted MRI from 973 children and adolescents with and without ADHD across eight international sites, with accompanying phenotypic and diagnostic labels.

label_schema: Subject-level phenotypic labels (no image segmentation masks). Primary label is diagnosis (DX): DX 0 - Typically Developing Control (TDC)
Dimensional ADHD symptom measures (target for regression): ADHD Index, Inattentive score, Hyperactive/Impulsive score (from ADHD rating scales, which vary by site)
Demographic/covariate labels: age (7-21 yrs), gender/sex, handedness, medication (lifetime) status
IQ measures: Verbal IQ, Performance IQ, Full-scale IQ (instrument varies by site)
Per-scan QC label: usable vs. questionable (from visual quality assessment)
Site of acquisition (1 of 8 contributing imaging sites)
ADHD diagnostic labels and phenotypic data (age, sex, handedness, IQ, medication status, ADHD subtype)
details.file_structure: Per-subject T1 anatomical and resting-state fMRI images in NIfTI format, distributed as per-site tarballs via NITRC-R and via NITRC-IR (XNAT); subject-level labels/covariates are held in a phenotypic CSV table keyed by subject ID and site (raw DICOM/NIfTI originally, with separately released preprocessed derivatives from the Neuro Bureau/Athena, Burner and NIAK pipelines).
details.splits: Official ADHD-200 Global Competition split: 776 training datasets with diagnostic labels (491 TDC, 285 ADHD), released 2011-03-01; 197 held-out test scans released 2011-07-01 initially without diagnostic labels (labels later published). Contributed by 8 sites: Brown/Bradley, Kennedy Krieger Institute, NYU Langone, NeuroImage (Netherlands), Peking University, Univ. of Pittsburgh, OHSU, and Washington University-St. Louis.
details.extra: This is a phenotypic classification/regression dataset (predict ADHD diagnosis/subtype and symptom scores from resting-state fMRI + structural MRI), not a segmentation dataset; ADHD-Hyperactive/Impulsive cases are very rare, so many published analyses collapse labels to a binary TDC vs. ADHD problem.

name: M-CRIB
full_name: Melbourne Children's Regional Infant Brain atlas
protocol_note: T1-weighted and T2-weighted templates
size: 10 neonates (individual images plus group T1/T2 templates)
segmentation_detail: Desikan-Killiany (M-CRIB) and Desikan-Killiany-Tourville (M-CRIB 2.0) cortical parcellations plus subcortical segmentations, with FreeSurfer and ITK label lookup tables; includes hard segmentations and per-structure probability maps
license: Free for research use with required citation of the associated publication
description: Neonatal brain MRI atlas with FreeSurfer- and ITK-compatible cortical parcellations and subcortical segmentations, distributed as T1/T2-weighted NIfTI templates and individual subject images.

label_schema: Whole-brain neonatal parcellation label set delivered as a FreeSurfer-style integer lookup table (M-CRIB_labels_FreeSurfer_format.txt) and an ITK-format table (M-CRIB_labels_ITK_format.txt), each row = index, name, R, G, B, A. ~101 labeled structures total.

Cortical parcellation (M-CRIB, Desikan-Killiany-compatible): 34 regions per hemisphere. Left hemisphere indices 1000-1035 as 'ctx-lh-<region>', right hemisphere 2000-2035 as 'ctx-rh-<region>'. Examples: 1001 ctx-lh-bankssts, 1005 ctx-lh-cuneus, 1006 ctx-lh-entorhinal, 1024 ctx-lh-precentral, 1030 ctx-lh-superiortemporal, 1035 ctx-lh-insula (and 2001..2035 mirror for right).

Subcortical / non-cortical structures (FreeSurfer indices): 0 Unknown, 2 Left-Cerebral-White-Matter, 4 Left-Lateral-Ventricle, 9 Left-Thalamus, 11 Left-Caudate, 12 Left-Putamen, 13 Left-Pallidum, 14 3rd-Ventricle, 15 4th-Ventricle, 17 Left-Hippocampus, 18 Left-Amygdala, 24 CSF, 26 Left-Accumbens-area, and right-side counterparts 41/43/48/50/51/52/53/54/58.

Additional structures: 75 Cerebellar_vermis_superior_posterior, 76 Cerebellar_vermis_anterior, 90 Cerebellar_vermis_inferior_posterior, 91 LH_Cerebellar_hemisphere, 93 RH_Cerebellar_hemisphere, 89 RH_subcortical_matter, 92 LH_subcortical_matter, 170 brainstem, 192 Corpus_Callosum.
M-CRIB 2.0 variant relabels the cortex to a Desikan-Killiany-Tourville (DKT)-compatible scheme (individual data on OSF).
details.file_structure: Group-template atlas in NIfTI: T1- and T2-weighted templates (t1_M-CRIB_template.nii.gz, t2_M-CRIB_template.nii.gz) at repo root, a hard_segmentations/ folder holding integer-labeled volumes thresholded in 0.1 probability increments (0.1 = effectively unthresholded through 0.9), a structure_probability_maps/ folder with per-structure probability volumes, and two plain-text label lookup tables (FreeSurfer and ITK formats).
details.extra: Atlas derived from 10 M-CRIB neonatal participants; individual (per-subject) T1/T2/parcellation images are hosted on OSF (M-CRIB: osf.io/2yx8u, M-CRIB 2.0: osf.io/4vthr) and recommended over the group templates for more accurate labeling. Cite Alexander et al., NeuroImage 2017.

name: Neonatal Brain Atlases (ALBERTs / Gousias)
full_name: ALBERTs: Neonatal Brain Atlases (Gousias et al.)
protocol_note: T1-weighted and T2-weighted neonatal MRI
size: 20 neonates, 50 labeled regions each (with corresponding T1/T2 MRI scans)
segmentation_detail: Manual delineation of 50 cortical and subcortical anatomical regions per subject
license: Free Academic End User Licence Agreement (non-commercial research/teaching only)
host: brain-development.org (Biomedical Image Analysis Group, Imperial College London)
description: Twenty manually labeled neonatal brain MRI atlases (T1/T2) with 50 anatomical regions each for atlas-based segmentation and parcellation of the newborn brain.

label_schema: Label 5 - Anterior temporal lobe, medial part left
Label 6 - Anterior temporal lobe, medial part right
Label 7 - Anterior temporal lobe, lateral part left
Label 8 - Anterior temporal lobe, lateral part right
Label 9 - Gyri parahippocampalis et ambiens anterior part left
Label 10 - Gyri parahippocampalis et ambiens anterior part right
Label 11 - Superior temporal gyrus, middle part left
Label 12 - Superior temporal gyrus, middle part right
Label 13 - Medial and inferior temporal gyri anterior part left
Label 14 - Medial and inferior temporal gyri anterior part right
Label 15 - Lateral occipitotemporal gyrus (gyrus fusiformis) anterior part left
Label 16 - Lateral occipitotemporal gyrus (gyrus fusiformis) anterior part right
Label 24 - Gyri parahippocampalis et ambiens posterior part right
Label 25 - Gyri parahippocampalis et ambiens posterior part left
Label 26 - Lateral occipitotemporal gyrus (gyrus fusiformis) posterior part right
Label 27 - Lateral occipitotemporal gyrus (gyrus fusiformis) posterior part left
Label 28 - Medial and inferior temporal gyri posterior part right
Label 29 - Medial and inferior temporal gyri posterior part left
Label 30 - Superior temporal gyrus, posterior part right
Label 31 - Superior temporal gyrus, posterior part left
Label 32 - Cingulate gyrus, anterior part right
Label 33 - Cingulate gyrus, anterior part left
Label 34 - Cingulate gyrus, posterior part right
Label 35 - Cingulate gyrus, posterior part left
details.file_structure: Distributed (after registration) as 3D NIfTI volumes: for each of the 20 neonatal subjects a T1 and T2 MRI plus a manually-drawn label volume where each voxel holds an integer 1-50 encoding the anatomical region.
details.extra: The atlas covers 20 term-born and preterm neonates (Gousias et al., NeuroImage 2012 & PLoS ONE 2013); the same 50-region protocol is extended in derived software (e.g. DrawEM) to an 87-label version that additionally splits cortical regions into GM/WM and adds CSF/background/thalamus subparts.

name: CRL Fetal Brain Atlas
full_name: A Normative Spatiotemporal MRI Atlas of the Fetal Brain (Gholipour et al. 2017)
anatomy: Fetal brain (gestational weeks 21-38; source scans 19-39 GA weeks)
protocol_note: Spatiotemporal T2 intensity templates (one per gestational week, 21-38) built from in-utero MRI of 81 normal fetuses scanned at 19-39 weeks GA; a separate fetal DTI atlas (FA, color-FA, MD maps, GA 22-38, from 67 DTI scans) is also offered on Harvard Dataverse.
size: Atlas derived from MRI of 81 healthy fetuses (19-39 GA weeks); per-gestational-week template and label volumes (~weeks 21-38)
segmentation_detail: Tissue segmentation and regional parcellation label maps provided per gestational week alongside the intensity templates
host: Computational Radiology Lab (CRL), Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School
description: A normative spatiotemporal (4D) MRI atlas of the fetal brain spanning gestational weeks ~21-38, built from 81 healthy fetuses, with tissue and regional parcellation labels for automatic segmentation and brain-growth analysis.

label_schema: Two dense integer label maps per gestational week share ONE ITK-SnAP color/label key (labelkey.txt / labelnames.tab). 0 = Clear Label (background) in both.
REGIONAL PARCELLATION (STA*_regional.nii.gz), AAL-style, mostly L/R-split; values 1-124:

TISSUE SEGMENTATION (STA*_tissue.nii.gz): coarser tissue map drawn from the same key - cortical plate/gray matter, white matter, subcortical gray (caudate/putamen/pallidum/thalamus), CSF, lateral ventricles, brainstem, cerebellum; for GA weeks 21-30 additionally the transient developing zones subplate, intermediate zone, and ventricular zone (labels 114-119).
details.file_structure: Flat single-folder Harvard Dataverse deposit: for each gestational week the T2 intensity template STA{wk}.nii.gz is paired with STA{wk}_regional.nii.gz (regional parcellation) and STA{wk}_tissue.nii.gz (tissue segmentation), all gzip-compressed NIfTI (weeks 21-35 named STA21..STA35, expanded weeks as STA36exp/STA37exp/STA38exp), plus shared labelkey.txt (ITK-SnAP format), labelnames.tab, README.txt and cksum_output.txt (58 files total).
details.extra: This is a normative age-indexed brain atlas (one template per GA week), not a subject-level dataset - there are no per-patient scans or train/val/test splits; released CC0 1.0. Templates cover GA weeks 21-38, built from MRI of ~81 healthy fetuses scanned at 19-39 weeks (Gholipour et al., Scientific Reports 2017); the Feb 2018 'Superbowl edition' update added week 38 and the regional cortical parcellation. README explicitly warns segmentations are research-grade, not for medical use, with varying accuracy per structure.

name: MRI of 3-12 year old children (Pixar)
full_name: MRI data of 3-12 year old children and adults during viewing of a short animated film
anatomy: Pediatric brain (ages 3-12) plus adult comparison group
protocol_note: Anatomical T1-weighted plus movie-watching (Partly Cloudy) task fMRI
size: 155 subjects (122 children, 33 adults)
description: Structural T1 and movie-watching task fMRI from children aged 3-12 and adults for studying social-cognitive brain development.

label_schema: Child_Adult - participant group: child vs adult
ToM Booklet-Matched - theory-of-mind battery accuracy score (continuous, 0-1)
ToM Booklet-Matched-NOFB - ToM score excluding false-belief items (continuous)
WPPSI BD raw / scaled - Wechsler Block Design IQ subtest scores
KBIT_raw / KBIT_standard - Kaufman Brief Intelligence Test scores
DCCS Summary - Dimensional Change Card Sort executive-function score
Movie event annotations (events.tsv): 'Theory of Mind' (mental-state) segments vs 'Pain' (physical/social pain) segments, defined by reverse-correlation onsets/durations over the Partly Cloudy movie
details.file_structure: BIDS format on OpenNeuro: one folder per subject (sub-pixar001 ... sub-pixarNNN) each with anat/*_T1w.nii.gz (structural) and func/*_task-pixar_bold.nii.gz (movie-watching fMRI, TR=2s, 168 volumes); participant labels live in a top-level participants.tsv (phenotype/behavioral columns), and movie event annotations (ToM vs Pain) are provided as task-level events.tsv / stimulus timing files rather than image masks.
details.extra: No image segmentation or voxel masks exist; 'labels' are participant-level phenotype/behavioral metadata plus movie-timeline event annotations. Cohort is 155 participants: 122 children (ages ~3-12) plus 33 adults, all passively viewing the Pixar short 'Partly Cloudy' (Richardson et al., 2018, Nature Communications).

name: Queensland Twin Adolescent Brain (QTAB)
full_name: Queensland Twin Adolescent Brain
protocol_note: T1w, T2w, diffusion MRI, resting-state and task fMRI (partlycloudy movie, emotionalconflict), ASL
size: 417 subjects (twin pairs), ~683 GB, 27718 files; two timepoints
description: Multimodal longitudinal brain MRI from a cohort of over 400 adolescent twins for studying developmental and genetic influences on brain structure and function.

label_schema: No voxel/segmentation labels - QTAB is a raw BIDS neuroimaging cohort; 'labels' are participant-level demographic + phenotypic variables

Public participants.tsv columns: participant_id, family_id (shared by twins in a family), age (years at ses-01), age_ses02 (years at ses-02), sex (F/M), handedness, ses01_protocol (1a/1b/1c), ses02_protocol (2a/2b/2c), group (n/a - not grouped)
Restricted phenotype (Zenodo, access-controlled): age in months, zygosity, zygosity source, multiple-birth status, birth order

Restricted non-imaging measures (per data descriptor): standardised cognitive-function tests, anxiety symptoms, depression symptoms, perceived stress, sleepiness, pubertal development, peer relationships, early-life factors, family sociodemographic factors
Task fMRI conditions present as labels: rest, emotionalconflict (emotional conflict task, ses-02), partlycloudy (passive movie-watching / Theory-of-Mind task, ses-02)
Note: zygosity is provided but NOT in the public files - it is restricted-access, so twin MZ/DZ status cannot be confirmed from the open release
details.file_structure: BIDS-formatted OpenNeuro dataset (ds004146): per-subject folders sub-XXXX/ses-01|ses-02 containing raw MRI as NIfTI (.nii.gz) + JSON sidecars (T1w MP2RAGE, T2w, FLAIR, TSE, SWI, DWI, ASL, resting + task BOLD); only basic demographics ship in a top-level participants.tsv (with participants.json data dictionary), while the full non-imaging phenotype is distributed separately as restricted-access tabular data on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.7353053) under a data-usage agreement.
details.extra: Longitudinal twin cohort over two sessions: session 1 N=422 (age 9-14 yrs), session 2 N=304 (age 10-16 yrs); 417 subjects appear in the OpenNeuro metadata (current snapshot 1.0.4). No official ML train/val/test split - it is a research cohort, not a benchmark.

name: ABCD Study
full_name: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
anatomy: Child and adolescent brain (enrolled at ages 9-10, longitudinal)
protocol_note: T1w, T2w, diffusion MRI, resting-state and task fMRI
size: ~11,880 children
clinical_variables: Neurocognition, mental health, substance use, environment and genetics across adolescence, with biennial follow-up.
license: NIMH Data Archive Data Use Certification
description: Large longitudinal multimodal brain MRI study following roughly 11,900 US children from ages 9-10 through adolescence, hosted at the NIMH Data Archive under a Data Use Certification.

label_schema: Not a manually-labeled segmentation dataset - 'labels' are atlas-derived ROI imaging metrics plus deep phenotypic/behavioral tabulated variables
Cortical parcellation: Desikan-Killiany atlas (68 regions) and Destrieux atlas (148 regions), with per-ROI cortical thickness, surface area, volume, sulcal depth, and T1/T2 intensity
Subcortical segmentation: FreeSurfer ASEG automated volumetric segmentation (hippocampus, amygdala, thalamus, caudate, putamen, etc.) with per-structure volumes
Functional parcellation: Gordon network parcellation (default mode, fronto-parietal, dorsal attention, etc.) with rs-fMRI within/between-network connectivity
White-matter: AtlasTrack probabilistic fiber-tract atlas with per-tract dMRI/DTI/RSI metrics (FA, MD, etc.)
Task-fMRI ROI activation for MID (reward), SST (inhibition), and EN-back (working memory/emotion) tasks
Non-imaging labels: demographics, cognition (NIH Toolbox), mental/physical health, substance use, and other rich phenotypic assessments
Extensive cognitive, behavioral, environmental, and clinical phenotyping
details.file_structure: Raw imaging released as BIDS-organized NIfTI (T1/T2 sMRI, dMRI, rs-fMRI, three task fMRI) via the ABCD Community Collection/DCAN-BIDS derivatives; ROI-level imaging derivatives and all phenotypic measures distributed as tabulated data structures (CSV/tab-delimited tables) through the NIMH Data Archive (NDA).
details.extra: Longitudinal cohort of ~11,880 children enrolled at ages 9-10 with biennial imaging; access requires an approved NDA Data Use Certification (no fixed train/val/test partition).

name: COBRA2026
full_name: A Large-Scale Multicenter Pelvic Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Projection Dataset
protocol_note: Measured raw CBCT projections from routine image-guided pelvic radiotherapy (Elekta and Varian systems), RTK-format geometry, simulated projections from deformed planning CT, clinical and RTK-reconstructed CBCT, planning CT (original and deformably registered).
size: 867 cases (692 train / 52 val / 123 test); ~950 GB total
description: Multicenter raw pelvic radiotherapy cone-beam CT projection dataset of 867 cases from six European centers, providing measured CBCT projections, acquisition geometry, simulated projections, clinically reconstructed CBCT, and paired planning CT for reconstruction and image-correction research.

name: SegRap2025
full_name: Gross Tumor Volume and Lymph Node Segmentation Challenge for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
protocol_note: Radiotherapy-planning CT; paired non-contrast CT (ncCT) and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT), some Task02 cases with only one modality
size: 260 NPC patients with GTV annotations, 402 patients with LN CTV annotations, plus 500 unlabeled CT scans
segmentation_detail: Gross tumor volume (GTV, Task 01) and lymph node clinical target volume (LN CTV, Task 02) segmentation on radiotherapy planning CT
description: A head-and-neck CT benchmark for nasopharyngeal carcinoma providing gross tumor volume and lymph-node clinical-target-volume segmentation tasks, extending the SegRap2023 cohort with additional annotated and unlabeled scans.

label_schema: Task01 GTV segmentation (2 target structures): GTVnx (also called GTVp) - primary gross tumor volume of the nasopharynx; GTVnd - gross tumor volume of metastatic lymph nodes
Task02 LN CTV segmentation (6 target structures / lymph-node clinical target volumes): L_Ib, L_II+III+Va, L_IV+Vb+Vc, R_Ib, R_II+III+Va, R_IV+Vb+Vc (left/right neck nodal levels grouped)
Note: exact integer label indices are not published on the official page; each structure was annotated and stored individually as separate label maps
details.file_structure: Radiotherapy-planning CT volumes are provided per patient, generally as paired non-contrast CT (ncCT) and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) images (some Task02 cases have only one modality), with each target structure delineated by oncologists (MIM Software / ITK-SNAP) and stored as individual per-class label maps; data is distributed as password-protected ZIP archives via Google Drive / Baidu Netdisk (the page does not explicitly state the image file format).
details.splits: Task01: 120 labeled training patients + 500 shared unlabeled cases; 20 validation; 120 test (60 internal cohort + 60 external cohort). Task02: 262 labeled training patients (150 paired CT, 32 ncCT-only, 108 ceCT-only) + the same 500 unlabeled cases; 40 validation (20 paired, 10 ncCT-only, 10 ceCT-only); 100 test (40 paired, 30 ncCT-only, 30 ceCT-only).
details.extra: Task01 tests generalizability across internal/external cohorts and Task02 tests robustness to missing modality; validation/test labels are withheld, only official data is allowed (no external data), foundation models permitted, and OAR segmentation is optional supporting info.

related.name: SegRap2023
related.note: Extends the SegRap2023 NPC CT cohort with additional GTV and LN CTV annotated and unlabeled scans

name: Cyst-X
full_name: Cyst-X: A Multi-Center MRI Benchmark and Federated Learning Framework for Malignancy-Risk Stratification of Pancreatic Cystic Neoplasm
protocol_note: Abdominal MRI with emphasis on T2-weighted sequences
size: 1,461 abdominal MRI scans from 764 patients across 7 centers
segmentation_detail: Expert manual pancreas segmentation masks by experienced radiologists
description: Public multi-center benchmark of 1,461 abdominal MRI scans from 764 patients with expert pancreas segmentation masks and histopathology-anchored three-tier malignancy labels for pancreatic cystic neoplasm risk stratification.

label_schema: Segmentation mask: 1 - pancreatic cyst (IPMN lesion), foreground
Classification (IPMN risk assessment, per scan): 0 - No risk
Classification: 2 - High risk (some scans labeled N/A)
three-tier malignancy risk labels anchored to histopathology or 3-year imaging follow-up
details.file_structure: Imaging is distributed as one ZIP per center (AHN, MCF, EMC, IU, NYU, NU, MCA) under Cyst-X_Dataset/, each containing t1/ and t2/ subfolders that each split into images/ and masks/ holding matching .nii.gz NIfTI volumes (binary lesion masks); an IPMN_Classification/ folder holds t1.zip/t2.zip plus per-scan risk-label files IPMN_labels_t1_total.csv and IPMN_labels_t2_total.csv (columns: Patient ID = <scan>.nii.gz, risk assessment = 0/1/2/N/A), and Metadata.zip carries age/gender/risk demographic CSVs and a labels.txt legend.
details.extra: Multicenter, multivendor set of 1,461 abdominal MRI scans (723 T1W + 738 T2W) from 764 patients across 7 centers (697 patients have paired T1+T2); segmentation masks were manually annotated by experienced radiologists; no official train/val/test partition is provided.

name: RAM-W600
full_name: RAM-W600: A Multi-Task Wrist Dataset and Benchmark for Rheumatoid Arthritis
protocol_note: Conventional wrist radiographs from 6 medical centers
size: 1,048 wrist conventional radiographs from 388 patients across 6 medical centers (618 with instance segmentation masks, 800 with SvdH bone erosion scores)
segmentation_detail: Pixel-level wrist bone instance segmentation (14-channel .npy masks) for 618 radiographs
description: First public wrist radiograph (X-ray) dataset for rheumatoid arthritis, providing pixel-level bone instance segmentation masks and Sharp/van der Heijde erosion scores across 1,048 images from 388 patients (NeurIPS 2025).

label_schema: Sharp/van der Heijde (SvdH) bone erosion scores for 800 images
details.file_structure: Pixel-level bone instance segmentation labels are stored as 14-channel NumPy .npy arrays of shape (14, H, W), where each channel is a binary mask for one fixed wrist-bone class, distributed via the Hugging Face repo (git clone) alongside the wrist radiograph images.
details.extra: Multi-task wrist dataset for rheumatoid arthritis (NeurIPS 2026, Yang et al.); tagged for Segmentation and Classification, with benchmark code at github.com/YSongxiao/RAM-W600. Channel semantics are fixed across all samples regardless of hand-side canonicalization. Official train/val/test split counts are not stated in the dataset README.

name: LUND-PROBE
full_name: Lund Prostate Radiotherapy Open Benchmarking and Evaluation Dataset
anatomy: Prostate (radiotherapy target volumes and pelvic organs-at-risk)
protocol_note: MRI images plus deep-learning-generated synthetic CT (sCT) from MRI-guided radiotherapy
size: 467 patients (432 primary + 35 extended deep-learning subset), 176.56 GB
segmentation_detail: Manual ground-truth segmentations of target volumes and organs-at-risk; extended subset adds deep-learning segmentations with uncertainty maps and oncologist-adjusted annotations
license: AIDA BY (attribution) / controlled access for research
description: Open prostate radiotherapy dataset of 432+ patients with MRI, deep-learning synthetic CT, target/OAR segmentations, uncertainty maps and dose distributions, hosted on the AIDA Data Hub in NIfTI format.

details.file_structure: Per-patient folders in NIfTI format containing MRI and synthetic-CT (sCT) images plus manual gold-standard segmentations of the target volumes and OARs; the extended subset additionally provides DL-generated segmentations, DL uncertainty maps, and DL segmentations manually adjusted by four radiation oncologists, along with radiotherapy dose distributions (load/visualization code at github.com/jamtheim/LUND-PROBE).
details.extra: 432 prostate-cancer patients in the main manual-segmentation dataset plus a 35-patient extended subset with DL segmentations, uncertainty maps, and four-oncologist manual edits enabling inter-observer variability analysis; imaged on a 3T GE Healthcare Architect scanner (~467 scans, ~8,873 annotations).

name: ReXGroundingCT
full_name: A 3D Chest CT Dataset for Segmentation of Findings from Free-Text Reports
protocol_note: Non-contrast chest CT scans (from CT-RATE)
size: 3,142 non-contrast chest CT scans; 8,028 text-to-segmentation pairs; 16,301 annotated entities
segmentation_detail: Pixel-level 3D segmentation masks stored as 4D arrays (F,H,W,D) for report findings across 14 categories; 8,028 finding segmentations grounded to text
paired_text_detail: Free-text radiology findings/reports (derived from CT-RATE) paired with text-to-3D-segmentation grounding; separate reports_dataset.json with full extracted reports
description: 3,142 non-contrast chest CT scans in NIfTI format with radiologist-verified 3D segmentation masks grounded to free-text radiology report findings for text-to-segmentation modeling.

label_schema: Each label = a 3D pixel-level segmentation mask grounded to a free-text finding sentence from the radiology report, plus a taxonomy category code (e.g. '2b')
Finding taxonomy has 12 parent categories / 61 subcategories; the 8,028 annotated findings span 14 category groupings (8 focal + 6 non-focal, per Fig. 1B)
Parent category 1 - Typically non-focal lung/airway/pleural abnormalities
Parent category 2 - Typically focal lung/airway/pleural opacities
Within a mask, distinct positive pixel values denote separate entities of the same finding (16,301 entities total)
details.file_structure: CT volumes are NIfTI .nii.gz files ([512,512,D]); segmentation masks are 4D NIfTI arrays of shape (F,H,W,D) where F is the number of findings per scan (one finding per mask layer), and a dataset.json links each mask (e.g. train_1741_b_2.nii.gz) to its finding indices, free-text report sentences, category codes, entity_counts, pixels, shape, and protocol.
details.splits: Train 2,992 cases / public validation 50 cases / private test 100 cases (3,142 total); a MICCAI challenge variant uses validation 200 and test 300 (test masks withheld).
details.extra: Grounding is text-to-3D: each segmentation is tied to a specific sentence in the free-text CT report; totals are 8,028 text-to-3D-segmentation pairs and 16,301 annotated entities. Verified against arXiv 2507.22030 and the Hugging Face dataset card.

segmentation_detail: Voxel-wise segmentation masks for 167 whole-body anatomical structures, provided as NIfTI labelmaps alongside the original CT volumes
license: Mixed per source subset (CC BY 4.0, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and custom licenses)
description: A large-scale whole-body CT resource of 22,022 volumes with segmentation annotations for 167 anatomical structures, aggregated from 100+ imaging centers across 16 countries and released with models and clinical software.

MODEL 551 (organs): 1-Spleen, 2-Kidney R, 3-Kidney L, 4-Gallbladder, 5-Liver, 6-Stomach, 7-Aorta, 8-Inferior vena cava, 9-Portal vein and splenic vein, 10-Pancreas, 11-Adrenal gland R, 12-Adrenal gland L, 13-Upper lobe of lung L, 14-Lower lobe of lung L, 15-Upper lobe of lung R, 16-Middle lobe of lung R, 17-Lower lobe of lung R

MODEL 554 (bones/muscles): 1-Humerus L, 2-Humerus R, 3-Scapula L, 4-Scapula R, 5-Clavicle L, 6-Clavicle R, 7-Femur L, 8-Femur R, 9-Hip L, 10-Hip R, 11-Sacrum, 12-Gluteus maximus L, 13-Gluteus maximus R, 14-Gluteus medius L, 15-Gluteus medius R, 16-Gluteus minimus L, 17-Gluteus minimus R, 18-Deep muscle of back L, 19-Deep muscle of back R, 20-Iliopsoas L, 21-Iliopsoas R

MODEL 556 (thoracic/pelvic): 1-Spinal canal, 2-Larynx, 3-Heart, 4-Bowel space, 5-Sigmoid colon, 6-Rectum, 7-Prostate, 8-Seminal vesicle, 9-Mammary gland L, 10-Mammary gland R, 11-Sternum, 12-Psoas major R, 13-Psoas major L, 14-Rectus abdominis R, 15-Rectus abdominis L
MODEL 557 (brain tissue types): 1-White matter, 2-Gray matter, 3-Cerebrospinal fluid, 4-Scalp, 5-Eyeball, 6-Compact bone, 7-Spongy bone, 8-Blood, 9-Muscle of head

MODEL 558 (head & neck): 1-Carotid artery L, 2-Carotid artery R, 3-Arytenoid cartilage, 4-Mandible, 5-Brainstem, 6-Buccal mucosa, 7-Oral cavity, 8-Cochlear L, 9-Cochlear R, 10-Cricopharyngeus, 11-Cervical esophagus, 12-Anterior eyeball segment L, 13-Anterior eyeball segment R, 14-Posterior eyeball segment L, 15-Posterior eyeball segment R, 16-Lacrimal gland L, 17-Lacrimal gland R, 18-Submandibular gland L, 19-Submandibular gland R, 20-Thyroid, 21-Glottis, 22-Supraglottis, 23-Both lips, 24-Optic chiasm, 25-Optic nerve L, 26-Optic nerve R, 27-Parotid gland L, 28-Parotid gland R, 29-Pituitary gland

MODEL 559 (tissue compartments): 1-Subcutaneous tissue, 2-Muscle, 3-Abdominal cavity, 4-Thoracic cavity, 5-Bones, 6-Gland structure, 7-Pericardium, 8-Prosthetic breast implant, 9-Mediastinum, 10-Spinal cord
details.file_structure: All CT volumes and their segmentation masks are stored as NIfTI (.nii.gz) files in native spacing, organized by source into ~43 numbered subdirectories (0001-0043), each with images/ and segmentations/ subfolders, a per-source CSV index (e.g. 0003_kits21.csv) and a README; the full integer->structure mapping across the 9 sub-models is in resources/info/labelmap.md in the CADS model GitHub repo.
details.extra: Aggregation of 43 public/private CT datasets (22,022 fully annotated volumes from 100+ centers in 16 countries; largest contributors NLST ~7,172, CT-RATE ~3,134, STOIC2021 ~2,000, TotalSegmentator ~1,203); model code/weights at github.com/murong-xu/CADS, paper arXiv:2507.22953, plus a 3D Slicer plugin (SlicerCADSWholeBodyCTSeg). No official train/val/test split; HF configs expose a single 'all' split.

name: STS 2024
full_name: MICCAI STS 2024: Semi-Supervised Instance-Level Tooth Segmentation in Panoramic X-ray and CBCT Images
protocol_note: Two imaging tracks: 2D panoramic X-ray (OPG) and 3D cone-beam CT (CBCT)
size: ~2,380 panoramic X-ray (OPG) images + ~330 CBCT scans; ~968 MB total on Zenodo
segmentation_detail: Instance-level tooth segmentation masks with FDI tooth numbering; semi-supervised setup with labeled and unlabeled subsets
description: MICCAI STS 2024 challenge dataset for semi-supervised instance-level tooth segmentation, providing dental panoramic X-ray (OPG) and cone-beam CT (CBCT) images with FDI-numbered tooth annotations.

label_schema: Instance-level tooth segmentation: each individual tooth is a separate polygon instance whose class is its FDI World Dental Federation two-digit code (the LabelMe 'label' field); 52 distinct FDI codes appear across the labeled set
details.file_structure: A single Train-Labeled.zip expands to Train-Labeled/Images/*.jpg (panoramic dental X-rays, e.g. STS24_Train_Labeled_0001.jpg) and Train-Labeled/Masks/*_Mask.json, where each mask is a LabelMe v1.0.0 JSON storing per-tooth polygon shapes (fields: label=FDI code, points, shape_type='polygon', group_id) with imageWidth/imageHeight; one JSON per image, matched by filename.
details.splits: This Zenodo record hosts only the labeled training subset: 30 labeled panoramic X-ray images with 30 matching mask JSONs; no official train/val/test partition is provided within the record.
details.extra: Annotations are LabelMe polygon vertices (not raster masks), so instance masks must be rasterized from the polygons. The Zenodo record is titled for the MICCAI STS 2024 semi-supervised challenge covering both panoramic X-ray and CBCT, but only the panoramic X-ray labeled-training subset is included here (the unlabeled subset and any CBCT/test data are not in this file).

name: BRISC2025
full_name: BRISC: Annotated Dataset for Brain Tumor Segmentation and Classification (2025)
anatomy: Brain (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumors; and no-tumor cases)
protocol_note: Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI only
size: 6,000 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI images across axial, sagittal, and coronal planes
segmentation_detail: Expert-annotated (radiologist/physician) high-resolution tumor segmentation masks across axial, sagittal, and coronal planes
description: 6,000 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted brain MRI images (JPG) collated from public sources and annotated by experts with high-resolution tumor segmentation masks and tumor-type classification labels (glioma, meningioma, pituitary, no tumor).

label_schema: Classification labels (4 classes): glioma, meningioma, pituitary, no_tumor
Segmentation label: binary tumor mask per image (background vs. delineated tumor region); expert-annotated for all images including no_tumor cases
Imaging plane metadata: axial, coronal, sagittal (near-uniform distribution)
tumor type classification: glioma, meningioma, pituitary, no tumor
details.file_structure: The dataset supports two tasks: a classification split organized into train/test folders each containing one subfolder per class (glioma, meningioma, pituitary, no_tumor) holding the contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI images, plus a segmentation split pairing each MRI image with a corresponding expert-annotated binary tumor mask (masks refined with the AnyLabeling tool); the exact on-disk image/mask file format is not stated in the paper.
details.splits: Classification: 5,000 train / 1,000 test (no official validation split). Per-class train/test totals: glioma 1,147/254 (1,401), meningioma 1,329/306 (1,635), pituitary 1,457/300 (1,757), no_tumor 1,067/140 (1,207).
details.extra: 6,000 total contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI scans; segmentation masks are binary (single tumor foreground class), not multi-class per tumor type, and were added by certified radiologists/physicians to a dataset originally built for classification (arXiv:2506.14318).

name: crossMoDA 2023
full_name: Cross-Modality Domain Adaptation for Medical Image Segmentation 2023
protocol_note: Contrast-enhanced T1 (ceT1, source domain) and high-resolution T2 (hrT2, target domain) MRI
segmentation_detail: Intra-meatal and extra-meatal vestibular schwannoma plus cochlea labels
description: Multi-institutional brain MRI (ceT1/hrT2) for unsupervised cross-modality domain-adaptation segmentation of vestibular schwannoma and cochlea.

label_schema: Label 1 - intra-meatal (intracochlear) vestibular schwannoma tumour component (shown red)
Label 2 - extra-meatal (extracochlear) vestibular schwannoma tumour component (shown green)
details.file_structure: 3D volumes distributed as NIfTI (.nii.gz); the crossmoda23_training folder holds a TrainingSource subfolder with annotated contrast-enhanced T1 scans and their masks (crossmoda2023_{site}_{#}_ceT1.nii.gz + crossmoda2023_{site}_{#}_Label.nii.gz, site codes e.g. etz=Tilburg, ldn=London) and a TrainingTarget subfolder with unannotated hrT2 scans (crossmoda2023_{site}_{#}_T2.nii.gz), plus a separate crossmoda23_validation folder of unannotated T2 scans.
details.splits: Per the official summary paper (Table 1): Training Source (labeled ceT1) = 227 scans, Training Target (unlabeled hrT2) = 295, Validation Target (unlabeled hrT2) = 96, Test Target (unlabeled hrT2) = 341.
details.extra: Unsupervised cross-modality domain adaptation: only the source ceT1 scans carry labels; models must segment the target hrT2 scans with no manual T2 annotations. 2023 added the intra-/extra-meatal tumour sub-segmentation (vs. a single VS label in 2021/2022) and heterogeneous multi-institution routine data (London SC-GK, Tilburg SC-GK, UK MC-RC); hosted on Synapse (syn51236108) under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
