details.extra: The molecular 1p/19q label is the intended classification target (genotype prediction from imaging); it is stored as tabular metadata linked to subjects rather than as image annotations.

name: Brain-Tumor-Progression
full_name: Brain-Tumor-Progression
protocol_note: T1w pre/post-contrast, FLAIR, T2w, ADC and perfusion imaging, co-registered to T1+C; two exams per patient (post-treatment and at progression)
segmentation_detail: Binary tumor masks generated from T1w images included
license: TCIA Data Usage Policy (NIH controlled access for facial-reconstructable series)
description: Longitudinal multi-sequence brain MRI with tumor masks for 20 glioblastoma patients imaged post-treatment and at tumor progression.

label_schema: Binary tumor mask (2 classes) - value 1 = tumor, value 0 = background/non-tumor

Masks were generated (segmented) on the T1-weighted post-contrast (T1+C) images; a single whole-tumor region per exam (no multi-class tumor sub-region labels such as edema/necrosis/enhancing are provided)
details.file_structure: All data (imaging and labels) is distributed in DICOM format via TCIA; each of the 20 subjects has 2 studies (baseline and progression), and each study contains multiple co-registered series including the anatomical sequences and a separate binary tumor-mask series, all spatially registered to the T1+C image (no NIfTI/CSV; masks stored as DICOM image series rather than DICOM-SEG/RTSTRUCT).
details.extra: 20 subjects, 40 studies, ~383 series / ~8,798 images (~3.16 GB) of primary glioblastoma; each subject imaged twice (within 90 days of chemoradiation completion and at tumor progression). Co-registered series per exam include T1 pre/post-contrast, FLAIR, T2, ADC, normalized cerebral blood flow (nCBF), normalized relative CBF, standardized relative cerebral blood volume, plus the binary tumor mask.

name: CPTAC-GBM
full_name: Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium - Glioblastoma Multiforme
protocol_note: Multiple MR sequences (T1, post-contrast T1, T2, FLAIR) plus CT studies
size: 41.1 GB radiology (192.6 GB with histopathology)
license: TCIA / NIH Controlled Data Access (radiology); CC BY 4.0 (pathology)
description: Radiology (MR and CT) imaging of 70+ glioblastoma patients from the CPTAC proteogenomic cohort, hosted on TCIA for radiogenomic research.

label_schema: The base CPTAC-GBM collection ships imaging only (no native voxel labels); tumor segmentation labels come from the associated RSNA-ASNR-MICCAI-BraTS-2021 analysis result, which covers CPTAC-GBM cases

Separately, Crowds-Cure-2018 provides crowd-sourced lesion annotations: bi-directional lesion measurements plus lesion location, characteristics (e.g. ill-defined, ground-glass), image-quality notes, and metastatic-disease identification
details.file_structure: Radiology data is DICOM (MR + CT) in the standard TCIA patient/study/series folder hierarchy, with matching histopathology whole-slide images in SVS; BraTS-2021 tumor segmentations are distributed as label volumes (T1/T1Gd/T2/FLAIR co-registered and resampled to 240x240x155, provided in NIfTI and DICOM formats), and Crowds-Cure-2018 annotations come as a CSV of measurements plus DICOM-SR structured reports.
details.extra: Collection scale: 70 subjects with radiology imaging (154 studies, 1,835 series, ~162,934 images) plus 200 subjects with histopathology; the BraTS-2021 segmentation set aggregates 1,480 subjects across multiple collections (TCGA-GBM/LGG, UPENN-GBM, IvyGAP, UCSF-PDGM, ACRIN-FMISO-Brain, CPTAC-GBM), so only a subset of its labels correspond to CPTAC-GBM.

name: Vestibular-Schwannoma-SEG
full_name: Segmentation of Vestibular Schwannoma from MRI - An Open Annotated Dataset
anatomy: Brain / skull base (vestibular schwannoma, cerebellopontine angle)
protocol_note: Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted (ceT1) and high-resolution T2-weighted (hrT2) MR sequences
segmentation_detail: Manual tumor segmentations consensus-annotated by neurosurgeon and physicist, provided as DICOM RTSTRUCT/contours (with RTDOSE, RTPLAN, registration matrices)
description: 242 patients with vestibular schwannoma imaged on a 1.5T MRI with expert manual tumor segmentations and radiotherapy planning data, released open-access on TCIA.

label_schema: Tumour (vestibular schwannoma) - manually segmented, typically on the contrast-enhanced T1 (ceT1) image
Cochlea - manually segmented, typically on the high-resolution T2 (hrT2) image
details.file_structure: 242 patients with contrast-enhanced T1 (ceT1) and high-resolution T2 (hrT2) MRI in DICOM; manual tumour and cochlea segmentations provided as DICOM RTSTRUCT plus JSON contour-point files, with RTDOSE, RTPLAN, and .tfm T1-to-T2 registration matrices, organized per-patient in the TCIA DICOM folder hierarchy.
details.extra: All structures were manually segmented in consensus by the treating neurosurgeon and physicist using both the ceT1 and hrT2 images; patients were consecutive Gamma Knife stereotactic radiosurgery cases imaged 2012-2018 on a Siemens Avanto 1.5T scanner.

name: PPMI
full_name: Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative
protocol_note: Structural T1/T2, DTI, resting-state fMRI, plus DaTscan (SPECT) and PET (VMAT2/tau/amyloid) imaging
clinical_variables: Parkinson's clinical assessments, biospecimens, genetics and longitudinal disease progression.
description: Large longitudinal multimodal brain imaging and clinical study of Parkinson's disease, providing MRI, DaTscan SPECT and PET data to qualified researchers via LONI IDA.

label_schema: Diagnostic cohort / enrollment group (participant-level classification), not per-pixel segmentation
Prodromal PD (e.g. RBD, hyposmia, genetic risk)
SWEDD - Scans Without Evidence of Dopaminergic Deficit
Genetic cohort / Genetic Registry (LRRK2, GBA, SNCA variant carriers)
DaTscan-derived striatal binding ratio (SBR) values per striatal region provided as tabular biomarkers
details.file_structure: Imaging is downloaded from the LONI Image & Data Archive (IDA) as DICOM (raw) or preprocessed NIfTI, organized per-subject/per-visit (DaTSCAN SPECT and MRI including T1, DTI, resting-state fMRI); diagnosis/cohort labels, clinical assessments, and DaTscan SBR values are distributed separately as CSV/tabular data files keyed by subject ID and visit, with no per-voxel segmentation masks.
details.extra: PPMI is a longitudinal observational cohort (~5,500 participants) requiring a data-use application via LONI IDA; labels are subject/visit-level diagnosis and biomarker values rather than image annotations, and there is no official train/val/test partition.

name: AIBL
full_name: Australian Imaging, Biomarkers and Lifestyle Study of Ageing
protocol_note: Structural MRI plus amyloid PET (PiB and related tracers) for dementia/ageing research
description: Australian longitudinal study of ageing and Alzheimer's disease providing structural MRI and amyloid PET brain imaging with clinical/cognitive and biomarker data via LONI IDA.

label_schema: Image-level clinical diagnosis (classification), 3 groups: Healthy Control (HC/CN), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), Alzheimer's Disease (AD)
Diagnosis is coded numerically in the clinical CSV (aibl_pdxconv, field DXCURREN): 1 = Healthy Control, 2 = MCI, 3 = AD
No voxel-level segmentation/lesion masks are provided
Accompanying non-image labels/biomarkers: ApoE genotype, blood biomarkers, neuropsychological/cognitive scores (e.g., MMSE), amyloid PET status
details.file_structure: Imaging is distributed via the LONI IDA as DICOM series (T1-weighted MRI and amyloid PET with PiB, Florbetapir/AV45, or Flutemetamol tracers); labels are not per-pixel but come as separate tabular clinical CSV files keyed by subject RID and visit code (e.g. aibl_pdxconv for diagnosis), which community tools like Clinica convert to BIDS participants.tsv and per-session <subjectID>_session.tsv files.
details.extra: ~1,100 participants (211 AD, 133 MCI, 768 HC) with over 4.5 years of longitudinal follow-up; no official train/val/test split is defined.

name: Cam-CAN
full_name: Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience
protocol_note: T1, T2, DWI/DTI, resting-state and task fMRI, ASL, MTI, SWI across a healthy adult lifespan cohort (age 18-88)
size: ~700 subjects
host: Cam-CAN Data Access Portal (MRC CBU, University of Cambridge)
description: Cross-sectional healthy-ageing neuroimaging dataset of ~700 adults spanning ages 18-88 with multimodal MRI (and MEG), available to researchers after registration and a data use agreement.

label_schema: No image segmentation masks or voxel annotations - labels are participant-level metadata and behavioral scores
Cognitive/behavioral scores - Phase 1 (home interview): simple/choice reaction time, Spot-the-Word (crystallized IQ), Story Recall (Wechsler Logical Memory)

Cognitive/behavioral scores - Phase 2: Cattell fluid intelligence, face/emotion recognition & memory, motor learning/force matching, Hotel task (executive function), picture priming, proverb comprehension, tip-of-the-tongue, visual short-term memory
Common ML use: age is the regression target for brain-age prediction; cognitive scores as regression targets
details.file_structure: Data are BIDS-organized as separate per-modality repositories - imaging in NIfTI (structural T1/T2, DWI, resting-state/movie/sensorimotor fMRI, magnetization transfer; MEG from a 306-channel Elekta Neuromag) delivered via SFTP, and demographic/cognitive variables in tabular spreadsheet (CSV) files; access requires an approved data request.
details.extra: Population-based ageing cohort (Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience), not a labeled segmentation/detection dataset; sample sizes are by study phase - Phase 1 (home interview) ~2,700, Phase 2 Arm 1 (imaging) ~700 (~100 per decade, 18-88y), plus smaller Phase 2 Arm 2 and Phase 3 follow-up cohorts - with no official ML train/val/test partition.

name: FeTS 2021/2022
full_name: Federated Tumor Segmentation Challenge
protocol_note: Four co-registered MRI sequences: native T1, post-contrast T1 (T1Gd), T2, and T2-FLAIR
segmentation_detail: Expert tumor sub-region labels: enhancing tumor (label 4), peritumoral edema (label 2), and necrotic tumor core (label 1)
description: Federated brain-tumor segmentation challenge built on multi-institutional BraTS glioma MRI (T1/T1Gd/T2/FLAIR) with tumor annotations and source-institution partitioning for federated learning.

details.file_structure: Per-subject folders each containing four co-registered, skull-stripped multiparametric MRI volumes (native T1, post-contrast T1Gd/T1ce, T2, and T2-FLAIR) plus one expert segmentation mask, all as NIfTI (.nii.gz) files following the BraTS naming convention; institution-based data partitioning is provided via accompanying CSVs (partitioning_1.csv = natural per-institution split, partitioning_2.csv = institutions further split by median tumor size).
details.extra: FeTS 2021 was the first federated-learning tumor segmentation challenge; the labeled training set derives from BraTS glioma/GBM cases, and the test set includes a subset of BraTS 2020 testing data plus additional geographically distinct institutions. Segmentation evaluation typically uses the derived nested regions Whole Tumor (labels 1+2+4), Tumor Core (labels 1+4), and Enhancing Tumor (label 4).

related.name: BraTS (glioma MRI)
related.note: Training data derived from BraTS glioma cases, re-released with source-institution partitioning for federated learning

name: OCMR
full_name: Open-access multi-coil k-space dataset for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance imaging
protocol_note: Multi-coil k-space cardiac cine series; Siemens 1.5T Avanto, 3T Prisma, 1.5T Sola, 3T Vida and 0.55T Free.Max; fully sampled and prospectively undersampled; views SAX, LAX and others.
size: 165 fully sampled acquisitions (279 slices) and 212 prospectively undersampled acquisitions (842 slices)
description: OCMR is an open-access dataset of raw multi-coil k-space cardiac cine MRI acquisitions (both fully sampled and prospectively undersampled) for developing and benchmarking image reconstruction methods.

label_schema: No pixel-level segmentation, detection, or diagnostic disease labels. OCMR provides raw multi-coil k-space cardiac cine data with 8 per-file metadata attributes used to select subsets:
scn - scanner/field strength (e.g. 15avan = 1.5T Avanto, 30pris = 3T Prisma, 15sola = 1.5T Sola, 30vida = 3T Vida, 055freemax = 0.55T Free.Max)
smp - sampling: fs (fully sampled) vs pse/prospectively undersampled
ech - echo type: asy (asymmetric) vs sym (symmetric)
dur - acquisition duration: shr (short) vs lng (long)
viw - imaging view/plane: sax (short-axis), lax (long-axis), ch (chamber), aorta, transverse, sagittal, coronal, candy-cane, other
sli - slice mode: ind (individual) vs stk (stack)
fov - field-of-view alignment: noa (not aligned) vs ali (aligned)
sub - subject type: vol (volunteer) vs pat (patient)
(plus a 'slices' count field, 1-17, giving number of slices per series)
details.file_structure: Each cardiac cine series is one HDF5 (.h5) file in ISMRMRD format holding a 9-D k-space array [kx, ky, kz, coil, phase, set, slice, rep, avg]; a single CSV (ocmr_data_attributes.csv) maps each file_name to its 8 categorical attributes plus slice count. No mask/RTSTRUCT/NIfTI label files exist.
details.extra: OCMR is a reconstruction benchmark (fully sampled acquisitions act as reference/ground truth for undersampled reconstruction); v1.0 paper reports 53 fully sampled + 212 prospectively undersampled series, later expanded to ~165 fully sampled series (279 slices) and 212 undersampled (842 slices) as of Aug 2023.

name: Second Annual Data Science Bowl
full_name: Second Annual Data Science Bowl (Cardiac MRI Ejection Fraction)
protocol_note: Cine SSFP acquisitions including short-axis (SAX) and long-axis (2ch/4ch) views per study
size: ~1,140 patients (cine cardiac MRI studies)
description: A Kaggle competition dataset of cine cardiac MRI studies from ~1,140 patients (DICOM), with end-systolic/end-diastolic volume labels for automatically measuring left-ventricular ejection fraction.

label_schema: Systole - left ventricle end-systolic volume (mL), per-patient continuous scalar
Diastole - left ventricle end-diastolic volume (mL), per-patient continuous scalar
(Ejection fraction is derivable as (Diastole - Systole)/Diastole; no per-pixel segmentation masks are provided)
details.file_structure: Per-patient folders of cardiac cine-MRI DICOM images (short-axis SAX plus 2-chamber/4-chamber views, each a ~30-frame time series), split into train/validate/test directories; ground-truth labels are two scalar volumes per patient given in CSV files (train.csv, validate.csv) with columns Id, Systole, Diastole.
details.splits: 500 training patients and 200 validation patients (confirmed as cases 1-700); a separate held-out test set of roughly 440 patients was used for final scoring.
details.extra: This is a regression/probabilistic task: submissions are a 600-bin cumulative distribution function (P(volume<=x) for x=0..599 mL) for each of Systole and Diastole, scored by Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS); the dataset ships no segmentation annotations, so contour ground truth came from the external Sunnybrook Cardiac Data.

name: SPIE-AAPM Lung CT Challenge (LUNGx)
full_name: SPIE-AAPM-NCI Lung Nodule Classification Challenge
protocol_note: Thoracic CT (DICOM); contrast/phase not stated on the collection page.
size: 70 subjects, 22,489 images (~12 GB)
segmentation_detail: Nodule locations provided as coordinates in spreadsheets (points, not pixel masks)
description: A TCIA collection of thoracic CT scans from 70 subjects (10 calibration, 60 test) with nodule locations and benign/malignant diagnoses, used for the 2015 SPIE-AAPM lung nodule classification challenge.

label_schema: Nodule location - center of each pulmonary nodule given as coordinates (x-y position plus the DICOM image/slice number), NOT a pixel segmentation mask
Diagnosis - per-nodule classification: benign vs. malignant (provided for the 10 calibration cases; the 60 test-case diagnoses were withheld during the challenge and released later in Version 2)
details.file_structure: Chest CT scans are stored as DICOM series (70 studies / ~22,489 images, one folder per subject); nodule annotations live in two separate Excel spreadsheets, CalibrationSet_NoduleData.xlsx (10 CT-Training subjects, with locations and diagnoses) and TestSet_NoduleData.xlsx (60 LUNGx subjects, nodule locations plus later-added diagnoses).
details.splits: 70 subjects total: 10 calibration/training subjects (IDs prefixed CT-Training) and 60 test subjects (IDs prefixed LUNGx).
details.extra: This was a challenge for computer-aided diagnosis (benign vs. malignant classification) rather than segmentation; participants received only nodule center coordinates, not delineated contours or masks.

name: VinDr-SpineXR
full_name: VinDr-SpineXR: A large annotated dataset for spinal lesions detection and classification from radiographs
protocol_note: Spine radiographs (cervical, thoracic, lumbar) in DICOM collected from PACS of Hanoi Medical University Hospital and Hospital 108, 2011-2020
size: 10,466 spine X-ray images from 5,000 studies
segmentation_detail: Radiologist-drawn bounding boxes marking lesions (localization, not pixel-level masks)
description: A dataset of 10,466 spine radiographs (DICOM) from 5,000 studies with radiologist bounding-box annotations for 13 types of spinal abnormalities for lesion detection and classification.

label_schema: Detection task: radiologist-drawn bounding boxes each tagged with one of 13 lesion/abnormality classes: Ankylosis
Image-level classification label: 'No finding' (normal) vs 'Abnormal' (image contains >=1 lesion); no-finding images have a single row with empty box coordinates
13 spinal abnormality categories (fracture, osteophytes, disc space narrowing, vertebral collapse, etc.)
details.file_structure: DICOM images in train_images/ and test_images/ folders; annotations in annotations/train.csv and test.csv, where each row is one lesion instance with image_id, series_id, study_id, rad_id (rad1/rad2/rad3), lesion_type, and box coords xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax (bounding boxes only, no pixel masks).
details.splits: Train: 8,389 images from 4,000 studies; Test: 2,077 images from 1,000 studies (total 10,466 images from 5,000 studies).
details.extra: Each abnormal image was read and annotated by a single radiologist (rad_id identifies which of 3 experienced radiologists); labels are localization boxes, not segmentation masks.

name: CheXlocalize
full_name: CheXlocalize: Radiologist-annotated segmentations for chest X-ray pathology localization
protocol_note: CheXpert validation and test set chest radiographs (frontal and lateral views), JPEG
size: 234 validation images (200 patients) and 668 test images (500 patients)
segmentation_detail: Radiologist ground-truth pixel-level segmentations (RLE-encoded) for 10 pathologies, plus most-representative-point benchmark segmentations and Grad-CAM saliency heatmaps
license: MIT (code); CheXpert images via Stanford AIMI agreement
description: CheXlocalize provides CheXpert chest X-ray images with radiologist pixel-level ground-truth segmentations and saliency heatmaps for evaluating localization of 10 thoracic pathologies.

label_schema: Radiologist ground-truth pixel-level segmentation masks (binary, one per image-pathology pair) for 10 chest pathologies: Atelectasis
Also provided: model saliency-heatmap segmentations (Grad-CAM from a DenseNet121 CheXpert classifier) and human-benchmark 'most-representative-point' segmentations for the same 10 pathologies
binary presence/absence for 10 pathologies (atelectasis, cardiomegaly, consolidation, edema, enlarged cardiomediastinum, lung lesion, lung opacity, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, support devices)
details.file_structure: Chest X-rays are the CheXpert JPGs (referenced by CXR ID); segmentations are stored in JSON files keyed by CXR ID then pathology name, where each mask is a pycocotools RLE object {'size':[h,w], 'counts':'...'}; raw human annotations are also provided as nested polygon-contour coordinate lists in JSON (multiple contours per pathology for multiple instances).
details.splits: No training set (models trained on CheXpert); segmentation ground truth covers a validation set of 234 CXRs (from 200 patients) and a held-out test set of 668 CXRs (from 500 patients).
details.extra: Ground-truth masks were drawn by two board-certified radiologists; a separate group of three radiologists produced the human-benchmark segmentations, enabling human-vs-model saliency localization comparison.

related.name: CheXpert
related.note: Radiologist pixel-level segmentations and most-representative points added to CheXpert validation (234 CXRs) and test (668 CXRs) images

name: OPTIMAM (OMI-DB)
full_name: OPTIMAM Mammography Image Database
protocol_note: Includes both 2D full-field digital mammography and 3D digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT)
size: ~750,000 cases (2D full-field digital mammography and 3D tomosynthesis)
segmentation_detail: Expert lesion annotations/markings available for a subset (localization, not full pixel masks)
license: Sharing agreement via Cancer Research Horizons
description: The OPTIMAM Medical Image Database is a large collection of ~750,000 NHS Breast Screening Programme mammography and tomosynthesis cases (DICOM) with cancer outcomes and expert annotations, available to research groups via a Data Access Committee application.

label_schema: Case-level cancer status: screen-detected cancer / interval cancer / normal / benign (also non-malignant follow-ups)
Lesion markings: rectangular regions of interest (bounding boxes) giving location and area of each lesion (localization, not pixel masks)
Per-marking attributes: radiologic appearance/lesion type (e.g., mass, calcification) and conspicuity, recorded at initial read and at assessment
Pathology / clinical labels: biopsy results, surgical outcomes, screening history and prior cancer occurrences from the National Breast Screening System
details.file_structure: Mammograms are stored as de-identified DICOM images with DICOM tags extracted into a searchable index; expert lesion markings (rectangular ROI coordinates plus attribute fields) and associated clinical/pathology data are held in linked relational-database/metadata records rather than DICOM-SEG or RTSTRUCT masks.
details.extra: As of May 2020 the database held ~3,072,878 images from 172,282 women with 7,661 screen-detected cancers; only a subset of cancers were marked (~5,097, about 67%), and access requires a formal data-sharing application.

name: mini-MIAS
full_name: Mammographic Image Analysis Society Digital Mammogram Database
protocol_note: Films from the UK National Breast Screening Programme digitised at 50 micron with a Joyce-Loebl scanning microdensitometer (8-bit); mini-MIAS reduced to 200 micron pixel edge and padded/clipped to 1024x1024.
size: 322 images (~2.3 GB original; ~100 MB distributed)
description: A classic openly available database of 322 digitised screening mammograms (1024x1024, 200-micron) with radiologist truth-markings of abnormality location, class, and severity.

label_schema: SEVERITY: B (benign) or M (malignant), given only for abnormal cases
Abnormality location: image x,y coordinates of the abnormality centre plus an approximate radius (pixels) of a circle enclosing it
abnormality class (calcification, masses, architectural distortion, asymmetry, normal)
details.file_structure: 322 grayscale mammogram images (mdb001-mdb322) as 1024x1024 8-bit PGM files (~200 micron pixels); a single plain-text annotation file (info.txt / All-MIAS README) lists one row per image with 7 whitespace-separated fields: REFNUM, background-tissue character, abnormality class, severity, x, y, radius (coordinate/severity/radius fields omitted for NORM images).
details.extra: Region-level ground truth is given only as a centre point + enclosing-circle radius (no pixel-wise segmentation masks); NORM rows and some diffuse abnormalities have no coordinates.

name: MOOD
full_name: Medical Out-of-Distribution Analysis Challenge
protocol_note: Brain scans are T2-weighted MRI; abdominal scans are CT (one modality per anatomy)
size: ~800 brain MRI + ~600 abdominal CT scans
description: A benchmark of normal brain MRI and abdominal CT volumes for unsupervised out-of-distribution and anomaly detection, evaluated at both sample and pixel level.

label_schema: This is an unsupervised out-of-distribution (OoD)/anomaly-detection benchmark, so training scans carry NO labels (only healthy/normal volumes are provided); ground-truth labels exist only for the toy and hidden test cases
Sample-level task label: one binary integer per scan stored in a .txt file - 0 = in-distribution/normal, 1 = out-of-distribution/anomalous
Pixel-level task label: a per-voxel binary anomaly mask stored as NIfTI, same shape as the input volume - voxel value 1 = anomalous, 0 = normal
Corresponding predictions mirror the labels: sample-level = a single float anomaly score clipped to [0,1] in a .txt file; pixel-level = a per-voxel anomaly score volume clipped to [0,1] as NIfTI
out-of-distribution / anomaly (sample-level and voxel-level scoring on hidden test set)
details.file_structure: Images are single-channel NIfTI (.nii.gz) 3D volumes organized by anatomy into two roots (brain/ and colon/ = abdominal); each has an unlabeled training folder (brain_train/, colon_train/) of normal scans plus toy/ (synthetic-anomaly test volumes) and toy_label/ holding matching ground truth (NIfTI binary masks for the pixel task, .txt integer files for the sample task).
details.extra: Two independent anatomies - brain MRI and abdominal CT; evaluated with AUROC/average-precision via sklearn over voxel scores (pixel task) or per-sample scores (sample task); submissions run as Docker containers. Verified from the official MIC-DKFZ/mood repo (scripts/evalresults.py and repo folder layout); exact per-set scan counts and native voxel dimensions could not be confirmed from fetchable sources so splits left null.

related.name: Human Connectome Project Young Adult
related.note: Brain T2w MRI volumes reportedly drawn from HCP and repackaged as NIfTI for the challenge

related.name: CT Colonography (ACRIN 6664)
related.note: Abdominal CT volumes reportedly drawn from the TCIA CT colonography collection and repackaged as NIfTI

name: QUBIQ
full_name: Quantification of Uncertainty in Biomedical Image Segmentation
protocol_note: Spans MRI (brain growth, brain tumor, prostate, kidney) and CT (pancreas) across 2D and 3D tasks
size: Multiple tasks across brain, kidney, prostate and pancreas (dozens of cases per task)
segmentation_detail: Binary segmentation tasks each with multiple annotations from several domain-expert raters to capture inter-rater uncertainty
description: A multi-organ, multi-modality (MRI/CT) segmentation benchmark providing multiple expert annotations per case to quantify segmentation uncertainty.

label_schema: All tasks are BINARY segmentation masks (value 1 = target structure, 0 = background), stored as .nii/.nii.gz; each case carries multiple independent expert annotations (masks) rather than one consensus label, to capture inter-rater uncertainty
Brain growth - 1 task, 7 annotations per case (MRI)
Brain tumor - 3 separate binary tasks per case (task01/task02/task03, different tumor sub-region definitions), 3 annotations per case (multimodal MRI, 4 MR modalities)
Prostate - 2 separate binary tasks per case (task01/task02), 6 annotations per case (one case has 5) (MRI)
Pancreas / pancreatic lesion - binary task(s) added in later QUBIQ edition (CT)
details.file_structure: Data is organized per-organ into case folders (e.g. brain-tumor/case##, prostate/case##), each holding one .nii/.nii.gz image file plus one binary label file per task per rater (taskNN filenames); brain-tumor image files bundle slices from all four MR modalities; predictions are submitted as a Results/ tree mirroring organ/case/taskNN.nii.gz.
details.splits: No fixed published counts as a single train/val/test table; per-organ case totals in the released set: prostate 55, brain growth 39, brain tumor 32, kidney 24. Challenge protocol released labeled training data, a validation set for the leaderboard, and a held-out test set of roughly 20% of cases per task.
details.extra: Multi-edition MICCAI challenge (QUBIQ 2020/2021) benchmarking uncertainty quantification in segmentation; datasets span 2D and 3D and modalities MRI and CT. Cite arXiv:2405.18435 and the QUBIQ Grand Challenge page.

name: Prostate-3T
full_name: Prostate-3T
protocol_note: Transversal T2-weighted MRI only, acquired on 3.0T Siemens TrioTim
size: 59 subjects, 1161 images (~269 MB)
segmentation_detail: Structure segmentations available including central gland, peripheral zone, neurovascular bundle, and seminal vesicles (MHA/NRRD)
description: An openly downloadable TCIA collection of transversal T2-weighted 3T prostate MRI from 59 patients with structure segmentations.

details.file_structure: MR images are stored as DICOM per subject; expert segmentations are provided as separate downloadable ZIP packages of volumetric label files (central gland and peripheral zone as NRRD from the NCI-ISBI 2013 challenge; neurovascular bundle and seminal vesicles as MHA), constructed in MeVisLab.
details.extra: Collection contains 64 subjects (3T MR). The CG/PZ segmentations originate from the NCI-ISBI 2013 Automated Segmentation of Prostate Structures challenge; the exact integer label-value-to-structure mapping is not documented on the official page and must be read from the NRRD/MHA files themselves.

name: AeroPath
full_name: AeroPath Airway Segmentation Benchmark Dataset
protocol_note: 27 thoracic CT scans (high-resolution, '_CT_HR'); contrast phase not stated.
size: 27 CT scans (~5 GB)
segmentation_detail: Voxel-level airway and lung annotations, including cases with challenging pathology
description: An openly available benchmark of 27 thoracic CT scans with airway and lung segmentations, including cases with challenging pulmonary pathology.

label_schema: Airway segmentation - binary mask (trachea and bronchi); 1 = airway, 0 = background, stored as *_label_airways.nii.gz
Lung segmentation - binary mask; 1 = lungs, 0 = background, stored as *_label_lungs.nii.gz
details.file_structure: One folder per case (1/ through 27/), each containing the CT volume (N_CT_HR.nii.gz) plus two separate binary NIfTI label masks (N_CT_HR_label_airways.nii.gz and N_CT_HR_label_lungs.nii.gz); all files are compressed NIfTI (.nii.gz).
details.extra: 27 chest CT cases, many with challenging airway pathology (e.g. stenosis, tumors, atelectasis); distributed via GitHub/Zenodo and the Hugging Face Hub (andreped/AeroPath), where all cases are exposed under a single 'test' split rather than train/val/test partitions.

name: AIIB23
full_name: Airway-Informed Quantitative CT Imaging Biomarker for Fibrotic Lung Disease Challenge 2023
protocol_note: High-resolution CT (HRCT) of fibrotic lung disease patients, DICOM converted to NIfTI
segmentation_detail: Voxel-level airway (bronchial tree) segmentation annotations on CT of fibrotic lung disease patients
description: A MICCAI 2023 challenge dataset of thoracic CT scans with airway segmentation annotations aimed at quantitative imaging biomarkers for fibrotic lung disease.

label_schema: Task I (airway segmentation): binary 3D voxel mask of the airway tree — Label 1 = airway (bronchial tree lumen), Label 0 = background
Task II (mortality prediction): per-case mortality/survival status provided as clinical metadata for training cases (used as a prognostication target, not a voxel label)
details.file_structure: HRCT scans were collected in DICOM and released as NIfTI volumes (converted via SimpleITK), each paired with a same-geometry NIfTI binary airway segmentation mask; mortality status and clinical metadata (from OSIC) accompany the training cases.
details.splits: Task I: 120 training / 52 online-validation / 140 offline-test (90 fibrosis + 50 COVID-19); Task II uses 95 training / 52 validation / 140 test. Only the 120 OSIC training cases (images + airway masks + mortality status) were publicly released; validation and test ground-truth were held out for CodaLab/Docker evaluation.
details.extra: First public airway dataset for fibrotic lung disease. Annotations were AI-preinitialized (BAS-trained model) then revised by three junior and refined by two senior radiologists in ITK-SNAP; inter-observer agreement Cohen's Kappa = 0.937. License CC-BY-NC-ND.

name: TCGA-KIRC
full_name: The Cancer Genome Atlas Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma
protocol_note: MRI studies include multiple sequences; collection spans CT, MR, and computed radiography series
paired_text_detail: Extensive matched clinical, demographic, pathological, and genomic data available via the NCI Genomic Data Commons (GDC) Data Portal through matched patient identifiers
description: Radiology imaging (CT, MRI, and computed radiography) of 267 kidney renal clear cell carcinoma patients from The Cancer Genome Atlas, paired with matched clinical and genomic data.

label_schema: Cohort/classification label: kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (ccRCC) patients; matched TCGA clinical, genomic, and pathology labels available via the Genomic Data Commons using shared patient IDs (not stored in the imaging files)
The base imaging collection ships with NO per-image or per-voxel labels (radiology DICOM only)
Segmentation classes from the linked BAMF AIMI Annotations analysis result (contrast-enhanced CT): Kidney
BAMF AIMI segmentation class: Tumor (kidney tumor)
BAMF AIMI segmentation class: Cyst (kidney cyst)
Crowds-Cure-2017 analysis result: reader-placed lesion annotations/measurements (crowdsourced radiologist markups)
details.file_structure: Images are DICOM organized per patient (267 subjects / 439 studies / 2,654 series; modalities CT, MR, CR). No labels are bundled with the base collection; segmentation labels are distributed separately as the BAMF AIMI Annotations analysis result in DICOM-SEG format (kidney-ct, hosted on Zenodo at 10.5281/zenodo.8345959) with an accompanying qa-results.csv, and Crowds-Cure-2017 annotations are a separate downloadable result.
details.extra: Segmentation labels are AI-generated (BAMF nnU-Net-style model); ~10% of predictions were reviewed by board-certified radiologists with Likert-scale quality scores recorded in qa-results.csv. Integer label values per DICOM-SEG segment were not confirmed from the source and are omitted.
details.reference_standard: Cohort = TCGA kidney renal clear cell carcinoma cases (tissue-based TCGA diagnosis); clinical, genomic and pathology data via GDC

label_variants.name: BAMF AIMI annotations (kidney/tumor/cyst CT)
label_variants.note: AI-generated masks with ~10% radiologist review (IDC Zenodo)

label_variants.name: TCGA-KIRC-Radiogenomics
label_variants.note: TCIA analysis result

label_variants.name: Crowds-Cure-2017
label_variants.note: crowdsourced radiologist lesion markups

details.third_party_note: CC BY 3.0 permits redistribution with attribution; no clause restricting external services (TCIA Data Usage Policy additionally requires citation).

name: OASIS-2
full_name: Open Access Series of Imaging Studies 2 (Longitudinal MRI in Nondemented and Demented Older Adults)
protocol_note: T1-weighted MRI only (3-4 T1 acquisitions per session)
size: 150 subjects, 373 imaging sessions
paired_text_detail: Dementia status and clinical/cognitive data: 72 nondemented, 64 demented at baseline (51 with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's), 14 converters; includes CDR ratings, MMSE, age, and other metadata
license: Non-commercial academic research use only (OASIS data use terms)
description: Longitudinal T1-weighted brain MRI of 150 older adults (aged 60-96) across 373 sessions, labeled with dementia/Alzheimer's status for studying age-related and pathological brain change.

label_schema: Clinical/demographic labels per imaging session (no per-voxel segmentation ground truth). Key label columns:
Group - diagnostic status: Nondemented / Demented / Converted (nondemented at baseline then demented at follow-up)
Visit - visit number; MR Delay - days between baseline and this session
details.file_structure: Per-subject/per-session folders named OAS2_XXXX_MRn (e.g., OAS2_0001_MR1), each containing 3-4 raw T1-weighted MRI scans plus FSL-processed derivatives (motion-corrected/averaged, atlas-registered, brain-masked, and FSL tissue-segmented GM/WM/CSF), distributed as Analyze 7.5 format (.img/.hdr) inside tar.gz archives (~18 GB total); labels are supplied in a separate demographic/clinical spreadsheet (commonly distributed as oasis_longitudinal.csv) keyed by Subject ID and MRI ID.
details.extra: 150 subjects aged 60-96 with 373 total imaging sessions (>=2 visits >=1 year apart); groups: 72 nondemented throughout, 64 demented at baseline (51 with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's), 14 converted from nondemented to demented. This is a longitudinal cohort intended for dementia classification/progression rather than organ segmentation.

name: NAKO
full_name: NAKO Gesundheitsstudie (German National Cohort)
anatomy: Whole-body coverage including brain, heart, abdominal organs (liver, pancreas), spine, knee joints and vasculature
protocol_note: Standardized 3T whole-body protocol (Siemens Skyra): brain T1 MPRAGE, FLAIR, T2*, TOF-MRA, DTI, resting-state fMRI; cardiac cine; whole-body T1 Dixon (VIBE); abdominal/liver PDFF; spine and knee sequences.
size: ~30,000 imaging participants (of 205,000 total cohort)
segmentation_detail: No public voxel-wise labels released; central image-analysis working groups generate derived quantitative measures (organ volumes, fat fractions) for approved projects.
paired_text_detail: No routine free-text radiology reports; standardized incidental-findings assessments and derived quantitative image parameters are provided instead.
clinical_variables: Extensive linkable data including anthropometry, blood pressure, ECG, spirometry, laboratory biomarkers, cognitive testing, questionnaires on lifestyle/diet/medication, genome-wide genotyping and omics from biosamples, plus follow-up of incident cardiometabolic disease, cancer, and mortality.
description: Germany's largest population cohort with a standardized 3T whole-body MRI sub-study in ~30,000 participants linkable to deep phenotyping, labs, genetics and outcomes.

name: SHIP
full_name: Study of Health in Pomerania
anatomy: Whole-body coverage including brain, heart, liver, kidney, spleen and abdominal organs, major vessels, and optional breast (mammography) imaging
protocol_note: Standardized 1.5T whole-body MRI protocol (Siemens Magnetom Avanto): brain structural imaging and MR angiography, cardiac cine (optional), abdominal Dixon/liver-fat and organ sequences, and whole-body sequences; optional mammography for women.
size: ~3,300 whole-body MRI participants (SHIP-2 and SHIP-TREND); ~15,000 total cohort participants
segmentation_detail: Derived organ and body-fat measures produced for approved projects; no public voxel-level segmentation labels released.
paired_text_detail: Standardized incidental-findings documentation and derived quantitative parameters rather than clinical free-text radiology reports.
clinical_variables: Linkable anthropometry, blood pressure, laboratory panels, oral/dental health, thyroid ultrasound, medications, lifestyle and dietary questionnaires, genome-wide genotyping, metabolomics and other omics, and follow-up of cardiometabolic disease, cancer and mortality.
host: University Medicine Greifswald - SHIP Transfer Office (Forschungsverbund Community Medicine)
description: Longstanding population-based cohort from Northeast Germany (West Pomerania) offering standardized whole-body 1.5T MRI linkable to deep phenotyping, biobank samples and long-term outcome follow-up, accessible by research application to the SHIP Transfer Office.

name: Rhineland Study
full_name: Rhineland Study (DZNE Bonn)
anatomy: Brain (structural, microstructural, functional, perfusion) and abdomen for body-composition (visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue)
protocol_note: 3T protocol: T1 MPRAGE, FLAIR, multi-shell DTI, resting-state fMRI, ASL perfusion, and QSM/susceptibility for the brain, plus abdominal Dixon imaging for adipose-tissue and body-composition quantification (visceral vs subcutaneous fat).
size: ~20,000-participant target (>10,000 enrolled)
segmentation_detail: Derived brain morphometry and body-composition metrics generated for approved analyses; no released voxel-level masks.
paired_text_detail: Standardized incidental-findings review and derived imaging measures; no free-text radiology reports for research use.
clinical_variables: Linkable cognitive and physical-performance testing, cardiometabolic measures (ECG, blood pressure, metabolic-syndrome risk), retinal/OCT imaging, blood labs, medications, extensive lifestyle/environmental questionnaires, and genome-wide genotyping/omics with repeated follow-up visits.
host: German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE), Bonn
description: Prospective Bonn population cohort combining deep multimodal brain MRI with abdominal body-composition MRI and repeated follow-up for healthy-aging research.

name: Hamburg City Health Study
full_name: Hamburg City Health Study (HCHS)
protocol_note: 3T cardiac cine and mapping in imaged participants plus a multimodal brain MRI sub-study (structural T1, FLAIR, DTI) and carotid MR imaging.
size: ~45,000-participant target (>17,000 enrolled)
segmentation_detail: Cardiac function parameters and white-matter/brain volumetric metrics derived centrally for approved projects; voxel-level segmentation masks not routinely distributed.
paired_text_detail: Standardized incidental-findings assessment and centrally derived cardiac/brain metrics rather than free-text clinical radiology reports.
clinical_variables: Linkable deep phenotyping including ECG, echocardiography and vascular function, blood/urine labs, lung function, cognitive testing, medications, lifestyle and medical-history questionnaires, genotyping/omics, and follow-up of incident cardiovascular events and mortality.
description: Large Hamburg population cohort with cardiac MRI in imaged participants and a multimodal brain and carotid MRI sub-study linkable to deep cardiovascular and neurological phenotyping.

name: Rotterdam Study
full_name: Rotterdam Study (Erasmus Rotterdam Gezondheid Onderzoek, ERGO)
anatomy: Brain (repeated 1.5T MRI) plus whole-body/regional DXA for bone mineral density and fat/lean body composition
protocol_note: 1.5T brain MRI protocol (T1, proton density, FLAIR, plus diffusion and gradient-echo sequences in extended waves) repeated across visits; DXA for bone density and fat/lean mass.
size: ~20,000 participants aged 40+ enrolled overall; ~5,000+ with repeated brain MRI
segmentation_detail: Brain tissue, white-matter lesion and microbleed volumes derived centrally; DXA provides quantitative fat/lean body-composition output.
paired_text_detail: Research imaging with centrally derived phenotypes and incidental-findings documentation; no clinical radiology report distribution.
clinical_variables: Linkable cardiometabolic measures, blood/urine laboratory markers, cognitive and physical testing, medication and pharmacy records, genome-wide genotyping and omics, and long-term follow-up of dementia, stroke, cardiovascular disease, cancer and mortality.
description: Classic Dutch aging population cohort with repeated 1.5T brain MRI and DXA body composition linkable to decades of clinical, genetic and mortality follow-up.

name: Generation R
full_name: Generation R Study
anatomy: Developing brain plus cardiac, lung and hip MRI, and whole-body DXA for pediatric body composition
protocol_note: 3T pediatric brain MRI (T1, DTI, resting-state fMRI) repeated at Focus visits (ages ~9, 13, 17); additional cardiac, lung and hip MRI; whole-body DXA for fat and lean mass.
size: ~several thousand children with repeated brain MRI and DXA (birth cohort of ~9,700 mothers/children)
segmentation_detail: Brain morphometry and DXA body-composition measures derived centrally; voxel-level segmentation masks not routinely distributed.
paired_text_detail: Research pediatric imaging with centrally derived phenotypes; incidental findings reviewed clinically but radiology reports are not distributed as part of the dataset.
clinical_variables: Linkable prenatal/perinatal records, anthropometry and growth trajectories, cardiometabolic measures, cognition/behavior assessments, laboratory/blood and urine biomarkers, genome-wide genotyping and omics, and extensive parental and lifestyle questionnaires across repeated visits.
description: Population-based birth cohort with repeated pediatric brain MRI and whole-body DXA body composition from childhood through adolescence, accessible via collaborative application.

name: The Maastricht Study
full_name: The Maastricht Study
anatomy: Brain (3T MRI: structural/T1, FLAIR, diffusion); the cohort also includes extensive non-imaging cardiometabolic, vascular (ultrasound), and retinal phenotyping
protocol_note: 3T brain MRI protocol including structural (T1), FLAIR, and diffusion-weighted sequences.
size: ~10,000 participants (deep-phenotyping cohort target)
segmentation_detail: Derived brain volumetric and cerebral small-vessel-disease measures generated for approved projects; no distributed voxel segmentation masks confirmed.
paired_text_detail: No free-text radiology reports; standardized incidental-findings assessment and derived imaging parameters only.
clinical_variables: Linkable oral glucose tolerance test/glycemic status, extensive cardiometabolic and vascular function measures, blood/urine labs, retinal imaging, carotid ultrasound, medications, lifestyle and accelerometry data, biobank genotyping/omics, and outcome follow-up.
description: Deeply phenotyped Dutch population cohort enriched for type 2 diabetes with 3T brain MRI linkable to extensive cardiometabolic, vascular, and biobank data.

name: ALSPAC
full_name: Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (Children of the 90s)
anatomy: Whole-body and regional DXA for body composition and bone, plus brain MRI (structural/functional/DTI/MT) in ~900-participant sub-studies
protocol_note: Repeated whole-body DXA across childhood and adulthood; brain MRI sub-studies include structural MRI, functional MRI, diffusion tensor imaging and magnetization transfer MRI (plus MEG).
size: ~14,000 index children (thousands with repeated DXA; ~900 with brain MRI at 18-24y)
segmentation_detail: DXA yields quantitative fat/lean/bone output; MRI-derived measures produced per sub-study; no distributed voxel segmentations.
paired_text_detail: Derived DXA body-composition variables and MRI-derived phenotypes documented in variable catalogues; no clinical radiology reports distributed.
clinical_variables: Linkable anthropometry and growth, cardiometabolic and pubertal measures, blood/biochemistry labs, cognition, extensive questionnaires, genome-wide genotyping and omics, and record linkage to health, hospitalization and mortality outcomes.
description: Landmark British birth cohort with repeated whole-body DXA body-composition scans across the life course and targeted brain MRI sub-studies, richly linkable to phenotype, health outcomes and genetics.

name: Tromsø Study
full_name: The Tromsø Study
anatomy: Whole-body/regional DXA for body composition and bone density, plus brain in an MRI sub-study
protocol_note: Whole-body and regional DXA for fat, lean and bone mineral across waves (hip DEXA and forearm SXA in Tromsø 4-6, whole-body DXA body composition in Tromsø 7) plus a brain MRI sub-study.
size: Tens of thousands of participants across seven survey waves (DXA and brain MRI collected in sub-samples)
segmentation_detail: DXA quantitative body-composition output; brain metrics derived in the MRI sub-study; no distributed voxel segmentations.
paired_text_detail: Derived DXA body-composition/bone measures and MRI-derived phenotypes; no clinical report distribution.
clinical_variables: Linkable cardiometabolic and anthropometric measures, blood and biochemical labs, medications, lifestyle and dietary questionnaires, genotyping/omics, and linkage to Norwegian health, cancer and cause-of-death registries.
host: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
description: Repeated Norwegian population survey with DXA body composition and bone density and a brain MRI sub-study, linkable to national health, cancer and mortality registries.

name: KORA-MRI
full_name: Cooperative Health Research in the Region of Augsburg – Whole-Body MRI sub-study (KORA-FF4)
anatomy: Whole-body coverage including heart, liver/pancreas, visceral and subcutaneous adipose depots, brain, spine, vasculature and knee
protocol_note: 3T whole-body protocol (Siemens Magnetom Skyra) including cardiac cine/mapping, T1 Dixon for adipose tissue, liver and pancreas PDFF/proton-density fat fraction, brain, spine, MR angiography and knee sequences.
size: ~400 participants (whole-body MRI sub-study of KORA-FF4)
segmentation_detail: Central derivation of visceral/subcutaneous adipose depots, hepatic and pancreatic fat, and cardiac function measures for approved projects; per-voxel segmentation masks not distributed by default.
paired_text_detail: No radiology reports; standardized incidental-findings review and centrally derived quantitative measures only.
clinical_variables: Linkable oral glucose tolerance test / glycemic status, cardiometabolic and anthropometric measures, laboratory panels, medications, lifestyle questionnaires, genome-wide genotyping, metabolomics and other omics, and prospective disease/outcome follow-up.
host: Helmholtz Munich (KORA), via KORA.PASST project agreement
description: Deeply phenotyped Augsburg population sub-cohort with whole-body 3T MRI enabling opportunistic body-composition and organ-fat quantification.

name: SCAPIS
full_name: Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study
anatomy: Coronary arteries and heart, lungs, carotid arteries, and abdominal body-composition (visceral/subcutaneous fat and muscle)
protocol_note: Coronary CT angiography, coronary artery calcium CT, and low-dose chest/lung CT, plus abdominal body-composition CT; complemented by carotid ultrasound.
size: ~30,000 participants
segmentation_detail: No public voxel segmentation masks; coronary calcium scores, plaque, lung metrics and body-composition variables (VAT, subcutaneous fat, muscle) derived centrally for approved projects.
paired_text_detail: Standardized central image reading and derived quantitative scores (e.g., coronary calcium, plaque, lung and body-composition measures); no free-text radiology report distribution.
clinical_variables: Linkable cardiometabolic and pulmonary function measures, laboratory tests, ECG, medications, anthropometry, lifestyle and diet questionnaires, genotyping/omics, and linkage to Swedish national health, cancer and cause-of-death registries.
host: SCAPIS (Swedish national consortium); imaging distributed via AIDA, Linkoping University
description: Large Swedish population imaging cohort (~30,000) with coronary CT angiography, calcium scoring, lung CT and abdominal body-composition CT, linkable to deep phenotyping and national health registries.

name: AGES-Reykjavik
full_name: Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility – Reykjavik Study
anatomy: Brain (structural MRI) and quantitative CT of the thigh and abdomen for skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, plus coronary/aortic calcium CT
protocol_note: 1.5T brain MRI (T1/PD/T2 structural, FLAIR, gradient-echo/SWI for microbleeds); quantitative CT of the mid-thigh and abdomen for muscle area, muscle attenuation/fat infiltration and visceral/subcutaneous fat; coronary and aortic calcium CT.
size: ~5,764 participants (baseline); brain MRI in most, thigh/abdomen QCT in sub-samples
segmentation_detail: Brain tissue and white-matter lesion volumes and CT-based muscle and fat areas were derived centrally; per-image segmentation masks not the primary distributed product.
paired_text_detail: Research imaging with centrally derived quantitative phenotypes; no clinical radiology report distribution.
clinical_variables: Linkable cardiometabolic measures (blood pressure, lipids, glucose/diabetes), cognitive and dementia assessments, bone density and body composition, extensive labs, medications, lifestyle and diet questionnaires, genome-wide genotyping and other omics, and long-term follow-up of cardiovascular disease, fractures, dementia and mortality.
host: Icelandic Heart Association (in collaboration with US National Institute on Aging)
description: Icelandic population aging cohort combining brain MRI with quantitative thigh/abdominal CT for muscle and fat, linkable to genetics and long-term health outcomes.

name: LIFE-Adult
full_name: Leipzig Research Centre for Civilization Diseases – LIFE-Adult Study
protocol_note: 3T brain MRI protocol including T1 MPRAGE, FLAIR, DTI, resting-state fMRI and time-of-flight angiography.
size: ~2,600 participants with 3T brain MRI (of ~10,000-participant cohort)
segmentation_detail: No public voxel masks; brain volumetrics and white-matter hyperintensity measures derived centrally for approved projects.
paired_text_detail: No radiology reports; standardized incidental-findings review and centrally derived imaging phenotypes only.
clinical_variables: Linkable cardiometabolic and anthropometric measures (incl. 3D laser body scanning), laboratory biomarkers (lipoproteins, steroid hormones, leukocyte subsets), carotid ultrasound, cognitive and psychological assessments, ophthalmologic and sleep phenotypes, medications, lifestyle questionnaires, and genome-wide genotyping.
host: Leipzig University – LIFE Research Centre for Civilization Diseases
description: Leipzig urban population cohort of ~10,000 deeply phenotyped adults with a large 3T brain MRI sub-study linkable to metabolic, cognitive, cardiovascular and genetic phenotyping, accessible to researchers by application via the LIFE Data Portal.

name: Fenland Study
full_name: Fenland Study (MRC Epidemiology Unit, University of Cambridge)
anatomy: Whole-body and regional adiposity, hepatic fat, and bone/body composition assessed by DXA (with liver ultrasound)
protocol_note: DEXA body-composition data (derived metrics); liver ultrasound scores not currently available for Phase 3.
size: ~12,435 participants
paired_text_detail: No clinical radiology reports distributed; derived body-composition, DEXA and biochemistry metrics only.
clinical_variables: Linkable oral glucose tolerance test (glucose, insulin, C-peptide, leptin, adiponectin), HbA1c, lipids, liver function and vitamin C biochemistry, objectively measured physical activity and cardiorespiratory fitness, anthropometry, grip strength, Intake24 nutrition, genome-wide genotyping/GWAS and metabolomics, and health/lifestyle questionnaires.
host: MRC Epidemiology Unit, University of Cambridge
description: Cambridgeshire population cohort (n=12,435) with DEXA body-composition and liver ultrasound linkable to detailed metabolic, physical-activity and genetic phenotyping, available to researchers by application.

name: Whitehall II Imaging Sub-study
full_name: Whitehall II Imaging Sub-study (Oxford / UCL)
protocol_note: 3T multimodal brain MRI including T1-weighted, T2/FLAIR, T2*/susceptibility-weighted, diffusion MRI, resting-state fMRI and task fMRI.
size: ~800 participants (brain MRI sub-study of the Whitehall II cohort)
segmentation_detail: No public voxel segmentation masks; brain morphometric, white-matter-hyperintensity, diffusion and functional-connectivity measures derived centrally.
paired_text_detail: Research multimodal brain MRI with centrally derived imaging phenotypes; no clinical radiology reports distributed.
clinical_variables: Linkable repeated Whitehall II phase measures: cardiometabolic risk factors (blood pressure, lipids, glucose/diabetes, adiposity), cognitive testing, blood biomarkers, socioeconomic and lifestyle factors, medications, and long-term follow-up of morbidity and mortality via record linkage.
host: Dementias Platform UK (DPUK) Data Portal / University of Oxford (WIN-FMRIB) / UCL
description: Multimodal 3T brain MRI sub-study of roughly 800 participants from the British Whitehall II civil-servant cohort, linkable to decades of life-course cardiometabolic, cognitive and lifestyle data, with access via the DPUK Data Portal.

name: Heinz Nixdorf Recall / 1000BRAINS
full_name: Heinz Nixdorf Recall Study and 1000BRAINS MRI cohort
protocol_note: Cardiac/coronary CT for calcium scoring plus multimodal 3T brain MRI (T1, FLAIR, DTI, resting-state fMRI) in the 1000BRAINS sub-study.
size: ~4,800 base cohort (Recall); ~1,300 in 1000BRAINS MRI sub-study
segmentation_detail: Coronary calcium scores and brain volumetric/connectivity measures derived centrally; no distributed voxel segmentation masks.
paired_text_detail: Centrally standardized image reading and derived scores; no free-text clinical report distribution.
clinical_variables: Linkable cardiometabolic and vascular measures, blood/urine labs, ECG, blood pressure, anthropometry, cognition (1000BRAINS), medications, lifestyle and environmental exposure questionnaires, genotyping, and prospective follow-up of cardiovascular events and mortality.
description: German Ruhr-area population cohort pairing coronary artery calcium CT with the 1000BRAINS multimodal brain MRI sub-study, linkable to deep cardiometabolic and cognitive phenotyping.

name: MESA
full_name: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis
anatomy: Heart, coronary arteries, thoracic aorta, carotid arteries, abdominal fat depots
protocol_note: Cardiac MRI protocol includes cine SSFP for ventricular mass/function plus tagged MRI for strain; separate cardiac/chest CT (EBCT and multidetector CT) for coronary calcium; carotid MRI and ultrasound in ancillary studies.
size: 6,814 participants
segmentation_detail: No public voxel-level masks distributed; reading centers produced quantitative measures (LV mass/volumes, Agatston calcium scores, VAT/SAT areas) rather than shareable segmentation masks.
paired_text_detail: No radiology narrative reports; imaging is paired with quantitative reading-center measurements and extensive clinical/exam datasets rather than free-text reports.
clinical_variables: Standard CVD risk factors (blood pressure, lipids, glucose/diabetes, smoking), ECG, inflammatory/metabolic biomarkers and stored blood, sociodemographics, medications, genome-wide genotyping and other omics, and adjudicated incident CVD events, hospitalization and mortality through 2020.
host: NHLBI BioLINCC / MESA Coordinating Center (dbGaP phs000209 for genetics)
description: A six-center prospective multi-ethnic cohort of ~6,814 adults aged 45-84 with serial cardiac MRI, coronary/chest CT and vascular imaging linked to deep cardiovascular phenotyping and event follow-up.

name: COPDGene
full_name: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD Study
anatomy: Lungs, airways, and thoracic musculature/adipose tissue (pectoralis muscle, subcutaneous and intrathoracic fat) captured on chest CT
protocol_note: Volumetric inspiratory and expiratory chest CT acquired across multiple study phases enabling emphysema, air-trapping and airway-wall quantification.
size: 10,719 participants (over 40,000 inspiratory/expiratory chest CT scans through Phase 3)
segmentation_detail: Airway, lobe and emphysema quantifications were produced by the imaging cores; voxel-level segmentation masks are not part of the standard controlled-access release.
paired_text_detail: No narrative radiology reports are distributed; CT scans are paired with quantitative densitometric/airway measures plus extensive clinical, spirometric and genetic data.
clinical_variables: Spirometry and lung function, smoking history, respiratory symptoms and exacerbations, comorbidities, blood biomarkers, genome-wide genotyping/GWAS data, medications, and longitudinal COPD progression and mortality outcomes.
description: A longitudinal genetic-epidemiology COPD cohort of over 10,000 current and former smokers with more than 40,000 paired inspiratory/expiratory chest CT scans linked to genetics, spirometry and long-term outcomes.

name: SPIROMICS
full_name: SubPopulations and InteRmediate Outcome Measures In COPD Study
anatomy: Lungs, airways, thoracic skeletal muscle (pectoralis) and fat
protocol_note: Standardized paired inspiratory and expiratory volumetric chest CT enabling emphysema densitometry, functional small-airways disease via parametric response mapping (PRM), and airway metrics; repeat imaging at follow-up.
size: 2,982 participants
segmentation_detail: Imaging core distributes derived densitometric, PRM and airway measures rather than publicly released voxel segmentation masks.
paired_text_detail: No free-text radiology reports; CT is paired with quantitative imaging measures and deep respiratory phenotyping.
clinical_variables: Spirometry and lung function, respiratory symptoms and exacerbation/hospitalization history, smoking exposure, blood and airway biomarkers, genetics/omics, medications, and longitudinal respiratory and mortality outcomes.
host: SPIROMICS Data Coordinating Center (UNC) / NCBI dbGaP (phs001119)
description: An NHLBI/COPD Foundation COPD cohort of 2,982 participants with standardized paired inspiratory/expiratory chest CT and deep phenotyping designed to define intermediate imaging outcomes and disease subpopulations.

name: Qatar Biobank
full_name: Qatar Biobank (Qatar Precision Health Institute)
anatomy: Whole-body composition (DXA), carotid arteries (ultrasound IMT), and liver (FibroScan)
protocol_note: Whole-body DXA body composition and bone density; carotid ultrasound IMT and FibroScan liver stiffness also collected.
size: ~60,000 participants target (DXA and carotid ultrasound on examination subsets)
clinical_variables: Cardiometabolic disease outcomes, comprehensive clinical labs, anthropometry, whole-genome sequencing and multi-omics (Qatar Genome Program), medications, and lifestyle/dietary questionnaires with follow-up recall.
description: Qatari population cohort with whole-body DXA body composition, carotid ultrasound and FibroScan measures linked to extensive labs, whole-genome sequencing/omics and lifestyle data, accessed by application through the QPHI research portal.

name: NEO Study
full_name: Netherlands Epidemiology of Obesity Study
anatomy: Abdominal visceral/subcutaneous fat and liver, heart, brain, and aorta imaged by MRI in random subsamples
protocol_note: Abdominal MRI for visceral/subcutaneous fat, hepatic MR spectroscopy for liver fat, cardiac MRI, brain MRI, and aortic MRI/pulse-wave velocity performed in random subsamples
size: 6,671 participants
clinical_variables: Anthropometry and body composition, glucose/lipid metabolism and other labs, cardiometabolic and metabolic disease outcomes, medications, lifestyle and diet questionnaires, genetics/omics, and follow-up morbidity/mortality linkage.
host: Leiden University Medical Center (LUMC), Dept. of Clinical Epidemiology
description: Dutch obesity-oversampled population cohort of 6,671 adults with abdominal fat MRI, hepatic MR spectroscopy, cardiac and brain MRI in subsamples linked to detailed cardiometabolic phenotyping.

name: Lifelines (ImaLife)
full_name: Lifelines Cohort Study (including ImaLife low-dose chest CT sub-study)
anatomy: Lungs/chest, heart/coronary arteries, thoracic vertebrae and thoracic soft tissue
protocol_note: ImaLife sub-study: low-dose chest CT (12,055 scans) for lung, coronary calcium and vertebral/body-composition measures
size: ~167,000 total cohort; 12,055 low-dose chest CT (ImaLife)
clinical_variables: Respiratory, cardiovascular and metabolic disease outcomes, blood and biochemical labs, medications, lifestyle/anthropometry, questionnaires, and genome-wide genotyping, with longitudinal multi-year follow-up and healthcare/mortality linkage.
description: Large multigenerational Dutch population cohort whose ImaLife sub-study adds 12,055 low-dose chest CT scans (lung, coronary calcium, vertebral/body-composition measures) linked to broad health and genetic data.

name: BLSA
full_name: Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging
anatomy: Brain (structural/diffusion/perfusion MRI, amyloid PET) and whole-body/bone via DXA
protocol_note: Serial brain MRI (structural T1, diffusion/DTI, ASL perfusion) plus amyloid PET (PiB) in the neuroimaging sub-study
size: ~3,000+ active participants with serial imaging (study cohort >3,200 enrolled since 1958)
clinical_variables: Cognitive and functional aging outcomes, incident dementia/Alzheimer's, cardiometabolic labs, medications, lifestyle, genetics/omics, and mortality.
description: Long-running NIA/NIH aging cohort providing serial brain MRI, amyloid PET and DXA body composition linked to deep longitudinal clinical phenotyping, accessible to researchers via application (with an open-data subset via the ADDI AD Workbench).

name: Framingham Heart Study MDCT
full_name: Framingham Heart Study Multidetector CT Body Composition Substudy (Offspring and Third Generation cohorts)
anatomy: Abdomen (L2-L5 level for visceral/subcutaneous adipose tissue, liver, muscle) and thorax/heart (pericardial and periaortic fat)
protocol_note: Multidetector CT of chest and abdomen (8-slice MDCT, non-contrast) for coronary/aortic calcium and abdominal fat; protocol details not on the official overview page.
size: ~3,500 participants in the MDCT substudy (of >15,000 total FHS cohort)
segmentation_detail: Reading-center measured visceral (VAT) and subcutaneous (SAT) adipose tissue volumes, liver attenuation (fatty liver / Hounsfield units), pericardial and periaortic fat volumes from abdominal and thoracic MDCT
clinical_variables: Decades of serial cardiovascular phenotyping including blood pressure, lipids, glucose/diabetes status, biomarkers, medications, adjudicated CVD and cancer events, and mortality follow-up, plus SHARe genome-wide genotyping (100K/550K/Omni5 SNPs) and omics data linkable via dbGaP/BioLINCC.
license: Data Use Agreement / research proposal (BioLINCC and dbGaP for phenotype/genetics; imaging via FHS Research Application)
host: NHLBI BioLINCC / Framingham Heart Study / dbGaP
description: Long-running family-based cardiovascular cohort whose abdominal and thoracic multidetector-CT substudy provides VAT/SAT, liver and ectopic-fat body-composition imaging accessible to researchers by application.

name: Health ABC
full_name: Health, Aging and Body Composition Study
anatomy: Whole-body DXA plus quantitative CT at the abdomen (L4-L5 for visceral/subcutaneous fat) and mid-thigh (quadriceps/hamstring muscle cross-sectional area, attenuation, and intermuscular fat)
protocol_note: Quantitative CT at abdomen (L4-L5) and mid-thigh for muscle/fat; whole-body DXA
size: 3,075 older adults (aged 70-79 at baseline)
segmentation_detail: Quantitative CT-derived muscle cross-sectional area and attenuation (intramuscular fat) at mid-thigh and abdomen, visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue at L4-L5, plus whole-body DXA fat/lean/bone mass and appendicular lean mass
clinical_variables: Aging phenotypes including physical function/gait speed, muscle strength, laboratory biomarkers and inflammatory markers, medications, chronic disease incidence, disability, cognitive measures, genetic/GWAS data, and long-term mortality follow-up.
host: NIA Aging Research Biobank (Health ABC collection)
description: Landmark NIA aging cohort built for body composition, with mid-thigh and abdominal quantitative CT for muscle/fat plus whole-body DXA and long-term functional and mortality outcomes, shared via controlled access.

label_schema: DXA appendicular lean mass and bone density

name: MrOS
full_name: Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study
anatomy: Hip and lumbar spine (DXA and quantitative CT), whole-body DXA, lateral thoracic and lumbar spine radiographs
protocol_note: Whole-body and regional (hip, lumbar spine) DXA; quantitative CT of hip and spine; lateral thoracic and lumbar spine radiographs.
size: 5,994 men (aged 65+)
segmentation_detail: Quantitative CT of hip/spine yielding volumetric BMD and bone geometry; whole-body and regional DXA-derived lean and fat mass; lateral spine radiographs assessed for vertebral fractures
clinical_variables: Bone and aging phenotypes including incident fractures, falls, physical function and performance measures, anthropometrics, laboratory/biomarker measures, medications, prostate and cardiovascular disease outcomes, cognition, and long-term mortality follow-up.
host: MrOS Online / University of California San Francisco
description: Large longitudinal cohort of older men with archived whole-body and regional DXA, quantitative CT of the hip and spine, and lateral spine radiographs, linked to long-term fracture and mortality outcomes and accessible under a data-use agreement.

name: SOF
full_name: Study of Osteoporotic Fractures
anatomy: Hip and lumbar/thoracic spine (DXA BMD and subset hip quantitative CT), lateral spine radiographs for vertebral fracture assessment, and whole-body DXA for body composition
protocol_note: DXA hip/spine BMD and whole-body body composition; lateral spine radiographs for vertebral fracture assessment; hip QCT in a subset (per entry; not detailed on homepage).
size: 9,704 older women (plus ~662 Black women in a later supplement)
clinical_variables: Aging and osteoporosis phenotypes: incident fractures, falls, physical function and performance, cognition, bone and hormonal biomarkers, medications, cardiovascular and cancer outcomes, hospitalizations, and long-term mortality follow-up.
host: UCSF San Francisco Coordinating Center (SOF Online)
description: Large longitudinal cohort of older women with archived DXA body-composition and BMD scans, subset hip quantitative CT, and lateral spine radiographs linked to long-term fracture, falls, and mortality outcomes, available to researchers under a data-use agreement.

label_schema: DXA total/regional lean and fat mass

name: NHANES DXA
full_name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey - Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry
anatomy: Whole-body composition (fat mass, lean mass, bone mineral) plus femur and lumbar spine bone density and android/gynoid/visceral fat regions
protocol_note: Whole-body DXA body-composition files for 1999-2000, 2001-2002, 2003-2004 and 2005-2006 (DXX, DXX_B, DXX_C, DXX_D), distributed as five multiply-imputed sets of measured and imputed values. Later cycles add femur/spine bone density and visceral fat (per entry).
size: ~30,000+ participants with whole-body DXA (1999-2006 cycles); additional femur/spine bone-density and visceral-fat DXA in later cycles
paired_text_detail: Linked NHANES demographic, dietary, examination, laboratory, and questionnaire files mergeable by participant sequence number
clinical_variables: Laboratory panels (glucose, HbA1c, lipids, CBC, biochemistry), blood pressure and anthropometry, dietary intake, physical activity, medications, smoking/alcohol, self-reported and examined disease conditions (diabetes, cardiovascular disease), and linked National Death Index mortality follow-up.
license: US public-domain (NCHS public-use data; multiply-imputed DXA release)
host: CDC / National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS)
description: NHANES released whole-body DXA-derived body-composition and bone-density measures for tens of thousands of nationally representative US participants, linkable to the survey's rich exam, lab, and mortality data.

name: CARDIA
full_name: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study
anatomy: Coronary arteries (calcium CT), abdominal adipose tissue (CT), brain (structural MRI), and whole-body composition (DXA)
protocol_note: Brain MRI protocol includes T1, T2/FLAIR and diffusion sequences; cardiac assessment via echocardiography
size: 5,115 participants enrolled (1985-86); imaging performed in subsets or the full cohort across follow-up exams
segmentation_detail: Coronary artery calcium (Agatston) scoring, abdominal visceral/subcutaneous fat quantification from CT, and brain volumetric/white-matter-hyperintensity measures
paired_text_detail: 35+ years of longitudinal exam, laboratory, questionnaire, and adjudicated outcome data linked to each imaging exam
clinical_variables: Repeated labs (lipids, glucose, insulin, inflammatory markers), blood pressure, anthropometry, lifestyle (diet, smoking, physical activity), medications, incident cardiovascular/diabetes/hypertension outcomes, cognitive testing, GWAS/genetic data, and mortality.
license: NHLBI restricted, non-commercial use via BioLINCC data use agreement
host: CARDIA Coordinating Center (Univ. of Alabama at Birmingham) / NHLBI BioLINCC
description: CARDIA is a 35+ year prospective cohort of young adults with repeated coronary-calcium CT, abdominal-fat CT, brain MRI and whole-body DXA, accessible to researchers through BioLINCC and ancillary-study application.

name: ARIC
full_name: Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study
anatomy: Brain (structural MRI and amyloid PET); carotid arteries (ultrasound intima-media thickness)
protocol_note: Brain MRI includes T1, T2, FLAIR and diffusion sequences; florbetapir amyloid PET in ARIC-PET
size: 15,792 participants enrolled (1987-89); brain MRI in subsets (~1,900 at visit 3 and ~1,900 in ARIC-NCS) and amyloid PET in a smaller subset (ARIC-PET)
segmentation_detail: Brain volumetrics, white-matter-hyperintensity volumes and infarct measures; amyloid SUVR quantification
paired_text_detail: Decades of exam, laboratory, cognitive, and adjudicated cardiovascular/dementia/mortality outcome data linked to imaging
clinical_variables: Labs (lipids, glucose, HbA1c, cardiac/kidney biomarkers), blood pressure, carotid IMT, cognitive testing and adjudicated dementia, incident stroke/coronary heart disease/heart failure, medications, GWAS and multi-omics, and hospitalization/mortality follow-up.
license: NHLBI restricted, non-commercial use via BioLINCC / ARIC Coordinating Center agreements
host: ARIC Coordinating Center (UNC Chapel Hill) / NHLBI BioLINCC
description: ARIC is a large biracial prospective cohort with repeated brain MRI and amyloid PET substudies plus carotid ultrasound, available to researchers via BioLINCC and ancillary-study application to the coordinating center.

name: CHS
full_name: Cardiovascular Health Study
anatomy: Brain (cranial MRI); carotid arteries (ultrasound) and heart (echocardiography) also assessed
protocol_note: Cranial MRI protocol includes T1, T2 and proton-density weighted sequences
size: 5,888 older-adult participants enrolled (1989-90, 1992-93); cranial MRI in ~3,600 (1991-94) with a repeat scan in ~2,900 (1997-99)
paired_text_detail: Extensive annual exam, laboratory, and adjudicated cardiovascular/dementia/mortality outcome data linked to MRI readings
clinical_variables: Labs (lipids, glucose, inflammatory and cardiac biomarkers), blood pressure, carotid IMT, echocardiographic and ECG measures, cognitive testing and adjudicated dementia, incident myocardial infarction/stroke/heart failure, medications, GWAS/genetic data, and hospitalization/mortality follow-up.
license: NHLBI restricted, non-commercial use via BioLINCC data use agreement
host: CHS Coordinating Center (University of Washington) / NHLBI BioLINCC
description: The Cardiovascular Health Study collected cranial MRI (with a repeat timepoint), carotid ultrasound and echocardiography in older adults, with derived imaging measures and outcomes available to researchers through BioLINCC.

name: Jackson Heart Study (JHS)
full_name: Jackson Heart Study
anatomy: Heart (left ventricle, coronary arteries), carotid arteries, abdominal aorta and abdominal fat depots
protocol_note: Cardiac MRI ancillary substudy acquired cine/structure-function sequences (LV mass, volumes, ejection fraction).
size: 5,306 participants
segmentation_detail: Derived quantitative reads from a core reading center: coronary artery calcium and abdominal aortic calcium scores, abdominal visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue areas from CT, LV measures from cardiac MRI, carotid IMT.
clinical_variables: Extensive cardiometabolic phenotyping (blood pressure, lipids, fasting glucose/HbA1c, kidney function, anthropometry, echocardiography), medications, lifestyle/socioeconomic questionnaires, biospecimens with GWAS/whole-genome sequencing and metabolomics, and adjudicated cardiovascular events, hospitalization and mortality follow-up.
host: NHLBI BioLINCC / dbGaP (data coordinating center at Wake Forest / University of Mississippi Medical Center)
description: Community-based cohort of 5,306 African American adults in Jackson, Mississippi with cardiac MRI, cardiac/abdominal CT (coronary and aortic calcium plus abdominal fat), carotid ultrasound and echocardiography, accessible to researchers through NHLBI data use agreement.

name: MASALA
full_name: Mediators of Atherosclerosis in South Asians Living in America
anatomy: Coronary arteries, heart, carotid arteries, abdominal fat depots (visceral, subcutaneous, intermuscular), liver, pericardial fat
protocol_note: Cardiac CT for coronary artery calcium and abdominal CT for visceral/subcutaneous/intermuscular fat and liver attenuation; carotid IMT by ultrasound (per entry; not detailed on the researcher page).
size: ~1,164 participants at baseline (expanded in later exams)
segmentation_detail: Reading-center quantification of visceral, subcutaneous and intermuscular adipose tissue areas, hepatic and pericardial fat, and coronary artery calcium from CT.
clinical_variables: Cardiometabolic labs (glucose/insulin/HbA1c, lipids, adipokines, inflammatory markers), blood pressure, anthropometry, diet and physical-activity/lifestyle questionnaires, medications, genetics/omics, and incident diabetes and cardiovascular outcomes across exams.
host: UCSF MASALA Coordinating Center (UCSF and Northwestern field centers)
description: Longitudinal cohort of South Asian adults in the US with repeated cardiac and abdominal CT quantifying coronary calcium and visceral/ectopic fat, released to collaborators under a UCSF data use agreement.

name: HCHS/SOL
full_name: Hispanic Community Health Study / Study of Latinos
protocol_note: SOL-INCA-MRI brain protocol includes structural T1, FLAIR and related sequences with repeated scans for aging/brain-health tracking.
size: 16,415 participants
segmentation_detail: Brain MRI biomarkers (total/regional brain and hippocampal volumes, white-matter hyperintensity burden, infarcts) from the SOL-INCA-MRI reading center.
clinical_variables: Cardiometabolic and pulmonary phenotypes (labs, blood pressure, glucose/diabetes, spirometry), cognitive testing, diet/lifestyle and sociocultural questionnaires, medications, genome-wide genotyping, and incident cardiovascular, diabetes, cognitive and mortality outcomes.
