host: HCHS/SOL Coordinating Center, UNC Chapel Hill / dbGaP / NHLBI BioLINCC
description: Large US Hispanic/Latino population cohort whose imaging ancillary studies (SOL-INCA-MRI repeated brain MRI and ECHO-SOL echocardiography) are available to investigators through data use agreements and dbGaP.

name: ELSA-Brasil
full_name: Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Adult Health (Estudo Longitudinal de Saude do Adulto)
anatomy: Coronary arteries, heart, carotid arteries, aorta and retina
protocol_note: Cardiac MRI substudy with cine and structure/function sequences; primary cardiovascular imaging is CT and ultrasound.
size: 15,105 participants
clinical_variables: Cardiometabolic labs (glucose/HbA1c, lipids, inflammatory markers), blood pressure, anthropometry and hepatic ultrasound, mental-health and lifestyle questionnaires, medications, biobank with GWAS/EPIGEN genetics, and adjudicated cardiovascular, diabetes and mortality outcomes across multiple waves.
host: ELSA-Brasil consortium (six Brazilian public universities/research institutes; Fiocruz and coordinating centers)
description: Longitudinal cohort of 15,105 Brazilian civil servants across six centers with coronary calcium CT, carotid ultrasound, echocardiography, retinal photography and a cardiac MRI substudy, available to researchers by proposal to the study committee.

name: HUNT Study
full_name: Trondelag Health Study (Helseundersokelsen i Nord-Trondelag)
protocol_note: HUNT-MRI brain substudy acquired structural and vascular sequences; population body-composition relies on DXA and bioimpedance.
size: ~250,000 participants across HUNT1-4 since 1984
clinical_variables: Questionnaire and clinical measurements (blood pressure, anthropometry, lung function, labs), lifestyle data, biospecimens with GWAS/SNP genotyping and proteomics, and family and total-population linkage to national health, cancer, cause-of-death and other registries for longitudinal outcomes and mortality.
license: HUNT Research Centre data access agreement
host: HUNT Databank / HUNT Research Centre, NTNU, Norway
description: One of the largest population health studies, with DXA bone densitometry, bioimpedance body composition and a brain MRI substudy alongside deep phenotyping and registry linkage, available by application to the HUNT Databank.

name: CONSTANCES
full_name: Cohorte des consultants des Centres d'examens de sante (French population-based cohort)
anatomy: Heart and liver (ICONIC cardiac and hepatic imaging database)
protocol_note: ICONIC national cardiac-and-hepatic imaging reference database in the general population (ages 20-80) with multiparametric MRI.
size: ~220,000 participants
clinical_variables: Standardized health-examination data (blood pressure, ECG, spirometry, labs), extensive questionnaires and occupational/environmental exposures, biobank, and linkage to the French national health data system (SNDS) for hospitalizations, disease outcomes and mortality.
license: CONSTANCES scientific committee data access agreement
description: Large French general-population cohort of ~220,000 volunteers whose ICONIC substudy builds a national cardiac and hepatic MRI imaging reference database, accessible to researchers by application to the scientific committee.

name: Three-City Study (3C)
full_name: Three-City Study (Etude des Trois Cités)
anatomy: Brain (with carotid ultrasound and cardiovascular assessment)
protocol_note: 1.5T brain MRI including T1, T2 and PD/proton-density sequences used to derive gray/white matter volumes and white-matter hyperintensity load
size: ~9,294 participants (~3,442 with baseline brain MRI in the 3C-Dijon substudy)
segmentation_detail: Derived brain tissue volumes and white-matter hyperintensity (WMH) segmentations available as imaging-derived phenotypes
clinical_variables: Extensive linkable phenotypes including blood pressure and cardiovascular risk factors, lipids/glucose and other labs, medications, repeated neuropsychological testing and adjudicated incident dementia, stroke and cardiovascular events, APOE and genome-wide genotyping, and vital status/mortality.
host: Inserm / Three-City Study Scientific Committee (Bordeaux, Dijon, Montpellier)
description: French population-based cohort of adults aged 65+ across three cities with a brain-MRI substudy (3C-Dijon) built to study the relationship between vascular disease and dementia.

name: Raine Study
full_name: The Raine Study (Western Australian Pregnancy Cohort Study)
anatomy: Whole-body (DXA body composition), brain, plus organ/vascular imaging (liver, heart, bone)
protocol_note: Brain MRI (structural/functional) at adult follow-ups plus whole-body DXA for fat mass, lean mass and bone density collected across multiple waves
size: ~2,900 Gen2 offspring (born 1989-1991) plus Gen1 parents and Gen3 grandchildren
clinical_variables: Rich linkable data across the life course including cardiometabolic labs and blood pressure, DXA fat/lean/bone measures, asthma/respiratory and allergy phenotypes, mental health and behavioral assessments, lifestyle and diet, GWAS/epigenetic omics, and linkage to health and hospital records.
host: The Raine Study, University of Western Australia (ROSS application system)
description: Multi-generational Australian pregnancy-birth cohort with repeated whole-body DXA body composition and adult brain MRI collected from before birth across the life course.

name: Dunedin Study
full_name: Dunedin Multidisciplinary Health and Development Study
protocol_note: Multimodal 3T MRI at the age-45 assessment: structural T1, diffusion MRI, resting-state and task fMRI, and arterial spin labeling
size: 1,037 birth cohort (born 1972-73); ~875 completed brain MRI at age 45
segmentation_detail: FreeSurfer-derived cortical/subcortical parcellations and morphometry provided as imaging-derived measures
clinical_variables: Deep life-course phenotyping including cardiometabolic and inflammatory labs, blood pressure and physical function, repeated psychiatric diagnoses and cognitive/IQ measures, aging biomarkers (Pace of Aging), lifestyle and social variables, genome-wide genotyping and polygenic scores.
host: University of Otago, Dunedin Study (concept-paper/collaboration application)
description: New Zealand 1972-73 birth cohort with a single multimodal brain-MRI wave at age 45 embedded in life-long health, psychiatric and social phenotyping.

name: IMAGEN
full_name: IMAGEN: Reinforcement-related behaviour in normal brain function and psychopathology
protocol_note: 3T MRI including structural T1, diffusion tensor imaging, resting-state fMRI and task fMRI (monetary incentive delay, stop-signal, faces tasks)

clinical_variables: Linkable psychosocial and clinical phenotypes including substance-use and addiction measures, psychiatric symptom and behavioral assessments, personality and cognitive testing, environmental/life-events data, and genome-wide genotyping.
host: IMAGEN Consortium (data access application via imagen-project.org)
description: Largest longitudinal adolescent brain-imaging and genetics cohort, imaging youth from age 14 with repeated follow-ups to study reward behavior and mental health.

name: HCP Lifespan (HCP-Aging & HCP-Development)
full_name: Human Connectome Project Lifespan: HCP-Aging (Aging Human Connectome) and HCP-Development
protocol_note: High-resolution 3T multimodal MRI: structural T1/T2, diffusion MRI, resting-state and task fMRI, arterial spin labeling, and high-resolution hippocampal T2

host: Human Connectome Project / NIMH Data Archive (NDA) and ConnectomeDB/BALSA
description: Multimodal 3T lifespan connectome datasets imaging typically-developing youth and healthy aging adults with cross-sectional and longitudinal visits.

name: Lothian Birth Cohorts (1936/1921)
full_name: Lothian Birth Cohorts 1936 and 1921
protocol_note: Structural MRI (T1/T2/T2*/FLAIR), diffusion tensor imaging and susceptibility/iron imaging acquired across repeated waves for brain volumes, white-matter integrity and lesions
size: LBC1936 ~1,091 (born 1936); LBC1921 ~550 (born 1921), with brain MRI from age ~73/78
segmentation_detail: Imaging dictionary provides derived brain tissue volumes, white-matter hyperintensity segmentations and DTI white-matter tract measures
clinical_variables: Linkable phenotypes including lifelong cognitive/IQ trajectories (from age 11), cardiometabolic and inflammatory labs, blood pressure and physical function/frailty, lifestyle, GWAS and DNA-methylation/epigenetic-clock omics, and record-linked morbidity and mortality.
host: University of Edinburgh, Lothian Birth Cohorts (data request form to Dr Simon Cox)
description: Scottish birth cohorts (1936 and 1921) with repeated longitudinal brain MRI from the eighth decade linked to childhood-to-late-life cognitive and health data.

name: Insight 46 (MRC NSHD 1946 birth cohort)
full_name: Insight 46 neuroimaging sub-study of the MRC National Survey of Health and Development (1946 British Birth Cohort)
anatomy: Brain (simultaneous amyloid PET-MRI); whole-body DXA in the wider NSHD cohort
protocol_note: Multi-modal PET-MRI: volumetric T1, FLAIR/T2 for white-matter hyperintensities, plus 18F-florbetapir amyloid PET (SUVR)
size: ~500 imaged participants (Insight 46); ~5,300 in the NSHD birth cohort
clinical_variables: Life-course phenotypes collected from birth to age 70+ including blood pressure, cardiometabolic and anthropometric measures, cognition, lifestyle, socioeconomic factors, DXA body composition, blood biomarkers, genome-wide genotyping and linked morbidity/mortality outcomes.
host: MRC Unit for Lifelong Health and Ageing at UCL / NSHD Data Sharing Committee
description: Neuroimaging sub-study of the 1946 British birth cohort providing simultaneous amyloid PET-MRI at two timepoints, linkable to uniquely rich life-course clinical, cognitive and DXA data via managed application.

name: DIAN (Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network)
full_name: Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network Observational Study (DIAN-OBS)
protocol_note: Structural T1/T2/FLAIR, DTI and resting-state fMRI plus multi-tracer PET: 11C-PiB amyloid PET, 18F-flortaucipir tau PET and FDG PET
size: ~500+ participants from autosomal-dominant Alzheimer's disease families
clinical_variables: Standardized clinical and cognitive testing (CDR, neuropsychology), CSF and blood biomarkers (Abeta42/40, total tau, phospho-tau), causal AD mutation genetics (PSEN1, PSEN2, APP), and estimated age at symptom onset.
host: Washington University in St. Louis / Knight ADRC (DIAN)
description: Longitudinal multi-site observational study of autosomal-dominant Alzheimer's disease mutation carriers and non-carriers with serial multimodal MRI and amyloid/tau/FDG PET, available to researchers by data request.

name: ROSMAP
full_name: Religious Orders Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project
anatomy: Brain (postmortem/ex vivo MRI of cerebral hemispheres on a subset)
protocol_note: Ex vivo/postmortem structural and diffusion MRI of fixed brain hemispheres registered to detailed neuropathology
size: ~3,600+ enrolled participants; ex vivo MRI on a subset of donated brains
clinical_variables: Annual cognitive and motor assessments, dementia/MCI clinical diagnoses, detailed postmortem neuropathology, cause-of-death and mortality, plus genome-wide genotyping/WGS, transcriptomics, proteomics and DNA methylation.
host: Rush Alzheimer's Disease Center / RADC Research Resource Sharing Hub
description: Longitudinal clinical-pathologic cohorts of aging and dementia providing ex vivo brain MRI on a subset linked to deep annual clinical, neuropathologic and multi-omic data, released to researchers under a data use agreement.

label_schema: neuropathology (amyloid, tau tangles, TDP-43, Lewy bodies, infarcts)

name: Tohoku Medical Megabank (TMM)
full_name: Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization Cohort Studies (TMM CommCohort and TMM BirThree Cohort)
protocol_note: Brain-MRI study protocol including structural T1/T2/FLAIR and angiographic sequences
size: ~150,000 total cohort participants (CommCohort ~80,000; BirThree ~70,000); brain-MRI sub-study on a subset
clinical_variables: Physiological and lifestyle measures, blood/urine biochemistry, clinical questionnaires, whole-genome sequencing/genotyping and multi-omics, with perinatal and dental health variables in the birth cohort.
host: Tohoku University / ToMMo Sample and Data Access Committee (dbTMM)
description: Large Japanese community-based and birth/three-generation cohorts with a dedicated brain-MRI study, distributed to approved researchers through the dbTMM sample-and-data access system.

name: CoLaus | PsyCoLaus
full_name: CoLaus | PsyCoLaus Study (Cohorte Lausannoise), including BrainLaus and OsteoLaus sub-studies
protocol_note: BrainLaus multimodal brain MRI (structural, diffusion, functional) with repeated follow-up waves; OsteoLaus DXA including vertebral fracture assessment and body composition
size: ~6,700 baseline participants; imaging sub-studies (BrainLaus, OsteoLaus) on subsets
clinical_variables: Cardiovascular and metabolic risk factors, blood biochemistry, medications, lifestyle, semi-structured psychiatric interviews (PsyCoLaus), DXA bone/body composition, and genome-wide genetic and omics data.
host: Lausanne University Hospital (CHUV) / CoLaus-PsyCoLaus research team
description: Population-based Lausanne cohort with deep cardiometabolic, psychiatric and genetic phenotyping plus repeated brain MRI (BrainLaus) and DXA body-composition imaging (OsteoLaus), available to researchers via proposal/application.

label_schema: DXA bone mineral density and fat/lean mass

name: GUSTO
full_name: Growing Up in Singapore Towards healthy Outcomes
anatomy: Child and infant brain; abdominal adipose tissue; whole-body composition; peripheral bone
protocol_note: Neonatal and childhood brain MRI (structural T1/T2, diffusion, resting-state) and abdominal MRI quantifying visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue; DXA whole-body composition and pQCT bone imaging
size: ~1,200 mother-offspring pairs
clinical_variables: Repeated maternal and child anthropometry and growth, metabolic and cardiovascular measures, blood biomarkers, neurodevelopmental and cognitive assessments, DXA/MRI body composition, lifestyle/diet, and genetic and epigenetic data.
host: A*STAR / National University of Singapore (KK Women's and Children's Hospital) - GUSTO Data Vault
description: Singapore mother-offspring birth cohort with longitudinal pediatric brain MRI, abdominal adiposity MRI and DXA/pQCT body-composition imaging, accessible to researchers through the GUSTO Data Vault collaboration request.

label_schema: derived brain volumetric and connectivity measures

name: Duke Liver Dataset
full_name: Duke Liver Dataset (DLDS) — Liver MRI with Series-Type Labels and Segmentation Masks
protocol_note: 17 series/contrast types across routine liver protocols: T1 in-/opposed-phase, precontrast fat-sat T1, dynamic post-contrast (arterial, portal venous, hepatobiliary), T2, DWI, MRCP, localizer
size: 2,146 MRI series (113,280 images) from 105 patients; liver masks for 310 series / 95 patients
segmentation_detail: manual whole-liver binary masks (DICOM stacks) for 310 series across 95 patients, on 4 series types
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (or custom Duke license for commercial use)
description: Abdominal liver MRI from Duke University — 2,146 series from 105 patients (87/105 with imaging findings of cirrhosis), each labeled with one of 17 series types for automated sequence classification, plus whole-liver segmentation masks for a 310-series subset; files are restricted on Zenodo (login + license agreement + justification).

label_schema: Series-type classification — 1 of 17 classes per series; class codes are randomized letters with the mapping in SeriesClassificationKey.csv and SequenceTypes.csv; class 17 is a catch-all 'anything else'

Liver segmentation — whole-liver binary masks (0 = background, 1 = liver) stored as DICOM stacks matching image dimensions, for 310 series across 95 patients on 4 series types: axial in-phase, axial opposed-phase, axial precontrast fat-sat T1w, portal-venous fat-sat T1w
details.file_structure: Two archives: Series_Classification.zip (2,146 series / 105 subjects + SeriesClassificationKey.csv, SequenceTypes.csv) and Segmentation.zip (310 series / 95 subjects + SegmentationKey.csv); segmentation cases organized by DLDS patient ID → series number → image/ and mask/ DICOM subfolders.
details.splits: No official split in v2; v1 withheld ~25% of labels/masks (26 DLDS IDs, listed in v2) so the original 75/25 train/test design can be reproduced.
details.extra: Paper: Macdonald et al., Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2023 (DOI 10.1148/ryai.220275); dataset DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7774566. Scanners: 96 Siemens / 9 GE; 54 exams at 1.5T, 51 at 3.0T. Companion dataset: Duke Spleen Data Set. The paper says all image metadata were de-identified with an in-house tool but does not say whether SeriesDescription was kept, so check before using headers for series-type labels.
details.label_readers: Liver masks: 3 readers (an abdominal radiologist, 12 y, and two research fellows, ~2 y), one reader per liver, fellows' masks validated/adjusted by the radiologist; series-type labels 'human-derived' (annotator not stated)
details.third_party_note: Per the catalog license CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial, no derivatives); no API-specific clause.

name: RSNA 2026 Knee Abnormality Detection
full_name: RSNA Knee Abnormality Detection AI Challenge (Knee MRI, 2026)
protocol_note: Sagittal, coronal and axial series per study (3–14 series; fluid-sensitive fat-suppressed series in all three planes for 3,991/4,407 studies)
size: >5,000 knee MRI exams (train: 4,407 studies / 24,371 series / 819,078 DICOM files)
paired_text_detail: Free-text radiology reports in 12 languages for 4,349 of 4,407 training studies (weak supervision); only 58 training studies carry gold labels
license: Competition rules (research use; winning models open-sourced)
description: RSNA's 2026 challenge — its first MSK-MRI challenge and first to pair images with report text: >5,000 multi-planar knee MRI exams from 16 sites across five continents, labeled for 12 abnormalities (ACL/MCL tears, menisci, OA compartments, effusion, synovitis, Baker's cyst, contusion, fracture), with multilingual radiology reports for weak supervision; runs through Oct 2026.

label_schema: 12 study-level binary targets: ACL, MCL, medial meniscus, lateral meniscus, medial tibiofemoral OA, lateral OA, patellofemoral OA, joint effusion, synovitis, Baker's (popliteal) cyst, bone contusion, fracture
Gold labels (two MSK radiologists + adjudicator, severity-thresholded) for only 58 training studies; the other 4,349 studies have free-text radiology reports only
Hidden test set annotated by expert MSK radiologists
Series-level metadata: anatomical plane, Fluid_Sensitive and Fat_Suppression flags
details.file_structure: train.csv (StudyInstanceUID + 12 label columns for gold studies), train_series.csv / test_series.csv (series-level plane/sequence metadata), per-study radiology report text, DICOM folders organized study → series → slice, sample_submission.csv (12 probability columns).
details.splits: Train: 4,407 studies (58 gold-labeled + 4,349 report-only). Hidden expert-annotated test set scored via Kaggle code-competition rerun (macro ROC-AUC over the 12 findings).
details.extra: Launched Aug 5, 2026; final submission Oct 22, 2026; $77,000 prizes incl. a first-time efficiency track. Code competition — submissions run in offline Kaggle notebooks (≤9 h). Sagittal 9,864 / coronal 8,609 / axial 5,898 training series.

name: UW-Madison GI Tract
full_name: UW-Madison GI Tract Image Segmentation (Kaggle 2022)
anatomy: GI tract (stomach, small bowel, large bowel)
protocol_note: 0.35T ViewRay MRIdian MR-Linac, TrueFISP (balanced SSFP, T2/T1-weighted) sequence; serial scans on 1-5 radiotherapy fractions; 1.5 x 1.5 x 3 mm
size: 85 cases / 38,496 slices (competition train); full release 107 patients / 467 scans / 67,248 slices
segmentation_detail: RLE-encoded 2D masks of stomach, small bowel and large bowel per axial slice, converted from DICOM-RT contours
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (post-competition full release); competition data under Kaggle competition rules
description: Serial abdominal MRIs (0.35T ViewRay MRIdian MR-Linac, TrueFISP) of cancer patients scanned on 1-5 treatment days during MR-guided radiotherapy at UW-Madison, released as 16-bit grayscale PNG axial slices with RLE-encoded stomach, small-bowel and large-bowel masks; the post-competition release adds the formerly hidden test set (107 patients, 467 scans).

label_schema: train.csv columns: id ('case{N}_day{D}_slice_{SSSS}'), class, segmentation (RLE run-length pairs on the flattened slice; empty when the organ is absent on that slice)
3 foreground classes, one row per slice-class pair (3 rows per slice): large_bowel, small_bowel, stomach; background implicit
Competition training set: ~16,590 of 38,496 slices have at least one non-empty mask (annotated slices: large_bowel ~14,085, small_bowel ~11,201, stomach ~8,627)
Contours drawn manually by a UW-Madison annotation team under supervision of a board-certified radiation oncologist, then converted from DICOM-RT to RLE
details.file_structure: train/case{N}/case{N}_day{D}/scans/ holds one 16-bit grayscale PNG per axial slice named slice_{SSSS}_{width}_{height}_{spacingW}_{spacingH}.png — slice size in pixels and pixel spacing in mm are encoded in the filename because DICOM headers were stripped during de-identification; all masks are RLE strings in a single train.csv. Slice sizes range 234x234 to 360x310 px (median 266x266); most scans have 144 slices at 1.5 x 1.5 x 3 mm.
details.splits: Competition: 85 cases / 38,496 slices public training; hidden test set reachable only via Kaggle code submission, no public labels during the challenge. Post-competition release ('UW Madison GI Tract Image Segmentation Dataset' by co-author Yin Li on Kaggle, ~4.1 GB zip) contains both challenge partitions: 107 patients / 467 scans / 67,248 slices; no official validation split.
details.extra: Scans acquired on a 0.35T ViewRay MRIdian MR-Linac (TrueFISP sequence) across 1-5 radiotherapy fractions per patient on different days (serial adaptive-RT imaging). Evaluation combined 3D Dice and 3D Hausdorff distance (official evaluation code in the data-tools repo). Companion data descriptor: Lee et al., 'Dataset for gastrointestinal tract segmentation on serial MRIs for abdominal tumor radiotherapy', Data in Brief 57:111159 (2024). De-identification/packaging code: https://github.com/happyharrycn/UW-Madison-GI-Tract-Segmentation-Data-Tools; full release: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/happyharrycn/uw-madison-gi-tract-image-segmentation-dataset

name: PanSegData
full_name: PanSegData — Large-Scale Multi-Center Pancreas MRI Segmentation Dataset (PanSegNet)
protocol_note: T1W and T2W abdominal MRI; most participants contribute both sequences (released as two parallel nnUNet-style datasets, t1 and t2)
size: 767 MRI (385 T1W + 382 T2W; 499 participants, 5 centers)
segmentation_detail: pancreas (whole organ, binary mask on every T1W and T2W scan)
description: The largest public pancreas MRI segmentation dataset: 767 T1W/T2W abdominal MRI scans from 499 adults across five US centers, each with an expert binary pancreas mask, released with the PanSegNet paper (Zhang et al., Medical Image Analysis 2024).

label_schema: Voxel-wise binary segmentation mask per scan, 2 values
Label 1 - pancreas (single whole-organ class; no tumor or subregion labels)

Ground truth: pancreas manually contoured on axial T1W and T2W scans by five radiologists (one per center) in ITK-SNAP, with senior-radiologist quality review; paper reports moderate inter-observer (kappa 0.624 T1W / 0.638 T2W) and high intra-observer agreement
details.file_structure: OSF project holds Pancreas_MRI_Dataset/ with two nnUNet-style archives — t1.zip (~4.3 GB) and t2.zip (~1.5 GB). Each unpacks to imagesTr/ ({CENTER}_{NNNN}_0000.nii.gz volumes) and labelsTr/ ({CENTER}_{NNNN}.nii.gz masks); center prefixes are NYU (New York University), MCF (Mayo Clinic Florida), NWU (Northwestern), AHN (Allegheny Health Network), MCA (Mayo Clinic Arizona). A 'Meta informations' folder adds T1/T2 name-mapping JSONs (original -> released filenames) and t2_info_osf.xlsx; LICENSE.txt at the root.
details.splits: No held-out test folder — all 767 scans ship with labels (t1: 385 image/mask pairs; t2: 382 pairs, verified from the zip directories). The paper trains/internally validates on Centers 1-2 (NYU 162 T1W/162 T2W; Mayo Florida 151/150) and uses Centers 3-5 as external test sets (Northwestern 30/19; AHN 17/28; Mayo Arizona 25/23).
details.extra: Companion to PanSegNet (nnUNet + linear-attention Transformer); code and pretrained CT/T1/T2 weights at github.com/NUBagciLab/PaNSegNet. The paper's 1,350 CT scans come from existing public sets (AbdomenCT-1K, AMOS, WORD, BTCV) and are NOT redistributed here — the OSF release is MRI only. License note: the OSF node's license metadata is set to 'Other' and defers to the LICENSE.txt in OSF Storage (uploaded 2025-07-29), which declares CC BY-NC 4.0 with required citation. Cite: Zhang et al., 'Large-scale multi-center CT and MRI segmentation of pancreas with deep learning', Medical Image Analysis 99:103382 (2025; online 2024), doi:10.1016/j.media.2024.103382.

name: OAI-ZIB
full_name: OAI-ZIB Knee MRI Manual Segmentations (Zuse Institute Berlin)
protocol_note: Baseline right-knee sagittal 3D DESS with water excitation MRIs from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (images not included; obtained from OAI)
size: 507 manual segmentation masks (384x384x160 voxels) + 116 bone-only masks; ~90 MB zip (matching OAI MRIs obtained separately)
segmentation_detail: Manual voxel-wise masks of femoral bone, femoral cartilage, tibial bone and tibial cartilage for 507 OAI baseline 3D DESS knee MRIs, plus a 116-scan bone-only subset for shape-based OA classification
license: CC BY 4.0 (ZIB record; bundled README restricts use to scientific purposes); underlying OAI MRIs under OAI/NDA data-use agreement
description: 507 manual reference segmentations of femoral/tibial bone and cartilage for baseline right-knee sagittal 3D DESS MRIs from the Osteoarthritis Initiative, released by Zuse Institute Berlin alongside Ambellan et al. (Medical Image Analysis 2019). The masks download freely, but the corresponding MRI scans must be obtained from the OAI database under its data-use agreement.

label_schema: segmentation/ masks (507 volumes, one per OAI subject ID): integer voxel labels 0 background, 1 femoral bone, 2 femoral cartilage, 3 tibial bone, 4 tibial cartilage

classification/ masks (116 volumes, 108 overlapping the 507): labels 0 background, 1 femoral bone, 2 tibial bone (bone-only, used for statistical-shape OA classification in companion MICCAI/MedIA papers)

Each mask is a 160x384x384 uint8 MET_UCHAR volume at 0.7 x 0.36 x 0.36 mm matching the OAI sagittal DESS scan; masks carry identity transforms only, so they align with the MRIs up to rigid alignment (scanner pose must be removed/applied for overlay)
OAIZIB-CM community mirror refines labels to 5 classes: femur, femoral cartilage, tibia, medial tibial cartilage, lateral tibial cartilage
details.file_structure: Single ~90 MB zip (OAI-ZIB/): segmentation/segmentation_masks/ holds 507 {OAI_subject_ID}.segmentation_masks.mhd+.raw pairs and classification/segmentation_masks/ holds 116 more; each doc/ folder contains oai_mri_paths.txt (per-subject relative path of the matching baseline DESS scan inside the OAI download), citation bibtex, a SimpleITK reader snippet, and (segmentation only) two cross-validation ID lists. The MRI images themselves are NOT included.
details.splits: No train/test split; the release ships an official 2-fold cross-validation setup (List1: 253 IDs, List2: 254 IDs). The OAIZIB-CM mirror instead defines 404 train / 103 test.
details.extra: DOI 10.12752/4.ATEZ.1.0 resolves to the ZIB OPUS record (opus4.kobv.de docId 6995) with direct download https://www.zib.de/ext-data/2019_ATEZ_MEDIA-Supplementary-Material-OAI-ZIB.zip; the former pubdata.zib.de repository now redirects to a ZIB Zenodo community that does not list this record. Matching images are right-knee baseline sagittal 3D DESS with water excitation from OAI, requiring an OAI/NDA account (https://nda.nih.gov/oai/). Mirror OAIZIB-CM (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14934086, Hugging Face YongchengYAO/OAIZIB-CM, CC BY-NC 4.0) repackages images+masks as NIfTI with the medial/lateral tibial-cartilage split and adds the CLAIR-Knee-103R template/atlas.

related.name: Osteoarthritis Initiative
related.note: Manual femoral/tibial bone and cartilage masks for 507 baseline right-knee sagittal 3D DESS MRIs; MRIs must be obtained from OAI

name: fastMRI+
full_name: fastMRI+: Clinical Pathology Annotations for the fastMRI Knee and Brain Datasets
protocol_note: Labels key to fastMRI knee volumes and fastMRI brain volumes (file names such as file_brain_AXFLAIR_…); the images were converted from fastMRI HDF5 to DICOM for labelling. Sequences are inherited from fastMRI (knee coronal PD with and without fat suppression; brain axial T1, T1 post-contrast, T2 and FLAIR).
size: 24,380 annotations, no images: knee 16,154 bounding boxes + 13 study-level labels (22 classes, all 1,172 knee volumes) and brain 7,570 bounding boxes + 643 study-level labels (30 classes, 1,001 of 5,847 brain studies)
license: CC BY 4.0 (annotations, per Scientific Data paper); repo carries MIT license; underlying fastMRI images require the separate NYU fastMRI data-sharing agreement
description: Radiologist-created clinical pathology annotations (slice-level 2D bounding boxes plus study-level labels) for the NYU fastMRI knee and brain datasets, distributed as open CSV files. No images are included — the fastMRI k-space/DICOM data must be obtained separately from fastmri.med.nyu.edu under its data-sharing agreement.

label_schema: CSV columns: file, slice, study_level, x, y, width, height, label — one row per annotation
Bounding-box rows: study_level='No', pixel coordinates x,y,width,height on the given slice of the named fastMRI volume
Study-level rows: study_level='Yes', no box coordinates (whole-study finding, e.g. 'artifact', 'Normal for age', 'Global label: Small vessel chronic white matter ischemic change')

Knee (knee.csv): 16,154 boxes + 13 study-level labels across 22 classes; most frequent: Meniscus Tear (5,658), Cartilage Partial-Thickness loss/defect (2,985), Joint Effusion (1,311), Bone Fracture/Contusion/dislocation (1,060), Subchondral edema (986)

Brain (brain.csv): 7,570 boxes + 643 study-level labels across 30 classes; most frequent: Nonspecific white matter lesion (1,826), Posttreatment change (1,262), Craniotomy (1,025), Nonspecific lesion (757), Possible artifact (505)
knee_file_list.csv / brain_file_list.csv enumerate every reviewed volume; reviewed files with no row in knee.csv/brain.csv were read as having no findings
2D bounding boxes per slice (x, y, width, height in pixels)

22 knee pathology classes (Meniscus Tear, Cartilage Partial/Full-Thickness defect, Joint Effusion, Bone Fracture/Contusion, Subchondral edema, ACL/MCL/PCL/LCL sprains by grade, Periarticular cysts, Displaced Meniscal Tissue, Bone/Soft-Tissue Lesion, Muscle Strain, Joint Bodies, Patellar Retinaculum sprain, artifact)

30 brain pathology classes (Nonspecific white matter lesion, Posttreatment change, Craniotomy, Nonspecific lesion, Possible artifact, Mass, Normal for age, Edema, Dural thickening, Enlarged ventricles, Resection cavity, Encephalomalacia, Lacunar infarct, Extra-axial mass, and rarer findings)
details.file_structure: Annotations/ folder with four plain CSVs (knee.csv, brain.csv, knee_file_list.csv, brain_file_list.csv); rows key to fastMRI volumes via the 'file' column (fastMRI HDF5 filename, e.g. file_brain_AXFLAIR_200_6002425) plus slice index. Repo also ships fastmri_to_dicom.py; that conversion flips pixel arrays up/down relative to raw HDF5 orientation, which must be accounted for when overlaying boxes.
details.splits: No splits of its own — annotations key to fastMRI volumes, which carry the official fastMRI train/val splits (knee: all 1,172 train+val volumes annotated; brain: 1,001 randomly selected of 5,847 studies)
details.extra: Published in Scientific Data 9:152 (2022) by Microsoft Research + NYU Langone. Each study was labeled by a single subspecialist radiologist (knee reader 6 yrs experience, brain reader 2 yrs) on MD.ai, without other views or clinical history — authors explicitly caution the labels are not clinical ground truth. Also mirrored on a Synapse repository. Knee study-level labels are all 'artifact' (13); brain has 643 study-level labels including 'Normal for age' and global small-vessel ischemic change.

related.name: fastMRI Knee
related.note: Radiologist bounding-box and study-level pathology labels for all 1,172 knee volumes; images not included.

related.name: fastMRI Brain
related.note: Radiologist bounding-box and study-level pathology labels for about 1,001 randomly selected brain studies; images not included.

name: MOST
full_name: Multicenter Osteoarthritis Study
protocol_note: Knee MRI on a 1.0T ONI OrthOne extremity scanner: sagittal and axial fat-suppressed PD-weighted FSE plus coronal STIR (3 mm slices, no gap); later visits (144-168 months) used 1.5T scanners; radiographs include bilateral fixed-flexion PA and weight-bearing lateral knee views plus full-limb alignment films
size: 4,551 participants (3,026 original cohort enrolled 2003 + 1,525 new-cohort participants 2016-18); longitudinal knee radiographs, full-limb radiographs and 1.0T knee MRI through the 168-month visit
clinical_variables: Demographics and OA risk factors, WOMAC pain/stiffness/function and knee symptoms, physical performance, gait and strength measures, quantitative sensory testing, whole-body DXA body composition (baseline, 30 months), and banked biospecimens (serum, plasma, DNA, urine).
license: MOST / NIA Aging Research Biobank data-use agreement
host: NIA Aging Research Biobank / MOST Online (UCSF SF Coordinating Center)
description: Longitudinal knee-osteoarthritis cohort of 3,026 adults aged 50-79 (two US sites, enrolled 2003; plus a 1,525-participant new cohort from 2016-18) with serial fixed-flexion PA and lateral knee radiographs, full-limb films and 1.0T knee MRI through 168 months, all centrally read (KL/OARSI, WORMS/MOAKS). Companion cohort to OAI; public-use clinical datasets require MOST Online registration + DUA, and images are requested via the NIA Aging Research Biobank.

label_schema: Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grade 0-4 (with an additional 3.5 category) for tibiofemoral OA from central longitudinal radiograph readings at baseline, 15, 30, 60 and 84 months (later visits read in MOST2/MOST4 phases)

OARSI-atlas individual radiographic features: joint space narrowing and osteophytes graded 0-3 per compartment with half-grade increments; quantitative full-limb alignment (hip-knee-ankle) measurements

WORMS (Whole-Organ MRI Score) semiquantitative knee MRI readings for MRI sub-study participants: cartilage morphology, bone marrow lesions, meniscal tear/extrusion, bone attrition, osteophytes, Hoffa-synovitis and effusion-synovitis; MOAKS used for later-phase readings
Patient-reported/clinical outcomes: WOMAC pain, stiffness and function, knee symptoms, physical performance, gait, strength; whole-body DXA body composition at baseline and 30 months
Labels are tabular clinical + central-read variables keyed to participant/knee/visit, NOT pixel-level image annotations
details.file_structure: Clinical and central-reading public-use datasets are distributed as documented tabular files (with data dictionaries) via MOST Online / the NIA Aging Research Biobank, keyed by participant ID, knee side and visit; knee radiographs, full-limb radiographs and knee MRIs through the 168-month visit are obtained separately by submitting a Request for Materials on the Biobank (material type 'Images'); no segmentation masks are included.
details.splits: No official train/val/test split; longitudinal visits at baseline, 15, 30, 60, 72 (phone) and 84 months for the original cohort, with 144-, 152-, 160- and 168-month visits for the enriched cohort (new cohort of 1,525 recruited 2016-18).
details.extra: Formerly hosted at most.ucsf.edu / mostdata.ucsf.edu (domains no longer resolve); current portals are MOST Online (mostonline.ucsf.edu, registration + acceptance of a Data Use Agreement) and the NIA Aging Research Biobank (data/image requests need an online form, study protocol, IRB approval or waiver, and investigator CV). Two clinical sites (Univ. of Alabama at Birmingham n=1,517; Univ. of Iowa n=1,509), ~60% women, ~15% African American; Boston University was the radiograph reading center and UCSF the MRI reading center; 83% of the cohort had baseline MRI on the 1.0T extremity scanner. Widely used alongside OAI for deep-learning KL grading and knee-OA progression/TKR prediction.

name: SPR Head CT Age Prediction
full_name: SPR Head CT Age Prediction Challenge (Sociedade Paulista de Radiologia, Kaggle 2024)
protocol_note: Head CT studies (axial DICOM slices), face-redacted; contrast phase not stated
size: 2,525 head CT studies (2,377 train + 148 test)
description: 2,525 face-redacted (defaced) head CT studies donated by multiple Brazilian institutions and labeled with patient age, released by the Sao Paulo Radiological Society (SPR) for a 2024 Kaggle age-prediction regression challenge.

label_schema: Single regression target: patient chronological age (continuous, in years), one value per CT study
train.csv: StudyID (study/accession folder name) + Age (target); test studies unlabeled
Submission format: StudyID, Age; leaderboard metric = Mean Columnwise Mean Absolute Error (single column, i.e. MAE in years)
No abnormality/diagnosis labels, segmentation masks, bounding boxes, or radiology reports
details.file_structure: Raw axial DICOM (.dcm) slices grouped per study: the train archive (dataset_jpr_train/) contains subfolders 1/, 2/, 3/, each holding per-study folders named by StudyID with the study's DICOM slice files; the test archive (dataset_jpr_test2/) holds per-study DICOM folders; age labels are in train.csv keyed by StudyID. Faces are redacted in-volume (skin/subcutaneous and surrounding-air voxels replaced) while files remain standard DICOM with rescale/window metadata intact.
details.splits: Fixed challenge split: 2,377 studies train / 148 studies test (test ages withheld; scored via Kaggle submissions, late submission still open)
details.extra: Organized by Sociedade Paulista de Radiologia (Eduardo Farina, Felipe Kitamura, Gustavo Corradi); ran Mar 2 - May 1, 2024 alongside JPR 2024. Companion paper: 'Pixel Tampering: Does Face Redaction Harm Medical AI Performance?' (J Imaging Inform Med 2025, doi:10.1007/s10278-025-01776-0) reports top MAEs of 2.8 and 3.4 years on the redacted test set (3.2/3.8 on non-redacted). Redaction used the organizers' open-source face_deid_ct-style tool. Download requires a Kaggle account and accepting competition rules.

name: SPR X-Ray Age Prediction
full_name: SPR X-Ray Age Prediction Challenge (2023)
protocol_note: De-identified chest radiographs in PNG from four Brazilian institutions (Dasa, Fleury, InCor, Unifesp)
size: 11,747 chest radiographs (~10.7K train / ~1.1K test)
license: Subject to competition rules (non-commercial use; no redistribution)
description: 11,747 de-identified chest radiographs in PNG donated by four Brazilian institutions (Dasa, Fleury, InCor, Unifesp), released by the São Paulo Radiology Society (SPR) with AWS for patient age prediction scored by mean absolute error. The companion SPR X-Ray Gender Prediction Challenge uses the same images and the same train/test partition with sex labels.

label_schema: Regression target: age — patient age in years, one value per image (train_age.csv columns: imageId, age; imageId matches the PNG filename)
Test-partition images carry no public labels; submissions predict age for every image and are scored by mean absolute error on the hidden test split
Patient sex labels for the identical images and identical partition are available through the companion SPR X-Ray Gender Prediction Challenge (spr-x-ray-gender)
details.file_structure: Chest radiographs distributed as individual PNG files named by imageId; labels supplied in train_age.csv (imageId, age) with a sample_submission_age.csv template; images are de-identified PNGs without DICOM metadata.
details.splits: ~10.7K labeled training images + ~1.1K unlabeled test images (11,747 total images per the official solution file); test labels withheld for leaderboard scoring.
details.extra: Organized by the Sociedade Paulista de Radiologia e Diagnóstico por Imagem (SPR) with Amazon Web Services; images donated by Dasa, Fleury, InCor, and Unifesp; ran Feb 28 - Apr 26, 2023 with winners recognized at JPR 2023. Rules prohibit redistribution and re-identification and restrict data use to non-commercial competition purposes. The full data remains available post-competition as the host-published public Kaggle dataset 'SPR X-Ray Age and Gender Dataset' (kaggle.com/datasets/felipekitamura/spr-x-ray-age-and-gender-dataset, archive.zip ~15.6 GB, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, includes train_age.csv and train_gender.csv). Do not conflate with the separate SPR Head CT Age Prediction Challenge.

name: TCGA-LIHC
full_name: The Cancer Genome Atlas Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma Collection
protocol_note: MRI studies include multiple sequences (the BAMF liver-MR annotations target the T1 series); collection spans CT, MR, and PET series
size: 56.38 GB (97 subjects / 237 studies / 1,688 series / 125,397 images)
paired_text_detail: Matched clinical, demographic, pathological, and genomic data available via the NCI Genomic Data Commons (GDC) Data Portal through shared TCGA patient identifiers
description: Radiology imaging (CT, MRI, and PET) of 97 hepatocellular carcinoma patients from The Cancer Genome Atlas, paired with matched clinical, genomic, and histopathology data via the Genomic Data Commons.

label_schema: Cohort/classification label: liver hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients; matched TCGA clinical, genomic, and pathology labels available via the Genomic Data Commons using shared patient IDs (not stored in the imaging files)
The base imaging collection ships with NO per-image or per-voxel labels (radiology DICOM only)
Segmentation class from the linked BAMF AIMI Annotations liver-CT analysis result: Liver (single foreground class, AI-generated on 89 CT scans; no tumor class)
Segmentation class from the linked BAMF AIMI Annotations liver-MR analysis result: Liver (single foreground class, AI-generated on 67 T1-weighted MR scans; no tumor class)
Crowds-Cure-2017 analysis result: reader-placed lesion annotations/measurements (crowdsourced radiologist markups)
SAROS analysis result: sparsely annotated body-region and organ segmentations covering CT series from many TCIA collections including this one
details.file_structure: Images are DICOM organized per patient (97 subjects / 237 studies / 1,688 series / 125,397 images; modalities CT, MR, PT), downloaded via the NBIA Data Retriever. No labels are bundled with the base collection; BAMF AIMI liver segmentations are distributed separately as DICOM-SEG (optionally NIfTI) via the IDC Zenodo community (10.5281/zenodo.13244892), and Crowds-Cure-2017 / SAROS annotations are separate downloadable analysis results.
details.splits: No official train/val/test split; the BAMF AIMI liver annotations reserve ~10% of scans as a validation subset that was Likert-scored and manually corrected by a radiologist and a non-expert.
details.extra: TCIA collection DOI 10.7937/K9/TCIA.2016.IMMQW8UQ; version 5 (updated 2020-05-29), status Complete. BAMF liver labels are AI-generated (nnU-Net ensemble; CT model trained on TotalSegmentator+FLARE21, MR model on AMOS+Duke Liver Dataset V2) with radiologist corrections for the ~10% validation subset. Integer label values inside the DICOM-SEG segments were not confirmed from the source and are omitted.
details.reference_standard: Cohort = TCGA hepatocellular carcinoma cases (tissue-based TCGA diagnosis); clinical, genomic and pathology data via GDC

label_variants.name: BAMF AIMI annotations (liver CT/MR)
label_variants.note: AI-generated liver masks with ~10% radiologist review (IDC Zenodo)

label_variants.name: LiverHccSeg
label_variants.note: 2-radiologist liver and HCC masks on 17 multiphasic MRI studies; ships the DICOMs (catalog id liverhccseg)

label_variants.name: Crowds-Cure-2017
label_variants.note: crowdsourced radiologist lesion markups

label_variants.name: SAROS
label_variants.note: sparse body-region/organ CT segmentations (catalog id saros)

details.third_party_note: CC BY 3.0 permits redistribution with attribution; no clause restricting external services (TCIA Data Usage Policy additionally requires citation).

name: Duke Spleen Data Set
full_name: Duke Spleen Data Set (DSDS) — Spleen MRI and CT with Segmentation Masks
anatomy: spleen (chronic liver disease / portal hypertension cohort)
protocol_note: Two MRI contrasts (coronal SSFSE, axial T1w opposed-phase) plus axial post-contrast CT; 109 series drawn from 69 patients, so many patients contribute more than one series type
size: 109 CT/MRI series (6,322 images) from 69 patients: 29 axial post-contrast CT, 40 coronal SSFSE MRI, 40 axial T1w opposed-phase MRI
segmentation_detail: Manual binary spleen masks for all 109 series, provided as separate binary DICOM image stacks (0 = background, 1 = spleen)
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (or custom Duke license for commercial use)
description: Multi-modality, multi-vendor spleen segmentation dataset from Duke University — 109 abdominal CT and MRI series (6,322 images) from 69 patients with known or suspected chronic liver disease and portal hypertension, each with a manual binary spleen mask; spleens range from normal to markedly abnormal (104–2,025 cm³) with confounders such as ascites and varices, and files are restricted on Zenodo (access by request).

label_schema: Voxel-wise binary spleen segmentation — masks distributed as separate binary DICOM images matching the source series (pixel value 0 = background, 1 = spleen)
All 109 series are segmented: 29 axial CT post-contrast, 40 coronal MRI SSFSE, 40 axial MRI T1w opposed-phase

Segmentation provenance: manual segmentation by one of four trained imaging core-lab technologists, reviewed and adjusted by a fellowship-trained abdominal radiologist (12 years post-fellowship experience)
details.file_structure: Anonymized image series and their matching binary spleen masks are both stored as DICOM (Zenodo version 2023.02); the total archive size is not publicly listed because the files are restricted (the ~80.7 GB figure on the record page is Zenodo's cumulative download-traffic 'Data volume' stat, not the dataset size), and the exact folder layout inside the restricted archives is not publicly documented on the record page.
details.splits: No official train/validation/test split is defined in the paper or on Zenodo.
details.extra: Paper: Wang et al., arXiv:2305.05732. Cohort: 69 patients (47 M / 22 F, age 41–88) randomly selected from prior studies of known or suspected chronic liver disease, with and without cirrhosis/portal hypertension; GE and Siemens scanners at 1.5T and 3.0T; CT 34–150 slices at 2.5–5.0 mm, SSFSE 20–45 slices at 6–7 mm, opposed-phase 26–80 slices at 4–8 mm. Companion dataset: Duke Liver Dataset (DLDS, catalog id duke-liver-mri). Access: Zenodo files are restricted — request CC BY-NC-ND access via DOCR.Help@dm.Duke.edu, or a custom unrestricted/commercial license via Duke OTC (otcquestions@duke.edu).

name: CDD-CESM
full_name: Categorized Digital Database for Low energy and Subtracted Contrast Enhanced Spectral Mammography images
protocol_note: Contrast-enhanced spectral mammography (CESM): dual-energy acquisition 2 min after IV iodinated contrast (1.5 mL/kg); low energy 26-31 kVp, high energy 45-49 kVp, recombined/subtracted images; CC and MLO views; GE Senographe DS and Hologic Selenia Dimensions
size: 2,006 images (1,003 low-energy + 1,003 subtracted CESM) / 326 patients; ~1.5 GB
segmentation_detail: Hand-drawn outlines of abnormal findings drawn by an experienced radiologist with VGG Image Annotator, provided as a CSV
paired_text_detail: Full radiology reports per case (DOCX, zipped)
description: Contrast-enhanced spectral mammography dataset of 326 Egyptian patients with 2,006 paired low-energy and subtracted JPEG images, BI-RADS annotations by two radiologists, normal/benign/malignant outcome, hand-drawn lesion segmentations and full reports.

label_schema: Per-image outcome class: Normal / Benign / Malignant (Sci Data Table 2: 757 normal, 587 benign, 662 malignant images)

protocol_note: Chest radiographs from MIDRC (previously unreleased)

description: RSNA benchmark of previously unreleased MIDRC chest radiographs for evaluating multimodal LLMs, with 12 cardiothoracic labels verified by three cardiothoracic radiologists per study; 100 studies are released and 100 are held out by RSNA.

label_schema: 12 study-level benchmark labels (multi-label): airspace opacity, aneurysm, cardiomegaly, COPD, hiatal hernia, interstitial opacity, lung mass, lung nodule, lymphadenopathy, pleural effusion, pleural thickening, pneumothorax
Expert agreement level per study (radiologist ratings 'Agree All' / 'Agree Mostly' / 'Disagree' of the LLM-suggested labels)
details.file_structure: Zip archive with the 100 released studies in DICOM plus benchmark labels and expert agreement levels (per RSNA's AWS Open Data registry submission, S3 bucket reveal-cxr, us-west-2, controlled access via MIRA).

details.extra: Built from 13,735 deidentified MIDRC chest radiograph studies and reports: GPT-4o extracted findings from reports and locally hosted Phi-4-Reasoning mapped them to the 12 labels; 1,000 sampled studies were reviewed, 381 had >=2 'Agree All' ratings and 200 were selected. Paper: Wei et al., arXiv:2601.15129 (Jan 2026). MIRA download requires email registration and acceptance of the terms of use. An AWS Open Data registry entry was submitted by RSNA (awslabs/open-data-registry PR #3459, opened 2026-11-06, not merged as of 2026-11-15).
details.label_readers: 17 fellowship-trained cardiothoracic radiologists (10 institutions, 4 countries); 3 independent blinded radiologists per study rated the LLM-suggested labels; studies kept when >=2 rated 'Agree All' (majority vote)
details.reference_standard: Report-derived LLM labels (GPT-4o extraction + Phi-4-Reasoning mapping) accepted by majority of 3 cardiothoracic radiologists; no pathology/CT confirmation
details.third_party_note: Governed by the RSNA MIRA Dataset Research Use Agreement (accepted on MIRA before download; MIRA states datasets are for non-commercial research). The agreement text was not viewable without starting a download request, so no API/online-service clause could be verified, even though the benchmark is designed for evaluating multimodal LLMs.

CXR-LT 2024 (45 labels): the 26 above + 19 new: Adenopathy, Azygos Lobe, Clavicle Fracture, Fissure, Hydropneumothorax, Infarction, Kyphosis, Lobar Atelectasis, Pleural Other, Pulmonary Embolism, Pulmonary Hypertension, Rib Fracture, Round Atelectasis, Tuberculosis, Bulla, Cardiomyopathy, Hilum, Osteopenia, Scoliosis

details.splits: 2023: train / development / test (70/10/20, patient-level); 2024: shared labeled training set with task-specific development and test sets; MICCAI 2023 subset: train/val/test
details.extra: Versions 1.0.0 (2023-06-12), 1.1.0 (2023-09-28), 2.0.0 (2025-03-19). Requires credentialed access to MIMIC-CXR-JPG v2.0.0+. CXR-LT 2026 (ISBI 2026) switched to PadChest/PadChest-GR images; its labels were distributed to registered participants via GitHub with a no-sharing / delete-after-competition condition, so they are not part of this record.
details.label_readers: Bulk labels parsed automatically from reports (RadText for the 2023 new findings); gold-standard subset: 451 reports annotated by 6 human readers (>=2 per report, disagreements adjudicated by a third annotator), 406 retained (CXR-LT 2023 overview; reader specialty not stated)
details.reference_standard: Report-derived NLP labels (not image-verified), except the 406-report manually annotated gold-standard subset used as the 2024 Task 2 test set
details.third_party_note: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0; PhysioNet guidance 'Use of MIMIC Data with Large Language Models and Online Services' (2025-09-24): the DUA 'explicitly prohibits sharing access to the data with third parties', including 'sending it through APIs or using it on online platforms'; only services verified for zero retention, no training use and no human review (or local LLMs) are acceptable.

Distributed via a Google Form (https://forms.gle/bmYPtLy4qsJahVKFA); images come from NIH (Box) or the requester-pays GCS bucket gcs-public-data--healthcare-nih-chest-xray.

description: 831 multiphase CT exams of renal masses up to 7 cm (UCSF, 2002-2018), distributed as per-patient HDF5 volumes with registered phases, mass masks or boxes, and post-surgical pathology labels.

label_schema: attrs.pathology, attrs.pathology_grade, attrs.tumor_type from post-surgery pathology (value sets listed in the repo tutorials, not on the page)
mask: bounding box or polygon mask of the renal mass
details.file_structure: One .hdf5 per patient (random 10-character ID) with keys noncon, arterial, portven, delay, mask and attrs (manufacturer, age, sex, *_pixdim, pathology fields); phase_reg_key.csv; S3 bucket s3://ucsf-rmac-dataset (us-west-2, --no-sign-request) or imagingdatasets.ucsf.edu/dataset/3.
details.extra: Only masses <=7 cm (T1) were included. Volumes are HDF5 arrays, not DICOM, so original series headers are not available. Citation: Larson P et al., UCSF RMaC, UCSF Ci2 Datasets for Medical Imaging 2025, doi 10.58078/C2WC74.
details.reference_standard: Post-surgery pathology (diagnosis, grade, tumor type)
details.third_party_note: CC BY 4.0 per the AWS Open Data registry entry; CC BY 4.0 permits redistribution and adaptation with attribution; no clause restricting external services.

name: UniToBrain
full_name: UniToBrain Dataset (DeepHealth Use Case 3, University of Turin)
protocol_note: 4D CT perfusion time series (GE 64-slice, 80 kV, typically 89 volumes over 44.5 s, 40 mm coverage) - perfusion time frames, not separate contrast phases; per subject raw, registered and filtered CTP plus derived perfusion maps
size: Zenodo: 115 subjects (100 train / 15 test), 50.8 GB; full 258-subject collection on IEEE DataPort (80.04 GB)
description: Brain CT perfusion series of consecutive patients from Turin's Molinette hospital, released with registered/filtered data and algorithm-derived perfusion maps (CBF, CBV, MTT, TTP, delay) for learning perfusion-map estimation.

label_schema: Per-subject perfusion maps used as regression targets: NLR_CBF, NLR_CBV, NLR_MTT, NLR_TTP, NLR_Delay
No lesion segmentations or diagnosis labels
perfusion maps per subject (CBF, CBV, MTT, TTP, delay)
details.file_structure: Per subject: <patID> (raw DICOM), <patID>_Registered, <patID>_Registered_Filtered_3mm_20HU and <...>_Maps (5 map subfolders); ctp_data.7z holds training (100) and test (15) folders; dati_ctp.csv acquisition metadata; dicomtonpy.py converts DICOM to NumPy.
details.splits: 100 training / 15 test subjects (Zenodo subsample)
details.extra: Zenodo holds only the 115-subject subsample; the full 258-subject collection is on IEEE DataPort (doi 10.21227/x8ea-vh16, CC BY 4.0, open access but needs a free IEEE account). Both copies are CC BY 4.0. Dataset paper arXiv 2208.00650; CNN paper arXiv 2101.05992.
details.label_readers: Perfusion maps computed algorithmically ('state-of-the-art algorithms' per arXiv 2208.00650; software not named on the record)
details.third_party_note: Zenodo and IEEE DataPort copies are both CC BY 4.0; CC BY 4.0 permits redistribution and adaptation with attribution; no clause restricting external services.

name: WAW-TACE
full_name: WAW-TACE: A Hepatocellular Carcinoma Multiphase CT Dataset with Segmentations, Radiomics Features, and Clinical Data
protocol_note: Pre-TACE multiphase CT with phase codes 0-3: native/precontrast (n=200), late arterial (n=230), portal venous (n=231), delayed (n=193)
size: 233 patients, 854 CT volumes, 377 tumor masks (48.2 GB)
segmentation_detail: 377 HCC lesion masks drawn on the phase where each tumor was most visible (radiologist-corrected TotalSegmentator drafts validated by two more radiologists); automated TotalSegmentator multi-organ masks for every phase, not manually corrected
description: Pre-treatment four-phase CT of 233 treatment-naive HCC patients treated with TACE at the Medical University of Warsaw (2016-2021), with radiologist tumor masks, automated organ masks, radiomics and survival outcomes.

label_schema: Tumor masks: 377 HCC lesions (NIfTI/NRRD), each drawn on its best-visualized phase
Organ masks: automated TotalSegmentator labels per phase (not manually corrected)
Radiomics table: 32 features x 102 volumes of interest + 75 gray-level features for HCC (3,339 columns; not normalized, no imputation)
Clinical data: demographics, labs, TACE details, technical success, LI-RADS treatment response, PFS and OS (definitions in Supplementary Table S1)
details.file_structure: ct_scans_1..4 zips (NIfTI per phase), tumor_masks zip, organ_masks zip, radiomics XLSX, clinical_data XLSX, ct_hcc_metadata_v2.csv (incl. section thickness), supplementary_table_s1 definitions.
details.extra: Central Clinical Hospital of the Medical University of Warsaw, May 2016 - April 2021. Paper: Bartnik et al., Radiology: AI 2024 (doi 10.1148/ryai.240296). Treatment response and PFS were read by one author, so they are more subjective than OS.
details.label_readers: Tumor masks: TotalSegmentator lesion drafts corrected by 1 radiologist (6 y) in 3D Slicer, then validated/edited by 2 radiologists (14 y, 11 y); organ masks automated only; treatment response by one author (LI-RADS TRA)
details.reference_standard: HCC = LI-RADS v2018 LR-5, or pathology for 9 equivocal cases; OS/PFS from follow-up
details.third_party_note: CC BY 4.0 permits redistribution and adaptation with attribution; no clause restricting external services.

name: MR-ART
full_name: Movement-Related Artefacts (MR-ART) dataset
protocol_note: Single sequence (3D T1w MPRAGE, Siemens Magnetom Prisma 3T, 1 mm isotropic) repeated under three conditions: acq-standard (still), acq-headmotion1 (low motion), acq-headmotion2 (high motion)
size: 148 healthy adults, up to 3 T1-weighted scans each (8 participants miss one motion scan)
description: Matched motion-free and motion-corrupted T1-weighted brain MRI of 148 healthy adults (still, low and high instructed head motion) with neuroradiologist artefact scores and MRIQC metrics, in BIDS.

label_schema: Artefact score per scan: 1 = clinically good, 2 = medium, 3 = bad (unusable for diagnosis)
Acquisition condition per scan (BIDS acq- entity): standard, headmotion1, headmotion2
artefact score per scan (1 good / 2 medium / 3 bad)
details.file_structure: BIDS: sub-<id>/anat/sub-<id>_acq-{standard,headmotion1,headmotion2}_T1w.nii.gz with JSON sidecars; derivatives/scores.tsv (artefact scores) and MRIQC outputs; participants.tsv.

details.label_readers: Two neuroradiologists (>10 y), blinded to condition; each scan rated by one of them after harmonizing on 100 scans
details.reference_standard: Motion level defined by acquisition instruction; clinical usability by neuroradiologist score
details.third_party_note: CC0 (public-domain dedication) per dataset_description.json; no restrictions.

name: VinDr-Multiphase
full_name: VinDr-Multiphase: A Benchmark Dataset for Phase Recognition in Abdominal Contrast-Enhanced CT Scans
protocol_note: Each scan labeled with one of 4 phase classes: non-contrast, arterial, venous, others

license: VinDr-Multiphase Data Use Agreement (text not reviewed)
description: Abdominal CT from two Hanoi hospitals (265 studies, 1,188 scans) with radiologist scan-level contrast-phase labels (non-contrast, arterial, venous, other) for phase recognition.

label_schema: Scan-level phase class: non-contrast, arterial, venous, others
details.splits: 830 scans training / 358 scans internal test (~70/30, per paper)
details.extra: Paper: Dao et al., Med Phys 2022 (doi 10.1002/mp.15551; arXiv 2203.11206). Sources: Hospital 108 and Hanoi Medical University Hospital PACS. details.label_readers: Two radiologists annotated remotely in VinDr Lab (per-scan reading scheme not stated)
details.reference_standard: Phase assigned visually by radiologists
details.third_party_note: Access only via a signed DUA that was not publicly readable; no verified clause on external services.

name: PLC-CECT
full_name: Primary Liver Cancer CECT Imaging Dataset
protocol_note: 4 phases per subject: plain (non-contrast), arterial, venous, delayed - each stored as a separate NIfTI file
size: 361 subjects (278 primary liver cancer: 94 HCC, 99 ICC, 85 cHCC-CCA; 83 non-liver-cancer controls); 1,444 3D CECT volumes; ~42 GB
segmentation_detail: Liver masks (automated LiverMask model refined by clinicians in ITK-SNAP) and lesion masks (two independent clinicians, consensus; mean inter-observer Dice 0.7586); ~50,560 lesion-containing slices
description: Four-phase contrast-enhanced CT (plain, arterial, venous, delayed) of 278 pathologically confirmed primary liver cancer patients (HCC, ICC, cHCC-CCA) and 83 controls from one Chongqing hospital (2015-2022), with liver and lesion masks.

label_schema: Diagnostic label per patient: HCC, ICC, cHCC-CCA, or non-liver-cancer control
details.file_structure: Per patient (P0001-P0361) separate NIfTI files per phase plus liver and lesion mask NIfTI files; patient_data.csv with ID, age, sex, cancer type, phases and file paths.

Paper: Luo et al., Sci Data 12:768 (2025), doi 10.1038/s41597-025-05125-2 (the article is CC BY-NC-ND; the dataset is CC BY 4.0). Short name follows the code repo github.com/ljwa2323/PLC_CECT.
details.label_readers: Lesions: two independent clinicians (expert physicians), disagreements reconciled to consensus; liver: automated LiverMask model refined by clinicians
details.reference_standard: Cancer type confirmed by histology and/or cytology of resected or biopsied tissue
details.version: V4 (DataCite, updated 2025-05-11; the paper cites V3)
details.third_party_note: Dataset CC BY 4.0; the paper states users may download, use and redistribute it, including commercially, with attribution.

name: BrainMetShare
full_name: Stanford BrainMetShare brain metastases MRI dataset
protocol_note: 4 co-registered axial sequences resampled to 256x256: T1 gradient-echo post-contrast (IR-FSPGR/BRAVO), T1 spin-echo pre-contrast, T1 spin-echo post-contrast (CUBE), T2 FLAIR post-contrast
size: 156 patients (105 labeled training / 51 unlabeled test); 1,517 annotated metastases in the 105 training scans
segmentation_detail: Binary metastasis masks (0/255) for the 105 training cases, drawn on T1 gradient-echo post-contrast images
license: Stanford School of Medicine Brain Mets Dataset Research Use Agreement (personal, non-commercial research)
description: Multisequence brain MRI of 156 patients with brain metastases (Stanford, 2016-2018), with radiologist-drawn metastasis masks for 105 training cases.

label_schema: Binary metastasis mask in folder 'seg' (0 = background, 255 = metastasis), training group only
Sequence folders: 0 = T1 gradient-echo post, 1 = T1 spin-echo pre, 2 = T1 spin-echo post, 3 = T2 FLAIR post
details.file_structure: mets_stanford_release_train/<subject>/{0,1,2,3,seg} and mets_stanford_release_test/<subject>/{0,1,2,3}; the official page does not state the image file extension.
details.splits: 105 labeled (train) / 51 unlabeled (test); the paper used 100 train / 5 development / 51 test
details.extra: GE 1.5T/3T and Siemens Skyra 3T, patients imaged June 2016 - June 2018; primaries mostly lung (99) and breast (33). Paper: Grovik et al., JMRI 2020;51:175-182 (arXiv 1903.07988). Dataset DOI 10.71718/z66c-qr59. The agreement also forbids modification and derivative works.
details.label_readers: Two neuroradiologists (8 and 2 years) manually delineated each enhancing lesion in OsiriX, cross-checking ROIs
details.third_party_note: AIMI page agreement: personal non-commercial research only; no distribution, publication or reproduction without written permission; no sharing of the download link; no derivative works. No explicit clause on external services.

name: LiverHccSeg
full_name: LiverHccSeg: A Publicly Available Multiphasic MRI Dataset with Liver and HCC Tumor Segmentations and Inter-Rater Agreement Analysis
protocol_note: Pre-contrast, arterial, portal-venous and delayed phases (files pre, art, pv, del) plus versions registered to the arterial phase (art_pre, art_pv, art_del; BioImage Suite, visually verified)
size: 17 patients with liver masks / 14 with tumor masks (one multiphasic MRI study each); 2.6 GB
segmentation_detail: Liver and HCC tumor masks from each of two board-certified abdominal radiologists (rater1/rater2 files) with inter-rater metrics
description: Multiphasic contrast-enhanced liver MRI of TCGA-LIHC patients with liver and HCC tumor segmentations from two abdominal radiologists and an inter-rater agreement analysis.

label_schema: Per-rater, per-tumor HCC mask (e.g. rater1_tumor1.nii.gz), 14 cases
segm_metrics.xlsx: inter-rater Dice/Jaccard/HD95 (liver Dice 0.95 +/- 0.01; tumor Dice 0.85 +/- 0.16)

details.extra: Data in Brief 2023 (doi 10.1016/j.dib.2023.109662). Hosted on Zenodo (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7957515), not a TCIA analysis result. Typed 'dataset' rather than 'annotation' because it ships the TCGA-LIHC MRI DICOMs it annotates. v1.1 fixed an incorrect liver mask.
details.label_readers: Two board-certified abdominal radiologists (9 and 10 y) segmented in 3D Slicer 4.10.2; masks provided per rater; the paper mentions a consensus meeting for disagreements

related.name: TCGA-LIHC
related.note: One multiphasic MRI per TCGA-LIHC patient selected, converted to NIfTI, phases co-registered to arterial phase, and liver/HCC masks from two radiologists added

details.third_party_note: Zenodo record is CC BY 4.0 (the Data in Brief article is CC BY-NC-ND); CC BY 4.0 permits redistribution and adaptation with attribution; no clause restricting external services.

name: MRE-IBD
full_name: A comprehensive dataset of magnetic resonance enterography images with intestinal segment annotations

size: 114 patients, one coronal HASTE volume each (25-31 slices); 441.5 MB
segmentation_detail: Pixel-level labels of 10 gastrointestinal segments (stomach, duodenum, small intestine, appendix, cecum, ascending/transverse/descending/sigmoid colon, rectum)

details.file_structure: One zip ('A comprehensive dataset.zip') with per-case xx_data.nii.gz (image) and xx_label.nii.gz (label).
details.extra: Paper: Zhong et al., Sci Data 12:425 (2025), doi 10.1038/s41597-025-04760-z (the article is CC BY-NC-ND; the Zenodo data record is CC BY 4.0). Zenodo describes the cohort as IBD; the paper specifies Crohn's disease. Scans December 2019 - May 2022.
details.label_readers: Two radiologists (3 and 6 y) refined pre-trained-model drafts slice by slice in ITK-SNAP; an abdominal imaging expert (>10 y) reviewed and resolved disagreements by discussion
details.third_party_note: Zenodo data record is CC BY 4.0; CC BY 4.0 permits redistribution and adaptation with attribution; no clause restricting external services.

name: MRISegmentator-Abdomen
full_name: MRISegmenter (MRISegmentator-Abdomen) T1-weighted abdominal MRI dataset, NIH Clinical Center
protocol_note: 4 axial T1-weighted series per patient: pre-contrast (PRE), arterial (ART), portal venous (VEN), delayed (DEL); phase is encoded in file names (e.g. train_001_ART_0000.nii.gz); 1.5T and 3T
size: 195 patients, 780 T1-weighted series (69,248 slices); 4.8 GB zip
segmentation_detail: Voxel labels for 62 abdominal organs and structures (15 organs, 7 vessels, 8 muscles, 32 bones) on every series
license: NIH Clinical Center data terms: no restrictions on use; cite the 2025 Radiology paper, link the NIH download site, acknowledge NIH CC, no re-identification
description: T1-weighted abdominal MRI of 195 NIH Clinical Center patients (2019-2021) with pre-contrast, arterial, portal venous and delayed series, each annotated for 62 organs and structures.

label_schema: 62 integer labels per series (e.g. 1 = spleen ... 62 = vertebrae_T7); full table and ITK-SNAP label file in the GitHub repo
Structure groups: G1 15 organs, G2 7 vessels, G3 8 muscles, G4 32 bones
details.file_structure: MRISegmenter_FINAL_Data_T1only_public_5Aug2025.zip -> Release/ImageTr (540), labelsTr (540), ImageTs (240), labelsTs (240) NIfTI in nnU-Net naming <split>_<nnn>_<PRE|ART|VEN|DEL>; crosswalk_*_ANONYMIZED_withScannerInfo.xlsx for train and test.
details.splits: 135 training patients (540 series) / 60 test patients (240 series)

Model weights (MRISegmentator.zip) sit in the same folder. The paper's external tests used AMOS22 and Duke Liver.
details.label_readers: TotalSegmentator pseudo-labels (via synthetic CT for organs/vessels; via registered same-day CT for muscles/bones) refined over 4 nnU-Net human-in-the-loop rounds by a main grader; a radiology resident verified one sequence per patient for 60 training patients and reviewed test sequences; a senior radiologist (30+ y) reviewed two sequences per test patient
details.reference_standard: Radiologist-verified reference annotations
details.third_party_note: GitHub README: 'There are no restrictions on the use of the NIH MRI volumes' (only citation, link, acknowledgement and no re-identification are required).

name: ACRIN-6698
full_name: ACRIN 6698/I-SPY2 Breast DWI
protocol_note: Breast MRI per visit: T2-weighted, DWI (b = 0, 100, 600, 800 s/mm2, 3 directions; some GE scans as merged 'MSMB' series) and T1 DCE; derived 4-b trace DWI, ADC maps, PE-early/PE-late and SER maps; visits T0 (baseline), T1 (~3 weeks), T2 (mid), T3 (pre-surgery), plus test-retest scans
size: 385 subjects / 1,123 studies / 18,747 series / 2,911,334 images (~842 GB download)
segmentation_detail: Manual multi-slice whole-tumor DWI ROIs (DICOM SEG) and DCE functional tumor volume (FTV) masks (DICOM SEG)
description: Multi-center breast MRI with quantitative DWI from the ACRIN 6698 sub-study of the I-SPY 2 neoadjuvant chemotherapy trial (385 subjects, timepoints T0-T3), with tumor ROIs, ADC and DCE maps, and pCR outcomes.

label_schema: DWI tumor ROI: manual multi-slice whole-tumor segmentation (DICOM SEG), located on DCE subtraction and refined on ADC / high-b DWI, excluding fat, fibroglandular tissue, clips and necrosis/seroma
DCE functional tumor volume (FTV) analysis masks (DICOM SEG) with PE-early, PE-late and SER maps
Outcome: pathologic complete response (pCR) at surgery (withheld for the BMMR2 test set)
Cohort flags: primary analysis subgroup (242), test-retest (71), BMMR2 train (117) / test (74)
details.file_structure: DICOM MR and SEG via TCIA Data Retriever manifests per subset; ancillary XLSX/CSV files (clinical/outcome, DWI QC, MRI acquisition parameters, analysis-mask description, private tag dictionaries).
details.splits: BMMR2 challenge: 117 training / 74 test subjects
details.extra: 406 women enrolled at 10 sites (Aug 2012 - Jan 2015); 272 randomized to I-SPY 2 arms, 242 in the primary analysis cohort; 116 'Not Randomized' subjects contribute baseline MRI only. TCIA's I-SPY2 Imaging Cohort 1 combines 719 ISPY2 and 266 ACRIN-6698 cases (985). Some derived objects are not fully DICOM-compliant, and SER/FTV values differ slightly from the original I-SPY 2 analysis.
details.label_readers: DWI tumor ROIs drawn manually at the UCSF Breast Imaging Research Program processing lab with in-house IDL tools (reader profession/count not stated)
details.reference_standard: pCR = pathologic complete response at surgery
details.third_party_note: CC BY 4.0 (TCIA); TCIA Data Usage Policy requires citation; no clause restricting external services.

name: C4KC-KiTS

description: TCIA DICOM release of the 210 KiTS19 training cases: preoperative contrast-enhanced CT of nephrectomy patients (University of Minnesota) with manual kidney and tumor DICOM-SEG segmentations and clinical data.

label_schema: Clinical CSV (210 subjects): demographics, exposure, measurements, diagnosis, treatment, follow-up
clinical data: demographics, exposure, measurements, diagnosis, treatment, follow-up (CSV)

name: ISLES 2015-2018
full_name: ISLES (Ischemic Stroke Lesion Segmentation/Prediction) Challenge Datasets (2015, 2016, 2017, 2018)
protocol_note: 2015 SISS: T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI; 2015 SPES: T1c, T2, DWI, CBF, CBV, TTP, Tmax; 2016/2017: raw 4D PWI, ADC, MTT, rCBF, rCBV, Tmax, TTP; 2018: CT perfusion (4D CTP source plus CBF, CBV, MTT, Tmax maps) and a CT image
size: ~8.4 GB zipped across the Zenodo versions; ISLES 2015 SISS 28 train / 36 test and SPES 30 train / 20 test; ISLES 2016 30 train (Zenodo folders; paper reports 35) / 19 test; ISLES 2017 43 train / 32 test; ISLES 2018 94 train / 62 test CT perfusion slabs (63 / 40 patients)
segmentation_detail: Binary lesion masks (OT): 2015 SISS sub-acute lesion (on FLAIR); 2015 SPES hypoperfused tissue (penumbra) plus DWI core and merged labels; 2016/2017 final infarct on follow-up T2; 2018 DWI-derived infarct core on the CTP slab. Masks ship for training sets, plus 13 ISLES 2017 test cases in the 2026-10 version; other test-set labels stay private
license: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo record); archives also carry the original SMIR ODbL 1.0 / DbCL 1.0 notice
description: Zenodo re-release of the ISLES 2015-2018 stroke challenge data (formerly on SMIR): multi-center multiparametric MRI (2015-2017) and CT perfusion (2018) of ischemic stroke with expert lesion masks for sub-acute lesion segmentation, perfusion lesion estimation and lesion outcome prediction.

label_schema: OT = binary lesion mask (0 background, 1 lesion), one NIfTI per labelled case
ISLES 2015 SISS: sub-acute ischemic lesion segmented on FLAIR (other sequences used as support)
ISLES 2015 SPES: penumbralabel = hypoperfused tissue (Tmax > 6 s threshold, manually corrected), corelabel = manual DWI core (training only, not used for ranking), mergedlabels = combined map
ISLES 2016/2017: final infarct delineated on follow-up T2 (paper: 90-day follow-up; 2016 text also cites 3-9 month scans), predicted from acute perfusion/diffusion maps
ISLES 2018: infarct core manually delineated on DWI acquired within 3 h after CTP, co-registered to the CTP slab
ISLES 2017 test CSV columns: case, TICIScaleGrade, timeSinceStroke, timeToTreatment
TICI grade, time since stroke, time to treatment (ISLES 2017 test CSV)
details.file_structure: Zip per edition/split (e.g. ISLES2015.zip, ISLES2016_Training_Native/CoRegistered.zip, ISLES2017_Training.zip, ISLES2018_Training.zip); inside, one folder per case holding one folder per image named VSD.Brain.XX.O.<MR_|CT_><map>.<id> (SMIR.Brain... for 2017/2018) with a .nii volume and a License_ODC_ODBL.txt; 2016/2017 4D PWI folders add a CSV of acquisition number / instance creation time / slice position; 2017/2018 folders add SMIR metadata JSON. 2016 comes in native and co-registered versions. The 2017 test-with-labels zip has coregmask/ (maps + OT) and 'Testing Raw' acute/follow-up folders for 13 cases.
details.splits: Official challenge splits: 2015 SISS 28/36, SPES 30/20; 2016 35/19 (Zenodo training folders hold 30 cases); 2017 43/32 (extended versions of the 2016 sets, test = 19 ISLES 2016 + 13 new cases); 2018 63/40 patients = 94/62 slabs. Test labels released only for the 13 new ISLES 2017 test cases.
details.label_readers: Training labels from one expert per case: 2015 SISS one rater (test set had two raters, labels not released); 2015 SPES one expert (semi-manual); 2016/2017 a board-certified neuroradiologist (2016 test labels: two raters merged with STAPLE, not released); 2018 a stroke neurologist with >10 years of experience, then group review until accepted, blinded to perfusion imaging
details.reference_standard: Lesion = expert manual or semi-manual delineation: sub-acute lesion on FLAIR (2015 SISS); Tmax > 6 s hypoperfusion (2015 SPES); final infarct on follow-up T2 (2016/2017); DWI infarct core within 3 h of CTP (2018). No histological confirmation.

related.name: SICAS Medical Image Repository (SMIR) ISLES archive (smir.ch, offline)

details.version: Zenodo concept 10.5281/zenodo.17736411 with four versions, each holding different files: 17736412 (2025-11-27; 2015 test, 2016, 2017, 2018), 18655348 (2026-02-16; SPES 2015 training), 19135955 (2026-03; full ISLES2015.zip), 23760681 (2026-10-29; ISLES 2017 testing with labels)
details.third_party_note: Zenodo lists CC BY 4.0. The embedded SMIR notice says the data are 'made available under the Open Database License' with contents under the Database Contents License; both allow sharing with attribution (ODbL adds share-alike for derived databases).
details.extra: ISLES 2018 is CT perfusion, not MRI: no MR_DWI folder was found in the Zenodo 2018 training archive, although the 2018 paper says DWI was provided to participants. ISLES 2016 and 2017 overlap: the 2017 sets extend the 2016 sets, so they cannot serve as independent test sets. One ISLES 2016 native training case lacks an rCBV map. isles-2022 and isles-2024 are separate releases with their own catalog entries.

links.label: Zenodo version 2026-03 (ISLES2015.zip: SISS + SPES training and testing)

name: BraTS-Lighthouse 2025
full_name: BraTS 2025 Lighthouse Challenge (MICCAI 2025)
