segmentation_detail: Tumor sub-region masks for glioma and metastases: NETC (1), SNFH (2), ET (3), resection cavity RC (4). Other tasks keep the label sets of their source BraTS datasets.
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (BraTS data, 'unless otherwise indicated') + BraTS-Lighthouse 2025 challenge terms
description: The 2025 MICCAI BraTS Lighthouse challenge bundles 11 brain-tumor MRI tasks: segmentation of glioma, meningioma, metastases, sub-Saharan African glioma and pediatric tumors, plus synthesis, inpainting and response classification, adding a new pre- and post-treatment brain metastasis set and a multiply-annotated test set.

label_schema: Label 1 - NETC: non-enhancing tumor core (necrosis, cysts) enclosed by enhancing tumor
Label 2 - SNFH: surrounding non-enhancing FLAIR hyperintensity (edema, infiltrative tumor, post-treatment changes)
Evaluated regions: ET; tumor core = ET + NETC; whole tumor = ET + SNFH + NETC (+ RC for glioma)
Glioma case IDs encode timepoint: 000/001 pre-operative baselines, 100/101 post-treatment scans
Task 11 (BraTSPRO): RANO response class (complete response, partial response, stable disease, progressive disease) between consecutive scans
RANO response categories (Task 11; training data = LUMIERE)
glioma histology classes (Task 10, pathology slides - out of scope)
details.file_structure: Per-case folders of co-registered mpMRI NIfTI (.nii.gz) volumes plus a segmentation volume, in per-task Synapse folders (final QC'd 'BraTS-25 datasets' folder syn64377310, access-restricted). Glioma: skull-stripped, 1 mm^3, common template. METS 2025: 968 UCSF/UCSD cases in native space, 328 cases in SRI24 space.
details.splits: METS 2025: 1,296 training (labels) / 179 validation (no labels) / 305 test (hidden), from Duke, NCI, Missouri, WashU, Yale, UCSF, Northwestern, UCSD. Task 11: train on LUMIERE (91 patients, 616 scans); hidden validation/test 306 patients (6 val / 300 test). Lighthouse test: 150 cases. Other tasks reuse the splits of the earlier BraTS editions.
details.label_readers: Glioma: one to four raters following one protocol, approved by experienced neuroradiologists. METS 2025: STAPLE fusion of algorithm outputs, manually refined by neuroradiology experts, approved by board-certified attending neuroradiologists (UCSD longitudinal cases: formal neuroradiologist evaluation, no extra BraTS-METS board review). Lighthouse test set: each case annotated four times by two neuroradiology faculty (two from scratch, two refining nnU-Net pre-segmentations, 7-day gaps between rounds).
details.reference_standard: Expert-approved manual or refined segmentations of MRI tumor sub-regions; no histopathologic confirmation of voxel labels. Task 11 response labels follow RANO criteria.
details.version: Final QC-approved training/validation data released 2025-06-26 (preliminary release 2025-03-10)
details.third_party_note: Challenge Rules: 'BraTS data is subject to a CC BY-NC license, unless otherwise indicated. You are free to use, redistribute and/or refer to the BraTS datasets in your own research, provided that the data is used for non-commercial use'. No clause on external online services; whether a commercial API that keeps or trains on uploads is 'non-commercial' use is not addressed.
details.extra: Most segmentation tasks reuse data already listed separately (see related), so do not count them as new cohorts. As of 2026-11 the Synapse registration/download steps on the Data Access page are hidden (challenge closed). The page says the post-challenge training+validation release 'will be hosted on TCIA', but no BraTS 2025 collection was found on TCIA at check time. It also says the Lighthouse test set 'will be released to the public after the conclusion of the challenge', and that the BraTS 2026 challenge reuses some 2025 datasets. Task 10 (BraTS-Path) is histopathology and out of scope.

name: EPVS 2024
full_name: Enlarged Perivascular Spaces (EPVS) Segmentation Challenge - MICCAI 2024
anatomy: Brain (perivascular spaces in basal ganglia and centrum semiovale)
protocol_note: T1-weighted, T2-weighted, T2-FLAIR, co-registered to the highest-resolution native space (T1w for SG70/MACC, T2w for Edinburgh/Shanghai) and skull-stripped
size: 200 brain MRI scans: 100 training (with masks), 50 validation, 50 test, from 4 cohorts (Edinburgh, NUS-SG70, NUS-MACC, Shanghai TCM); training set ~3.3 GB (400 NIfTI files)
segmentation_detail: Binary EPVS masks following STRIVE, in basal ganglia and centrum semiovale regions of interest
license: EPVS Challenge Terms of Use (research/education; challenge use only; no redistribution)
description: Multi-site brain MRI (T1w, T2w, FLAIR) from UK, Singapore and Chinese cohorts with STRIVE-based manual masks of enlarged perivascular spaces, released for the MICCAI 2024 EPVS segmentation challenge.

label_schema: <case>_PVS.nii.gz: binary mask, 1 = enlarged perivascular space, 0 = background
Annotations follow STRIVE (Wardlaw et al. 2013); evaluation restricted to basal ganglia (BG) and centrum semiovale (CSO) ROI templates
details.file_structure: EPVS_challenge_data/<site: ED | MACC | SG70>/<case>/ with <case>_T1w.nii.gz, <case>_T2w.nii.gz, <case>_FLAIR.nii.gz and <case>_PVS.nii.gz (manual mask); converted from DICOM with dcm2niix or mriconvert, co-registered with FSL-FLIRT, skull-stripped with FreeSurfer or BET2.
details.splits: Training 100 (Edinburgh 60, SG70 20, MACC 20); validation 50 (Edinburgh 30, SG70 10, MACC 10; images only); test 50 (Edinburgh 10, SG70 10, MACC 10, Shanghai TCM 20 as an unseen clinical site). The Synapse overview text says 70 test scans, but its per-site table and the overview paper give 50.
details.label_readers: Edinburgh: priors from the Ballerini et al. 2018 method, edited independently by two blinded trained observers, then consensus, with a third experienced annotator resolving disagreements. SG70/MACC: pretrained U-Net priors edited by experienced neuroradiologists and neuroimaging researchers, with a third annotator if no consensus. Shanghai TCM: fully manual segmentation by experienced neuroradiologists. The challenge site says ground truth was approved by board-certified neuroradiologists.
details.reference_standard: EPVS = MRI-visible enlarged perivascular spaces under STRIVE criteria. Imaging-only reference, no histology. Masks are limited to the BG/CSO regions of interest.
details.version: Challenge release (training data and registration opened 2024-05-15; validation 2024-07)
details.third_party_note: Terms of Use v3: 'EPVS Challenge Dataset is used for the EPVS Challenge 2024 ONLY. Any form of data sharing and distribution (including raw data and pre-processed data) is strictly not allowed'. Other uses, including publication, need consent from each site PI. No explicit clause on online services.
details.extra: Access needs a signed Terms of Use emailed to the organizers and an invitation to the Synapse participant team. The terms limit use to the 2024 challenge, so any use after the challenge needs per-site PI consent (SG70: J.H. Zhou; MACC: C. Chen; Shanghai TCM: X. Chen; Edinburgh: M. Valdes Hernandez). Synthetic training images from PVSDRO templates are public. Shanghai TCM scans have 5-6 mm slices (clinical protocol) and appear only in the test set.

name: PCCT/DECT Phantom Dose Levels
full_name: Dual-energy and photon-counting CTs from a tissue-equivalent phantom by scanning in different imaging dose levels
anatomy: Tissue-equivalent phantom (Gammex Advanced Electron Density phantom, large 300 x 400 x 165 mm ellipsoidal configuration) - no patient anatomy
protocol_note: Multi-energy, not multiphase: virtual monoenergetic images at 40, 50, 60, 70, 150, 160, 170, 180 and 190 keV from each PCCT and DECT (80/140 kVp) acquisition
size: PCCT: 270 series / 42,029 DICOM images (~29.7 GB unzipped); DECT: 267 series / 24,243 DICOM images (~13.0 GB unzipped); ~19.8 GB zipped
description: Phantom CT dataset of a Gammex Advanced Electron Density phantom with tissue-equivalent inserts scanned on a photon-counting CT (Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha) and a dual-energy CT (Siemens SOMATOM Confidence) at 5, 20 and 40 mGy in triplicate, with virtual monoenergetic reconstructions from 40 to 190 keV.

phantom.model: Gammex Advanced Electron Density phantom (large ellipsoidal configuration) with tissue-equivalent inserts
phantom.purpose: Evaluate PCCT vs DECT virtual monoenergetic image quantitation across dose levels for radiotherapy-oriented quantitative imaging

label_schema: Configuration 1 (Soft Tissue): lung LN300 and LN450, HE general adipose, HE brain, HE breast 50:50, HE liver, liquid water and HE solid water inserts at 16 positions
Configuration 2 (Inner Bone): HE inner bone insert at the phantom center
Configuration 3 (Cortical Bone): HE cortical bone insert at the phantom center
Dose level folder: 5, 20 or 40 mGy CTDIvol,32cm (DECT: 80 kVp part matched to the PCCT dose; the 140 kVp part adds extra exposure)
VMI energy: 40-70 keV and 150-190 keV in 10 keV steps
insert material and position per configuration (README Figure 1)
details.file_structure: PCCT.zip and DECT.zip: <scanner>/<first|second|third>_batch/<Soft Tissue | Inner Bone | Cortical Bone>/<5|20|40 mGy>/<series>/ DICOM slices (PCCT batches 2-3 add a 'Body' level; DECT adds DICOM/CT/). One series per VMI energy; README.pdf describes the insert layout and folder tree.
details.reference_standard: Ground truth is the phantom design: the known tissue-equivalent reference inserts and their positions, the nominal dose level and the VMI energy. The README does not list nominal electron density or elemental composition values.
details.third_party_note: Zenodo record licensed CC BY 4.0. Phantom data only, no patient information.
details.extra: Inserts without high-Z elements (lung, adipose, soft tissue) were scanned together; bone inserts were scanned one at a time at the center. Each acquisition was repeated 3 times, removing and repositioning the phantom between repeats. Sample headers keep acquisition metadata (manufacturer, model, kernel Qr40, series description, institution); PCCT VMIs are ORIGINAL/PRIMARY, while DECT VMIs are DERIVED/SECONDARY syngo.via reconstructions. Per the DICOM headers, the PCCT scans come from MUMC and the DECT scans from Maastro Clinic; the record keywords describe radiotherapy-oriented quantitative imaging.

name: VSD Lower Extremities Seg
full_name: vsd-lower-extremities-seg: 63-bone lower-body CT segmentation from the VSDFullBody collection
anatomy: Lower-body bones: sacrum, hips, femora, patellae, tibiae, fibulae and all foot bones
protocol_note: Post-mortem (cadaver) whole-body CT from the Virtual Skeleton Database. Some subjects were scanned in two parts and merged; slice thickness and kVp are given in the metadata for some cases.
size: 30 lower-body CT scans (14 female / 16 male, aged 19-95) with 63-label bone maps and per-bone STL meshes; ~8.7 GB
segmentation_detail: Filled label maps of 63 individual bones (left/right separate) rasterized from closed surface meshes, plus one STL mesh per bone
description: 30 post-mortem lower-body CT scans from the Virtual Skeleton Database (VSDFullBody), in nnU-Net format, with filled label maps of 63 individual bones from sacrum to toes and per-bone STL surface meshes.

label_schema: 0 background; 1 Sacrum; 2/3 Hip L/R; 4/5 Femur L/R; 6/7 Patella L/R

8-63: tibia, fibula and every foot bone (talus, calcaneus, navicular, cuboid, 3 cuneiforms, 5 metatarsals, 14 phalanges per foot); even = left, odd = right; equals the 56 total-feet-seg labels shifted by +7
subject metadata: sex, age, height, weight; slice thickness and kVp for some scans
details.file_structure: lower_extremity_ct/ (nnU-Net raw format: dataset.json, imagesTr/001_0000.nii.gz ... 030_0000.nii.gz in Hounsfield units, labelsTr/001.nii.gz ... 030.nii.gz); meshes/<case>/ one STL per bone plus the original fused tarsal/metatarsal/phalanx meshes; metadata/<case>.json = original VSD record + source_subject; dataset_creation/ scripts (MATLAB, Rhino, Python).
details.splits: None: all 30 cases are in imagesTr/labelsTr (the card trains nnU-Net fold 'all')
details.label_readers: Not radiologists. Source bone models by a single author (Fischer 2023): threshold >= 200 HU in 3D Slicer, manual separation at joints and manual hole closing, visual and mesh-topology checks. Fused foot-bone meshes were split semi-manually in Rhino 3D by BoneHub and rasterized to filled label maps.
details.reference_standard: Bone = semi-automatic threshold segmentation with manual correction; no independent reader validation.

Benign_Cases.xlsx / Malign_Cases.xlsx case metadata spreadsheets in each project

segmentation_detail: COCO RLE masks of hand bones (carpals, radius, ulna, MC1-5, PP1-5, DP1-5, plus soft tissue/implant categories) and bone-erosion-related regions (Non-SvdH-BE, SvdH-BE-50, SvdH-BE-90)

BE joint detection over 16 joints/regions (R, U, L, CMC-T, S, Tm, IP, MCP-T..S, PIP-I..S) with per-joint SvdH BE scores
JSN joint detection over 15 joints (CMC-M/R/S, SC, SR, STT, MCP-T..S, PIP-I..S) with per-joint SvdH JSN scores

joint localization boxes (BE and JSN joints)
joint-level SvdH joint space narrowing scores

name: Visible Human 3D Bone Models
full_name: Visible Human Full-Skeleton 3D Bone Models (BoneHub)
protocol_note: Aligned CT (DICOM) series of the NLM Visible Human Male and Female cadavers, converted to NIfTI in 3D Slicer.
size: 2 whole-body CT volumes (Visible Human Male and Female); 142 (male) and 143 (female) individually labeled bones
segmentation_detail: Per-bone voxel labels for the whole skeleton (every vertebra, rib, carpal, metacarpal, tarsal, metatarsal; phalanges per digit; combined cranium+maxilla, mandible, sternum, sacrum+coccyx), plus an STL mesh and an IGES/STEP NURBS surface for each bone
description: Whole-body CT of the NLM Visible Human Male and Female with per-bone segmentations of the full skeleton (142/143 labels), plus STL meshes and NURBS CAD surfaces for each bone.

The female subject has an additional VERTEBRA_L6 label.
Hyoid, sesamoids other than the patella, and costal cartilages are not segmented.
details.file_structure: visible_human_3d_models/CT/: metadata.json (sex, age, height, weight, BMI); Image/<subject>.nii.gz; Segmentation/<subject>/<anatomy>.seg.nrrd (3D Slicer); Mesh/<subject>/<anatomy>/<BONE>.stl; NURBS/<subject>/<anatomy>/<BONE>.iges|.step. <subject> is 01_Male or 02_Female. <anatomy> is SKULL, SPINAL_COLUMN, THORAX, UPPER/LOWER_EXTREMITY_LEFT/RIGHT, HAND_LEFT/RIGHT or FOOT_LEFT/RIGHT.
details.label_readers: Two trained human annotators per subject using nnInteractive (model-assisted, human-verified segmentation); no inter-rater reliability figures provided
details.reference_standard: Annotator judgment on CT (model-assisted interactive segmentation)
details.third_party_note: Released under CC BY 4.0, consistent with the source release. Users must cite both this dataset and Andreassen et al. 2023.

That source release has only 28 lower-extremity bone geometries per subject. The subjects are cadavers (male 39 y, female 59 y). The elbow region is truncated in the source CT, so the distal humerus and proximal radius/ulna are incomplete. HF DOI 10.57967/hf/10464.

name: AAPM-RT-MAC

size: 55 patients / 55 studies / 110 series / 6,655 images (3.52 GB)

name: ACRIN-Contralateral-Breast-MR
full_name: ACRIN-Contralateral-Breast-MR: Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Women Recently Diagnosed With Unilateral Breast Cancer (ACRIN 6667)

description: Breast MRI (plus some CR) from 984 women with recently diagnosed unilateral breast cancer, enrolled in the ACRIN 6667 trial of MRI screening of the contralateral breast, with de-identified clinical trial form data.

label_schema: ACRIN 6667 case report forms exported as per-form CSV files (e.g. A0 patient confirmation form), with a Form Dictionary and per-form dictionaries giving variable names, descriptions and option codes
Imaging, clinical management and pathology/outcome variables, including days offset from the base date (e.g. surgery)
clinical trial case report form data (imaging, clinical management, pathology/outcome)
details.file_structure: Images: DICOM (MR, CR), 984 subjects / 1,103 studies / 10,184 series / 626,782 images, 199.59 GB, downloaded with the TCIA Data Retriever. Clinical data: CSV, ZIP and XLSX (278.77 kB), with Form Dictionary.csv and per-form dictionaries (e.g. 6667_A0_Dictionary.csv).
details.reference_standard: In the trial, MRI-detected cancer was confirmed by biopsy within 12 months of study entry. Absence of cancer was established by biopsy and/or negative repeat imaging and clinical examination at 1-year follow-up. Contralateral cancer was found in 30 of 969 analysed women (3.1%).
details.third_party_note: Images and clinical data are licensed CC BY 4.0. Users must also abide by the TCIA Data Usage Policy and cite DOI 10.7937/Q1EE-J082.
details.extra: Data exist for 984 patients, but only 969 were included in the primary trial analysis. Image data for Case 120 were removed because of corruption; its clinical data remain. Missing Sequence Variant tags (0018,0021) were filled with 'NONE'. DICOM dates are shifted to a 1960-01-01 baseline, with the offset in tag (0012,0052). Primary paper: Lehman et al., NEJM 2007;356:1295-1303 (doi:10.1056/nejmoa065447). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00058058.

protocol_note: Standard protocol: pre-contrast T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, post-Gd 2D spin-echo T1 and 3D volumetric T1. Advanced protocol: variable flip-angle T1 mapping, DCE T1, DSC perfusion and/or 2D CSI PRESS MR spectroscopy.
size: 123 subjects / 566 studies / 7,629 series / 717,070 images (86.89 GB)
license: Images: NIH Controlled Data Access Policy; clinical data: CC BY 4.0
description: Longitudinal multicenter brain MRI (with some CT) from 123 recurrent glioblastoma patients in the ACRIN 6677/RTOG 0625 bevacizumab trial, with standard and advanced (DCE, DSC, MRS) sequences and clinical trial forms covering progression and survival.

label_schema: Clinical trial forms as per-form CSVs, with a Form Description file and a Data Dictionary (e.g. A0 eligibility/registration form)
Progression status on post-treatment MRIs by Macdonald and RANO threshold criteria
Bidimensional (2D) and volumetric (3D) enhancement measurements on post-contrast T1 and FLAIR hyperintensity volume
Dates of progression and survival, given as day offsets from the base date
details.file_structure: Images: DICOM (86.89 GB), downloaded with the TCIA Data Retriever. Clinical data (2.2 MB) as XLSX, ZIP, CSV and PDF, in two spreadsheet sets: ACRIN-DSC-MR-Brain TCIA Anonymized and ACRIN-DSC-MR-Brain-HB TCIA Anonymized.
details.splits: Group 1 (ACRIN-DSC-MR-Brain) is a 75% random sample; Group 2 (ACRIN-DSC-MR-Brain-HB) is a 25% random sample initially held out for testing and validating algorithms.

details.extra: DOI 10.7937/tcia.2019.zr1pjf4i. DICOM dates are shifted to a baseline of 1960-01-01, and day offsets are stored in tag (0012,0050). Of 123 patients, 107 had a baseline and at least one post-treatment MRI. MRS analysis covered 13 patients. Paper: Boxerman et al., Neuro Oncol 2013;15:945-954 (doi:10.1093/neuonc/not049). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00433381.

name: AHEP0731
full_name: AHEP0731 | Risk-Based Therapy in Treating Younger Patients With Newly Diagnosed Liver Cancer
protocol_note: Data types CT, US, MR, PT, XA. Low-risk: CT chest for metastatic response; abdominal US at baseline. Intermediate/high-risk: abdominal US, CT and/or MRI for primary tumor response, CT chest for metastases. No sequence, phase or tracer details given.
size: 190 subjects / 855 studies / 5,704 series / 417,972 images (220.94 GB; includes ultrasound)
description: Controlled-access TCIA collection of CT, MR, PET, XA and ultrasound DICOM imaging from 190 children with newly diagnosed hepatoblastoma enrolled in the Children's Oncology Group phase III trial AHEP0731 (NCT00980460).

Version 1 had 80 subjects; version 2 added 110 subjects. A separate TCIA analysis result, AHEP0731-Tumor-Annotations, provides tumor annotations. Trial results: Katzenstein et al., Lancet Oncol 2019 (doi:10.1016/s1470-2045(18)30895-7). Dataset DOI: 10.7937/F2DB-8826.

aliases: Risk-Based Therapy in Treating Younger Patients With Newly Diagnosed Liver Cancer

MRI 1 pre-treatment, MRI 2 after one AC cycle, MRI 3 after AC; 17 taxane patients have MRI 4. 4 of 68 patients excluded; UCSF_BR_30, _53 and _27 have treatment anomalies; UCSF_BR_18 visit 1 has two pre-contrast acquisitions. Used as training data for QIN Breast MRI Metrics of Response (BMMR) challenge. TCIA analysis results: DICOM-SR-Breast-Clinical, DI-Cubed-Reports.

treatment between scans (surgery, radiotherapy, systemic therapy)

details.file_structure: CBCT/<PatientID_visit>/Slice_NNNN.dcm (typically 420 slices per scan); PaX-ray/<PatientID_visit>/Slice_0000.dcm; PeX-ray/<PatientID_visit>/{left,middle,right}/<jaw>_<tooth>.tif, each folder zipped (upper-jaw images flipped vertically); plus CBCT_info.csv, PaX_info.csv, PeX_info.csv, patient_statistics_info.csv and implant_marking.csv. The _0/_1 suffix in a file name gives the visit order.
details.label_readers: Implant labels: annotator not stated. Tooth positions in the CBCT scans (used to generate the periapical images) were marked by 13 researchers working in pairs with cross-checking, followed by an overall quality check by one person. Their clinical qualifications are not stated.
details.reference_standard: Implant presence is labelled per CBCT scan; the confirmation method is not stated.
details.version: 1.0.0 (2023-09-06); latest is 1.1.0 (2024-10-11), whose contents were not verified
details.third_party_note: Access requires signing the PhysioNet Restricted Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0, whose text was not included in the evidence. PhysioNet restricted-access terms generally forbid sharing the data with third parties, so check the DUA before sending images to external services.
details.extra:
Periapical radiographs are not real acquisitions; they were simulated from CBCT with Siddon-Jacobs ray tracing (ITK) at three angles and cropped to 40x30 mm, and the authors note their image quality is low. Only 13 panoramic radiographs are included. In DICOM, patient names and IDs were replaced with random IDs, UIDs were regenerated, date of birth was removed and study dates were randomized, while sex and age were kept. All CBCT scans come from a single machine. Data were acquired January 2021 to January 2022 (IRB GLMC20230502). v1.0.0 files are no longer available; the field values here are taken from the v1.0.0 page. Companion paper: Huang et al., Scientific Data 2024.
DOIs: v1.0.0 10.13026/s5z3-2766, latest 10.13026/bxzm-dg78.

aliases: A multimodal dental dataset facilitating machine learning research and clinic services

name: BHX
full_name: Brain Hemorrhage Extended (BHX): Bounding box extrapolation from thick to thin slice CT images
protocol_note: Head CT from CQ500; thick-slice (≥3 mm) series manually annotated, boxes extrapolated to thin-slice (≤1 mm) series matched via Image Position (Patient); version 3 restricted to soft-tissue non-contrast thin series, version 2 includes bone-filter and contrast series.
size: 6,283 manual boxes on 3,558 thick-slice images; 39,668 boxes on 23,409 images after extrapolation (clean set: 27,203 boxes on 15,979 images); from the 491-scan CQ500 dataset
description: Bounding-box annotations for intracranial hemorrhage subtypes on CQ500 head CTs, hand-drawn by neuroradiologists on thick slices and automatically extrapolated to thin-slice series.

label_schema: SOPInstanceUID: links each box to a DICOM image in CQ500
SeriesInstanceUID / StudyInstanceUID: series and scan grouping
data: bounding box X, Y, width, height
labelName: Intraparenchymal, Subarachnoid, Intraventricular, Epidural, Subdural (acute), Chronic Subdural Hematoma
labelType: thick-slices (manual), thin-slices (selected soft-tissue thin series, dataset 3) or other
hemorrhage subtype (intraparenchymal, subarachnoid, intraventricular, epidural, acute subdural, chronic subdural)
details.file_structure: 1_Initial_Manual_Labeling.csv (hand-drawn thick-slice boxes, 1.6 MB); 2_Extrapolation_to_All_Series.csv (manual + extrapolation to all corresponding series incl. bone filter/contrast, 10.5 MB); 3_Extrapolation_to_Selected_Series.csv (manual + extrapolation to selected soft-tissue non-contrast thin series, 7.3 MB); example_annotated_images.png; LICENSE.txt. Images must be obtained from qure.ai CQ500 (http://headctstudy.qure.ai/dataset).
details.label_readers: Three neuroradiologists (6, 4 and <1 year of practice) annotated thick-slice series; automatically extrapolated thin-slice boxes were randomly spot-checked by one neuroradiologist without corrections
details.reference_standard: Radiologist visual annotation on CT; no clinical or surgical confirmation stated
details.third_party_note: Label files are CC BY-SA 4.0 ('Anyone can access the files, as long as they conform to the terms of the specified license'); the CT images come from qure.ai CQ500 under its own terms, which were not verified here.
details.extra: Extrapolated boxes can have imperfect x/y match due to patient motion between series; matching used the Image Position (Patient) DICOM tag. Annotation done in MD.ai (one author employed by MD.ai); viewable at https://public.md.ai/annotator/project/Y2qr6vqv/workspace. DOI 10.13026/9cft-hg92.

name: CXLSeg
full_name: Chest X-ray Dataset with Lung Segmentation (CXLSeg)
protocol_note: Frontal (AP/PA) chest radiographs from MIMIC-CXR; lung-segmented images and masks resized to 224x224 JPEG
size: 243,324 frontal chest X-ray images (segmented image + lung mask, 224x224 JPEG)
segmentation_detail: Automatic lung masks generated by an SA-UNet model, refined with erosion/dilation; not verified by professionals
paired_text_detail: Preprocessed MIMIC-CXR free-text radiology report per image in CXLSeg-metadata.csv
description: Derived dataset of 243,324 frontal MIMIC-CXR chest radiographs with model-generated lung masks, lung-segmented 224x224 JPEG images, radiology reports and CheXpert/NegBio labels.

label_schema: Lung mask per frontal image (dicom_id-mask.jpg) and lung-segmented image (dicom_id.jpg)

CheXpert/NegBio labels: Atelectasis, Cardiomegaly, Consolidation, Edema, Enlarged Cardiomediastinum, Fracture, Lung Lesion, Lung Opacity, Pleural Effusion, Pneumonia, Pneumothorax, Pleural Other, Support Devices, No Finding
Metadata: dicom_id, subject_id, study_id, Reports, ViewPosition, PerformedProcedureStepDescription, Rows, Columns, StudyDate, StudyTime and DICOM code-meaning fields
details.file_structure: files/pXX/pSUBJECT/sSTUDY/{dicom_id}.jpg and {dicom_id}-mask.jpg, mirroring the MIMIC-CXR layout (10 folders, ~6,500 subfolders); CXLSeg-metadata.csv, CXLSeg-segmented.csv (image path + CheXpert labels), CXLSeg-split.csv, CXLSeg-mask.csv (mask paths).
details.splits: train/validate/test 80:10:10 (CXLSeg-split.csv)
details.label_readers: No human readers; the masks come from an SA-UNet trained on Shenzhen, Montgomery and V7-Labs COVID-19 CXR masks, and the findings come from the CheXpert labeler and NegBio
details.reference_standard: Lung masks are automatic model outputs that professionals did not examine; finding labels are NLP-derived from reports

related.name: MIMIC-CXR
related.note: 243,324 frontal images lung-segmented with an SA-UNet model; segmented images and masks resized to 224x224 JPEG with preprocessed reports

details.third_party_note: Credentialed Access on PhysioNet; the licence/DUA text was not in the fetched evidence. The dataset is derived from MIMIC-CXR-JPG under the same IRB.
details.extra: Images are resized to 224x224, so they are lower resolution than the source. About 10 of 243,334 frontal images were dropped because their reports were missing. Reported lung segmentation scores: Dice ~96%, IoU 91.97%. DOI 10.13026/9cy4-f535. Authors: Indeewara et al. (University of Moratuwa).

name: CheXchoNet
full_name: CheXchoNet: A Chest Radiograph Dataset with Gold Standard Echocardiography Labels
protocol_note: Posteroanterior (PA) chest radiographs only; portable AP films excluded; downsampled to 224x224 JPEG with CLAHE. Labels from transthoracic echocardiography (parasternal long-axis) within 12 months.
size: 71,589 PA chest X-rays / 24,689 patients
description: Columbia University Irving Medical Center posteroanterior chest radiographs (71,589 images, 24,689 patients) paired with echocardiography measurements and derived labels for severe left ventricular hypertrophy and dilated left ventricle.

label_schema: ivsd: interventricular septal thickness at end diastole (cm)
lvidd: left ventricular internal diameter at end diastole (cm)
lvpwd: left ventricular posterior wall thickness at end diastole (cm)
slvh: binary severe LV hypertrophy from sex-specific guideline thresholds
dlv: binary dilated LV from guideline thresholds
age, sex, pixel spacing, hashed patient ID, shifted time in days
IVSd, LVIDd, LVPWd (continuous echo measurements, cm)
details.file_structure: One metadata file (one row per CXR: patient ID, shifted time, JPEG path, pixel spacing, age/sex, echo measurements, binary labels, transplant/device flags) plus a directory of JPEG images named by 32-char patient hash + 8-char file hash.
details.label_readers: Measurements extracted from finalized echocardiography reports (parasternal long-axis view) in the enterprise data warehouse; binary labels derived via ASE/EACVI guideline thresholds
details.reference_standard: Echocardiogram within 12 months (before or after) of the CXR; if multiple, maximum of each measurement taken; SLVH/DLV defined by sex-specific guideline thresholds (Lang et al. 2015)
details.third_party_note: Access requires signing the PhysioNet Restricted Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0; the clause text on sharing with external online services was not included in the evidence.
details.extra: Images downsampled to 224x224 with bicubic interpolation and CLAHE contrast enhancement applied; only PA films (AP portable excluded); CUIMC, Jan 2013-Aug 2018; ages truncated to 18-90. Companion paper: Bhave et al., Eur Heart J 2024, doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehad782. DOI v1.0.0 10.13026/kp08-ws25; latest 10.13026/zsej-wt49. Project website: https://members.dbmi.columbia.edu/CRADLE/LVHnet.html

aliases: CheXchoNet: A Chest Radiograph Dataset with Gold Standard Echocardiography Labels

name: CheXmask
full_name: CheXmask Database: a large-scale dataset of anatomical segmentation masks for chest x-ray images
protocol_note: Chest radiographs from ChestX-ray8, CheXpert, MIMIC-CXR-JPG, PadChest and VinDr-CXR (CANDID-PTX was included in earlier versions); masks provided at original resolution and preprocessed 1024x1024.
size: 676,803 anatomical segmentation masks (v0.1) across 6 chest X-ray datasets; 37.7 GB uncompressed (v0.1)
segmentation_detail: Model-generated (HybridGNet) left lung, right lung and heart masks in RLE, plus landmark contours, at original resolution and preprocessed 1024x1024
description: Large-scale set of HybridGNet-generated left lung, right lung and heart segmentation masks with RCA-based quality scores for chest radiographs from CANDID-PTX, ChestX-ray8, CheXpert, MIMIC-CXR-JPG, PadChest and VinDr-CXR, released without the images.

label_schema: Image ID: matches the ID column of the original dataset (column name varies by dataset)
Dice RCA (Max): maximum RCA-estimated Dice, a segmentation quality estimate
Dice RCA (Mean): mean RCA-estimated Dice; authors recommend keeping masks with a value >= 0.7
Landmarks: HybridGNet landmark points outlining the organ contours
Left Lung / Right Lung / Heart: masks in run-length encoding
Height / Width: mask dimensions needed to decode the RLE
Reverse Classification Accuracy (RCA) estimated Dice quality scores
details.file_structure: One CSV file per source dataset, in OriginalResolution/ and Preprocessed/ (1024x1024) folders, plus LICENSE.txt and SHA256SUMS.txt; 15.8 GB ZIP (v0.1). No images or metadata are included.
details.label_readers: No human readers; masks come from a HybridGNet model retrained on the Chest-Xray-Landmark dataset, with quality estimated automatically by Reverse Classification Accuracy
details.reference_standard: No ground truth; mask quality is estimated per image by RCA (atlas-registration-based Dice estimate)
details.third_party_note: Masks are under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 ('Anyone can access the files, as long as they conform to the terms of the specified license'). The source images must be obtained from each original dataset under its own terms (MIMIC-CXR-JPG and CANDID-PTX require ethics training and a DUA), so those terms govern external processing.
details.extra: Versions 0.1 (2023-06-27), 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 and 1.0.0 (2025-01-22) exist; counts here are from v0.1. The PhysioNet page also lists VinDr-PCXR as a parent project. Code is at github.com/ngaggion/CheXmask-Database. DOI (latest): 10.13026/6eky-y831.

name: CheXmask-U
full_name: CheXmask-U: Uncertainty Estimation for Landmark-Based Anatomical Segmentation Masks in Chest X-ray Images
protocol_note: Chest radiographs from ChestX-ray8, CheXpert, MIMIC-CXR-JPG, PadChest and VinDr-CXR; images were preprocessed to 1024x1024 for mask generation; images are not distributed.
size: Annotations for 657,566 chest X-rays (112,120 ChestX-ray8; 187,825 CheXpert; 243,334 MIMIC-CXR-JPG; 96,287 PadChest; 18,000 VinDr-CXR); 39.9 GB uncompressed
segmentation_detail: Model-generated left lung, right lung and heart masks (RLE) built from mean HybridGNet landmark positions, at 1024x1024 and at original resolution
description: Extension of the CheXmask anatomical segmentation masks that adds HybridGNet node-wise landmark uncertainty estimates to lung and heart masks for 657,566 chest X-rays from ChestX-ray8, CheXpert, MIMIC-CXR-JPG, PadChest and VinDr-CXR.

label_schema: Image ID: identifier matching the source dataset's ID column (name varies per dataset)
Dice RCA (Max) and Dice RCA (Mean): Reverse Classification Accuracy estimates of segmentation Dice
Landmarks (Mean): mean landmark positions across 50 stochastic latent-space samples
Landmarks (Std): per-landmark standard deviation, i.e. node-wise predictive uncertainty
Left Lung, Right Lung, Heart: masks in run-length encoding
Height, Width: mask dimensions for RLE decoding
node-wise landmark uncertainty (std over 50 latent samples)
details.file_structure: One CSV per source dataset in folders OriginalResolution/ and Preprocessed/ (1024x1024), plus DATA_DICTIONARY.md, README.md, LICENSE.txt and SHA256SUMS.txt; no images are included. ZIP 16.8 GB; also on s3://physionet-open/chexmask-u/1.0.0/.
details.label_readers: No human labels in the release; HybridGNet trained on the 911-image Chest-Xray-Landmark set (JSRT, PadChest, Montgomery, Shenzhen). Uncertainty was validated on 255 manually annotated chest X-rays with two independent annotations.
details.reference_standard: Masks are automated predictions with RCA-estimated quality; the original CheXmask masks were validated against 250 manually annotated images (50 per source dataset). The authors recommend Dice RCA (Mean) >= 0.7.
details.third_party_note: The label files are licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Public License. The images must be obtained from the source datasets under their own terms (e.g. the MIMIC-CXR-JPG credentialed DUA), which govern any external processing.
details.extra: Derived from the CheXmask Database v1.0.0 (Gaggion et al., Sci Data 2024), which is not in the catalog, and uses the same HybridGNet weights. Paper: Cosarinsky et al., MIDL 2026 (arXiv:2512.10715). Uncertainty reflects model predictive uncertainty, not clinical confidence. Code: https://github.com/mcosarinsky/CheXmask-U. DOI 10.13026/6vn3-3j51.

aliases: CheXmask-U: Quantifying uncertainty in landmark-based anatomical segmentation for X-ray images

name: CDSL
full_name: COVID Data for Shared Learning (CDSL): A comprehensive, multimodal COVID-19 dataset from HM Hospitales
protocol_note: Chest X-rays (CR/DX; AP, PA, lateral views) and chest CT scans converted from DICOM to JPG (quality 95, VOI LUT applied); contrast phase not stated.
size: 1,444,764 JPG images (4,608 X-rays; 1,440,156 CT images) from 1,859 patients; structured EHR for 4,479 hospitalized patients
description: Multimodal COVID-19 database from the Spanish HM Hospitales group with de-identified EHR tables for 4,479 hospitalized patients, plus chest X-rays and CT scans (JPG) for 1,859 of them, collected December 2019 to February 2021.

label_schema: patient_01.csv: demographics, ED/hospital/ICU admission and discharge, first/last ED vital signs, mechanical ventilation, discharge destination
diagnosis_er_02.csv / diagnosis_hosp_03.csv: ICD-10 diagnoses (with POA indicators for inpatient), ICD-10-PCS procedures, ICD-O-3 neoplasm codes
medication_05.csv: 115,649 medication records with ATC codes
CDSL-1.0.0-dicom-metadata.csv: StudyDate (shifted), StudyTime, Modality (CR/DX/CT), StudyDescription, BodyPart, procedure code, ViewPosition (AP/PA/LL), PatientPosition, SpatialResolution
ICD-10 ED and inpatient diagnoses and procedures
details.file_structure: Six CSV relational tables linked by patient_id, an additional_tables folder (ICD-10 dictionary, ATC descriptions), and IMAGES/files/pNN/pXXXXXXXX/sZZZZZZZZ/ZZZZZZZZ_VVVV.jpg (MIMIC-CXR-JPG-style layout). Single-image studies are X-rays; CT studies contain hundreds of slice JPGs. A DICOM metadata CSV accompanies the images.
details.reference_standard: Hospitalized patients with confirmed or suspected COVID-19. Diagnoses come from hospital EHR coding; there are no radiologist image labels.
details.third_party_note: Access requests are assessed by the HM Hospitales Data Science Commission and, where appropriate, reviewed by the HM Hospitales Clinical Research Ethics Committee. The licence/DUA text was not visible in the fetched page.
details.extra: DICOMs were converted to lossy JPG (quality 95) with VOI LUT applied; DICOM UIDs, identifiers and dates were removed. Dates are shifted per patient. Some columns are in Spanish. An earlier alpha version was shared on the HM Hospitales website as 'Covid Data Saves Lives' (from April 2020). DOI 10.13026/1176-6c44.

name: CXR-Align
full_name: CXR-Align: A Benchmark for CXR-Report Alignment with Negations
protocol_note: Chest X-ray reports from MIMIC-CXR; images obtained separately from MIMIC-CXR
paired_text_detail: Original MIMIC-CXR report statements plus an 'omitted' variant (sentences about a chosen finding removed) and a 'negation' variant (templated negated statement inserted)
description: Benchmark of MIMIC-CXR chest X-ray reports with systematically omitted findings and inserted templated negations, used to evaluate negation handling in image-report alignment by vision-language models.

label_schema: report: original report text segmented into statements
chosen: clinical entity selected for negation/omission (e.g. cardiomegaly, atelectasis, edema, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, consolidation)
location: position where the negated statement is inserted (beginning, middle, end)
omitted: report with all sentences about the chosen entity removed
negation: omitted report with a templated negated statement inserted at the location
details.file_structure: Single JSON file with top-level key 'mimic' mapping MIMIC-CXR object identifiers to report/chosen/location/omitted/negation fields; images must be obtained from MIMIC-CXR.
details.label_readers: CheXbert identified positive entities; one researcher with four years of chest X-ray experience reviewed a random sample of 500 negation-annotated reports and corrected inconsistencies
details.reference_standard: Positive findings come from CheXbert extraction on the original reports; the negated and omitted variants are synthetic by construction. No image-level confirmation is described.
details.third_party_note: Credentialed access only: users must be credentialed, complete CITI Data or Specimens Only Research training and sign the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0. The specific DUA clause on external services was not shown on the page; check the DUA before use.
details.extra: Normal-only reports and reports describing multiple timepoints are excluded. The abstract mistakenly cites MIMIC-III, while the Methods section states the reports come from MIMIC-CXR. Users must cite both CXR-Align and MIMIC-CXR. Code: https://github.com/lukeingawesome/cxralign. DOI 10.13026/7ebc-s018.

name: CXReasonBench / CheXStruct
full_name: CXReasonBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Structured Diagnostic Reasoning in Chest X-rays (with CheXStruct structured labels)
protocol_note: Chest X-rays from MIMIC-CXR-JPG; structured labels derived via CXAS segmentation, landmarks and measurement thresholds (e.g. CTR 0.5 in PA view).

label_schema: Radiological findings: cardiomegaly, mediastinal widening, carina angle, trachea deviation, aortic knob enlargement, ascending aorta enlargement, descending aorta enlargement, descending aorta tortuous (normal/abnormal or deviated)
Image quality: inclusion (included/excluded), inspiration (good/poor), rotation (rotated/not), projection (small/large overlap)
Labels are derived from anatomical measurements and indices (e.g. CTR, mediastinal-to-lung width ratio) using standard or expert-defined thresholds
CXReasonBench QA: Path 1 (direct reasoning, 8,044), Path 2 (guided reasoning, 3,600) and Re-evaluated Path 1 (7,344) multiple-choice questions
details.file_structure: CSV files with CheXStruct structured labels and JSON files for the CXReasonBench evaluation pipeline, organised in folders by diagnostic task and evaluation path; images come from MIMIC-CXR-JPG.
details.splits: Benchmark only: 100 randomly sampled cases per task (1,200 total)
details.label_readers: Automated pipeline (CXAS segmentation, landmark and measurement rules, QC); a clinical expert manually reviewed the segmentation masks for the 1,200 benchmark cases
details.reference_standard: Threshold-based labels computed from model-derived anatomical measurements (e.g. CTR > 0.5 in PA view for cardiomegaly); not radiologist reads or clinical confirmation
details.third_party_note: Credentialed access on PhysioNet; the licence/DUA text was not shown in the evidence. MIMIC-derived data are typically under PhysioNet credentialed terms, so re-read the DUA before sending data to external services.
details.extra: DOI 10.13026/z3dn-nh22. Authors: Lee, Choi, Lee, Yoon, Hong, Choi. QA items are paired with up to four visual inputs (original X-ray and overlaid segmentation masks). Strong label imbalance in some tasks (e.g. descending aorta enlargement: 360 abnormal of 106,634).

name: CIED-CXR

size: 13,393 images: 2,321 chest radiographs + 11,072 smartphone photos of them / 896 patients
segmentation_detail: Manual CIED masks for a subset of images (PNG; 0 = background, 1 = pacemaker/defibrillator, 2 = event/heart monitor)
description: Single-centre Charité Berlin dataset of 2,321 AP/PA chest radiographs, converted to PNG, and 11,072 smartphone photos of them, showing cardiac implantable electronic devices, with manufacturer/model labels (28 classes) and radiologist segmentation masks.

label_schema: pat_id: anonymized patient ID (use for patient-level splits)
dataset: originals or smartphone type (galaxys4, galaxys5, iphone8, iphone13, iphone13mini)
manufacturer: Biotronik, Medtronic, St. Jude Medical (Abbott) or Boston Scientific
model: exact CIED model, 28 classes including Other
seg_mask: filename of the segmentation mask where available (0 background, 1 PM/ICD, 2 heart monitor)
details.file_structure: README.md; originals/ (radiograph PNGs); galaxys4/, galaxys5/, iphone8/, iphone13/, iphone13mini/ (smartphone photo PNGs); seg_masks/ (PNG label masks); data.json (metadata and labels)
details.splits: The page's device table reports train/validation/test counts per device (e.g. Medtronic 849/240/129); how the split is encoded in the files is not stated.

details.third_party_note: Access requires signing the PhysioNet Restricted Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0. The DUA text was not included in the evidence, so whether images may be sent to external online services was not verified.
details.extra: Single-centre (Charité, 2012-2022), adult patients. Images were center-cropped and OCR-redacted for anonymization. Smartphone photos were taken of a monitor display, up to 5 per radiograph. Example code: github.com/AndreasZhukov/cied. DOI 10.13026/swv0-cd11.

name: EHRXQA
full_name: EHRXQA: A Multi-Modal Question Answering Dataset for Electronic Health Records with Chest X-ray Images
protocol_note: Chest X-rays from MIMIC-CXR (referenced via TB_CXR table with viewposition); structured EHR tables from MIMIC-IV
size: 46,152 QA samples from 417 templates (16,366 image-related, 16,529 table-related, 13,257 image+table); silver database 800 patients, gold database 400 patients
paired_text_detail: Natural-language questions (GPT-4 paraphrased, manually reviewed) with SQL/NeuralSQL annotations and answers linking MIMIC-CXR images to MIMIC-IV EHR tables
description: Multi-modal EHR question answering dataset of 46,152 template-generated questions with SQL/NeuralSQL annotations that require reasoning over MIMIC-CXR chest X-rays and MIMIC-IV structured records.

label_schema: Question template category: Image-related, Table-related, Image+Table-related
Patient scope: none, single patient, group of patients
SQL or NeuralSQL query and executed answer
TB_CXR image reference table: subject_id, hadm_id, study_id, image_id, studydatetime, viewposition

related.name: Chest ImaGenome

details.third_party_note: Credentialed access on PhysioNet; the specific licence/DUA text was not captured in the fetched evidence.
details.extra: Built from MIMIC-CXR images, MIMIC-IV tables and Chest ImaGenome labels; event times condensed to 2100-2105 with 2105-12-31 23:59 as current time. Includes the MIMIC-CXR-VQA image QA resource and EHRSQL (MIMIC-IV) table templates. Paper: Bae et al., NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv:2310.18652); PhysioNet DOI 10.13026/bp5y-qt70. name: EGD-CXR
full_name: Eye Gaze Data for Chest X-rays
protocol_note: Chest radiographs from MIMIC-CXR (DICOM, obtained separately); gaze recorded with Gazepoint GP3 HD eye tracker at 1920x1080, dictation audio transcribed with Google Speech-to-Text and manually corrected.

label_schema: master_sheet.csv: DICOM_ID (MIMIC-CXR), granular CheXpert NLP disease labels, reason-for-exam sentences, case group (Normal, Pneumonia, CHF)
fixations.csv / eye_gaze.csv: DICOM_ID, TIME, FPOGX/FPOGY (screen fraction), X_ORIGINAL/Y_ORIGINAL (DICOM image coordinates)
bounding_boxes.csv: dicom_id, bbox_name (anatomy), x1, y1, x2, y2

full_name: MS-CXR-T: Learning to Exploit Temporal Structure for Biomedical Vision-Language Processing
protocol_note: Frontal chest X-ray current/prior image pairs from MIMIC-CXR v2 (labels only; images from MIMIC-CXR).
size: 1,326 frontal chest X-ray image pairs (800 subjects) with progression labels; 361 sentence pairs
paired_text_detail: 361 radiology report sentence pairs from MIMIC-CXR labelled as paraphrase or contradiction with respect to disease progression
description: Credentialed PhysioNet benchmark of radiologist-reviewed temporal progression labels (improving/stable/worsening for five findings) on 1,326 current/prior MIMIC-CXR frontal image pairs, plus 361 radiologist-verified temporal sentence pairs.

label_schema: study_id / previous_study_id: MIMIC-CXR report IDs of current and prior study
dicom_id / previous_dicom_id: MIMIC-CXR DICOM IDs of current and prior frontal image
{FINDING}_progression: improving / stable / worsening for Consolidation, Edema, Pleural Effusion, Pneumonia, Pneumothorax
Sentence similarity: sentence_1, sentence_2, category (paraphrase/contradiction), subset_name (Swaps/RadGraph)
temporal progression (improving / stable / worsening) for consolidation, edema, pleural effusion, pneumonia, pneumothorax
details.file_structure: Two CSV files: MS_CXR_T_temporal_image_classification_v1.0.0.csv and MS_CXR_T_temporal_sentence_similarity_v1.0.0.csv; images must be obtained from MIMIC-CXR.
details.label_readers: A board-certified radiologist accepted/rejected Chest ImaGenome silver report-derived progression labels (with access to the report); a subset was re-annotated blinded by a second radiologist to measure agreement; sentence pairs verified by a board-certified radiologist
details.reference_standard: Progression class derived from the radiology report (Chest ImaGenome gold/silver labels) and confirmed by radiologist review of the report; class distribution 18% improving / 40% stable / 42% worsening
details.third_party_note: PhysioNet credentialed access; the licence/DUA text was not included in the fetched evidence. Underlying MIMIC-CXR images are under PhysioNet credentialed terms.
details.extra: Builds on Chest ImaGenome progression dataset; recommend macro-F1/accuracy per pathology due to class imbalance. Cohort slightly older (mean age 64.99) and less female (45.88%) than full MIMIC-CXR. Paper: Bannur et al., arXiv:2301.04558; DOI 10.13026/pg10-j984.

aliases: Learning to Exploit Temporal Structure for Biomedical Vision-Language Processing

name: RadGraph
full_name: RadGraph: Extracting Clinical Entities and Relations from Radiology Reports
protocol_note: Text-only annotations of chest X-ray radiology reports from MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert; no images included.
size: 600 radiologist-annotated reports (500 MIMIC-CXR train/dev + 100 test: 50 MIMIC-CXR, 50 CheXpert); model-generated graphs for 220,763 MIMIC-CXR and 500 CheXpert reports
paired_text_detail: Full-text chest X-ray radiology reports (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert) with entity and relation annotations
description: Entity and relation annotations of chest X-ray radiology reports from MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert, with 600 radiologist-annotated reports and model-generated graphs for 220,763 MIMIC-CXR and 500 CheXpert reports that map to the associated radiographs.

label_schema: Entities: ANAT-DP (anatomy), OBS-DP (observation definitely present), OBS-U (observation uncertain), OBS-DA (observation definitely absent); each entity is a contiguous token span with start_ix/end_ix
Relations: suggestive_of (Observation->Observation), located_at (Observation->Anatomy), modify (Observation->Observation or Anatomy->Anatomy)
details.file_structure: train.json (425 MIMIC-CXR reports), dev.json (75 MIMIC-CXR), test.json (100 reports, 50 MIMIC-CXR + 50 CheXpert, with labeler_1 and labeler_2), MIMIC-CXR_graphs.json (220,763 model-annotated reports), CheXpert_graphs.json (500 model-annotated reports), models/ (DYGIE++ checkpoint, README, inference.py). Keys are MIMIC-CXR report paths or CheXpert study paths; the CheXpert test split has no mapping to images.
details.splits: Train 425 / dev 75 (MIMIC-CXR, patient-disjoint); test 100 (50 MIMIC-CXR + 50 CheXpert, patient-disjoint from the other splits); inference split is model-generated
details.label_readers: 3 board-certified radiologists with at least 8 years of experience; each train/dev report was labeled by one radiologist, and each test report was labeled independently by two radiologists (both kept, not adjudicated)
details.reference_standard: Radiologist annotation of report text against the information-extraction schema; the inference split comes from a DYGIE++/PubMedBERT model (micro F1 0.82 on the MIMIC-CXR test set and 0.73 on the CheXpert test set)
details.third_party_note: Credentialed access; the DUA stipulates that '(1) the user will not share the data, (2) the user will make no attempt to re-identify individuals, and (3) any publication that makes use of the data will also make the relevant code available'. Sending data to external services is not explicitly addressed on the page.
details.extra: Text-only annotations; no images are included (images come from MIMIC-CXR / CheXpert). Annotations do not cover the Comparison/History sections of reports. CheXpert reports were de-identified with hiding-in-plain-sight surrogate PHI. DOI 10.13026/hm87-5p47.

aliases: RadGraph: Extracting Clinical Entities and Relations from Radiology Reports

name: RaDialog Instruct Dataset
full_name: RaDialog Instruct Dataset (image-grounded chest X-ray instruct dataset for RaDialog)
protocol_note: Chest X-rays from the MIMIC-CXR-JPG training set (referenced by dicom_id; images not included).
paired_text_detail: Instruction/response conversations: MIMIC-CXR ground-truth findings reports for report generation, plus instruct tasks (CheXpert findings QA, MIMIC-NLE explanations, and LLM-generated region QA, easy-language rewrites, summaries and report corrections)
description: Semi-automatically generated, image-grounded instruct dataset of eight chest X-ray tasks, including report generation, findings QA, explanation, region QA, summarization, easy language and report correction, linked by dicom_id to the MIMIC-CXR-JPG training set.

label_schema: output: natural-language ground-truth answer (from MIMIC-CXR / MIMIC-NLE or LLM-generated)
instruction: natural-language prompt with placeholders, possibly containing a report and a question or instruction
dicom: dicom_id of the corresponding MIMIC-CXR-JPG image
Tasks: report generation, findings QA (complete and binary), natural language explanation, region QA, easy language, summarization, correction
details.file_structure: Single bz2-compressed JSON file (mimic_cxr_instruct_stratified.json.gz) containing a list of {output, instruction, dicom} records; the instruct prompts are in the GitHub repo under data/instruct_prompts.
details.splits: Built only from the MIMIC-CXR / MIMIC-NLE training sets (stratified so that no-finding samples are about 1/4); one instruct sample per image plus an equal number of report-generation samples.
details.label_readers: No human readers; CheXbert labeler outputs, MIMIC-NLE and zero-shot vicuna-13b generations
details.reference_standard: No clinical reference standard; the authors state that the instruct data are not claimed to be completely medically correct

related.name: MIMIC-CXR
related.note: Ground-truth findings/impression reports and CheXbert labels from MIMIC-CXR training reports; LLM (vicuna-13b) generated region QA, summaries, easy-language and corrections.

details.third_party_note: Credentialed-access PhysioNet resource; the licence/DUA text was not shown in the fetched evidence. The data contain MIMIC-CXR report text, so check the PhysioNet credentialed DUA before sending it to external services.
details.extra: Paper: Pellegrini et al., RaDialog, arXiv:2311.18681. DOI 10.13026/zecj-bh52. Images are not included and must be obtained from MIMIC-CXR-JPG.

name: RadVLM Instruction Dataset
full_name: RadVLM Instruction Dataset (PhysioNet v1.0.0)
protocol_note: Frontal chest X-rays only (lateral views excluded); images referenced from MIMIC-CXR-JPG, Chest ImaGenome, MS-CXR and VinDr-CXR
size: 719,675 image–instruction instances (PhysioNet release; full RadVLM set 1,115,021 incl. CheXpert/PadChest-derived data not released)
paired_text_detail: LLaVA-format user–assistant instructions: GPT-4o-filtered MIMIC-CXR reports, CheXbert abnormality lists, bounding-box grounding answers, and ~87k GPT-4o-generated multi-turn conversations
description: Credentialed PhysioNet release of 719,675 LLaVA-format chest X-ray image–instruction pairs for report generation, abnormality classification, anatomy/abnormality/phrase grounding and multi-turn conversations, referencing frontal images from MIMIC-CXR-JPG, Chest ImaGenome, MS-CXR and VinDr-CXR.

label_schema: Report generation: MIMIC-CXR Findings/Impression with prior-study references removed by GPT-4o (230,980 pairs)
Abnormality classification: 14 CheXpert labels from CheXbert, uncertain treated as absent (237,912 pairs)
Anatomical grounding: one of 29 Chest ImaGenome regions per image, normalized [x1,y1,x2,y2] (80,000)
Abnormality grounding/detection: VinDr-CXR boxes fused across 3 readers via weighted box fusion (16,089 x3; 15,000 x2)
Phrase grounding: MS-CXR sentence-box pairs (971 x3)
Conversations: 86,155 GPT-4o multi-turn from MIMIC-CXR; 862 grounded conversations from MS-CXR (x4)
details.file_structure: Single JSON file containing a list of dicts {image: path to image, conversations: [{from: human, value: '<image>\n<question>'}, {from: gpt, value: answer}]}; images must be downloaded separately from the source PhysioNet datasets and arranged per the paths.
details.label_readers: VinDr-CXR boxes from 3 radiologists per image fused by weighted box fusion; report filtering and conversations generated by GPT-4o, not manually reviewed by experts
details.reference_standard: Labels inherited from source datasets (CheXbert NLP labels, Chest ImaGenome, MS-CXR and VinDr-CXR annotations); no new clinical confirmation

related.name: Chest ImaGenome
related.note: 29 anatomical region boxes turned into anatomical grounding instructions (80,000)

related.name: MS-CXR
related.note: Sentence-box pairs used for phrase grounding and grounded conversations

related.name: MIMIC-CXR
related.note: Free-text reports filtered of prior-study references by GPT-4o

details.third_party_note: The page notes that 'MIMIC-CXR terms of use include a prohibition of sharing the data with third parties'; the authors used a special Azure OpenAI instance per PhysioNet's responsible-LLM-use guidance. The dataset itself is credentialed access; its exact licence text was not shown in the evidence.
details.extra: DOI 10.13026/et5g-h222; paper: Deperrois et al., RadVLM, arXiv:2502.03333. CheXpert- and PadChest-derived datapoints are excluded owing to DUA terms; GPT-4o outputs may contain errors.

name: ReFiSco
full_name: ReFiSco: Report Fix and Score Dataset for Radiology Report Generation (ReFiSco-v0)
protocol_note: Single frontal-view chest radiographs from MIMIC-CXR (images not included; obtain from MIMIC-CXR)
size: 60 MIMIC-CXR studies (single frontal view); 3 report sources; annotations by 4 radiologists
paired_text_detail: Report impressions from X-REM, CXR-RePaiR and the original MIMIC-CXR report, with line-by-line radiologist edits and error-severity scores
description: Radiologist line-level error-severity scores and corrections for model-generated (X-REM, CXR-RePaiR) and original MIMIC-CXR report impressions on 60 frontal chest X-ray studies, for evaluating radiology report generation.

label_schema: impression_original: one line of the report impression, unedited
impression_edited: radiologist's revision of the line
score: error severity - No error, Not actionable, Actionable nonurgent error, Urgent error, Emergent error
source: X-REM, CXR-RePaiR or 'expert' (human-written MIMIC-CXR report)
details.file_structure: refisco-v0.csv (one row per report line; consecutive rows with the same study id form one report annotation) and Data_Analysis.ipynb (example analysis notebook); also mirrored on GitHub rajpurkarlab/ReFiSco-v0. Images must be obtained from MIMIC-CXR.
details.label_readers: 4 practicing radiologists, blinded to report source; each was shown one frontal image and one randomly chosen report (X-REM, CXR-RePaiR or MIMIC-CXR) for each of the 60 studies
details.reference_standard: Radiologist judgement of each report line against the frontal chest radiograph; a generated comparison to a prior study counted as a non-actionable error
details.third_party_note: Access requires credentialing, CITI training and signing the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0. The DUA clause on external services is not quoted on the page; re-read the DUA before sending data to online services.
details.extra: Introduced in Jeong et al., 'Multimodal Image-Text Matching Improves Retrieval-based Chest X-Ray Report Generation' (MIDL 2023, arXiv:2303.17579). The authors note the dataset is small and preliminary. IRB22-0364. DOI 10.13026/cneg-zk64.

aliases: Report Fix and Score Dataset for Radiology Reports

name: CXR-Phone
full_name: Smartphone-Captured Chest X-Ray Photographs
protocol_note: Smartphone photographs of frontal-view CXR images displayed on computer monitors (multiple smartphones and monitors, varied lighting; Photo-MED taken by nine resident doctors, mostly with Microsoft Office Lens)
size: 6,453 smartphone photographs of frontal CXRs in 4 subsets (Photo-MMC 1,759; Photo-CXP 1,337; Photo-MED 1,337; Photo-DEV 2,020)
description: Smartphone photographs of 6,453 frontal chest X-rays from MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert, taken with varied phones, monitors and users, with CheXpert/NegBio report-derived labels for 14 findings, for evaluating AI robustness on photographed CXRs.

label_schema: 14 CheXpert observations per image; CSV coding not_mentioned = 0, negative = 1, uncertain = 2, positive = 3
Photo-DEV: positive/negative labels taken from the CheXpert validation set
Image names encode subject_ID, study_num and image_num of the source MIMIC-CXR/CheXpert image

14 CheXpert observations (no finding, enlarged cardiomediastinum, cardiomegaly, airspace opacity, lung lesion, edema, consolidation, pneumonia, atelectasis, pneumothorax, pleural effusion, pleural other, fracture, support devices)
details.file_structure: Four directories (Photo-MMC, Photo-CXP, Photo-MED, Photo-DEV), each with JPEG photographs, a CSV of labels and a TXT Readme of capture settings. Only the Photo-MMC images are downloadable from PhysioNet. The Photo-CXP, Photo-MED and Photo-DEV images come from the Stanford Photo-CheXpert site (http://eepurl.com/hcIi0T); their labels and Readmes are on PhysioNet.
details.splits: Photo-DEV corresponds to the CheXpert validation set (202 images photographed 10 times under different device and lighting settings); no other official splits stated

details.reference_standard: Labels inherited from the source datasets: automatic NLP extraction from radiology reports (CheXpert validation labels for Photo-DEV)

details.third_party_note: PhysioNet Restricted Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0: the user 'will not share the data and will make no attempt to reidentify individuals'. Users must also accept the Photo-CheXpert Research Use Agreement. Sending images to external services may count as sharing; re-read the DUA before doing so.
details.extra: Photos were taken off computer monitors with many smartphones; Photo-MED was taken by nine resident doctors, mostly using Microsoft Office Lens. Created in the HST.953 course at Harvard-MIT. DOI 10.13026/7b2j-nq93.

name: Symile-MIMIC
full_name: Symile-MIMIC: a multimodal clinical dataset of chest X-rays, electrocardiograms, and blood labs from MIMIC-IV
protocol_note: PA or AP chest X-rays from MIMIC-CXR-JPG taken 24-72 h after admission; resized to 320 px smaller edge, square crop, ImageNet-normalised tensors (n,3,320,320). Paired with 12-lead ECG and up to 50 blood labs within 24 h of admission.
size: 11,622 admissions / 9,573 patients (one CXR, one ECG and up to 50 blood labs per admission)
description: Multimodal benchmark derived from MIMIC-IV, MIMIC-IV-ECG and MIMIC-CXR-JPG that links, for 11,622 admissions, an admission ECG and blood labs to a PA/AP chest X-ray taken 24-72 hours after admission, for zero-shot CXR retrieval.

label_schema: symile_mimic_data.csv columns: subject_id, hadm_id, admission/discharge times and locations, deathtime, hospital_expire_flag, race, gender, age
CXR: cxr_dicom_id, cxr_study_id, view position, StudyDateTime, cxr_path, and 14 CheXpert label columns (Atelectasis ... Support Devices)
50 lab itemid columns (earliest value within 24 h of admission) plus labs_all_nan
Retrieval splits: label_hadm_id (query) and binary label (1 = positive candidate)
details.file_structure: symile_mimic_data.csv; train.csv, val.csv, val_retrieval.csv and test.csv (with lab percentile columns); labs_means.json; data_npy/<split>/ with cxr_<split>.npy (n,3,320,320, ImageNet-normalised), ecg_<split>.npy (n,1,5000,12), labs_percentiles/missingness, hadm_id and label tensors; code/ with generation scripts; symile_mimic_model.ckpt
details.splits: Patient-disjoint splits: train 10,000 admissions / 8,374 patients; val 750 / 738 (val_retrieval 7,500 rows = 750 queries x 10 candidates); test 464 / 461 (4,640 rows)
details.reference_standard: Retrieval positive = the CXR from the same admission as the query ECG+labs; 9 negatives sampled from the same split. CheXpert labels are inherited from MIMIC-CXR-JPG.

related.name: MIMIC-IV-ECG

description: Standardized lightweight collection of 12 2D and 6 3D biomedical image classification datasets (e.g. ChestMNIST, PneumoniaMNIST, OrganA/C/SMNIST, NoduleMNIST3D, FractureMNIST3D, AdrenalMNIST3D, VesselMNIST3D) pre-processed to small fixed sizes with classification labels, released as NPZ files.

name: CT-RATE-Refined
full_name: CT-RATE-Refined: LLM-assisted cleaned report-derived abnormality labels for CT-RATE chest CT
protocol_note: Labels for CT-RATE chest CT volumes; no acquisition details given in this label-only release.
size: Labels for all CT-RATE train/validation volumes (24,446 unique reports after deduplication); 100-report development reference set; 250-report confirmatory radiologist reference set
description: Refined report-aligned labels for the 18 CT-RATE chest CT abnormalities, produced by multi-LLM majority voting (GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 mini, DeepSeek-V3.2) and released with per-model outputs and radiologist reference annotations for validation.

label_schema: 18 CT-RATE binary labels (1 = present, 0 = absent): Medical material, Arterial wall calcification, Cardiomegaly, Pericardial effusion, Coronary artery wall calcification, Hiatal hernia, Lymphadenopathy, Emphysema, Atelectasis, Lung nodule, Lung opacity, Pulmonary fibrotic sequela, Pleural effusion, Mosaic attenuation pattern, Peribronchial thickening, Consolidation, Bronchiectasis, Interlobular septal thickening
Majority vote: a label is assigned when at least two models chose the same class; it is empty otherwise (11 reports)
positive_votes: number of models assigning 1 per label

Confirmatory reference: four-level label (present, uncertain, negated, not_mentioned), temporality (current, prior_only, resolved), source (agreed or adjudicated), and a binary label under Rule A (present and uncertain = 1)
per-model LLM labels and positive-vote counts
four-level radiologist reference labels (present/uncertain/negated/not_mentioned) with temporality
details.file_structure: labels/volume_level/{train,valid}_predicted_labels.csv are drop-in replacements for the CT-RATE multi_abnormality_labels files. labels/report_level/ holds majority_vote.csv, positive_votes.csv and per-model CSVs (gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, deepseek-v3.2). mapping/volume_to_report.csv maps volumes to reports. reference/development/ holds random_set.csv and the discordance review sets. reference/confirmatory/ holds design.csv, preconsensus_reader_{1,2}.csv, reference_standard.csv and llm_runs/. All files are keyed by the CT-RATE VolumeName.
details.splits: Follows the CT-RATE train/validation splits; the 250-report confirmatory reference set is a stratified sample from the validation split with design weights.
details.label_readers: Full-dataset labels come from majority voting across 3 LLMs applied to report text. Reference sets were annotated by two readers each; the confirmatory set was read independently and then agreed or adjudicated to consensus.
details.reference_standard: All labels are derived from report text and reflect report alignment, not image-level truth. The confirmatory reference is a two-reader consensus reading of the reports (250 reports, stratified sampling).
details.third_party_note: The labels are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The underlying CT-RATE terms state 'Redistribution of the dataset or any portion thereof is not allowed' and limit use to academic, research and educational purposes. Neither licence addresses sending data to external services.
details.extra: Labels were assigned per unique report and propagated to every volume sharing that report. LLM extraction failed for 12 reports with GPT-5.4 and 10 with GPT-5.4 mini. Paper: Yamagishi et al., 'Large Language Model-Assisted Cleaning of Report-Derived Labels in a Large-Scale Chest CT Dataset', accepted in the Journal of Medical Systems (arXiv:2606.22382). Images and reports must be requested from CT-RATE.

aliases: Large Language Model-Assisted Cleaning of Report-Derived Labels in a Large-Scale Chest CT Dataset

name: CT2XR Projections
full_name: Component-wise Translated CT Projections (Anatomy-Decomposed Chest CT Projections for Bone Suppression)
protocol_note: Synthetic PA chest radiographs (DRRs) projected from CT-RATE chest CTs (slice spacing <=1 mm) with a polychromatic attenuation model at simulated 100 kVp, one fixed PA geometry; bone and soft-tissue components translated by an unpaired image-to-image model; 512x512 8-bit grayscale.
size: 22,124 synthetic PA radiographs (each with 4 aligned 512x512 images) from 22,124 CT-RATE volumes / 14,538 patients; ~7.9 GB
description: Qure.ai release of 22,124 synthetic PA chest radiographs projected from CT-RATE chest CTs. Each radiograph comes with pixel-aligned translated bone, translated soft-tissue and lung component projections for bone-suppression research, plus six report-derived binary findings.

label_schema: bone_translated: bone projection after unpaired appearance translation
soft_translated: non-lung soft-tissue projection after translation
translated: recombined synthetic radiograph (weighted/normalised, not a plain sum)
lung_opacity, pleural_effusion, atelectasis, cardiomegaly, consolidation, lung_lesion: int8 0/1 copied from CT-RATE report-derived multi-abnormality labels
volume_name (CT-RATE {origin}_{patient}_{scan}_{reconstruction}), kvp (simulated, 100), source-CT spacing_x, spacing_z, rows, columns, num_slices
details.file_structure: Parquet shards data/train-*.parquet (18 shards in v1.1.0); one row per source CT with four 512x512 8-bit grayscale images plus label and metadata columns.
details.splits: Single 'train' packaging split with the whole release (20,844 volumes from CT-RATE train, 1,280 from CT-RATE valid); not a prescribed partition. Group by patient (first two tokens of volume_name) to avoid patient leakage.
details.label_readers: No new reading; labels copied from CT-RATE's report-derived multi-abnormality labels
details.reference_standard: Findings reflect the source CT report: 0 means not reported, not confirmed absent. A finding may not be visible on the PA projection. lung_opacity and lung_lesion are broader CT concepts and should not be read as chest-radiograph ground truth.

related.name: CT-RATE
related.note: 22,124 chest CT volumes decomposed into bone/lung/soft tissue, projected to PA DRRs, bone and soft tissue translated toward real CXR appearance; six report-derived abnormality labels copied from CT-RATE

details.third_party_note: Released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike). The images are derived from CT-RATE, whose terms restrict use to academic/research purposes, prohibit redistribution and require derived data sharing to respect its privacy and confidentiality terms.
details.extra: Synthetic images, not acquired radiographs. Pipeline: CT segmented into bone, lung and soft tissue, each projected through a fixed PA geometry at 100 kVp (polychromatic model), then bone and soft tissue translated with an unpaired image-to-image model. Only CT-RATE volumes with slice spacing <=1 mm were used. Manuscript reports FID 8.2 vs VinDr-CXR and 16.3 vs CheXpert in a CXR-pretrained feature space. Untranslated bone and soft-tissue projections are not included. 5,231 patients contribute multiple volumes (up to 25). Paper: arXiv:2609.24937. label provenance per anatomy (manual vs pseudo)

protocol_note: Skull-stripped T1w MRI resampled to 1 mm, pooled from 607 OpenNeuro datasets (heterogeneous scanners/field strengths)

r1-r7: percentile of each Q over all cases (higher is riskier); R: mean of r1-r7; tier: HighConf (lowest quarter of R), Standard (middle half), Flagged (top quarter)
seven automated quality checks (Q1-Q7) with percentile risk scores and HighConf/Standard/Flagged tier

name: HVM

details.extra: Centers: The University of Hong Kong-Shenzhen Hospital (2019-2021) and Peking University Shenzhen Hospital (2018-2019). Scanners from three manufacturers; slice thickness 1-1.25 mm (≤3 mm per the inclusion criteria). Center 2 images were previously used in earlier hepatic and portal vein segmentation work, and 62.41% of cases were used in preoperative planning for major hepatectomy. No radiomic features are included. Paper: Xie et al., Sci Data 13, 1259 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41597-026-07550-3.

name: LIDC-annot-NLST501
full_name: LIDC-annot-NLST501: LIDC-IDRI-like Multi-Reader annotations of lung nodules on NLST CT scans
protocol_note: NLST low-dose chest CT; GE, Philips, Siemens, Toshiba; slice thickness 0.75-3.2 mm; thinnest hard kernel selected per patient (Ardila et al. 2019 rules); one scan per patient
size: 501 NLST low-dose chest CT scans / 501 patients (152 cancer, 349 non-cancer); 4 independent reads per scan; 23,099 lesions; 6,505 segmented nodules in 2,004 mask files; 13.65 GB

description: LIDC-IDRI-style annotations of 501 NLST low-dose chest CT scans, each read independently by four of 20 radiologists, with 23,099 localized lesions and 6,505 3D-segmented and characterized nodules including malignancy ratings.

label_schema: Target lesion (TL): nodule 4-30 mm; Mass: 30-60 mm; Non-target lesion (NTL): other focal abnormality, subtyped (pleural plaque, scar, atelectasis, focal fibrosis, etc.), max 5 per read
Centroid and size for each Mass/TL/NTL

For up to 6 most suspicious TL/Mass per read: malignancy likelihood 1-10, sphericity (3-step), margin (3-step), lobulation (3-step), spiculation (3-step), texture (solid / part-solid / GGO), calcification (popcorn, laminated, solid, central, non-central, absent), relation to bronchus and to vessel (absent / adjacent / passing through)
Per segmented lesion: volume, center of mass, long axis, short axis, largest average diameter
readers.csv: reader_id, experience in years, class (junior / middle / senior)
correction.csv: original and corrected series UIDs, pid, study_yr, slice counts, correction_type
lesion localization, type and size (target lesion / mass / non-target lesion subtype)
sphericity, margin, lobulation, spiculation, texture, calcification
details.file_structure: The TCIA manifests cover 501 source NLST CT series, 24 corrected CT series and 2,004 DICOM SEG series (2,529 series in total). NIfTI masks are at /masks_nifti/[s01-s04]/[pid]_[series_uid].nii.gz, one folder per independent read; each lesion has an integer index in the mask. All findings are consolidated in a single CSV; readers.csv, correction.csv and LIDC-annot-NLST501_workflow.png are also provided.
details.label_readers: 20 board-certified radiologists hired through Ingedata (8 junior, 7 mid-level, 5 senior). Each scan was read independently by 4 readers under a split-plot MRMC design; readers were blinded to NLST clinical data. There is no consensus step.
details.reference_standard: Cancer status comes from NLST histopathology-confirmed diagnoses; non-cancer patients required 3 years of follow-up. The set is enriched to 30.3% cancer (152/501). Nodule features and malignancy ratings are subjective per-reader assessments.
details.third_party_note: The page states 'Data Citation Required'; no license text was captured in the evidence.
details.extra: TCIA page last updated 2026/08/05. DOI 10.7937/y2dx-e334. The annotation campaign ran from December 2022 to October 2023 using Median Technologies' Annot tool. 410 of the 501 patients overlap the Ardila et al. 2019 NLST subset, enabling Lung-RADS comparison. Inter-reader agreement on the characterization criteria is low (Krippendorff alpha 0.152 on the 5-step scale, 0.228 on the 3-step scale). Pure-GGO-only cancers and lesions >30 mm (except masses) are excluded from patient selection. Associated paper: 'Rethinking Lung Cancer Screening: AI Nodule Detection and Diagnosis Outperforms Radiologists...' (in submission).

description: Token-aligned 3D patch-level localization labels for nine abnormalities on 2,201 non-contrast chest CT studies from CT-RATE, made by medical students and reviewed by a senior physician.

label_schema: One binary .npz array of shape (24, 12, 12) (Z, Y, X patch grid) per abnormality present in a volume; 1 = patch positive
Missing file for a class = volume negative for that class
Classes: arterial_wall_calcification, coronary artery wall calcification, pericardial_effusion, hiatal_hernia, lymphadenopathy, atelectasis, lung_opacity, consolidation, bronchiectasis
The grid refers to CT-RATE volumes resampled to 0.75x0.75x1.5 mm and center-cropped to 384x384x192 voxels (patch 32x32x8 voxels, ~6.9 cm3)
volume-level presence of 9 abnormalities (implied by file presence)
details.file_structure: Zenodo v3: annotations-train.zip (3.3 MB) and annotations-valid.zip (305.2 KB); one subfolder per CT-RATE volume ID (e.g. train_1003_a_1/) containing <abnormality>.npz files. No images, reports or metadata are included. Alignment code is at https://github.com/SadVoxel/PatchChestCT.
details.splits: annotations-train / annotations-valid aligned with the official CT-RATE splits; no separate test set; 185 validation volumes
details.label_readers: Trained medical students annotated 24 reference axial slices per volume, with labels propagated ±4 slices. A single senior physician reviewed every annotation. Flagged cases were re-annotated by two further annotators, and the senior physician adjudicated disagreements. The senior physician also reviewed and corrected all 185 validation volumes.
details.reference_standard: Visual image-based annotation correcting the NLP-derived CT-RATE report labels (abnormality labelled only if visible). Inter-rater volume-level mean AC1 is 0.921; blind patch-level Dice is 0.477 (hiatal hernia 0.214). The authors recommend use as a training resource rather than a strict benchmark. Cases were enriched: annotators preferentially chose cases with visible abnormalities.
details.third_party_note: Annotations are CC BY 4.0, which 'applies only to the PatchChestCT annotation files and does not grant rights to any underlying CT-RATE data'. The images are CT-RATE (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with terms): 'Redistribution of the dataset or any portion thereof is not allowed', and the terms require maintaining data confidentiality.
details.extra: Paper: Li et al., Scientific Data 13:1180 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41597-026-07793-0. Pleural effusion and nodules were deliberately excluded. Strong class imbalance exists; lung opacity covers ~2.5% of patches in train.
